text.id: Menurut sebagian ahli, penyebutan tertua ada dalam Epos Gilgamesh (sekitar 2100 SM); sumber awal lain mencakup Petronius (27–66) dan Gervase of Tilbury (1150–1228).
text.en: According to some scholars the earliest mention is in the Epic of Gilgamesh (ca. 2100 BCE); other early sources include Petronius (27–66) and Gervase of Tilbury (1150–1228).

short_description.id: Werewolf adalah manusia dalam cerita rakyat yang dapat berubah menjadi serigala, secara sukarela atau tidak, karena keturunan, kutukan, sihir, atau gigitan.
short_description.en: A werewolf is a human in folklore who can change into a wolf, voluntarily or involuntarily, through heredity, a curse, magic, or a bite.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, werewolf ialah laki-laki, perempuan, atau anak yang berubah menjadi serigala, secara sukarela atau tidak. Perubahan itu biasanya sementara, tetapi kadang permanen, dan sang werewolf tampak sebagai serigala bagi dirinya sendiri maupun orang lain, baik dalam wujud maupun perilaku. Berbagai kisah mengaitkannya dengan keturunan, kutukan, sihir, atau gigitan, dan salah satu tradisi menyebut kemampuan itu diperoleh dengan meminum air dari jejak serigala. Sumber yang sama membedakan werewolf dari lycanthrope, yang menurutnya kehilangan akal sehat sepenuhnya setelah berubah.
long_description.en: In folklore, a werewolf is a man, woman, or child who turns into a wolf, voluntarily or involuntarily. The change is usually temporary but sometimes permanent, and the werewolf appears as a wolf to himself and to others, in shape and in behavior. Stories attribute it to heredity, curses, magic, or bites, and one tradition says the power is gained by drinking water from a wolf's footprint. One source distinguishes werewolves from lycanthropes, who in its account lose their sanity entirely after transforming.

long_description.id: Kisah tertua yang dikutip sumber-sumber ini beragam. Sebagian ahli menunjuk Epos Gilgamesh, tempat dewi Ishtar mengubah seorang gembala menjadi serigala. Metamorphoses karya Ovid mengisahkan Lycaon yang dihukum Zeus menjadi serigala dan memberi nama pada lycanthropy, sedangkan Satyricon menampilkan prajurit yang berubah di depan Niceros. Baring-Gould mengutip Herodotus tentang orang Neuri yang berubah menjadi serigala sekali setahun.
long_description.en: The earliest tales in these sources vary. Some scholars point to the Epic of Gilgamesh, in which the goddess Ishtar turns a shepherd into a wolf. Ovid's Metamorphoses tells of Lycaon, whom Zeus punished by turning him into a wolf, and gives lycanthropy its name, while the Satyricon features a soldier who changes before Niceros. Baring-Gould cites Herodotus on the Neuri, who turn into wolves once a year.

long_description.id: Tradisi lain menampilkan variasi. Dalam Völsunga Saga, kulit serigala mengubah Sigmund dan Sinfjötli; dalam kisah Finlandia, perubahan tidak disengaja biasanya merupakan hukuman, sedangkan orang bijak dapat berubah secara sukarela. Dalam kisah Armenia, perempuan serigala lenyap setelah kulitnya dibakar, dan di antara orang Rusia Putih werewolf digambarkan ramah pada kerabatnya.
long_description.en: Other traditions show variations. In the Völsunga Saga wolf skins transform Sigmund and Sinfjötli; in Finnish stories involuntary change is usually a punishment while cunning folk can change voluntarily. In an Armenian story the wolf-woman vanishes after her skin is burned, and among the White Russians the werewolf is described as kind to his kin.

long_description.id: Ciri yang kini paling akrab, seperti bulan purnama dan senjata perak, ternyata muncul belakangan. Menurut Wikipedia, bulan purnama sebagai pemicu baru menjadi umum dalam penggambaran werewolf pada abad ke-20, dan kerentanan terhadap perak muncul dalam sastra Jerman abad ke-19. Kepercayaan pada werewolf berkembang sejajar dengan kepercayaan pada penyihir; pengadilan terhadap orang yang dituduh werewolf muncul pada awal abad ke-15 dan memuncak pada abad ke-17. Bulan purnama juga mengingatkan pada 'kegilaan' (lunacy), penyakit jiwa sementara yang pada Abad Pertengahan diyakini terkait fase bulan, dan werewolf perempuan dalam kisah abad ke-19 dan awal abad ke-20 digambarkan sebagai siren.
long_description.en: The features most familiar today, such as the full moon and silver weapons, turn out to be late arrivals. According to Wikipedia the full moon as a trigger only became widespread in depictions of werewolves in the twentieth century, and vulnerability to silver appears in 19th-century German literature. Belief in werewolves developed in parallel with belief in witches; trials of supposed werewolves emerged in the early 15th century and peaked in the 17th. The full moon also evokes 'lunacy', a temporary mental illness believed in the Middle Ages to be related to the phases of the moon, and female werewolves in 19th- and early 20th-century stories are depicted as sirens.

cultural_context.id: Peneliti Finlandia menafsirkan wujud serigala sebagai simbol keliyanan sosial yang berlandaskan moral, sebab perubahan tak disengaja dalam kisah mereka biasanya hukuman dan kadang menyerupai penjara atau pengusiran. Penulis lain menyebut werewolf, seperti banyak monster yang dapat menyerupai manusia, sebagai cermin ketakutan dan keinginan manusia. Menurut penulis yang sama, werewolf bukan mayat hidup melainkan manusia hidup yang terjebak di antara keadaan manusia dan hewan. Robert Eisler menafsirkan bahwa dasar legenda werewolf di dunia terletak pada evolusi berburu dengan mengenakan kulit hewan pada zaman es terakhir.
cultural_context.en: The Finnish researchers read the wolf shape as standing for a socially defined otherness grounded in morality, since involuntary change in their stories is usually a punishment and sometimes resembles prison or expulsion. Another author describes werewolves, like many monsters that can take our form, as a mirror of human fears and desires. According to the same author, werewolves are not the undead but living people trapped between human and animal states. Robert Eisler interprets the basis of werewolf legends worldwide as lying in the evolution of hunting in animal skins during the last ice age.

literal_meaning.id: 'Manusia-serigala'; rekonstruksi alternatif mengusulkan 'berpakaian serigala'.
literal_meaning.en: 'Man-wolf'; an alternative reconstruction proposes 'wolf-clothed'.

who.id: Werewolf adalah manusia dalam cerita rakyat yang berubah menjadi serigala.
who.en: A werewolf is a human in folklore who changes into a wolf.

origin.id: Kisah werewolf ditemukan di banyak tempat di dunia, dari teks klasik sampai cerita rakyat berbagai bangsa.
origin.en: Werewolf tales are found in many places around the world, from classical texts to the folk tales of various peoples.

role.id: Dalam banyak kisah perubahan menjadi serigala berfungsi sebagai hukuman atau akibat kutukan, sihir, keturunan, atau gigitan.
role.en: In many stories turning into a wolf serves as punishment or the result of a curse, magic, heredity, or a bite.

famous_for.id: Werewolf paling dikenal sebagai manusia yang berubah menjadi serigala.
famous_for.en: Werewolves are best known as humans who turn into wolves.

did_you_know.id: Bulan purnama sebagai pemicu perubahan werewolf baru menjadi bagian penggambaran yang luas pada abad ke-20, dan film pertama yang menampilkannya adalah Frankenstein Meets the Wolf Man pada 1943.
did_you_know.en: The full moon as a werewolf trigger only became a widespread part of depictions in the twentieth century, and the first film to feature it was Frankenstein Meets the Wolf Man in 1943.

description.id: Werewolf berubah wujud menjadi serigala, secara sukarela atau tidak; perubahan biasanya sementara tetapi kadang permanen.
description.en: A werewolf changes shape into a wolf, voluntarily or involuntarily; the change is usually temporary but sometimes permanent.

description.id: Dalam kisah Finlandia, orang bijak yang berubah secara sukarela sementara memiliki kemampuan berguna hewan itu.
description.en: In Finnish stories, cunning folk who change voluntarily temporarily possess the animal's useful abilities.

description.id: Dalam tradisi Serbia, vlkoslak terbebas dari sihirnya jika kulitnya dibakar; dalam kisah Armenia perempuan itu lenyap ketika kulit serigalanya terbakar habis.
description.en: In Serbian tradition the vlkoslak is disenchanted if its skin is burned; in the Armenian story the woman vanishes when her wolf-skin is consumed by fire.

description.id: Sebagian besar fiksi modern menggambarkan werewolf rentan terhadap senjata perak dan sangat tahan terhadap cedera lain.
description.en: Most modern fiction describes werewolves as vulnerable to silver weapons and highly resistant to other injuries.

name.en: Wounds carry over to the human form

description.id: Dalam kisah Satyricon, serigala yang ditombak di leher berkaitan dengan prajurit yang ditemukan dengan luka leher keesokan harinya.
description.en: In the Satyricon story, the wolf speared through the neck corresponds to the soldier found with a neck wound the next day.

description.id: Dalam kisah Finlandia, orang bijak berubah secara sukarela, sedangkan perubahan tak disengaja biasanya hukuman, misalnya bagi pencuri yang tersisa buntut pendek, atau seluruh rombongan pernikahan yang diubah oleh penyihir atau pengemis yang tidak diundang.
description.en: In Finnish stories cunning folk change voluntarily, while involuntary change is usually punishment, for example a thief left with a stub of a tail, or a whole wedding party turned by a witch or beggar who was not invited.

description.id: Lelaki yang dihukum setan dengan diubah menjadi serigala dan dikirim kepada kerabatnya, yang mengenali dan memberinya makan; ia digambarkan ramah dan tidak berbuat jahat.
description.en: A man punished by the devil by being turned into a wolf and sent among his relations, who recognize and feed him; he is described as amiable and does no mischief.

description.id: Menurut Olaus Magnus, werewolf Livonia diinisiasi dengan menghabiskan secangkir bir khusus dan mengulang rumus tertentu; dalam kisah lain perubahan berlangsung dua belas hari dan kawanan itu menyerang ternak tetapi tidak mampu membunuh manusia.
description.en: According to Olaus Magnus Livonian werewolves were initiated by draining a cup of special beer and repeating a set formula; in another account the change lasts twelve days and the pack attacks livestock but cannot slay men.

description.id: Kata Proto-Slavia yang berarti 'berambut serigala' direkonstruksi dari bentuk Serbia, Slovenia, dan Ceko, termasuk vlkodlak; dalam tradisi yang dicatat Baring-Gould, vlkoslak terbebas dari sihirnya jika kulitnya dibakar.
description.en: A Proto-Slavic word meaning 'wolf-haired' is reconstructed from Serbian, Slovenian, and Czech forms, including vlkodlak; in the tradition Baring-Gould records, the vlkoslak is disenchanted if its skin is burned.

description.id: Werewolf Polandia mengamuk dua kali setahun, pada Natal dan pertengahan musim panas.
description.en: Polish werewolves rage twice a year, at Christmas and at midsummer.

role.id: Raja yang dihukum Zeus menjadi serigala.
role.en: The king whom Zeus turned into a wolf.

summary.id: Menurut Metamorphoses karya Ovid, Lycaon, raja Arcadia, menguji kemahatahuan Zeus dengan menyajikan daging putranya, Nyctimus, dan sebagai hukuman Zeus mengubahnya menjadi serigala. Kisah ini memberi nama pada lycanthropy.
summary.en: In Ovid's Metamorphoses, Lycaon, king of Arcadia, tested Zeus's omniscience by serving him the flesh of his son Nyctimus, and as punishment Zeus turned him into a wolf. The story gives lycanthropy its name.

role.id: Prajurit berubah menjadi serigala di depan Niceros.
role.en: A soldier turns into a wolf before Niceros.

summary.id: Niceros menceritakan perjalanan bersama temannya, seorang prajurit, yang berubah menjadi serigala di depan matanya lalu lari. Kemudian ia mendengar seekor serigala membunuh domba dan ditombak di leher, dan menemukan temannya di tempat tidur dengan luka leher.
summary.en: Niceros tells of traveling with a soldier friend who turned into a wolf before his eyes and ran off. He later heard that a wolf killed sheep and was speared through the neck, and found his friend in bed with a neck wound.

role.id: Dua pahlawan berubah menjadi serigala dengan mengenakan kulit curian.
role.en: Two heroes become wolves by putting on stolen skins.

summary.id: Sigmund dan Sinfjötli menemukan dua orang yang tampak tidur dengan kulit serigala tergantung di atasnya, mencuri dan mengenakan kulit itu, lalu berubah menjadi serigala. Setelah Sinfjötli selamat berkat sejenis ramuan, keduanya meninggalkan kulit itu.
summary.en: Sigmund and Sinfjötli find two apparently sleeping men with wolf skins hanging above them, steal and put on the skins, and become wolves. After Sinfjötli is saved by an unnamed herb, the two abandon the skins.

role.id: Bangsa yang dikatakan berubah menjadi serigala sekali setahun.
role.en: A people said to turn into wolves once a year.

summary.id: Baring-Gould mengutip Herodotus: setiap orang Neuri berubah menjadi serigala sekali setahun, bertahan dalam wujud itu beberapa hari, lalu kembali ke wujud semula.
summary.en: Baring-Gould quotes Herodotus: each Neurian changes into a wolf once a year, stays in that form for several days, then resumes his former shape.

title.id: Gembala dan Ishtar dalam Epos Gilgamesh
title.en: The shepherd and Ishtar in the Epic of Gilgamesh

role.id: Dewi mengubah gembala menjadi serigala.
role.en: A goddess turns a shepherd into a wolf.

summary.id: Sebagian ahli menganggap perubahan ini penyebutan lycanthropy tertua di Barat; dalam kisahnya dewi Ishtar mengubah seorang gembala yang patah hati menjadi serigala.
summary.en: Some scholars consider this the earliest mention of lycanthropy in the west; in the story the goddess Ishtar turns a lovelorn shepherd into a wolf.

role.id: Perempuan lenyap ketika kulit serigalanya dibakar.
role.en: A woman vanishes when her wolf-skin is burned.

summary.id: Seorang lelaki menemukan kulit serigala di gua dan melemparnya ke api; seorang perempuan muncul, melolong, dan mencoba menyelamatkan kulit itu, lalu lenyap dalam asap setelah kulit itu hangus.
summary.en: A man found a wolf-skin in a cave and cast it into a fire; a woman appeared, howled, and tried to rescue the skin, then vanished in the smoke once the hide was consumed.

description.id: Wilayah Raja Lycaon dalam kisah Ovid.
description.en: The realm of King Lycaon in Ovid's tale.

description.id: Wilayah yang dikaitkan dengan orang Neuri dalam kutipan Herodotus.
description.en: The region associated with the Neuri in the Herodotus passage.

description.id: Wilayah werewolf yang diinisiasi dengan bir khusus menurut Olaus Magnus.
description.en: Region of werewolves initiated with special beer according to Olaus Magnus.

description.id: Di wilayah yang kini menjadi Swiss inilah pengadilan terhadap orang yang dituduh werewolf muncul.
description.en: In what is now Switzerland, where trials of supposed werewolves emerged.

description.id: Menurut sebagian ahli, perubahan manusia menjadi serigala dalam epos ini adalah penyebutan lycanthropy tertua di Barat.
description.en: According to some scholars, the man-to-wolf transformation in this epic is the earliest mention of lycanthropy in the west.

description.id: Wikipedia menyebut Petronius (27–66) sebagai salah satu sumber awal kepercayaan pada lycanthropy.
description.en: Wikipedia lists Petronius (27–66) among the early sources for belief in lycanthropy.

description.id: Metamorphoses mengisahkan Lycaon yang diubah menjadi serigala.
description.en: Metamorphoses tells of Lycaon turned into a wolf.

description.id: Gervase of Tilbury (1150–1228) disebut sebagai sumber awal kepercayaan pada lycanthropy.
description.en: Gervase of Tilbury (1150–1228) is listed as an early source for belief in lycanthropy.

description.id: Pengadilan terhadap orang yang dituduh werewolf muncul di wilayah yang kini menjadi Swiss, menyebar pada abad ke-16, memuncak pada abad ke-17, dan mereda pada abad ke-18.
description.en: Trials of supposed werewolves emerged in what is now Switzerland, spread in the 16th century, peaked in the 17th, and subsided by the 18th.

description.id: Kasus ini memicu puncak minat dan penganiayaan terhadap orang yang dituduh werewolf, terutama di Eropa berbahasa Prancis dan Jerman.
description.en: The case led to a significant peak of interest in and persecution of supposed werewolves, primarily in French- and German-speaking Europe.

title.en: The Book of Werewolves first published

description.id: Sabine Baring-Gould pertama kali menerbitkan The Book of Werewolves pada 1865.
description.en: Sabine Baring-Gould first published The Book of Werewolves in 1865.

note.id: Raja yang diubah menjadi serigala; lycanthropy memakai namanya.
note.en: The king turned into a wolf; lycanthropy takes its name from him.

note.id: Menurut seorang penulis, werewolf dan vampir terhubung dalam kemampuan supernatural dan nafsu akan daging manusia.
note.en: According to one author, werewolves and vampires are connected in supernatural abilities and appetite for human flesh.

description.id: Film panjang pertama yang memakai werewolf antropomorfik.
description.en: The first feature film to use an anthropomorphic werewolf.

description.id: Film pertama yang menampilkan efek perubahan wujud akibat bulan purnama.
description.en: The first movie to feature the transformative effect of the full moon.

traditional.id: Kisah tradisional dan klasik menyebut perubahan karena keturunan, kutukan, sihir, gigitan, atau hukuman dewa; kerentanan terhadap perak muncul dalam sastra Jerman abad ke-19.
traditional.en: Traditional and classical tales attribute the change to heredity, curses, magic, bites, or divine punishment; vulnerability to silver appears in 19th-century German literature.

modern.id: Pada abad ke-20 bulan purnama menjadi pemicu perubahan yang lazim dalam penggambaran werewolf, dan fiksi modern menggambarkan werewolf rentan terhadap perak.
modern.en: In the twentieth century the full moon became a common trigger in depictions of werewolves, and modern fiction describes werewolves as vulnerable to silver.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa banyak budaya memiliki kisah manusia yang berubah menjadi serigala?
learning_questions.en: Why do so many cultures have stories of humans who turn into wolves?

learning_questions.id: Bagaimana perubahan menjadi serigala berfungsi sebagai hukuman dalam kisah Lycaon dan kisah Finlandia?
learning_questions.en: How does turning into a wolf work as punishment in the Lycaon story and the Finnish stories?

learning_questions.id: Ciri werewolf mana yang berasal dari tradisi lama dan mana yang baru muncul di fiksi modern?
learning_questions.en: Which werewolf features come from old tradition and which only appeared in modern fiction?

statement.en: A werewolf is a human who changes into a wolf voluntarily or involuntarily.

claims.quote: The change is most often temporary, but can sometimes be permanent.

statement.id: Perubahan werewolf biasanya sementara, meski kadang permanen.
statement.en: Werewolf transformation is usually temporary, though sometimes permanent.

claims.quote: Folk tales, stories, and myths from around the world have different methods by which werewolves exist or are created: through heredity, via a curse, from magic, or by being bitten by another who suffers from the affliction.

statement.id: Kisah werewolf menyebut keturunan, kutukan, sihir, atau gigitan sebagai asal perubahan.
statement.en: Werewolf stories describe heredity, curses, magic, or bites as causes.

claims.quote: The soldier turned into a wolf before Niceros’ eyes, then ran off.

statement.en: In the Satyricon story, a soldier transformed into a wolf before Niceros.

statement.en: In the Völsunga Saga, wolf skins transformed Sigmund and Sinfjötli into wolves.

claims.quote: Finnish belief narratives about humans turning into wolves involve both voluntary and involuntary transformations.

statement.id: Cerita kepercayaan Finlandia memuat perubahan menjadi serigala yang disengaja ataupun tidak.
statement.en: Finnish belief narratives include voluntary and involuntary transformations into wolves.

claims.quote: The involuntary transformation is usually a punishment and sometimes parallels with prison or expulsion.

statement.id: Dalam cerita Finlandia, perubahan tak disengaja biasanya merupakan hukuman.
statement.en: In Finnish stories, involuntary transformation is usually a punishment.

claims.quote: To punish Lycaon for his transgressions, he transformed him into a wolf.

statement.id: Zeus mengubah Lycaon menjadi serigala sebagai hukuman.
statement.en: Zeus transformed Lycaon into a wolf as punishment.

claims.quote: One feature of twentieth-century werewolf lore which also relates to anxieties about women – the full moon as a stimulant for transformation

statement.id: Bulan purnama sebagai pemicu perubahan menjadi ciri kisah werewolf abad ke-20.
statement.en: The full moon as a trigger for transformation is a feature of twentieth-century werewolf lore.

claims.quote: The change is most often temporary, but can sometimes be permanent. They appear to themselves and to others as wolves, in both shape and behavior.

statement.id: Menurut sumber ini, werewolf tampak sebagai serigala bagi dirinya sendiri maupun orang lain, baik dalam wujud maupun perilaku.
statement.en: According to this source, werewolves appear as wolves both to themselves and to others, in shape and in behavior.

claims.quote: Unlike werewolves, lycanthropes lose their sanity entirely after transformation

statement.id: Menurut sumber ini, berbeda dengan werewolf, lycanthrope kehilangan akal sehat sepenuhnya setelah berubah wujud.
statement.en: According to this source, unlike werewolves, lycanthropes lose their sanity entirely after transformation.

claims.quote: Some scholars believe the transformation from man into wolf in the Epic of Gilgamesh (ca. 2100 BCE) is the first mention of lycanthropy in the west. In this story, the goddess Ishtar transforms a lovelorn shepherd into a wolf.

statement.id: Sebagian ahli meyakini perubahan manusia menjadi serigala dalam Epos Gilgamesh (sekitar 2100 SM) adalah penyebutan lycanthropy tertua di Barat; di sana dewi Ishtar mengubah seorang gembala yang patah hati menjadi serigala.
statement.en: Some scholars believe the man-to-wolf transformation in the Epic of Gilgamesh (ca. 2100 BCE) is the first mention of lycanthropy in the west; there the goddess Ishtar transforms a lovelorn shepherd into a wolf.

claims.quote: Ovid’s Metamorphoses (ca. 8 CE) tells of King Lycaon of Arcadia's attempt to deceive Jupiter via transformation into a wolf, and his subsequent punishment. It is this story that gives us the word lycanthrope.

statement.id: Metamorphoses karya Ovid (sekitar 8 M) mengisahkan Raja Lycaon dari Arcadia yang mencoba menipu Jupiter lewat perubahan menjadi serigala dan dihukum; kisah inilah yang memberi kita kata lycanthrope.
statement.en: Ovid's Metamorphoses (ca. 8 CE) tells of King Lycaon of Arcadia's attempt to deceive Jupiter through transformation into a wolf, and his punishment; this story gives us the word lycanthrope.

claims.quote: In The Satyricon of Patronius, Niceros tells a tale of travelling the road with a brave friend who was a soldier. ... Upon arrival at his destination, Niceros was told that a wolf had recently killed all the sheep, and been speared through the neck. At home the next day, Niceros found his friend in bed, with a doctor tending a neck wound.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Satyricon, Niceros mendengar bahwa seekor serigala baru saja membunuh semua domba dan ditombak di leher; keesokan harinya ia menemukan temannya di tempat tidur, lehernya sedang dirawat dokter.
statement.en: In the Satyricon story Niceros heard that a wolf had killed all the sheep and been speared through the neck; the next day he found his friend in bed with a doctor tending a neck wound.

claims.quote: The Völsunga Saga, a medieval Norse saga, also has a story of lycanthropy. ... Sinfjötli is saved by an unnamed herb, after which the two heros abandon the wolf skins. In this translation they burn the skins so that others will not come to harm.

statement.id: Dalam Völsunga Saga, Sinfjötli diselamatkan oleh sejenis ramuan, lalu kedua pahlawan meninggalkan kulit serigala; dalam terjemahan ini mereka membakar kulit itu agar orang lain tidak celaka.
statement.en: In the Völsunga Saga Sinfjötli is saved by an unnamed herb, after which the two heroes abandon the wolf skins; in this translation they burn the skins so that others will not come to harm.

claims.quote: Robert Eisler, in Man Into Wolf ... He claims the basis of werewolf legends throughout the world lie in the evolution of hunting while wearing animal skins, techniques developed during the last ice age.

statement.id: Robert Eisler berpendapat bahwa dasar legenda werewolf di seluruh dunia terletak pada evolusi berburu dengan mengenakan kulit hewan, teknik yang berkembang pada zaman es terakhir.
statement.en: Robert Eisler claims the basis of werewolf legends worldwide lies in the evolution of hunting while wearing animal skins, techniques developed in the last ice age.

One chapter is titled "Folk-Lore Relating to Were-Wolves," and highlights stories featuring transformation, though not necessarily into wolves, from India, Armenia, North America, and other places around the world.

statement.id: Salah satu bab buku Baring-Gould menyoroti kisah perubahan wujud, tidak selalu menjadi serigala, dari India, Armenia, Amerika Utara, dan tempat lain di dunia.

claims.quote: Finnish belief narratives about humans turning into wolves involve both voluntary and involuntary transformations. ... We interpret the wolf shape as a symbol of morally grounded social otherness.

claims.quote: Lycanthropy – the transformation from human to wolf – takes its name from Lycaon.

statement.id: Dalam banyak kisah sesudah Lycaon, menjadi werewolf dikaitkan secara khusus dengan memakan daging manusia.

claims.quote: some werewolf tales feature benign werewolves, far from the evil pig-, child-, or granny-eating wolves of children’s fairy stories.

statement.id: Sebagian kisah werewolf menampilkan werewolf yang jinak, jauh dari serigala jahat dalam dongeng anak-anak.

claims.quote: Female werewolf stories, in particular, emerge across the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries ... female werewolves are typically depicted as sirens luring strapping young heroes to their doom.

statement.id: Werewolf perempuan dalam kisah abad ke-19 dan awal abad ke-20 umumnya digambarkan sebagai siren yang memikat pahlawan muda menuju kehancuran.
statement.en: Female werewolves in these stories are typically depicted as sirens luring strapping young heroes to their doom.

claims.quote: They are not the undead, but fellow living people trapped between human and animal states.

statement.id: Menurut penulis artikel, werewolf bukan mayat hidup, melainkan manusia hidup yang terjebak di antara keadaan manusia dan hewan.
statement.en: According to the author, werewolves are not the undead but living people trapped between human and animal states.

claims.quote: the full moon as a stimulant for transformation ... It also evokes ‘lunacy’, temporary mental illness believed, in the Middle Ages (and to an extent, beyond), to have been related to the phases of the moon.

statement.id: Bulan purnama juga mengingatkan pada 'kegilaan' (lunacy), penyakit jiwa sementara yang pada Abad Pertengahan dan sesudahnya diyakini terkait fase bulan.

claims.quote: Werewolves – like many monsters, especially those that can take our form – hold a mirror up to us, showing us our fears and desires

statement.id: Menurut penulis, werewolf, seperti banyak monster yang dapat menyerupai manusia, menjadi cermin yang menunjukkan ketakutan dan keinginan kita.
statement.en: According to the author, werewolves, like many monsters that can take our form, hold a mirror up to us, showing our fears and desires.

claims.quote: In popular culture, werewolves have been somewhat overshadowed by their cousin, the sexier (and sparklier) vampire. Certainly, the two are connected in their supernatural abilities and appetite for human flesh.

statement.id: Menurut penulis, werewolf dan vampir terhubung dalam kemampuan supernatural dan nafsu akan daging manusia.
statement.en: According to the author, werewolves and vampires are connected in their supernatural abilities and appetite for human flesh.

claims.quote: Lycaon, a king of Arcadia who sought to test the omniscience of the god Zeus. To do so, he served Zeus the roasted flesh of his son, Nyctimus.

claims.quote: What is Lycanthropy? The change of manor woman into the form of a wolf, either through magical means, so as to enable him or her to gratify the taste for human flesh, or through judgment of the gods in punishment for some great offence.

statement.id: Baring-Gould mendefinisikan lycanthropy sebagai perubahan wujud menjadi serigala, entah lewat cara sihir agar dapat memuaskan selera akan daging manusia, entah lewat hukuman dewa atas pelanggaran besar.
statement.en: Baring-Gould defines lycanthropy as the change into a wolf, whether by magical means to gratify a taste for human flesh or by the judgment of the gods as punishment for a great offence.

claims.quote: And Herodotus:—“It seems that the Neuri are sorcerers, if one is to believe the Scythians and the Greeks established in Scythia; for each Neurian changes himself, once in the year, into the form of a wolf, and he continues in that form for several days, after which he resumes his former shape.
claims.locator: Chapter II, Lycanthropy among the Ancients

statement.id: Baring-Gould mengutip Herodotus: orang Neuri tampaknya penyihir; setiap orang Neuri berubah menjadi serigala sekali setahun, bertahan dalam wujud itu beberapa hari, lalu kembali ke wujud semula.
statement.en: Baring-Gould quotes Herodotus: the Neuri seem to be sorcerers; each Neurian changes himself once a year into a wolf, remains in that form for several days, then resumes his former shape.

claims.quote: According to Marcellus Sidetes ... men are attacked with this madness chiefly in the beginning of the year, and become most furious in February; retiring for the night to lone cemeteries, and living precisely in the manner of dogs and wolves.
claims.locator: Chapter II, Lycanthropy among the Ancients

statement.id: Menurut Marcellus Sidetes, seperti dikutip Baring-Gould, orang diserang kegilaan ini terutama pada awal tahun dan paling ganas pada Februari, bermalam di pemakaman terpencil dan hidup seperti anjing dan serigala.
statement.en: According to Marcellus Sidetes, as cited by Baring-Gould, men are attacked by this madness chiefly at the beginning of the year and are most furious in February, retiring at night to lone cemeteries and living like dogs and wolves.

claims.quote: The transformation lasts during twelve days, at the expiration of which period the wolf-skin vanishes, and the human form reappears.
claims.locator: Chapter V, The Were-Wolf in the Middle Ages

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Baring-Gould, perubahan itu berlangsung dua belas hari, setelah itu kulit serigala lenyap dan wujud manusia muncul kembali.
statement.en: In the account recorded by Baring-Gould, the transformation lasts twelve days, after which the wolf-skin vanishes and the human form reappears.

claims.quote: They fall upon herds of cattle and flocks of sheep, but they have no power to slay men.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu mereka menyerang kawanan ternak dan domba, tetapi tidak mampu membunuh manusia.

claims.quote: That the same belief in lycanthropy exists in Armenia is evident from the following story told by Haxthausen ... he found a cave, in which lay a wolf-skin. claims.quote: In folklore, a werewolf (from Old English werwulf 'man-wolf'), or occasionally lycanthrope (from Ancient Greek λυκάνθρωπος 'wolf-human'), is an individual who can shapeshift into a wolf or therianthropic hybrid wolf–humanlike creature, either voluntarily or involuntarily due to a curse or other affliction.

statement.en: In folklore a werewolf (from Old English werwulf 'man-wolf'), or occasionally lycanthrope (from Ancient Greek λυκάνθρωπος 'wolf-human'), is an individual who can shapeshift into a wolf or a wolf-humanlike hybrid, voluntarily or involuntarily due to a curse or other affliction.

claims.quote: Early sources for belief in this ability or affliction, called lycanthropy, are Petronius (27–66) and Gervase of Tilbury (1150–1228).

statement.en: The case of Peter Stumpp (1589) led to a significant peak of interest in and persecution of supposed werewolves, primarily in French- and German-speaking Europe.

short_description.id: Phoenix adalah burung legendaris berbulu merah keemasan dari mitologi Yunani yang memperbarui diri atau terlahir kembali dari pendahulunya, dan dikaitkan dengan Matahari.
short_description.en: The phoenix is a legendary red-and-gold bird of Greek mythology that renews itself or is reborn from its predecessor, and is associated with the Sun.

long_description.id: Phoenix adalah burung legendaris yang abadi dan terus memperbarui diri atau terlahir kembali; ia berasal dari mitologi Yunani dan punya padanan di banyak budaya. Ia digambarkan berbulu merah keemasan dan memancarkan sinar matahari, hidup lima ratus tahun menurut satu uraian, dan memakan balsam dan kemenyan Arabia. Herodotus menulis bahwa ia hanya pernah melihat gambarnya dan bahwa bulunya sebagian keemasan, sebagian merah, dengan bentuk dan ukuran seperti elang. Philostratus menyebut ia mirip elang, bersinar keemasan, dan bersarang dari rempah di mata air Sungai Nil, sedangkan Claudianus menyebutnya sekaligus ayah dan putranya sendiri.
long_description.en: The phoenix is a legendary immortal bird that cyclically renews itself or is reborn; it originates in Greek mythology and has analogues in many cultures. It is portrayed with red-and-gold feathers that emit rays of sunlight, living five hundred years in one account and feeding on Arabian balsam and frankincense. Herodotus wrote that he had seen it only in pictures and that its plumage is partly golden and partly red, with the shape and size of an eagle. Philostratus likens it to an eagle that shines with gold and nests on spices at the springs of the Nile, while Claudian calls it its own father and son.

long_description.id: Kisah tentang pergantian generasinya berbeda-beda. Menurut cerita yang didengar Herodotus, burung baru membawa jasad induknya terbungkus mur dari Arabia ke kuil Matahari di Heliopolis. Ovidius menulis bahwa phoenix membangun sarang di puncak palem dan burung kecil terlahir dari tubuh induknya, lalu membawa sarang itu ke kota Matahari. Dalam versi lain, phoenix yang sangat tua menyerahkan dirinya pada api, atau seekor cacing keluar dari tubuhnya dan tumbuh menjadi phoenix baru oleh panas matahari. Ada pula versi yang menyebut phoenix membangun timbunan rempah, duduk di atasnya, lalu mati dan bangkit kembali. Menurut kisah India dalam Philostratus, phoenix yang terbakar di sarangnya menyanyikan lagu duka bagi dirinya sendiri.
long_description.en: Accounts of its renewal differ. In the story Herodotus heard, the new bird carries its parent's body wrapped in myrrh from Arabia to the temple of the Sun at Heliopolis. Ovid wrote that the phoenix builds a nest on a palm and a small bird is reborn from the parent's body, then carries the nest to the Sun's city. In other versions an extremely old phoenix commits itself to the flames, or a worm emerges from its body and is developed into a new phoenix by the sun's heat. Another version has the phoenix build a pyre of spices, settle on it, die and rise again. In the Indian version reported by Philostratus, the phoenix being consumed in its nest sings funeral strains for itself.

long_description.id: Nama Latin phoenix berasal dari kata Yunani φοῖνιξ. Penyebutan paling awal yang jelas dalam sastra Yunani ada pada fragmen yang dikaitkan dengan Hesiodos, yang menyebut phoenix hidup lebih lama daripada sembilan gagak. Para sarjana mencatat bahwa phoenix sering digambarkan berlingkar cahaya untuk menekankan kaitannya dengan Matahari, bahwa burung matahari Bennu yang dimuliakan di Heliopolis mirip dalam beberapa hal, dan bahwa sumber tidak sepakat soal warna pastinya.
long_description.en: The Latin name phoenix comes from the Greek word φοῖνιξ. The earliest clear mention in Greek literature is in a fragment attributed to Hesiod, in which the phoenix outlives nine ravens. Scholars note that the phoenix is often shown with a halo emphasising its link to the Sun, that the solar bird Bennu, venerated at Heliopolis, is similar in some respects, and that sources give no clear consensus on its exact colouring.

long_description.id: Fenghuang Tiongkok sering diterjemahkan sebagai phoenix, tetapi The Met menyatakan fenghuang adalah spesies mitos tersendiri dengan rangkaian makna berbeda, dan dikatakan muncul hanya pada masa damai dan makmur.
long_description.en: The Chinese fenghuang is usually translated as phoenix, but The Met says it is a distinct mythical species with a different set of associations, said to appear only in times of peace and prosperity.

literal_meaning.en: The Greek word is probably a borrowing from a West Semitic word for madder, a red dye; the Mycenaean Greek po-ni-ke probably meant "griffin" or perhaps "palm tree".

text.id: Gambarnya terlihat pada makam kerajaan sejak Dinasti Pertama Mesir (sekitar 3150–2890 SM); ia diperkirakan muncul pada Periode Pradinasti (sekitar 6000–3150 SM).
text.en: His image is seen on royal tombs from the First Dynasty of Egypt (c. 3150-2890 BCE); he is thought to have developed in the Predynastic Period (c. 6000-3150 BCE).

short_description.id: Anubis adalah dewa Mesir kuno untuk mumifikasi, ritus pemakaman, dan penjagaan makam, serta pemandu jiwa ke alam baka; ia digambarkan sebagai kanid hitam atau pria berkepala jakal.
short_description.en: Anubis is the ancient Egyptian god of mummification, funerary rites, and the guarding of tombs, and a guide of souls to the afterlife; he is depicted as a black canine or a jackal-headed man.

long_description.id: Anubis (juga dikenal sebagai Inpu, Inpw, dan Anpu) adalah dewa Mesir untuk mumifikasi, ritus pemakaman, penjaga makam, dan pemandu ke alam baka, sekaligus dewa pelindung jiwa tersesat dan orang tak berdaya. Namanya adalah bentuk Yunani dari Anpu atau Inpu, yang berarti "membusuk". Ia salah satu dewa tertua Mesir dan kemungkinan berkembang dari dewa jakal Wepwawet, yang sering tertukar dengannya.
long_description.en: Anubis (known also as Inpu, Inpw, and Anpu) is the Egyptian deity of mummification and funerary rites. He guards tombs, guides the dead into the afterlife, and is also the patron of lost souls and the helpless. His name is the Greek form of Anpu or Inpu, which meant "to decay". He is one of the oldest Egyptian gods and most likely developed from the jackal god Wepwawet, with whom he is often confused.

long_description.id: Anubis digambarkan sebagai kanid hitam, persilangan jakal dan anjing bertelinga runcing, atau pria berotot berkepala jakal. Warna hitam dipilih karena maknanya, melambangkan pembusukan tubuh sekaligus tanah subur Nil. Sebuah arca memperlihatkannya sepenuhnya sebagai jakal, dan gambaran populernya adalah pria berkepala jakal yang memegang timbangan emas untuk menimbang hati terhadap bulu kebenaran. Salima Ikram menduga ia digambarkan sebagai "super-kanid", bukan sekadar jakal atau anjing.
long_description.en: Anubis is portrayed as a black canine, as a hybrid of jackal and dog with pointed ears, or as a muscular man whose head is that of a jackal. The color black was chosen for its meaning, symbolizing the decay of the body and the fertile soil of the Nile. One statue shows him wholly as a jackal, and his popular image is a jackal-headed man holding golden scales to weigh a heart against the feather of truth. Salima Ikram suggests he is represented as a "super-canid" rather than merely a jackal or a dog.

long_description.id: Sebelum Osiris bangkit pada Kerajaan Tengah, Anubis dikenal sebagai "Yang Pertama di antara Orang Barat", raja orang mati, dan pada Periode Dinasti Awal serta Kerajaan Lama ia satu-satunya Penguasa Orang Mati. Seiring mitos Osiris makin populer, Osiris mengambil semakin banyak atributnya, dan Anubis menjadi pelindung serta "tangan kanan" Osiris yang menjaga jasadnya, mengawasi mumifikasi, dan membantu penghakiman jiwa. Pada adegan penghakiman ia menimbang hati terhadap sosok dewi Ma'at, dan ia disebut membantu menghakimi orang mati serta menghukum pelanggar makam bersama pasukan utusannya.
long_description.en: Before the rise of Osiris in the Middle Kingdom, Anubis was known as "First of the Westerners", king of the dead, and in the Early Dynastic Period and Old Kingdom he was the sole Lord of the Dead. As the Osiris myth grew more popular, Osiris took on more of his attributes, and Anubis became Osiris' protector and "right-hand man", guarding his body, overseeing the mummification, and assisting in the judgement of souls. In judgment scenes he weighs the heart against a figure of the goddess Ma'at, and he is said to help judge the dead and to punish violators of tombs with his army of messengers.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah yang tercatat pada milenium pertama SM, Set menyamar sebagai macan tutul untuk mendekati jasad Osiris, lalu ditangkap Anubis dan dicap dengan besi panas; Anubis kemudian menguliti Set dan mengenakan kulitnya sebagai peringatan. Anubis juga diseru untuk perlindungan dan pembalasan, termasuk menegakkan kutukan atau menangkal kutukan. Putrinya, Qebhet, membawa air sejuk bagi jiwa orang mati di Balai Kebenaran.
long_description.en: In a story recorded in the first millennium BCE, Set disguises himself as a leopard to approach the body of Osiris and is seized by Anubis and branded with a hot iron; Anubis then flays Set and wears his skin as a warning. Anubis was also called upon for protection and vengeance, including enforcing curses or defending against them. His daughter, Qebhet, offers cool water to the souls of the dead gathered in the Hall of Truth.

long_description.id: Pada masa awal Anubis dianggap putra Ra dan Hesat, tetapi setelah diserap ke dalam mitos Osiris ia dianggap putra Osiris dan Nephthys. Dalam kisah ini Nephthys hamil dengan Anubis, meninggalkannya setelah lahir karena takut Set mengetahuinya, dan Isis kemudian menemukan serta mengangkatnya sebagai anak. Plutarch mencatat bahwa anak itu menjadi pengawal dan pengikut Isis dan dikabarkan menjaga para dewa seperti anjing menjaga manusia.
long_description.en: At an earlier stage Anubis was regarded as the child of Ra and Hesat, but once he was absorbed into the Osiris myth he was held to be the child of Osiris and Nephthys. In this story Nephthys becomes pregnant with Anubis and abandons him after his birth for fear that Set will find out; Isis later finds and adopts him. Plutarch records that the child became Isis's guard and follower and is reported to guard the gods as dogs do men.

long_description.id: Pusat kultus Anubis berada di Cynopolis, "kota anjing", di Mesir Hulu, dan para pendetanya sering memakai topeng kayu sang dewa dalam ritual. Ia menjadi dewa pelindung para pembalsem, yang kadang mengenakan topeng berbentuk kepalanya. Orang Yunani mengaitkannya dengan Hermes, dan Plutarch menilai kekuasaannya mirip dengan Hecate. Sumber menyebut bahwa meski banyak tampil dalam seni, Anubis tidak berperan besar dalam banyak mitos.
long_description.en: The cult center of Anubis was at Cynopolis, "the city of the dog", in Upper Egypt, and his priests often wore wooden masks of the god in rituals. He became the patron god of embalmers, who sometimes wore masks shaped like his head. The Greeks associated him with Hermes, and Plutarch judges his power to be much like that of Hecate. The source notes that although he appears widely in art, Anubis does not play a major role in many myths.

cultural_context.id: Menurut sumber, "super-kanid" Anubis memberi orang jaminan bahwa tubuh mereka akan dihormati saat mati, jiwa mereka dilindungi di alam baka, dan mereka akan menerima penghakiman yang adil.
cultural_context.en: According to the source, the "super-canid" Anubis gave people confidence that their bodies would be respected in death, their souls shielded in the afterlife, and their lives fairly judged.

statement.id: Warna hitam dipilih karena maknanya, bukan karena anjing atau jakal Mesir berwarna hitam; hitam melambangkan pembusukan tubuh sekaligus tanah subur Lembah Sungai Nil yang mewakili pembaruan dan kehidupan.
statement.en: The color black was chosen for its symbolism, not because Egyptian dogs or jackals were black; black symbolized the decay of the body as well as the fertile soil of the Nile River Valley, which represented regeneration and life.

claims.quote: The powerful black canine, then, was the protector of the dead who made sure they received their due rights in burial and stood by them in the life after death to assist their resurrection.

statement.id: Kanid hitam yang perkasa itu adalah pelindung orang mati yang memastikan mereka menerima hak penguburan dan mendampingi mereka dalam kehidupan setelah mati untuk membantu kebangkitan mereka.
statement.en: The powerful black canine was the protector of the dead, who made sure they received their due rites in burial and stood by them in the afterlife to assist their resurrection.

claims.quote: He was known as "First of the Westerners" prior to the rise of Osiris in the Middle Kingdom (2040-1782 BCE) which meant he was king of the dead

statement.id: Ia dikenal sebagai "Yang Pertama di antara Orang Barat" sebelum bangkitnya Osiris pada Kerajaan Tengah (2040–1782 SM), yang berarti ia adalah raja orang mati.
statement.en: He was known as "First of the Westerners" before the rise of Osiris in the Middle Kingdom (2040-1782 BCE), which meant he was king of the dead.

claims.quote: A popular image of Anubis is the standing or kneeling man with the jackal's head holding the golden scales on which the heart of the soul was weighed against the white feather of truth.

statement.id: Gambaran Anubis yang populer adalah pria berkepala jakal yang berdiri atau berlutut memegang timbangan emas tempat hati sang jiwa ditimbang terhadap bulu putih kebenaran.
statement.en: A popular image of Anubis is the standing or kneeling man with the jackal's head holding the golden scales on which the heart of the soul was weighed against the white feather of truth.

claims.quote: His daughter is Qebhet (also known as Kabechet) who brings cool water to the souls of the dead in the Hall of Truth and comforts the newly deceased.

statement.id: Putrinya adalah Qebhet (juga dikenal sebagai Kabechet) yang membawa air sejuk bagi jiwa orang mati di Balai Kebenaran dan menghibur mereka yang baru meninggal.
statement.en: His daughter is Qebhet (also known as Kabechet), who brings cool water to the souls of the dead in the Hall of Truth and comforts the newly deceased.

claims.quote: He had many epithets besides "First of the Westerners" and was also known as "Lord of the Sacred Land" (referencing the area of the desert where necropoleis were located)

statement.id: Ia memiliki banyak gelar selain "Yang Pertama di antara Orang Barat", antara lain "Penguasa Tanah Suci" (merujuk wilayah gurun tempat nekropolis berada).
statement.en: He had many epithets besides "First of the Westerners", including "Lord of the Sacred Land" (referring to the area of the desert where necropoleis were located).

claims.quote: "Master of Secrets" (since he knew what waited beyond death), "He Who is in the Place of Embalming" (indicating his role in the mummification process)

statement.id: Gelar lainnya mencakup "Penguasa Rahasia" (karena ia tahu apa yang menanti setelah kematian) dan "Dia yang Berada di Tempat Pembalseman" (menunjukkan perannya dalam proses mumifikasi).
statement.en: Other epithets include "Master of Secrets" (since he knew what waited beyond death) and "He Who is in the Place of Embalming" (indicating his role in the mummification process).

claims.quote: As his various epithets make clear, Anubis was central to every aspect of an individual's death experience in the role of protector and even stood with the soul after death as a just judge and guide.

statement.id: Seperti terlihat dari berbagai gelarnya, Anubis berperan sentral dalam setiap aspek pengalaman kematian seseorang sebagai pelindung, dan bahkan mendampingi jiwa setelah mati sebagai hakim yang adil dan pemandu.
statement.en: As his various epithets make clear, Anubis was central to every aspect of an individual's death experience as protector, and even stood with the soul after death as a just judge and guide.

claims.quote: Anubis helped to judge the dead and he and his army of messengers were charged with punishing those who violated tombs or offended the gods

statement.id: Menurut Geraldine Pinch yang dikutip sumber ini, Anubis membantu menghakimi orang mati, dan ia bersama pasukan utusannya ditugasi menghukum orang yang melanggar makam atau menyinggung para dewa.
statement.en: According to Geraldine Pinch, quoted by the source, Anubis helped to judge the dead, and he and his army of messengers were charged with punishing those who violated tombs or offended the gods.

claims.quote: A story recorded in the first millenium BCE tells how the wicked god Set disguised himself as a leopard to approach the body of Osiris. He was seized by Anubis and branded all over with a hot iron. This, according to Egyptian myth, is how the leopard got its spots.

statement.id: Sebuah kisah yang tercatat pada milenium pertama SM menceritakan bahwa dewa jahat Set menyamar sebagai macan tutul untuk mendekati jasad Osiris, lalu ditangkap Anubis dan dicap di sekujur tubuh dengan besi panas; menurut mitos Mesir, begitulah macan tutul mendapat bintik-bintiknya.
statement.en: A story recorded in the first millennium BCE tells how the wicked god Set disguised himself as a leopard to approach the body of Osiris, was seized by Anubis, and was branded all over with a hot iron; according to Egyptian myth, this is how the leopard got its spots.

claims.quote: Anubis then flayed Set and wore his bloody skin as a warning to evildoers. By this era, Anubis was said to command an army of demon messengers who inflicted suffering and death.

statement.id: Anubis kemudian menguliti Set dan mengenakan kulitnya yang berdarah sebagai peringatan bagi para pelaku kejahatan; pada masa itu Anubis dikatakan memimpin pasukan utusan-iblis yang menimpakan penderitaan dan kematian.
statement.en: Anubis then flayed Set and wore his bloody skin as a warning to evildoers; by this era Anubis was said to command an army of demon messengers who inflicted suffering and death.

claims.quote: In the Early Dynastic Period (c. 3150-2613 BCE) and Old Kingdom (c. 2613-2181 BCE) Anubis was the sole Lord of the Dead and righteous judge of the soul, but as the Osiris myth became more popular, the latter god took on more and more of Anubis' attributes.

statement.id: Pada Periode Dinasti Awal (sekitar 3150–2613 SM) dan Kerajaan Lama (sekitar 2613–2181 SM), Anubis adalah satu-satunya Penguasa Orang Mati dan hakim jiwa yang adil, tetapi seiring mitos Osiris makin populer, Osiris mengambil semakin banyak atribut Anubis.
statement.en: In the Early Dynastic Period (c. 3150-2613 BCE) and Old Kingdom (c. 2613-2181 BCE) Anubis was the sole Lord of the Dead and righteous judge of the soul, but as the Osiris myth grew more popular, Osiris took on more and more of Anubis' attributes.

claims.quote: Anubis remained a very popular god, however, and so was assimilated into the Osiris myth by discarding his earlier parentage and history and making him the son of Osiris and Nephthys born of their affair.

statement.id: Anubis tetap sangat populer sehingga ia diserap ke dalam mitos Osiris dengan membuang silsilah dan riwayat awalnya dan menjadikannya putra Osiris dan Nephthys yang lahir dari hubungan gelap mereka.
statement.en: Anubis nevertheless remained very popular and so was assimilated into the Osiris myth by discarding his earlier parentage and history and making him the son of Osiris and Nephthys, born of their affair.

claims.quote: After his assimilation into the Osiris myth, Anubis was regularly seen as Osiris' protector and "right-hand man" who guarded the god's body after death, oversaw the mummification, and assisted Osiris in the judgment of the souls of the dead.

statement.id: Setelah diserap ke dalam mitos Osiris, Anubis lazim dipandang sebagai pelindung dan "tangan kanan" Osiris yang menjaga jasad sang dewa setelah mati, mengawasi mumifikasi, dan membantu Osiris menghakimi jiwa orang mati.
statement.en: After his assimilation into the Osiris myth, Anubis was regularly seen as Osiris' protector and "right-hand man", who guarded the god's body after death, oversaw the mummification, and assisted Osiris in judging the souls of the dead.

claims.quote: Anubis was regularly called upon (as attested to from amulets, tomb paintings, and in written works) for protection and vengeance; especially as a powerful ally in enforcing curses placed on others or defending one's self from such curses.

statement.id: Anubis lazim diseru (dibuktikan dari jimat, lukisan makam, dan karya tulis) untuk perlindungan dan pembalasan, terutama sebagai sekutu kuat dalam menegakkan kutukan atas orang lain atau membela diri dari kutukan semacam itu.
statement.en: Anubis was regularly called upon (as attested by amulets, tomb paintings, and written works) for protection and vengeance, especially as a powerful ally in enforcing curses placed on others or defending oneself from such curses.

claims.quote: As the protector of the dead, who invented mummification and so the preservation of the human body

statement.id: Sebagai pelindung orang mati, Anubis disebut penemu mumifikasi dan dengan demikian pengawetan tubuh manusia.
statement.en: As the protector of the dead, Anubis is described as having invented mummification and so the preservation of the human body.

claims.quote: Osiris slept with Nephthys and she became pregnant with Anubis but abandoned him shortly after his birth in fear that the affair would be discovered by Set.

statement.id: Osiris tidur dengan Nephthys dan ia hamil dengan Anubis, tetapi meninggalkannya tak lama setelah lahir karena takut hubungan itu diketahui Set.
statement.en: Osiris slept with Nephthys and she became pregnant with Anubis but abandoned him shortly after his birth for fear that Set would discover the affair.

claims.quote: Isis found out about the affair and went searching for the infant and, when she found him, adopted him as her own.

statement.id: Isis mengetahui hubungan itu, mencari sang bayi, dan setelah menemukannya mengangkatnya sebagai anaknya sendiri.
statement.en: Isis found out about the affair, went searching for the infant, and, when she found him, adopted him as her own.

claims.quote: The priests of Anubis were male and often wore masks of the god made of wood in performing rituals. The god's cult center was in Upper Egypt at Cynopolis ("the city of the dog"), but there were shrines to him throughout the land and he was universally venerated in every part of the country.

statement.id: Para pendeta Anubis adalah laki-laki dan sering mengenakan topeng sang dewa dari kayu saat melakukan ritual. Pusat kultusnya berada di Mesir Hulu di Cynopolis ("kota anjing"), tetapi ada kuil-kuil baginya di seluruh negeri dan ia dihormati di segala penjuru.
statement.en: The priests of Anubis were male and often wore wooden masks of the god in performing rituals. His cult center was in Upper Egypt at Cynopolis ("the city of the dog"), but there were shrines to him throughout the land and he was universally venerated in every part of the country.

claims.quote: Because he was said to have prepared the mummy of Osiris, Anubis became the patron god of embalmers and in the Memphite necropolis an area associated with the embalmers seems to have become something of a focal point for the cult of Anubis in the Late Period and Ptolemaic times

statement.id: Karena dikatakan menyiapkan mumi Osiris, Anubis menjadi dewa pelindung para pembalsem, dan di nekropolis Memphis sebuah kawasan yang berkaitan dengan para pembalsem tampaknya menjadi pusat kultus Anubis pada Periode Akhir dan masa Ptolemeus.
statement.en: Because he was said to have prepared the mummy of Osiris, Anubis became the patron god of embalmers, and in the Memphite necropolis an area associated with the embalmers seems to have become a focal point of the cult of Anubis in the Late Period and Ptolemaic times.

claims.quote: The Greeks associated him with their god Hermes who guided the dead to the afterlife

statement.id: Orang Yunani mengaitkannya dengan dewa mereka, Hermes, yang memandu orang mati ke alam baka.
statement.en: The Greeks associated him with their god Hermes, who guided the dead to the afterlife.

claims.quote: became associated with Charon in the Graeco-Roman period and St. Christopher in the early Christian period

statement.id: Menurut kutipan Salima Ikram dalam sumber ini, Anubis dikaitkan dengan Charon pada periode Yunani-Romawi dan dengan Santo Christopher pada masa Kristen awal.
statement.en: According to Salima Ikram, quoted in the source, Anubis became associated with Charon in the Graeco-Roman period and with St. Christopher in the early Christian period.

claims.quote: It is probable that Anubis is represented as a super-canid, combining the most salient attributes of serveral types of canids, rather than being just a jackal or a dog.

statement.id: Menurut kutipan Salima Ikram, kemungkinan Anubis digambarkan sebagai "super-kanid" yang menggabungkan ciri paling menonjol dari beberapa jenis kanid, bukan sekadar jakal atau anjing.
statement.en: According to Salima Ikram, it is probable that Anubis is represented as a super-canid combining the most salient attributes of several types of canids, rather than being just a jackal or a dog.

claims.quote: This "super-canid" offered people the assurance that their body would be respected at death, that their soul would be protected in the afterlife, and that they would receive fair judgment for their life's work.

statement.id: "Super-kanid" ini memberi orang jaminan bahwa tubuh mereka akan dihormati saat mati, jiwa mereka dilindungi di alam baka, dan mereka akan menerima penghakiman yang adil atas jerih payah hidupnya.
statement.en: This "super-canid" offered people the assurance that their body would be respected at death, that their soul would be protected in the afterlife, and that they would receive fair judgment for their life's work.

claims.quote: Although Anubis is very well represented in artwork throughout Egyptian history he does not play a major role in many myths.

statement.id: Meski Anubis sangat banyak muncul dalam karya seni sepanjang sejarah Mesir, ia tidak berperan besar dalam banyak mitos.
statement.en: Although Anubis is very well represented in artwork throughout Egyptian history, he does not play a major role in many myths.

claims.quote: he afterwards became her guardsman and follower, being named Anubis, and reported to guard the Gods as dogs do men.

statement.id: Dalam Plutarch, anak itu kemudian menjadi pengawal dan pengikut Isis, dinamai Anubis, dan dikabarkan menjaga para dewa seperti anjing menjaga manusia.
statement.en: In Plutarch, the child afterwards became Isis's guard and follower, named Anubis, and is reported to guard the Gods as dogs do men.

claims.quote: Which made them say that Isis had a lawful son called Horus, and Nephthys a bastard called Anubis.

statement.id: Dalam Plutarch, dikatakan bahwa Isis memiliki putra sah bernama Horus dan Nephthys memiliki anak haram bernama Anubis.
statement.en: In Plutarch, it is said that Isis had a lawful son called Horus and Nephthys a bastard called Anubis.

claims.quote: that which touches upon both these, and is called the horizon (or bounding circle) and is common to them both, is called Anubis, and resembles in shape the dog, because the dog makes use of his sight by night as well as by day.

statement.id: Dalam tafsir Plutarch, apa yang menyentuh keduanya dan disebut cakrawala (atau lingkaran pembatas) dinamai Anubis dan berbentuk seperti anjing, karena anjing menggunakan penglihatannya pada malam maupun siang.
statement.en: In Plutarch's interpretation, that which touches upon both and is called the horizon (or bounding circle) is called Anubis and resembles the dog in shape, because the dog uses his sight by night as well as by day.

claims.quote: Anubis seems to me to have a power among the Egyptians much like to that of Hecate among the Grecians, he being as well terrestrial as Olympic.

statement.id: Plutarch menilai kekuasaan Anubis di antara orang Mesir mirip dengan kekuasaan Hecate di antara orang Yunani, karena ia bersifat bumi sekaligus Olimpia.
statement.en: Plutarch judges that Anubis has a power among the Egyptians much like that of Hecate among the Greeks, being as much terrestrial as Olympic.

summary.id: Dalam tradisi lebih awal, putra Ra dan Hesat.
summary.en: In an earlier tradition, son of Ra and Hesat.

summary.id: Dalam kisah Osiris, putra Osiris dan Nephthys; silsilah awalnya dibuang saat ia diserap ke mitos itu.
summary.en: In the Osiris myth, son of Osiris and Nephthys; his earlier parentage was discarded when he was assimilated into that myth.

summary.id: Digambarkan sebagai kanid hitam, persilangan jakal-anjing, atau pria berkepala jakal.
summary.en: Depicted as a black canine, a jackal-dog hybrid, or a man with a jackal's head.

summary.id: Salima Ikram menduga ia "super-kanid" yang menggabungkan ciri beberapa kanid, bukan sekadar jakal atau anjing.
summary.en: Salima Ikram suggests a "super-canid" combining attributes of several canids, rather than just a jackal or a dog.

summary.id: Plutarch menyebut Anubis berbentuk seperti anjing.
summary.en: Plutarch says Anubis resembles the dog in shape.

text.id: Kisah putri duyung telah ada selama ribuan tahun; salah satu legenda tertua muncul di Suriah sekitar 1000 SM.
text.en: Stories of mermaids have existed for thousands of years; one of the earliest legends appeared in Syria around 1000 BC.

short_description.id: Putri duyung adalah makhluk laut dalam cerita rakyat berbagai budaya, digambarkan berkepala dan bertubuh perempuan dengan ekor ikan, dan dipandang membawa nasib baik sekaligus bahaya bagi pelaut.
short_description.en: The mermaid is a sea creature of folklore across many cultures, described with a woman's head and body and a fish's tail, and seen as bringing both good fortune and danger to sailors.

long_description.id: Putri duyung digambarkan sebagai makhluk laut yang berkepala dan bertubuh perempuan dengan ekor ikan di bawah pinggang. Kisahnya telah ada selama ribuan tahun dan tersebar di berbagai budaya. Dalam cerita rakyat pelaut, ia melambangkan keberuntungan sekaligus bencana, dan sumber museum menyebutnya makhluk yang secara moral ambigu.
long_description.en: The mermaid is described as a sea-dwelling creature with a woman's head and body and a fish's tail below the waist. Her stories have existed for thousands of years and span many cultures. In sailor folklore she represents both good fortune and disaster, and a museum source calls her morally ambiguous.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Denmark yang dicatat dalam sebuah himpunan folklor, Havfrue digambarkan kadang baik dan kadang jahat. Nelayan melihatnya menyisir rambut emas dengan sisir emas; kemunculannya menandakan badai dan kegagalan menangkap ikan, dan ia dipercaya dapat meramalkan masa depan. Pasangan jantannya, Havmand, dianggap makhluk yang cukup baik dan murah hati.
long_description.en: In folklore from Denmark recorded in a folklore collection, the Havfrue is described as sometimes good and sometimes evil. Fishermen see her combing golden hair with a golden comb; her appearance prognosticates storm and ill success in fishing, and she is believed able to foretell the future. Her male counterpart, the Havmand, is regarded as a rather good and beneficent being.

long_description.id: Di tempat lain, kisahnya mengambil bentuk berbeda. Di Shetland, perempuan laut tidak dapat kembali ke keluarganya tanpa kulit anjing lautnya; di Irlandia, topi Cohuleen Driuth berperan serupa. Cerita Yunani tentang Thessalonike menyebut ia memunculkan badai bagi kapal yang menjawab salah. Di Asia Tenggara, Suvannamaccha dikisahkan membantu Hanuman.
long_description.en: Elsewhere her stories take different forms. In Shetland the sea-maiden cannot return to her family without her seal-skin; in Ireland a cap, the Cohuleen Driuth, plays a similar role. The Greek tale of Thessalonike says she conjured a storm against ships whose sailors answered wrongly. In Southeast Asia Suvannamaccha is said to help Hanuman.

long_description.id: Putri duyung kerap tertukar dengan siren, yang dalam mitologi Yunani awal berwujud setengah perempuan setengah burung. Sebagian laporan penampakan putri duyung pernah dikaitkan dengan dugong, kerabat manatee. Legenda Atargatis di Suriah dan ukiran di Kastil Durham termasuk jejak tertuanya.
long_description.en: Mermaids are often confused with sirens, which in early Greek mythology were half-women, half-bird creatures. Some reported sightings of mermaids have been associated with dugongs, relatives of the manatee. The legend of Atargatis in Syria and the carving in Durham Castle are among the earliest traces.

cultural_context.id: Bagi pelaut, putri duyung adalah lambang yang berubah-ubah seperti laut: di sebagian budaya melambangkan kehidupan dan kesuburan di samudra, di budaya lain melambangkan sifat perusak air. Ia sering dijadikan hiasan haluan kapal karena dipercaya menenangkan laut.
cultural_context.en: For sailors the mermaid is a symbol as changeable as the sea: in some cultures she signifies life and fertility within the ocean, in others the destructive nature of water. She often appeared as a ship's figurehead because she was believed to appease the sea.

literal_meaning.id: Gabungan "mere" (laut, bahasa Inggris Kuno) dan "maid" (gadis atau perempuan muda).
literal_meaning.en: A compound of "mere" (sea, Old English) and "maid" (a girl or young woman).

who.id: Putri duyung adalah makhluk laut mitos berkepala dan bertubuh perempuan dengan ekor ikan.
who.en: A mermaid is a mythical sea creature with a woman's head and body and a fish's tail.

origin.id: Kisahnya ditemukan di berbagai budaya, dari permukiman pesisir Irlandia hingga gurun Karoo di Afrika Selatan yang jauh dari laut.
origin.en: Tales of her are found in many cultures, reaching from coastal communities of Ireland to the Karoo desert of South Africa, far from the sea.

role.id: Dalam cerita rakyat pelaut ia menjadi pertanda keberuntungan atau bencana di laut.
role.en: In sailor folklore she is an omen of good fortune or disaster at sea.

famous_for.id: Ia paling dikenal sebagai makhluk setengah perempuan setengah ikan yang bisa memikat atau menolong manusia.
famous_for.en: She is best known as the half-woman, half-fish being who can lure or help people.

did_you_know.id: Penggambaran putri duyung tertua di Inggris ada di kapel Norman Kastil Durham, bersama dua macan tutul dan beberapa adegan berburu.
did_you_know.en: The earliest depiction of a mermaid in England is in the Norman chapel of Durham Castle, alongside two leopards and several hunting scenes.

description.id: Menurut tradisi rakyat Denmark dalam sebuah himpunan folklor, putri duyung dipercaya mampu meramalkan peristiwa masa depan.
description.en: In folk tradition from Denmark recorded in a folklore collection, mermaids are believed able to foretell future events.

description.id: Kemunculan putri duyung menandakan badai dan kegagalan menangkap ikan; dalam kisah Thessalonike, ia memunculkan badai bagi kapal yang menjawab salah.
description.en: A mermaid's appearance prognosticates storm and ill success in fishing; in the Thessalonike tale she conjures a storm against ships whose sailors answer wrongly.

description.id: Di sebagian budaya ia memikat pelaut menuju kematian; dalam cerita Denmark ia datang ke api para nelayan untuk memikat mereka.
description.en: In some cultures she lures sailors to their deaths; in tales from Denmark she comes to fishermen's fires to entice them.

name.id: Berganti wujud dengan kulit anjing laut

description.id: Dalam kisah Shetland, perempuan laut memakai kulit anjing laut dan berwujud anjing laut ketika terjun ke laut.
description.en: In the Shetland tale, the sea-maiden puts on a seal-skin and takes the form of a seal when plunging into the sea.

claims.quote: Stories of mermaids have existed for thousands of years and span cultures across the world

statement.id: Cerita putri duyung tersebar di berbagai budaya dunia.
statement.en: Mermaid stories span cultures around the world.

claims.quote: In some cultures, the mermaid signifies life and fertility within the ocean. In others, she embodies the destructive nature of the water, luring sailors to their deaths

statement.en: Mermaids are morally ambiguous creatures, whereas sirens were said to be always malicious and dangerous.

claims.quote: In sailor folklore, mermaids represent both good fortune and disaster.

statement.en: In sailor folklore, mermaids represent both good fortune and disaster.

claims.quote: While many different decorations have been used, mermaids proved popular with the sailors as they were believed to appease the sea, ensuring good weather and finding a safe way back to land.

statement.id: Putri duyung populer di kalangan pelaut sebagai hiasan haluan kapal karena dipercaya menenangkan laut, menjamin cuaca baik, dan menemukan jalan aman kembali ke daratan.
statement.en: Mermaids proved popular with sailors as decorations on ships because they were believed to appease the sea, ensuring good weather and a safe way back to land.

statement.en: A famous Greek folktale claimed that Thessalonike, sister of Alexander the Great, was transformed into a mermaid upon her death in 295 BC and lived in the Aegean sea.

claims.quote: Any other answer was said to anger her, and she would conjure a storm and doom the vessel and its sailors to a death at sea.

claims.quote: In West, South and Central Africa, a range of tales exist about mythical water spirits called Mami Wata (meaning "Water as Mother" or "Mother of the Waters").

statement.id: Di Afrika Barat, Selatan, dan Tengah ada berbagai kisah tentang roh air mitos bernama Mami Wata ("Air sebagai Ibu" atau "Ibu Perairan").
statement.en: In West, South and Central Africa, a range of tales exist about mythical water spirits called Mami Wata ("Water as Mother" or "Mother of the Waters").

claims.quote: The spirit is worshipped for both their benevolence in offering beauty, healing and wisdom, and as a way of warding off natural disasters.

statement.en: The spirit is worshipped for its benevolence in offering beauty, healing and wisdom, and as a way of warding off natural disasters.

claims.quote: Often translated as "mermaid," the Rusalki are water nymphs of Slavic mythology. While initially regarded as benevolent spirits of fertility and agriculture, Rusalki gained a more sinister description in the 1800s. They were believed to be the ghosts of women who died violent deaths by drowning. In their anger and sorrow, the Rusalki now lured men and children to their watery graves.

statement.id: Rusalki, nimfa air dalam mitologi Slavia, sering diterjemahkan sebagai "putri duyung"; semula dianggap roh kesuburan dan pertanian yang baik, tetapi pada tahun 1800-an digambarkan lebih jahat, sebagai hantu perempuan yang mati tenggelam dan memikat laki-laki serta anak-anak ke kuburan airnya.
statement.en: The Rusalki, water nymphs of Slavic mythology, are often translated as "mermaid"; initially regarded as benevolent spirits of fertility and agriculture, they gained a more sinister description in the 1800s as ghosts of women who died by drowning, luring men and children to their watery graves.

claims.quote: Female merrows, with their beauty and long green hair, resemble our traditional views of mermaids. Their counterpart, the male merrow is considered grotesque, cruel and more fish than man.

statement.id: Merrow betina, dengan kecantikan dan rambut hijau panjang, menyerupai gambaran tradisional putri duyung; pasangan jantannya dianggap menyeramkan, kejam, dan lebih mirip ikan daripada manusia.
statement.en: Female merrows, with their beauty and long green hair, resemble traditional views of mermaids; their male counterpart is considered grotesque, cruel and more fish than man.

claims.quote: These shape-shifting creatures live as seals while in the sea and transform into humans while on land.

claims.quote: A feminine spirit found in many medieval European folktales, the Melusine has a serpent or fish's tail and sometimes has wings.

statement.en: Melusine is a feminine spirit found in many medieval European folktales who has a serpent or fish's tail and sometimes has wings.

claims.quote: One of the earliest mermaid legends appeared in Syria around 1000 BC when the goddess Atargatis dove into a lake to take the form of a fish. As the gods there would not allow her to give up her great beauty, only her bottom half became a fish, and she kept her top half in human form.
claims.locator: What are the origins of mermaids?

statement.id: Salah satu legenda putri duyung tertua muncul di Suriah sekitar 1000 SM, ketika dewi Atargatis terjun ke danau dan berwujud ikan; hanya bagian bawahnya menjadi ikan, sedangkan bagian atasnya tetap manusia.
statement.en: One of the earliest mermaid legends appeared in Syria around 1000 BC when the goddess Atargatis dove into a lake to take the form of a fish; only her bottom half became a fish, and she kept her top half in human form.

claims.quote: The earliest depiction of a mermaid in England can be found in Norman chapel in Durham Castle, built around 1078 by Saxon stonemasons.
claims.locator: What are the origins of mermaids?

statement.en: The earliest depiction of a mermaid in England can be found in the Norman chapel in Durham Castle, built around 1078 by Saxon stonemasons.

claims.quote: The Havfrue, or Mermaid, is represented in the popular tradition sometimes as a good, at other times as an evil and treacherous being. She is beautiful in her appearance.

statement.id: Havfrue, atau putri duyung, dalam tradisi rakyat digambarkan kadang sebagai makhluk baik dan kadang sebagai makhluk jahat dan licik; ia cantik rupanya.
statement.en: The Havfrue, or Mermaid, is represented in popular tradition sometimes as good, at other times as an evil and treacherous being; she is beautiful in her appearance.

claims.quote: Fishermen sometimes see her in the bright summer's sun, when a thin mist hangs over the sea, sitting on the surface of the water, and combing her long golden hair with a golden comb, or driving up her snow-white cattle

statement.id: Nelayan kadang melihatnya di bawah matahari musim panas, duduk di permukaan air menyisir rambut emas panjangnya dengan sisir emas, atau menggiring ternak putih saljunya.
statement.en: Fishermen sometimes see her in the bright summer sun, sitting on the surface of the water combing her long golden hair with a golden comb, or driving up her snow-white cattle.

claims.quote: Her appearance prognosticates both storm and ill success in their fishing. People that are drowned, and whose bodies are not found, are believed to be taken into the dwellings of the Mermaids.

statement.id: Kemunculannya menandakan badai dan kegagalan menangkap ikan; orang yang tenggelam dan jasadnya tidak ditemukan dipercaya dibawa ke tempat tinggal para putri duyung.
statement.en: Her appearance prognosticates both storm and ill success in fishing; drowned people whose bodies are not found are believed to be taken into the dwellings of the Mermaids.

claims.quote: These beings are also supposed to have the power of foretelling future events. A Mermaid, we are told, prophesied the birth of Christian IV. of Denmark

claims.quote: The Havmand, or Merman, is described as of a handsome form, with green or black hair and beard. He dwells either in the bottom of the sea, or in the cliffs and hills near the sea shore, and is regarded as rather a good and beneficent kind of being

claims.quote: Near them he saw lying on the ground several seal-skins. As the man approached the dancers, all gave over their merriment, and flew like lightning to secure their garments; then clothing themselves, plunged in the form of seals into the sea.

claims.quote: she never could hope to rejoin her family and friends below the waters, but must remain an unwilling inhabitant of the region enlightened by the sun.

claims.quote: Thus the Lady of Gollerus resembles the Mermaid-wife and others which we have already related. Instead, however, of an entire dress, it is a kind of cap, named Cohuleen Driuth, without which she cannot return to her subaqueous abode.

statement.en: The Lady of Gollerus of Ireland resembles the Mermaid-wife stories; instead of an entire dress it is a cap, named Cohuleen Driuth, without which she cannot return to her subaqueous abode.
