short_description.id: Thor adalah dewa pembawa palu dalam mitologi Nordik yang dikaitkan dengan guntur, badai, kekuatan, dan perlindungan.
short_description.en: Thor is a hammer-wielding god of Norse mythology associated with thunder, storms, strength, and protection.

long_description.id: Thor, yang bernama Þórr dalam bahasa Nordik, adalah dewa pembawa palu dalam mitologi Nordik. Ia dikaitkan dengan guntur, badai, kekuatan, perlindungan, kesuburan, dan petani. Ia putra Odin dan Jord serta suami Sif, dan berkembang dari dewa Germanik yang lebih awal, Donar. Namanya hidup dalam kata Thursday dan Donnerstag.
long_description.en: Thor, called Þórr in Norse, is a hammer-bearing god of Norse myth. He is associated with thunder, storms, strength, protection, fertility, and farmers. He is the son of Odin and Jord and the husband of Sif, and developed from the earlier Germanic god Donar. His name lives on in the words Thursday and Donnerstag.

long_description.id: Thor berfungsi terutama sebagai dewa pelindung. World History Encyclopedia menyebutnya pembela Asgard dan Midgard yang melindungi lewat perbuatan menumpas raksasa, dan Museum Nasional Denmark juga menyatakan bahwa ia melindungi Midgard, dunia manusia, dengan Mjöllnir. Ia memiliki palu Mjölnir, sabuk Megingjörð yang melipatgandakan kekuatannya, dan sarung tangan besi, serta berkendara dengan kereta yang ditarik dua kambing yang dapat dihidupkan kembali.
long_description.en: Thor functioned primarily as a protector god. World History Encyclopedia describes him as defender of Asgard and Midgard who protects through slaying giants, and the National Museum of Denmark likewise says he protected Midgard, the human world, with Mjöllnir. He has the hammer Mjölnir, the belt Megingjörð that doubles his strength, and iron gloves, and rides a chariot drawn by two goats that can be brought back to life.

long_description.id: Sebagian besar kisah Thor menempatkannya melawan raksasa atau Ular Midgard. Ia memancing ular itu bersama raksasa Hymir, tetapi Hymir memotong tali pancing, dan dalam kisah lain ia dikelabui Utgarda-Loki, yang mengatur agar Thor meminum laut sehingga menciptakan pasang surut. Thor digambarkan tidak berlicik dan berangasan, dan pada Ragnarök ia membunuh ular itu lalu gugur karena bisanya.
long_description.en: Most stories of Thor set him against giants or the Midgard Serpent. He goes fishing for the serpent with the giant Hymir, but Hymir cuts the line, and in another tale he is deceived by Utgarda-Loki, whose trick has Thor drink from the sea and so create tides. Thor is portrayed as without guile and quick-tempered, and at Ragnarök he kills the serpent and then falls to its poison.

long_description.id: Pemujaan Thor memuncak pada Zaman Viking, ketika ia dianggap saingan terbesar Kristus. Banyak jimat palu Thor berasal dari masa persaingan itu, dan Museum Nasional Denmark mencatat temuan palu Thor sebagai bukti kepercayaan awal Viking. Pada abad ke-12 pemujaannya berangsur digantikan agama baru, dan World History Encyclopedia menyebutnya dewa orang biasa yang dapat diandalkan.
long_description.en: Thor's cult peaked in the Viking Age, when he was considered the greatest rival to Christ. Many amulets of Thor's hammer date from that period of contention, and the National Museum of Denmark notes finds of Thor's hammers as evidence of early Viking beliefs. By the 12th century his cult had gradually been replaced by the new religion, and World History Encyclopedia calls him the god of the everyman, someone people could depend on.

long_description.id: Sumber modern menekankan jarak antara Thor dalam tradisi dan citra populer masa kini. World History Encyclopedia menyebut Thor tradisional umumnya digambarkan berambut merah panjang dan berjanggut, sedangkan komik Marvel tahun 1962 menampilkannya klimis dan berambut pirang. Ia juga muncul dalam novel dan serial televisi yang lebih baru.
long_description.en: Modern sources stress the gap between Thor in tradition and the popular image of today. World History Encyclopedia says the traditional Thor is almost always shown with long red hair and a great beard, while the Marvel comics of 1962 present him clean-shaven and blonde. He also appears in more recent novels and television series.

cultural_context.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, kekuatan Thor dan caranya menanggapi masalah secara langsung menarik bagi semua lapisan masyarakat Zaman Viking, sehingga ia menjadi dewa orang biasa.
cultural_context.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Thor's strength and direct response to problems appealed across the social classes of the Viking Age, making him the god of the everyman.

description.en: The same deity appears as Thunor in Old English, Thuner in Old Frisian, Thunar in Old Saxon, and Donar in Old High German, and Thor developed from Donar.

summary.id: Thor memakai kepala lembu Hymer sebagai umpan dan menarik Ular Midgard ke tepi perahu. Hymir memotong tali pancing sehingga ular itu tenggelam kembali, dan sang pencerita meragukan bahwa ular itu mati.
summary.en: Thor uses the head of Hymer's ox as bait and hauls the Midgard Serpent to the side of the boat. Hymir cuts the line so the serpent sinks back, and the narrator doubts that it died.

role.id: Korban tipu daya yang tanpa sadar menciptakan pasang surut.

summary.en: Utgarda-Loki deceives Thor: his blows actually strike mountains, and the drinking horn is linked to the sea so that Thor lowers the sea level and creates tides.

summary.en: At Ragnarök Thor slays the Midgard Serpent, retreats nine paces, and falls dead of its poison; his sons Magni and Modi survive and inherit his hammer.

claims.quote: Thor (from Old Norse: Þórr) is a prominent god in Germanic paganism. In Norse mythology, he is a hammer-wielding god associated with thunder, storms, strength, protection, fertility, and farmers.

statement.id: Thor atau Þórr adalah dewa pembawa palu dalam tradisi Jermanik dan mitologi Nordik, terkait guntur, badai, kekuatan, perlindungan, kesuburan, dan petani.
statement.en: Thor or Þórr is a hammer-bearing Germanic and Norse god linked to thunder, storms, strength, protection, fertility, and farmers.

claims.quote: Thor wields the hammer Mjölnir, wears the belt Megingjörð and the iron gloves Járngreipr

statement.id: Thor menggunakan palu Mjölnir, sabuk Megingjörð, dan sarung tangan Járngreipr.
statement.en: Thor wields Mjölnir and wears Megingjörð and Járngreipr.

claims.quote: Thor was the defender of Asgard, realm of the gods, and Midgard, the human realm, and is primarily associated with protection through great feats of arms in slaying giants.

statement.id: Thor digambarkan sebagai pembela Asgard dan Midgard, terutama dengan melawan para raksasa.
statement.en: Thor is described as defender of Asgard and Midgard, especially through fighting giants.

claims.quote: Thor was the god of thunder and he protected Midgard – the world of humans – using his hammer Mjöllnir.

statement.id: Menurut Museum Nasional Denmark, Thor dewa guntur yang melindungi Midgard, dunia manusia, menggunakan Mjöllnir.
statement.en: According to the National Museum of Denmark, Thor was the thunder god who protected Midgard with Mjöllnir.

claims.quote: Apart from these sources, some archaeological objects have also been found, which tell us about the Vikings’ early beliefs and the pantheon of Norse gods. Thor’s hammers are a good example of this.

statement.id: Museum menyebut temuan benda berbentuk palu Thor sebagai bukti arkeologis kepercayaan awal Viking.
statement.en: The museum cites finds of Thor's hammers as archaeological evidence for early Viking beliefs.

claims.quote: Thor (Old Norse: Þórr) is the Norse god of thunder, the sky, and agriculture.

statement.id: World History Encyclopedia menyebut Thor dewa guntur, langit, dan pertanian Nordik.
statement.en: World History Encyclopedia calls Thor the Norse god of thunder, sky, and agriculture.

claims.quote: He is the son of Odin, chief of the gods, and Odin's consort Jord (Earth) and husband of the fertility goddess Sif, who is the mother of his son Modi and daughter Thrud; his other son, Magni, may be from a union with the giantess Jarnsaxa.

statement.id: Thor adalah putra Odin, pemimpin para dewa, dan Jord (Bumi), selir Odin, serta suami dewi kesuburan Sif, ibu putranya Modi dan putrinya Thrud; putranya yang lain, Magni, mungkin lahir dari hubungan dengan raksasi Jarnsaxa.
statement.en: Thor is the son of Odin, chief of the gods, and Odin's consort Jord (Earth), and husband of the fertility goddess Sif, mother of his son Modi and daughter Thrud; his other son, Magni, may be from a union with the giantess Jarnsaxa.

claims.quote: The majority of the tales featuring Thor, in fact, put him in conflict with a giant or with his nemesis the Midgard Serpent (Jörmungandr, the "huge monster"), a monstrous snake who coils and twists itself around the world.

statement.id: Sebagian besar kisah tentang Thor menempatkannya berhadapan dengan raksasa atau dengan musuh bebuyutannya, Ular Midgard (Jörmungandr, "monster besar"), ular raksasa yang melilit dunia.
statement.en: Most tales featuring Thor put him in conflict with a giant or with his nemesis the Midgard Serpent (Jörmungandr, the "huge monster"), a monstrous snake that coils around the world.

claims.quote: Like almost all of the Norse gods, Thor is doomed to die at Ragnarök, the end of the world and twilight of the gods, but falls only after killing the great serpent with his powerful hammer Mjollnir, dying to its poison

statement.id: Seperti hampir semua dewa Nordik, Thor ditakdirkan tewas pada Ragnarök, akhir dunia dan senja para dewa, tetapi ia gugur hanya setelah membunuh ular raksasa dengan palunya Mjollnir dan mati karena bisanya.
statement.en: Like almost all Norse gods, Thor is doomed to die at Ragnarök, the end of the world and twilight of the gods, but falls only after killing the great serpent with his hammer Mjollnir, dying to its poison.

claims.quote: He developed from the earlier Germanic god Donar and became the most popular deity of the Norse pantheon.

statement.id: Thor berkembang dari dewa Germanik yang lebih awal, Donar, dan menjadi dewa paling populer dalam panteon Nordik.
statement.en: Thor developed from the earlier Germanic god Donar and became the most popular deity of the Norse pantheon.

claims.quote: the modern English and German words for the fifth day of the week - Thursday and Donnerstag - both allude to Thor/Donar ("Thor's Day"/"Donar's Day").

statement.id: Kata bahasa Inggris dan Jerman modern untuk hari kelima dalam sepekan, Thursday dan Donnerstag, sama-sama merujuk kepada Thor/Donar ("Hari Thor"/"Hari Donar").
statement.en: The modern English and German words for the fifth day of the week, Thursday and Donnerstag, both allude to Thor/Donar ("Thor's Day"/"Donar's Day").

claims.quote: He was thought to have ruled the sky from his land of Þrúðvangr ("Power-Field" or "Plains of Strength") where he built his great hall of Bilskírnir, a palace of 540 rooms.

statement.id: Thor dipercaya memerintah langit dari tanahnya, Þrúðvangr ("Ladang Kuasa" atau "Dataran Kekuatan"), tempat ia membangun aula besarnya, Bilskírnir, istana berkamar 540.
statement.en: Thor was thought to have ruled the sky from his land of Þrúðvangr ("Power-Field" or "Plains of Strength"), where he built his great hall Bilskírnir, a palace of 540 rooms.

claims.quote: He was said to burst forth from his great hall in his chariot, drawn by two male goats - Tanngnjóstr (Tooth Gnasher) and Tanngrísnir (Snarl Tooth) - who could be killed and eaten by the god and then brought back to life the next day as long as their bones remained unbroken.

statement.id: Thor dikisahkan keluar dari aula besarnya dengan kereta yang ditarik dua kambing jantan, Tanngnjóstr (Penggertak Gigi) dan Tanngrísnir (Gigi Menggeram), yang dapat dibunuh dan dimakan lalu dihidupkan kembali keesokan harinya selama tulangnya tidak patah.
statement.en: Thor was said to burst forth from his hall in a chariot drawn by two male goats, Tanngnjóstr (Tooth Gnasher) and Tanngrísnir (Snarl Tooth), which he could kill and eat and bring back to life the next day as long as their bones stayed unbroken.

claims.quote: The roar of thunder was the rumble of Thor's chariot's wheels across the vault of the heavens and, in another story, he is credited with creating tides.

statement.id: Gemuruh guntur adalah deru roda kereta Thor di kubah langit, dan dalam kisah lain ia dianggap menciptakan pasang surut.
statement.en: The roar of thunder was the rumble of Thor's chariot wheels across the vault of the heavens, and in another story he is credited with creating tides.

claims.quote: Thor's popularity reached its height during the Viking Age (c. 790-1100) at which time he was considered the greatest rival to Christ when, roughly from the 10th century onwards, Christianity was introduced to Scandinavia.

statement.id: Popularitas Thor mencapai puncaknya pada Zaman Viking (sekitar 790-1100), ketika ia dianggap saingan terbesar Kristus saat agama Kristen mulai diperkenalkan ke Skandinavia kira-kira dari abad ke-10.
statement.en: Thor's popularity reached its height in the Viking Age (c. 790-1100), when he was considered the greatest rival to Christ as Christianity was introduced to Scandinavia from roughly the 10th century.

claims.quote: More amulets and charms of Thor's hammer date from the period when Christianity and the Norse religion were in contention than from any other.

statement.id: Lebih banyak jimat palu Thor berasal dari masa ketika agama Kristen dan agama Nordik bersaing daripada dari masa lain mana pun.
statement.en: More amulets and charms of Thor's hammer date from the period when Christianity and the Norse religion were in contention than from any other.

claims.quote: He had three magical items which helped him defend Asgard and Midgard: his hammer Mjollnir, his belt of strength Megingjörð (which doubled his strength when he wore it), and his great iron gloves which he needed to wield his hammer.

statement.id: Thor memiliki tiga benda ajaib yang membantunya membela Asgard dan Midgard: palu Mjollnir, sabuk kekuatan Megingjörð (yang melipatgandakan kekuatannya saat dikenakan), dan sarung tangan besi besar yang diperlukan untuk memegang palunya.
statement.en: Thor had three magical items that helped him defend Asgard and Midgard: his hammer Mjollnir, his belt of strength Megingjörð (which doubled his strength when worn), and the great iron gloves he needed to wield the hammer.

claims.quote: Thor was invoked to seal business contracts and consecrate marriages, for agricultural abundance, for protection during voyages (especially at sea) and for victory in battle, but he seems to have been called upon whenever any need arose.

statement.id: Thor diseru untuk mengesahkan kontrak dagang dan memberkati pernikahan, demi kelimpahan pertanian, perlindungan dalam pelayaran (terutama di laut), dan kemenangan perang, tetapi tampaknya ia dipanggil kapan pun kebutuhan muncul.
statement.en: Thor was invoked to seal business contracts and consecrate marriages, for agricultural abundance, for protection on voyages (especially at sea) and for victory in battle, and seems to have been called upon whenever any need arose.

claims.quote: These items embellish Thor's great strength, which is his main feature, and Thor also has a quick temper and shows impatience for following others' rules.

statement.id: Benda-benda itu menambah kekuatan besar Thor, yang menjadi ciri utamanya; Thor juga cepat naik darah dan tidak sabar mengikuti aturan orang lain.
statement.en: These items embellish Thor's great strength, his main feature, and Thor also has a quick temper and shows impatience with following others' rules.

claims.quote: Thor is completely without guile or the capacity to deceive and so cannot recognize these qualities in others; as a result, he is often tricked by magical spells or shape-shifting entities which cause things to appear other than they are.

statement.id: Thor sama sekali tidak berlicik dan tidak mampu menipu sehingga tak dapat mengenali sifat itu pada orang lain; akibatnya ia sering dikelabui mantra atau makhluk pengubah wujud yang membuat segala sesuatu tampak lain dari kenyataan.
statement.en: Thor is completely without guile or the capacity to deceive and so cannot recognize these qualities in others; as a result he is often tricked by magical spells or shape-shifting entities that make things appear other than they are.

claims.quote: he was not the brother of Loki and is never depicted as clean-shaven or blonde-haired except in chapter 3 of the Prose Edda (composed c. 1220), a mythography of earlier Norse myths reworked by the Icelander Snorri Sturluson into one structured account, written from a Christian context.

statement.id: Berbeda dari citra populer masa kini dari komik dan film Marvel, Thor bukan saudara Loki dan tidak pernah digambarkan klimis atau berambut pirang kecuali dalam bab 3 Prose Edda (disusun sekitar 1220), karya yang ditulis dari konteks Kristen oleh Snorri Sturluson dari Islandia.
statement.en: Contrary to the popular present-day image from Marvel comics and films, Thor was not Loki's brother and is never depicted as clean-shaven or blonde except in chapter 3 of the Prose Edda (composed c. 1220), written from a Christian context by the Icelander Snorri Sturluson.

claims.quote: Elsewhere, and in almost every image, Thor is always shown with long red hair and a great beard, often as not leaping into battle against giants or killing dwarves without pausing to consider alternatives to violence.

statement.id: Di tempat lain dan dalam hampir setiap gambar, Thor selalu ditampilkan berambut merah panjang dan berjanggut lebat, sering melompat ke pertempuran melawan raksasa atau membunuh kurcaci tanpa mempertimbangkan alternatif selain kekerasan.
statement.en: Elsewhere, and in almost every image, Thor is shown with long red hair and a great beard, often leaping into battle against giants or killing dwarves without considering alternatives to violence.

claims.quote: He first tells them that he was Skrýmir in the forest and that he deceived Thor each time Thor struck him; Thor was actually striking at mountains whose tops were now leveled from each blow.

statement.id: Utgarda-Loki mengungkapkan bahwa ia adalah Skrýmir di hutan dan telah mengelabui Thor setiap kali Thor memukulnya; Thor sebenarnya memukul gunung-gunung yang puncaknya kini rata oleh tiap pukulan.
statement.en: Utgarda-Loki reveals that he was Skrýmir in the forest and deceived Thor each time Thor struck him; Thor was actually striking mountains whose tops were leveled by each blow.

claims.quote: In the case of Thor's contest, Utgarda-Loki explains, the bottom of the drinking horn was in the sea so that, no matter how much Thor drank, he would never have been able to empty it. He did manage to drink so much, however, that the sea level had dropped and Thor had now created tides.

statement.id: Utgarda-Loki menjelaskan bahwa dasar tanduk minum itu berada di laut sehingga Thor tak akan pernah bisa mengosongkannya, tetapi Thor meminum sedemikian banyak hingga permukaan laut turun dan ia menciptakan pasang surut.
statement.en: Utgarda-Loki explains that the bottom of the drinking horn was in the sea, so Thor could never have emptied it, but he drank so much that the sea level dropped and Thor created tides.

claims.quote: In another popular tale, Thor's hammer is stolen by the giants and he must disguise himself as the goddess Freyja and pretend to be the giant's bride in order to get it back.

statement.id: Dalam kisah populer lain, palu Thor dicuri para raksasa dan ia harus menyamar sebagai dewi Freyja dan berpura-pura menjadi pengantin sang raksasa untuk mendapatkannya kembali.
statement.en: In another popular tale, Thor's hammer is stolen by the giants and he must disguise himself as the goddess Freyja and pretend to be the giant's bride to get it back.

claims.quote: Shortly afterwards, he goes fishing with the giant Hymir and catches the serpent but Hymir, fearful of drowning since Thor's fight with the beast is threatening their boat, cuts the line.

statement.id: Tak lama kemudian Thor memancing bersama raksasa Hymir dan menangkap ular itu, tetapi Hymir, takut tenggelam karena pertarungan Thor mengancam perahu mereka, memotong tali pancing.
statement.en: Shortly afterwards Thor goes fishing with the giant Hymir and catches the serpent, but Hymir, fearful of drowning because the fight threatens their boat, cuts the line.

claims.quote: was master of thunder and lightning, storm and rain, fair weather and crops, and the pagans sacrificed to him when threatened by hunger or disease

statement.id: Sarjana Preben Meulengracht Sørensen, yang dikutip World History Encyclopedia, menyebut Thor penguasa guntur dan kilat, badai dan hujan, cuaca cerah dan panen, dan bahwa kaum pagan berkurban kepadanya saat terancam kelaparan atau penyakit.
statement.en: The scholar Preben Meulengracht Sørensen, quoted by World History Encyclopedia, says Thor was master of thunder and lightning, storm and rain, fair weather and crops, and the pagans sacrificed to him when threatened by hunger or disease.

claims.quote: Christianity finally prevailed and the cult of Thor was gradually replaced by the new religion by the 12th century.

statement.id: Agama Kristen akhirnya menang dan pemujaan Thor berangsur digantikan agama baru itu pada abad ke-12.
statement.en: Christianity finally prevailed and the cult of Thor was gradually replaced by the new religion by the 12th century.

claims.quote: He is closely associated with water in many of the myths and is depicted rowing out further into the sea than others have gone and also crossing dangerous rivers

statement.id: Thor dikaitkan erat dengan air dalam banyak mitos dan digambarkan mendayung ke laut lebih jauh daripada yang lain serta menyeberangi sungai berbahaya.
statement.en: Thor is closely associated with water in many myths and is depicted rowing out further into the sea than others and crossing dangerous rivers.

claims.quote: Thor functioned primarily as a protector-god, although stories concerning him also explained natural phenomena

statement.id: Thor terutama berfungsi sebagai dewa pelindung, meski kisah-kisah tentangnya juga menjelaskan gejala alam.
statement.en: Thor functioned primarily as a protector-god, although stories about him also explained natural phenomena.

claims.quote: He is the strongest of all gods and men, and rules over the realm which is called Thrudvang. His hall is called Bilskirner.

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, Har menyebut Thor yang terkuat di antara semua dewa dan manusia; ia memerintah wilayah bernama Thrudvang dan aulanya bernama Bilskirner.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, Har says Thor is the strongest of all gods and men and rules the realm called Thrudvang; his hall is called Bilskirner.

claims.quote: Thor has two goats, by name Tangnjost and Tangrisner, and a chariot, wherein he drives. The goats draw the chariot

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor memiliki dua kambing bernama Tangnjost dan Tangrisner serta sebuah kereta; kambing-kambing itu menarik keretanya.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, Thor has two goats named Tangnjost and Tangrisner and a chariot, and the goats draw the chariot.

claims.quote: One of them is the hammer Mjolner, which the frost-giants and mountain-giants well know when it is raised; and this is not to be wondered at, for with it he has split many a skull of their fathers or friends.

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, palu Mjolner dikenal baik oleh raksasa es dan raksasa gunung ketika diangkat, karena dengannya Thor telah membelah banyak tengkorak ayah atau kawan mereka.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, the hammer Mjolner is well known to the frost-giants and mountain-giants when raised, for with it Thor has split many a skull of their fathers or friends.

claims.quote: The second treasure he possesses is Megingjarder (belt of strength); when he girds himself with it his strength is doubled. His third treasure that is of so great value is his iron gloves; these he cannot do without when he lays hold of the hammer's haft.

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, harta kedua Thor adalah Megingjarder (sabuk kekuatan) yang melipatgandakan kekuatannya saat dikenakan, dan harta ketiganya sarung tangan besi yang tak dapat ia tinggalkan saat menggenggam gagang palu.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, Thor's second treasure is Megingjarder (belt of strength), which doubles his strength when worn, and his third is his iron gloves, which he cannot do without when he grips the hammer's haft.

claims.quote: Then Thor turned away to where he saw a herd of oxen, that belonged to Hymer. He took the largest ox, which was called Himinbrjot, twisted his head off and brought it down to the sea-strand.
claims.locator: Gylfaginning (The Deluding of Gylfi), Thor and Hymer

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor mengambil lembu terbesar milik Hymer, bernama Himinbrjot, memelintir kepalanya hingga putus, dan membawanya ke pantai.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, Thor takes the largest of Hymer's oxen, called Himinbrjot, twists its head off, and brings it down to the sea-strand.

claims.quote: He pulled the serpent up to the gunwale; and in truth no one has ever seen a more terrible sight than when Thor whet his eyes on the serpent, and the latter stared at him and spouted venom.
claims.locator: Gylfaginning (The Deluding of Gylfi), Thor and Hymer

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor menarik ular itu hingga ke tepi perahu, dan tak pernah ada pemandangan lebih mengerikan daripada saat Thor menatap ular itu dan ular itu menatapnya sambil menyemburkan bisa.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, Thor pulls the serpent up to the gunwale, and no one has ever seen a more terrible sight than Thor fixing his eyes on the serpent as it stared back and spouted venom.

claims.quote: Thor threw the hammer after it, and it is even said that he struck off his head at the bottom, but I think the truth is that the Midgard-serpent still lives and lies in the ocean.
claims.locator: Gylfaginning (The Deluding of Gylfi), Thor and Hymer

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor melempar palunya mengejar ular itu dan konon memenggal kepalanya di dasar laut, tetapi sang pencerita berpendapat kebenarannya ialah Ular Midgard masih hidup dan berbaring di samudra.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, Thor threw the hammer after the serpent and it is even said that he struck off its head at the bottom, but the narrator thinks the truth is that the Midgard-serpent still lives and lies in the ocean.

claims.quote: Thor gets great renown by slaying the Midgard-serpent, but retreats only nine paces when he falls to the earth dead, poisoned by the venom that the serpent blows on him.

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor mendapat nama besar karena membunuh Ular Midgard, tetapi hanya mundur sembilan langkah sebelum jatuh mati, diracuni bisa yang disemburkan ular itu.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, Thor gains great renown by slaying the Midgard-serpent but retreats only nine paces before falling dead, poisoned by the venom the serpent blows on him.

claims.quote: He is called Asa-Thor, or Oku-Thor.

statement.id: Dalam Prose Edda, Thor disebut Asa-Thor atau Oku-Thor.
statement.en: In the Prose Edda, Thor is called Asa-Thor or Oku-Thor.

claims.quote: Besides Old Norse Þórr, the deity occurs in Old English as Thunor, in Old Frisian as Thuner, in Old Saxon as Thunar, and in Old High German as Donar, all ultimately stemming from the Proto-Germanic theonym *Þun(a)raz, meaning 'Thunder'.

statement.id: Selain Þórr dalam bahasa Nordik Kuno, dewa ini muncul dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno sebagai Thunor, Frisia Kuno sebagai Thuner, Saksen Kuno sebagai Thunar, dan Jerman Tinggi Kuno sebagai Donar, semuanya berasal dari nama dewa Proto-Germanik *Þun(a)raz yang berarti 'Guntur'.
statement.en: Besides Old Norse Þórr, the deity occurs in Old English as Thunor, Old Frisian as Thuner, Old Saxon as Thunar, and Old High German as Donar, all ultimately from the Proto-Germanic theonym *Þun(a)raz, meaning 'Thunder'.

claims.quote: In 1962, American comic book artist Jack Kirby, Marvel Comics editor Stan Lee, and his brother Larry Lieber created a feature in the comic book Journey Into Mystery, a series featuring Thor as a superhero. This version of Thor is portrayed as a clean-shaven blonde, instead of red-haired and bearded.

statement.id: Pada 1962, Jack Kirby, Stan Lee, dan saudaranya Larry Lieber menciptakan fitur dalam komik Journey Into Mystery yang menampilkan Thor sebagai pahlawan super; Thor versi ini digambarkan klimis dan berambut pirang, bukan berambut merah dan berjanggut.
statement.en: In 1962 Jack Kirby, Stan Lee, and his brother Larry Lieber created a feature in the comic Journey Into Mystery presenting Thor as a superhero; this version is portrayed as a clean-shaven blonde instead of red-haired and bearded.

claims.quote: From 2015 to 2017, a fictionalised version of Thor was a supporting character in Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard, a trilogy of fantasy novels written by American author Rick Riordan

statement.id: Dari 2015 hingga 2017, versi fiksi Thor menjadi tokoh pendukung dalam Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard, trilogi novel fantasi karya Rick Riordan.
statement.en: From 2015 to 2017 a fictionalised Thor was a supporting character in Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard, a fantasy trilogy by Rick Riordan.

claims.quote: In January 2020, the streaming service Netflix produced Ragnarok. In the show, a high school student, Magne Seier, receives Thor's powers and abilities to fight the giants that are polluting Norway and murdering people.

statement.id: Pada Januari 2020 Netflix memproduksi Ragnarok; dalam serial itu seorang siswa SMA, Magne Seier, menerima kekuatan dan kemampuan Thor untuk melawan raksasa yang mencemari Norwegia dan membunuh orang.
statement.en: In January 2020 Netflix produced Ragnarok, in which a high school student, Magne Seier, receives Thor's powers and abilities to fight the giants polluting Norway and murdering people.

claims.quote: Thor therefore became the Norse god of the everyman; the common-sense, no-nonsense deity anyone could relate to and everyone could depend on.

statement.id: Karena itu Thor menjadi dewa Nordik bagi orang biasa: dewa yang bernalar sederhana dan tanpa basa-basi, yang dapat dipahami siapa pun dan diandalkan semua orang.
statement.en: Thor therefore became the Norse god of the everyman, a common-sense, no-nonsense deity anyone could relate to and everyone could depend on.

short_description.id: Sphinx adalah makhluk mitos bertubuh singa, biasanya berkepala manusia, yang dikenal sebagai penjaga makam di Mesir dan sebagai pengaju teka-teki di Thebes menurut mitos Yunani.
short_description.en: A sphinx is a mythical creature with a lion's body and usually a human head, known as a tomb guardian in Egypt and as the riddler of Thebes in Greek myth.

long_description.id: Sphinx adalah makhluk mitos bertubuh singa, paling sering berkepala manusia dan kadang bersayap. Bangsa Mesir yang pertama menciptakannya, dan motifnya dikenal di Mediterania timur sejak Zaman Perunggu. Seni Yunani menampilkannya sebagai singa betina bersayap berkepala perempuan; menurut Theoi, ia juga berdada perempuan, bersayap elang, dan menurut sebagian sumber berekor ular.
long_description.en: A sphinx is a mythical creature with a lion's body, most often with a human head and sometimes wings. The Egyptians first created it, and the motif was known across the eastern Mediterranean from the Bronze Age. Greek art shows it as a winged lioness with a woman's head; according to Theoi it also has a woman's breast and eagle's wings, and according to some a serpent's tail.

long_description.id: Di Mesir, sphinx biasanya ditempatkan sebagai penjaga di luar atau di samping kuil pemakaman, makam, atau monumen pemakaman, dan arca sphinx menjaga makam dari gangguan. Dalam kisah Yunani, bangsa Yunani memandangnya sebagai makhluk yang lebih merepotkan: menurut Apollodorus, Hera mengirim Sphinx, putri Echidna dan Typhon, sedangkan Hesiodos menyebutnya lahir dari Chimaira.
long_description.en: In Egypt, sphinxes were typically stationed as guards at the exterior or flank of mortuary temples, tombs, and funerary monuments, and sphinx statues guarded tombs against disturbance. In Greek stories the Greeks saw it as a more troublesome creature: according to Apollodorus, Hera sent the Sphinx, whose mother was Echidna and father Typhon, while Hesiod says she was born from the Chimaera.

long_description.id: Dalam mitos Thebes, Sphinx duduk di Gunung Phicium dan mengajukan teka-teki yang ia pelajari dari para Muse. Siapa pun yang menjawab salah dilahap, dan kota itu menderita kekeringan dan kelaparan. Oedipus menjawab bahwa jawabannya manusia, lalu Sphinx melompat hingga tewas.
long_description.en: In the myth of Thebes, the Sphinx sat on Mount Phicium and put a riddle she had learned from the Muses. Anyone who answered wrongly was devoured, and the city suffered drought and famine. Oedipus answered that the answer was man, after which the Sphinx leapt to her death.

long_description.id: Makhluk serupa sphinx juga dikenal di India Selatan sebagai puruṣamr̥ga, di Burma sebagai Manussiha, dan di Thailand dengan nama seperti Norasingha; patungnya berfungsi sebagai penolak bala di kuil dan sebagai penghias sudut stupa.
long_description.en: Sphinx-like beings are also known in South India as puruṣamr̥ga, in Burma as Manussiha, and in Thailand under names such as Norasingha; their statues serve as apotropaic figures at temples and sit on the corners of stupas.

cultural_context.id: Di Mesir, sphinx ditempatkan sebagai penjaga di dekat kuil pemakaman dan makam, sedangkan bangsa Yunani memandangnya sebagai makhluk yang lebih merepotkan. Dalam lukisan vas arkais, sphinx sering muncul di tengah arak-arakan hewan dan makhluk ajaib. Sphinx juga menjadi lambang negara-kota Chios dan muncul pada koin dan segelnya.
cultural_context.en: In Egypt, sphinxes were placed as guards near mortuary temples and tombs, while the Greeks saw the sphinx as a more troublesome creature. In archaic vase paintings sphinxes often appear among processions of animals and fabulous creatures. The sphinx was also the emblem of the city-state of Chios and appeared on its coins and seals.

literal_meaning.id: dikaitkan oleh etimologi rakyat dengan kata kerja σφίγγω, "meremas" atau "mengencangkan"; usul lain menyebutnya perubahan dari nama Mesir "shesepankh", "citra hidup"
literal_meaning.en: associated by folk etymology with the verb σφίγγω, "to squeeze" or "to tighten up"; another suggestion is a corruption of the Egyptian name "shesepankh", "living image"

who.id: Makhluk mitos bertubuh singa, biasanya berkepala manusia dan kadang bersayap.
who.en: A mythical creature with a lion's body, usually a human head, and sometimes wings.

origin.id: Diciptakan lebih dulu di Mesir; dalam mitos Yunani, ia mengganggu Thebes.
origin.en: First created in Egypt; in Greek myth it plagued Thebes.

role.id: Penjaga makam di Mesir; pengaju teka-teki yang memangsa korban di Thebes menurut mitos Yunani.
role.en: Tomb guardian in Egypt; riddler who devoured victims at Thebes in Greek myth.

famous_for.id: Teka-teki tentang makhluk berkaki empat, dua, lalu tiga, yang dijawab Oedipus dengan "manusia".
famous_for.en: The riddle of the creature on four, two, then three feet, answered by Oedipus with "man".

did_you_know.id: Menurut sebuah kisah, Thutmose IV tertidur di bayangan Sphinx dan bermimpi Sphinx berjanji ia akan menjadi raja jika membersihkan pasir di kaki patung itu.
did_you_know.en: According to one story, Thutmose IV fell asleep in the Sphinx's shadow and dreamt that it promised him kingship if he cleared the sand around its feet.

description.id: Sphinx mengajukan teka-teki kepada orang Thebes dan melahap mereka yang gagal menjawab.
description.en: The Sphinx put a riddle to the Thebans and devoured those who failed to answer.

description.id: Arca sphinx menjaga makam dari gangguan, dan sphinx pahatan besar berbentuk banteng bersayap berdiri di luar istana untuk menjaga dari kekuatan jahat.
description.en: Sphinx statues guarded tombs against disturbance, and large sculpted sphinxes shaped like winged bulls stood outside palaces to guard against evil forces.

description.id: Ketika Oedipus menjawab teka-teki dengan benar, Sphinx melompat dari akropolis Thebes hingga tewas.
description.en: When Oedipus answered the riddle correctly, the Sphinx leapt to her death from the acropolis of Thebes.

description.id: Menurut uraian ini, "sphinx" di India Selatan bernama puruṣamr̥ga atau purushamirugam ("manusia-hewan") dan digambarkan di kuil dan istana dengan fungsi penolak bala.
description.en: In this account, the "sphinx" of South India is called puruṣamr̥ga or purushamirugam ("human-animal") and is depicted in temples and palaces with an apotropaic purpose.

description.id: Patung mirip sphinx berkepala manusia dan berbadan belakang singa, ditempatkan di sudut stupa Buddha.
description.en: A sphinx-like statue with a human head and two lion hindquarters, placed on the corners of Buddhist stupas.

description.id: Nora Nair, Norasingha, dan Thep Norasingha adalah nama "sphinx" di Thailand, digambarkan berjalan tegak.
description.en: Nora Nair, Norasingha, and Thep Norasingha are names of the "sphinx" in Thailand, depicted walking upright.

summary.id: Sphinx mengganggu Thebes: duduk di Gunung Phicium, mengajukan teka-teki yang ia pelajari dari para Muse, dan menyambar orang yang tidak dapat menjawabnya. Oedipus menjawab "manusia" dan Sphinx melompat hingga tewas. Teka-teki yang persis tidak ditentukan oleh penutur awal mitos dan baru dibakukan pada akhir sejarah Yunani.
summary.en: The Sphinx plagued Thebes: she sat on Mount Phicium, put a riddle she had learned from the Muses, and snatched those who could not answer. Oedipus answered "man" and the Sphinx leapt to her death. The exact riddle was not specified by early tellers of the myth and was standardized only late in Greek history.

note.en: According to Apollodorus, she sent the Sphinx to Thebes.

note.en: The Sphinx learned her riddle from the Muses.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa bangsa Mesir dan Yunani memandang sphinx dengan cara yang berbeda?
learning_questions.en: Why did the Egyptians and the Greeks view the sphinx differently?

learning_questions.id: Apa makna teka-teki Sphinx bagi cerita Oedipus?
learning_questions.en: What does the Sphinx's riddle mean for the story of Oedipus?

claims.quote: A sphinx is a mythical creature with the body of a lion, most often with a human head and sometimes with wings.

statement.id: Sphinx adalah makhluk mitos bertubuh singa dan biasanya berkepala manusia, kadang bersayap.
statement.en: A sphinx is a mythical creature with a lion's body, usually a human head, and sometimes wings.

claims.quote: The sphinx, a mythological creature with a lion's body and a human head, originated in Egypt and has been known throughout the eastern Mediterranean since the Bronze Age.

statement.id: Motif sphinx berasal dari Mesir dan dikenal di Mediterania timur sejak Zaman Perunggu.
statement.en: The sphinx motif originated in Egypt and was known across the eastern Mediterranean in the Bronze Age.

claims.quote: The Greeks represented the sphinx as a winged lioness with a woman's head.

statement.id: Orang Yunani menggambarkannya sebagai singa betina bersayap dan berkepala perempuan.
statement.en: Greek art portrayed the sphinx as a winged lioness with a woman's head.

claims.quote: THE SPHINX was a female monster with the body of a lion, the head and breast of a woman, eagle's wings and, according to some, a serpent's tail.

statement.id: Sphinx Yunani digambarkan memiliki tubuh singa, bagian atas perempuan, dan sayap elang; sebagian versi menambah ekor ular.
statement.en: The Greek sphinx has a lion's body, woman's upper body, eagle wings, and sometimes a serpent tail.

claims.quote: Statues of sphinxes flanked the entrance of tombs or crowned grave markers, guarding against and punishing those who would disturb the dead.

statement.id: Arca sphinx ditempatkan di makam sebagai penjaga dari pengganggu orang mati.
statement.en: Sphinx statues guarded tombs against disturbance.

claims.quote: Anyone who dared to answer the riddle and failed to do so correctly was killed and devoured by the sphinx.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Thebes, Sphinx memangsa orang yang gagal menjawab teka-tekinya.
statement.en: In the Theban myth, the sphinx devoured those who failed her riddle.

claims.quote: Oedipus took up the challenge and gave the correct answer —man— and in frustration and anger the sphinx leapt to her death from the acropolis of Thebes.

statement.id: Oedipus menjawab 'manusia', lalu Sphinx melompat hingga tewas.
statement.en: Oedipus answered 'human' and the sphinx leapt to her death.

claims.quote: The most famous sphinx plagued the city of Thebes, devouring anyone who gave the wrong answer to her riddle: what is that which has one voice and yet becomes four-footed, two-footed, and three-footed?

statement.id: Teka-teki Sphinx menanyakan makhluk bersuara satu yang berjalan dengan empat, dua, dan tiga kaki.
statement.en: The sphinx's riddle asks what has one voice and four, two, then three feet.

claims.quote: She was sent by the gods to plague the town of Thebes as punishment for some ancient crime, preying on its youths and devouring all who failed to solve her riddle.

statement.id: Menurut Theoi, para dewa mengirim Sphinx untuk menimpakan bencana pada kota Thebes sebagai hukuman atas kejahatan lama; ia memangsa para pemuda dan melahap semua yang gagal memecahkan teka-tekinya.
statement.en: According to Theoi, the gods sent the Sphinx to plague the town of Thebes as punishment for some ancient crime; she preyed on its youths and devoured all who failed to solve her riddle.

claims.quote: In archaic vase paintings they often appear amongst a procession of animals and fabulous creatures such as lions and bird-bodied sirens.

statement.id: Dalam lukisan vas arkais, sphinx sering muncul di tengah arak-arakan hewan dan makhluk ajaib seperti singa dan siren berbadan burung.
statement.en: In archaic vase paintings, sphinxes often appear among a procession of animals and fabulous creatures such as lions and bird-bodied sirens.

claims.quote: But she [Khimaira (Chimera)] also, in love with Orthos (Orthus), mothered the deadly Sphinx, the bane of the Kadmeians (Cadmeans) [Thebans].
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes: Hesiod, Theogony 326 ff

statement.id: Menurut kutipan Theogony karya Hesiodos di Theoi, Khimaira, yang jatuh cinta pada Orthos, melahirkan Sphinx yang mematikan, bencana bagi bangsa Kadmos (Thebes).
statement.en: In the quotation from Hesiod's Theogony on Theoi, Khimaira, in love with Orthos, mothered the deadly Sphinx, the bane of the Kadmeians (Thebans).

claims.quote: For Hera sent the Sphinx, ... whose mother was Echidna and her father Typhon; and she had the face of a woman, the breast and feet and tail of a lion, and the wings of a bird.

statement.id: Menurut Apollodorus, Hera mengirim Sphinx, yang ibunya Echidna dan ayahnya Typhon; ia berwajah perempuan, berdada, berkaki, dan berekor singa, serta bersayap burung.
statement.en: According to Apollodorus, Hera sent the Sphinx, whose mother was Echidna and father Typhon; she had a woman's face, a lion's breast, feet, and tail, and a bird's wings.

claims.quote: And having learned a riddle from the Muses, she sat on Mount Phicium, and propounded it to the Thebans.

statement.id: Setelah mempelajari teka-teki dari para Muse, Sphinx duduk di Gunung Phicium dan mengajukannya kepada orang Thebes.
statement.en: Having learned a riddle from the Muses, the Sphinx sat on Mount Phicium and put it to the Thebans.

claims.quote: so they often met and discussed the answer, and when they could not find it the Sphinx used to snatch away one of them and gobble him up.

statement.id: Orang Thebes sering berkumpul membahas jawabannya, dan bila tidak menemukannya, Sphinx menyambar salah satu dari mereka lalu melahapnya.
statement.en: The Thebans often met to discuss the answer, and when they could not find it the Sphinx snatched one of them and gobbled him up.

claims.quote: Oedipus found the solution, declaring that the riddle of the Sphinx referred to man; for as a babe he is four-footed, going on four limbs, as an adult he is two-footed, and as an old man he gets besides a third support in a staff.

statement.id: Oedipus menemukan jawabannya: teka-teki Sphinx merujuk pada manusia, yang saat bayi berkaki empat, saat dewasa berkaki dua, dan saat tua mendapat penopang ketiga berupa tongkat.
statement.en: Oedipus found the solution: the riddle referred to man, who as a babe goes on four limbs, as an adult on two feet, and as an old man gets a third support in a staff.

claims.quote: Hesiod tells us in his Theogony that the creature was born from the Chimaera (a fire-breathing monster with three heads and a body part lion, goat, snake and dragon) and was sister to the Nemean lion and half-sister of Kerberos (the three-headed dog that guarded Hades).

statement.id: Menurut Theogony karya Hesiodos, Sphinx lahir dari Chimaira, saudari Singa Nemea, dan saudari tiri Kerberos.
statement.en: According to Hesiod's Theogony, the sphinx was born from the Chimaera, sister of the Nemean lion and half-sister of Kerberos.

claims.quote: The sphinx created drought and famine and would only leave the Thebans alone if they solved her riddle.

statement.id: Sphinx menimbulkan kekeringan dan kelaparan dan hanya akan membiarkan orang Thebes jika mereka memecahkan teka-tekinya.
statement.en: The sphinx brought drought and famine and would leave the Thebans alone only if they solved her riddle.

claims.quote: Sphinxes were first created by the Egyptians and usually wore a nemes (head-dress) as worn by Pharaohs.

statement.id: Sphinx pertama kali dibuat oleh bangsa Mesir dan biasanya mengenakan nemes (tutup kepala) seperti yang dipakai para firaun.
statement.en: Sphinxes were first created by the Egyptians and usually wore a nemes (head-dress) like those worn by pharaohs.

claims.quote: In the reign of Chephren, sphinxes became more widespread and they were usually placed as guards outside or beside a mortuary temple, tomb or funerary monument.

statement.id: Pada masa pemerintahan Chephren, sphinx makin tersebar dan biasanya ditempatkan sebagai penjaga di luar atau di samping kuil pemakaman, makam, atau monumen pemakaman.
statement.en: In the reign of Chephren, sphinxes became more widespread and were usually placed as guards outside or beside a mortuary temple, tomb, or funerary monument.

claims.quote: There is a story that in the Eighteenth Dynasty, Pharaoh Thutmose IV, when he was a mere prince, went on a hunting expedition and fell asleep in the shadow of the Sphinx. Whilst asleep he dreamt that the Sphinx spoke to him and promised that he would become king if he cleared the sands that had accumulated around the feet of the statue.

statement.id: Ada kisah bahwa Thutmose IV, saat masih pangeran, tertidur di bayangan Sphinx dan bermimpi Sphinx berjanji ia akan menjadi raja jika membersihkan pasir di kaki patung itu.
statement.en: There is a story that Thutmose IV, still a prince, fell asleep in the shadow of the Sphinx and dreamt that it promised he would become king if he cleared the sand around the statue's feet.

claims.quote: Large, sculpted sphinxes in the shape of winged bulls often stood in pairs outside palaces and guarded against evil forces.

statement.id: Sphinx pahatan besar berbentuk banteng bersayap sering berdiri berpasangan di luar istana dan menjaga dari kekuatan jahat.
statement.en: Large sculpted sphinxes in the shape of winged bulls often stood in pairs outside palaces and guarded against evil forces.

claims.quote: Indeed, one of the most famous sphinxes was discovered at Delphi; originally sat on a 10m high Ionic column, it had been dedicated to the oracle by the Naxians around 560 BCE.

statement.id: Salah satu sphinx paling terkenal ditemukan di Delphi; semula bertengger di atas tiang Ionia setinggi 10 m dan dipersembahkan kepada oracle oleh orang Naxos sekitar 560 SM.
statement.en: One of the most famous sphinxes was found at Delphi; it originally sat on a 10 m Ionic column and was dedicated to the oracle by the Naxians around 560 BCE.

claims.quote: Sphinxes were also present in the art of the Minoan and Mycenaean cultures from the early second millennium BC.

statement.id: Sphinx juga hadir dalam seni budaya Minoa dan Mikenai sejak awal milenium kedua SM.
statement.en: Sphinxes were also present in the art of the Minoan and Mycenaean cultures from the early second millennium BC.

claims.quote: The word sphinx comes from the Greek Σφίγξ, associated by folk etymology with the verb σφίγγω (sphíngō), meaning "to squeeze", "to tighten up".

statement.id: Kata sphinx berasal dari bahasa Yunani Σφίγξ, yang menurut etimologi rakyat dikaitkan dengan kata kerja σφίγγω (sphíngō) yang berarti "meremas" atau "mengencangkan".
statement.en: The word sphinx comes from the Greek Σφίγξ, associated by folk etymology with the verb σφίγγω (sphíngō), meaning "to squeeze" or "to tighten up".

claims.quote: According to Hesiod, the Sphinx was a daughter of Orthrus and an unknown she—either the Chimera, Echidna, or Ceto. According to Apollodorus and Lasus, she was a daughter of Echidna and Typhon.

statement.id: Menurut Hesiodos, Sphinx putri Orthrus dan seorang perempuan yang tidak jelas (Chimera, Echidna, atau Ceto); menurut Apollodorus dan Lasus, putri Echidna dan Typhon.
statement.en: According to Hesiod, the Sphinx was a daughter of Orthrus and an unknown female (the Chimera, Echidna, or Ceto); according to Apollodorus and Lasus, a daughter of Echidna and Typhon.

claims.quote: The sphinx was the emblem of the ancient city-state of Chios, and appeared on seals and the obverse side of coins from the 6th century BC until the 3rd century AD.

statement.id: Sphinx adalah lambang negara-kota kuno Chios dan muncul pada segel serta sisi depan koin dari abad ke-6 SM hingga abad ke-3 M.
statement.en: The sphinx was the emblem of the ancient city-state of Chios and appeared on seals and the obverse of coins from the 6th century BC until the 3rd century AD.

claims.quote: The exact riddle asked by the Sphinx was not specified by early tellers of the myth, and was not standardized as the one given below until late in Greek history.

statement.id: Teka-teki yang tepat dari Sphinx tidak ditentukan oleh para penutur awal mitos dan baru dibakukan pada akhir sejarah Yunani.
statement.en: The exact riddle asked by the Sphinx was not specified by early tellers of the myth and was standardized only late in Greek history.

claims.quote: It was said in late lore that Hera or Ares sent the Sphinx from her Aethiopian homeland (the Greeks always remembered the foreign origin of the Sphinx) to Thebes in Greece

statement.id: Menurut cerita akhir, Hera atau Ares mengirim Sphinx dari tanah airnya di Aethiopia ke Thebes di Yunani; orang Yunani selalu mengingat asal asingnya.
statement.en: In late lore, Hera or Ares sent the Sphinx from her Aethiopian homeland to Thebes in Greece; the Greeks always remembered her foreign origin.

claims.quote: Bested at last, the Sphinx then threw herself from her high rock and died

statement.id: Setelah akhirnya dikalahkan, Sphinx melemparkan diri dari batu tinggi dan mati.
statement.en: Bested at last, the Sphinx threw herself from her high rock and died.

claims.quote: In South India, the "sphinx" is known as puruṣamr̥ga (Sanskrit) or purushamirugam (Tamil), meaning "human-animal". It is found depicted in sculptural art in temples and palaces where it serves an apotropaic purpose

statement.id: Di India Selatan, "sphinx" dikenal sebagai puruṣamr̥ga (Sanskerta) atau purushamirugam (Tamil), "manusia-hewan", dan digambarkan dalam seni pahat di kuil dan istana dengan fungsi penolak bala.
statement.en: In South India the "sphinx" is known as puruṣamr̥ga (Sanskrit) or purushamirugam (Tamil), "human-animal", and is depicted in sculpture in temples and palaces with an apotropaic purpose.

claims.quote: In Burma (Myanmar), the sphinx-like statue, with a human head and two lion hindquarters, is known as Manussiha (manuthiha). It is depicted on the corners of Buddhist stupas, and its legends tell how it was created by Buddhist monks to protect a new-born royal baby from being devoured by ogresses.

statement.id: Di Burma (Myanmar), patung mirip sphinx berkepala manusia dan berbadan belakang singa dikenal sebagai Manussiha; ditempatkan di sudut stupa Buddha, dan legendanya menyebut ia dibuat para biksu untuk melindungi bayi kerajaan dari raksasa betina.
statement.en: In Burma (Myanmar), the sphinx-like statue with a human head and two lion hindquarters is known as Manussiha; it is placed on the corners of Buddhist stupas, and its legends say Buddhist monks created it to protect a newborn royal baby from ogresses.

claims.quote: Nora Nair, Norasingha and Thep Norasingha are three of the names under which the "sphinx" is known in Thailand. They are depicted as upright walking beings with the lower body of a lion or deer, and the upper body of a human.

statement.id: Nora Nair, Norasingha, dan Thep Norasingha adalah tiga nama "sphinx" di Thailand; digambarkan berjalan tegak, berbadan bawah singa atau rusa dan berbadan atas manusia.
statement.en: Nora Nair, Norasingha, and Thep Norasingha are three names of the "sphinx" in Thailand; they are depicted walking upright, with the lower body of a lion or deer and the upper body of a human.

claims.quote: While the date of its construction is not known for certain, the consensus among Egyptologists is that the head of the Great Sphinx bears the likeness of the pharaoh Khafre, dating it to between 2600 and 2500 BC.

statement.id: Meski waktu pembangunannya tidak pasti, konsensus para Egiptolog adalah bahwa kepala Sphinx Agung menyerupai firaun Khafre dan berasal dari antara 2600 dan 2500 SM.
statement.en: Although the date of construction is uncertain, the consensus among Egyptologists is that the head of the Great Sphinx bears the likeness of the pharaoh Khafre, dating it to between 2600 and 2500 BC.

claims.quote: The exact date when the first sphinx appeared is not known and the most famous sphinx of all, the Great Sphinx of Giza, has not been precisely dated; some scholars date it as far back as the reign of Cheops, ca 2500 BCE.

statement.id: Waktu kemunculan sphinx pertama tidak diketahui dan Sphinx Agung Giza belum bisa ditentukan umurnya secara tepat; sebagian sarjana menempatkannya sejak masa Cheops, sekitar 2500 SM.
statement.en: The date of the first sphinx is unknown and the Great Sphinx of Giza has not been precisely dated; some scholars date it as far back as the reign of Cheops, ca 2500 BCE.

claims.quote: In contrast to the Egyptians, the ancient Greeks saw the sphinx as a more troublesome creature.

statement.id: Berbeda dari bangsa Mesir, bangsa Yunani kuno memandang sphinx sebagai makhluk yang lebih merepotkan.
statement.en: In contrast to the Egyptians, the ancient Greeks saw the sphinx as a more troublesome creature.

claims.quote: From the 6th century BCE, the Greek sphinx appeared in stone sculpture, sometimes with raised hind quarters.

statement.id: Sejak abad ke-6 SM, sphinx Yunani muncul dalam pahatan batu, kadang dengan bagian belakang tubuh terangkat.
statement.en: From the 6th century BCE the Greek sphinx appeared in stone sculpture, sometimes with raised hind quarters.

claims.quote: In the Boeotian dialect the name was phix (Hes. Theog. 326), whence the name of the Boeotian mountain, Phikion oros.

statement.id: Dalam dialek Boiotia, namanya adalah phix, dan dari situlah nama gunung Boiotia, Phikion oros.
statement.en: In the Boeotian dialect the name was phix, whence the name of the Boeotian mountain Phikion oros.

claims.quote: However, the historian Susan Wise Bauer suggests that the word "sphinx" was instead a Greek corruption of the Egyptian name "shesepankh", which meant "living image"

statement.id: Sejarawan Susan Wise Bauer mengusulkan bahwa kata "sphinx" justru merupakan perubahan Yunani dari nama Mesir "shesepankh" yang berarti "citra hidup".
statement.en: The historian Susan Wise Bauer suggests the word "sphinx" was instead a Greek corruption of the Egyptian name "shesepankh", meaning "living image".

summary.en: Hesiod: daughter of Orthos/Orthrus and Khimaira (one source says the mother could be the Chimera, Echidna, or Ceto).

text.id: kepanikan vampir abad ke-18 di Eropa; rujukan makhluk serupa jauh lebih tua
text.en: 18th-century vampire panics in Europe; similar beings are referenced far earlier

short_description.id: Vampir adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Eropa berwujud orang mati yang diyakini keluar pada malam hari untuk mengisap darah manusia hidup.
short_description.en: A vampire is a European folkloric undead being believed to leave the grave at night and drink living people's blood.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa, vampir digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip manusia yang hidup kembali dan mengambil darah manusia. Sebuah ensiklopedia lama menyatakan bahwa ia umumnya dianggap jiwa orang mati yang meninggalkan jasad terkubur pada malam hari untuk mengisap darah orang hidup, sehingga jasadnya ditemukan segar dan kemerahan. Vampir folklor mengenakan kain kafan, sering digambarkan kembung dengan wajah kemerahan atau gelap, dan pada umumnya tidak bertaring.
long_description.en: In European folklore, the vampire is a humanlike revenant said to draw blood from living people. An older encyclopedia says it is usually supposed to be the soul of a dead man leaving the buried body by night to suck the blood of the living, so that the corpse is found fresh and rosy. Folkloric vampires wear shrouds, are often described as bloated with ruddy or dark countenance, and in general were not fanged.

long_description.id: Menurut sumber-sumber ini, penyihir, korban bunuh diri, dan mereka yang mati secara kekerasan umumnya menjadi vampir, dan siapa pun dapat menjadi vampir bila hewan melompati jasadnya. Kehadiran vampir dikenali dari kematian ternak, kerabat, atau tetangga serta gangguan ala poltergeist, dan ia dipercaya lebih aktif pada malam hari tetapi tidak umumnya rentan terhadap sinar matahari. Sebagian tradisi menyatakan vampir tak dapat memasuki rumah tanpa diundang, tak dapat menyeberangi air mengalir, atau tak dapat berjalan di tanah yang disucikan.
long_description.en: According to these sources, witches, suicides, and those who met a violent end generally became vampires, and anyone could become one if an animal leaped over the corpse. A vampire's presence was recognized by deaths of cattle, relatives, or neighbours and by poltergeist-styled disturbances, and it was believed more active at night but not generally vulnerable to sunlight. Some traditions state that a vampire cannot enter a house uninvited, cross running water, or walk on consecrated ground.

long_description.id: Untuk menghentikan vampir, jasad ditusuk pasak, kepalanya dipenggal, atau jantungnya dicabut dan tubuhnya dibakar; pasak adalah cara yang paling sering disebut dan pemenggalan disukai di wilayah Jerman dan Slavia barat. Penangkalnya mencakup bawang putih, mawar liar, hawthorn, biji sawi, dan benda suci, serta menaburkan biji agar vampir sibuk menghitung; orang Romani menancapkan jarum besi atau baja ke jantung jenazah. Kajian makam di Polandia menemukan beberapa jasad yang diberi sabit atau batu, yang ditafsirkan sebagai usaha mencegahnya kembali dari kubur.
long_description.en: To stop a vampire the corpse was staked, beheaded, or had its heart torn out and the body burned; staking was the most commonly cited method and decapitation was preferred in German and western Slavic areas. Protections included garlic, wild rose, hawthorn, mustard seeds, and sacred items, and scattering seeds so the vampire would be busy counting; The Romani pushed steel or iron needles through a corpse's heart. A study of Polish burials found bodies furnished with sickles or stones, interpreted as attempts to keep them in the grave.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan ini terutama berkembang di negeri-negeri Slavia dan sangat marak di Hungaria antara 1730 dan 1735. Gelombang kepanikan abad ke-18 dimulai di Prusia Timur pada 1721 lalu di Monarki Habsburg pada 1725 hingga 1734, dan ketakutan akan vampir sering dikaitkan dengan kematian beruntun akibat penyakit menular. Varian lokal di Eropa Tenggara mencakup shtriga di Albania, vrykolakas di Yunani, dan strigoi di Rumania.
long_description.en: The belief chiefly flourished in Slavonic lands and became especially prevalent in Hungary between 1730 and 1735. The 18th-century wave of panic started in East Prussia in 1721, then reached the Habsburg monarchy between 1725 and 1734, and fear of vampires was often linked to clusters of deaths from contagious disease. Local variants in Southeastern Europe include shtriga in Albania, vrykolakas in Greece, and strigoi in Romania.

long_description.id: Vampir fiksi modern yang karismatik lahir pada 1819 lewat The Vampyre karya John Polidori, dan novel Dracula karya Bram Stoker terbit pada 1897 dan memengaruhi citra vampir. Sumber juga mencatat bahwa vampir modern yang kurus dan pucat berasal dari awal abad ke-19, berbeda dengan vampir folklor.
long_description.en: The charismatic vampire of modern fiction was born in 1819 with John Polidori's The Vampyre, and Bram Stoker's Dracula appeared in 1897 and influenced the vampire image. The sources also note that the modern gaunt, pale vampire dates from the early 19th century, in contrast to the folkloric vampire.

cultural_context.id: Kepanikan vampir biasanya diawali kematian seseorang, sering karena penyakit menular, yang disusul kematian orang lain di sekitarnya. Pada Abad Pertengahan Gereja-Gereja Kristen menafsirkan ulang vampir menjadi antek Setan.
cultural_context.en: Vampire scares typically started with one death, often from a contagious illness, followed by deaths among neighbours. In the Middle Ages the Christian Churches reinterpreted vampires as minions of Satan.

summary.id: Kepanikan bermula dari dugaan serangan vampir di Prusia Timur pada 1721 dan di Monarki Habsburg pada 1725 hingga 1734, lalu menyebar ke tempat lain. Di Austria, kontroversi berakhir ketika Permaisuri Maria Theresa mengutus dokter pribadinya, Gerard van Swieten, yang menyimpulkan vampir tidak ada; sang permaisuri melarang pembukaan makam dan penodaan jenazah.
summary.en: Supposed vampire attacks first stirred panic in East Prussia in 1721 and then in the Habsburg monarchy between 1725 and 1734, spreading elsewhere. claims.quote: In European folklore, vampires are undead humanoid creatures that visit loved ones and cause mischief or deaths in the neighbourhoods they inhabited while they were alive.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa vampir adalah makhluk mirip manusia yang hidup kembali.
statement.en: In European folklore vampires are undead humanlike creatures.

claims.quote: In the first-mentioned meaning a vampire is usually supposed to be the soul of a dead man which quits the buried body by night to suck the blood of living persons.

statement.id: Vampir diyakini keluar dari kubur malam hari dan mengisap darah orang hidup.
statement.en: A vampire was believed to leave the grave at night to drink living people's blood.

claims.quote: To put a stop to his ravages, a stake is driven through the -corpse, or the head cut off, or the heart torn out and the body burned

statement.id: Untuk menghentikan kerusakan yang ditimbulkan vampir, pasak ditancapkan ke jasadnya, kepalanya dipenggal, atau jantungnya dicabut dan tubuhnya dibakar.
statement.en: To put a stop to a vampire's ravages, a stake is driven through the corpse, the head cut off, or the heart torn out and the body burned.

claims.quote: They all had either sickles placed across their neck or body or large rocks stacked under their chin

statement.id: Makam di Polandia ditemukan dengan sabit atau batu yang ditaruh di tubuh jasad.
statement.en: Polish burials had sickles or stones placed on the bodies.

claims.quote: vampire scares usually began when a person died – often of a contagious disease, and in New England almost always of tuberculosis – and others in the vicinity began dying

statement.id: Kepanikan vampir sering mengikuti kematian akibat penyakit menular dan kematian beruntun.
statement.en: Vampire scares often followed contagious deaths and further deaths nearby.

claims.quote: the pre-eminent vampire novel in history: Dracula by Bram Stoker, published in 1897.

statement.id: Novel Dracula karya Bram Stoker diterbitkan pada tahun 1897 dan berpengaruh pada citra vampir.
statement.en: Bram Stoker's Dracula appeared in 1897 and influenced the vampire image.

claims.quote: Vampires were usually reported as bloated in appearance, and ruddy, purplish, or dark in colour; these characteristics were often attributed to the recent drinking of blood
claims.locator: Folk beliefs, Description and common attributes

statement.id: Vampir biasanya dilaporkan berperut kembung dengan warna kemerahan, keunguan, atau gelap, yang sering dianggap akibat darah yang baru diminum.
statement.en: Vampires were usually reported as bloated and ruddy, purplish, or dark in colour, characteristics often attributed to the recent drinking of blood.

claims.quote: It would be clad in the linen shroud it was buried in, and its teeth, hair, and nails may have grown somewhat, though in general fangs were not a feature.
claims.locator: Folk beliefs, Description and common attributes

statement.id: Vampir dikatakan mengenakan kain kafan linen tempat ia dikubur; gigi, rambut, dan kukunya mungkin tumbuh sedikit, tetapi pada umumnya taring bukan cirinya.
statement.en: The vampire would be clad in the linen shroud it was buried in, and its teeth, hair, and nails may have grown somewhat, though in general fangs were not a feature.

claims.quote: Corpses thought to be vampires were generally described as having a healthier appearance than expected, plump and showing little or no signs of decomposition.

statement.id: Jasad yang diduga vampir umumnya digambarkan tampak lebih sehat dari perkiraan, gemuk, dan hanya sedikit atau tanpa tanda pembusukan.
statement.en: Corpses thought to be vampires were generally described as healthier-looking than expected, plump, with little or no sign of decomposition.

claims.quote: Evidence that a vampire was active in a given locality included death of cattle, sheep, relatives or neighbours. Folkloric vampires could also make their presence felt by engaging in minor poltergeist-styled activity, such as hurling stones on roofs or moving household objects, and pressing on people in their sleep.

statement.id: Tanda vampir aktif di suatu tempat mencakup kematian ternak, kerabat, atau tetangga; vampir dalam cerita rakyat juga dapat membuat kehadirannya terasa lewat gangguan ala poltergeist, seperti melempar batu ke atap, menggeser perabot, dan menindih orang yang tidur.
statement.en: Signs of vampire activity included the death of cattle, sheep, relatives, or neighbours; folkloric vampires could also make their presence felt through poltergeist-styled activity such as hurling stones on roofs, moving household objects, and pressing on sleepers.

claims.quote: Garlic is a common example; a branch of wild rose and hawthorn are sometimes associated with causing harm to vampires, and in Europe, mustard seeds would be sprinkled on the roof of a house to keep them away. Other apotropaics include sacred items, such as crucifix, rosary, or holy water.

statement.id: Bawang putih adalah contoh penangkal yang umum; ranting mawar liar dan hawthorn kadang dikaitkan dengan melukai vampir, dan di Eropa biji sawi ditaburkan di atap rumah untuk menjauhkannya; penangkal lain mencakup salib, rosario, dan air suci.
statement.en: Garlic is a common apotropaic; wild rose and hawthorn branches are sometimes associated with harming vampires, and in Europe mustard seeds were sprinkled on roofs to keep them away; other apotropaics include crucifix, rosary, and holy water.

claims.quote: Some folklore also states that vampires are unable to walk on consecrated ground, such as that of churches or temples, or cross running water.

statement.id: Sebagian cerita rakyat menyatakan vampir tidak dapat berjalan di tanah yang disucikan, seperti gereja atau kuil, atau menyeberangi air mengalir.
statement.en: Some folklore states that vampires cannot walk on consecrated ground, such as that of churches or temples, or cross running water.

claims.quote: Some traditions also hold that a vampire cannot enter a house unless invited by the owner; after the first invitation they can come and go as they please. Though folkloric vampires were believed to be more active at night, they were not generally considered vulnerable to sunlight.

statement.id: Sebagian tradisi menyatakan vampir tak dapat memasuki rumah tanpa diundang pemiliknya; vampir dalam cerita rakyat dipercaya lebih aktif pada malam hari tetapi umumnya tidak dianggap rentan terhadap sinar matahari.
statement.en: Some traditions hold that a vampire cannot enter a house unless invited; folkloric vampires were believed more active at night but were not generally considered vulnerable to sunlight.

claims.quote: Methods of destroying suspected vampires varied, with staking the most commonly cited method, particularly in South Slavic cultures.

statement.id: Cara membinasakan tersangka vampir beragam, dengan penusukan pasak sebagai cara yang paling sering disebut, terutama dalam budaya Slavia Selatan.
statement.en: Methods of destroying suspected vampires varied, with staking the most commonly cited, particularly in South Slavic cultures.

claims.quote: Decapitation was the preferred method in German and western Slavic areas, with the head buried between the feet, behind the buttocks or away from the body.

statement.id: Pemenggalan kepala menjadi cara yang disukai di wilayah Jerman dan Slavia barat, dengan kepala dikubur di antara kaki, di belakang bokong, atau jauh dari tubuh.
statement.en: Decapitation was the preferred method in German and western Slavic areas, with the head buried between the feet, behind the buttocks, or away from the body.

claims.quote: Other methods commonly practised in Europe included severing the tendons at the knees or placing poppy seeds, millet, or sand on the ground at the grave site of a presumed vampire; this was intended to keep the vampire occupied all night by counting the fallen grains

statement.id: Cara lain yang lazim di Eropa mencakup memotong urat lutut atau menaburkan biji poppy, millet, atau pasir di kuburan tersangka vampir agar ia sibuk menghitung butiran sepanjang malam.
statement.en: Other common European methods included severing the tendons at the knees or scattering poppy seeds, millet, or sand at a presumed vampire's grave to keep it busy all night counting the grains.

claims.quote: Burying a corpse upside-down was widespread, as was placing earthly objects, such as scythes or sickles, near the grave to satisfy any demons entering the body or to appease the dead so that it would not wish to arise from its coffin.

statement.id: Menguburkan jenazah dengan posisi terbalik lazim, begitu pula menaruh benda seperti arit atau sabit di dekat makam untuk memuaskan setan yang memasuki jasad atau menenangkan orang mati agar tak ingin bangkit dari peti.
statement.en: Burying a corpse upside-down was widespread, as was placing objects such as scythes or sickles near the grave to satisfy any demons entering the body or to appease the dead so it would not wish to rise from its coffin.

claims.quote: Romani people drove steel or iron needles into a corpse's heart and placed bits of steel in the mouth, over the eyes, ears and between the fingers at the time of burial.

statement.id: Orang Romani menancapkan jarum baja atau besi ke jantung jenazah dan menaruh potongan baja di mulut, di atas mata, telinga, dan di sela jari saat penguburan.
statement.en: Romani people drove steel or iron needles into a corpse's heart and placed bits of steel in the mouth, over the eyes, ears, and between the fingers at burial.

claims.quote: In most cases, vampires are revenants of evil beings, suicide victims, or witches, but they can also be created by a malevolent spirit possessing a corpse or by being bitten by a vampire.

statement.id: Pada umumnya vampir adalah arwah yang kembali dari makhluk jahat, korban bunuh diri, atau penyihir, tetapi vampir juga dapat tercipta lewat roh jahat yang merasuki jasad atau lewat gigitan vampir.
statement.en: In most cases vampires are revenants of evil beings, suicide victims, or witches, but they can also be created by a malevolent spirit possessing a corpse or by a vampire's bite.

claims.quote: Local variants in Southeastern Europe were also known by different names, such as shtriga in Albania, vrykolakas in Greece and strigoi in Romania, cognate with Italian strega, meaning 'witch'.

statement.en: Local variants in Southeastern Europe were known by different names, such as shtriga in Albania, vrykolakas in Greece, and strigoi in Romania.
