short_description.id: Pegasus adalah kuda bersayap abadi dalam mitologi Yunani yang lahir dari leher Medusa dan menjadi tunggangan Bellerophon serta pembawa petir Zeus.
short_description.en: Pegasus is the immortal winged horse of Greek mythology, born from Medusa's neck, ridden by Bellerophon and later bearer of Zeus's thunderbolts.

long_description.id: Pegasus adalah kuda bersayap abadi dalam mitologi Yunani. Ia dikisahkan lahir dari leher Medusa ketika Perseus memenggalnya, dan menurut sumber ia dilahirkan bersama Chrysaor. Poseidon disebut sebagai ayahnya, meski Theoi juga mencatat tradisi yang hanya menyebut Medusa.
long_description.en: Pegasus is the immortal winged horse of Greek mythology. He is said to have been born from Medusa's neck when Perseus beheaded her, and according to the source he was born together with Chrysaor. Poseidon is named as his father, although Theoi also records a tradition naming only Medusa.

long_description.id: Bellerophon mendapatkan Pegasus dan, dengan bantuan Athena, menjinakkannya, lalu menungganginya dalam pertempuran melawan Chimaera. Kisah tentang cara Bellerophon memperolehnya berbeda-beda: ada yang menyebut kekang emas dari Athena, ada yang menyebut Athena sendiri yang menjinakkannya, dan ada yang menyebut Poseidon memberikannya kepada putranya. Setelah itu Bellerophon mencoba terbang menuju para dewa, tetapi Pegasus melemparkannya.
long_description.en: Bellerophon obtained Pegasus and, with Athena's help, tamed him and rode him against the Chimaera. Accounts of how Bellerophon acquired him differ: some mention a golden bridle from Athena, some say Athena herself tamed him, and some say Poseidon gave him to his son. Afterwards Bellerophon tried to fly toward the gods, but Pegasus threw him.

long_description.id: Pegasus melanjutkan perjalanan ke Olympos. Menurut satu tradisi ia menjadi pembawa petir Zeus dan, dalam tradisi lain, diserahkan kepada Eos. Ia juga dikreditkan dengan menciptakan mata air lewat hentakan kukunya, yang paling terkenal adalah Hippocrene di Gunung Helicon, dan dikenang sebagai rasi bintang.
long_description.en: Pegasus went on to Olympos. According to one tradition he became Zeus's thunderbolt-bearer, and in another he was given to Eos. He is also credited with creating springs with a stamp of his hoof, the most famous being Hippocrene on Mount Helicon, and he was commemorated as a constellation.

long_description.id: Gambar Pegasus muncul pada tembikar Yunani dan koin, dan salah satu penggambaran pahatnya yang terkenal berasal dari sebuah pedimen kuil. Dalam seni Romawi, kuda itu menjadi lambang keabadian. Pada 1941, siluet Bellerophon di atas Pegasus dipakai sebagai lambang pasukan penerjun payung United Kingdom.
long_description.en: Pegasus appears on Greek pottery and coins, and one famous sculptural depiction comes from a temple pediment. In Roman art the horse became a symbol of immortality. In 1941 a silhouette of Bellerophon on Pegasus was adopted as the insignia of the United Kingdom's parachute troops.

cultural_context.id: Menurut Theoi, terbitnya rasi bintang Pegasus menandai datangnya musim semi dan, di Yunani, badai petir musiman. Sumber yang sama mencatat bahwa gagasan Pegasus sebagai kuda para Muse lebih terkenal di zaman modern daripada di zaman kuno.
cultural_context.en: According to Theoi, the rising of the Pegasus constellation marks the arrival of spring and, in Greece, of seasonal thunderstorms. The same source notes that Pegasus as the horse of the Muses is more celebrated in modern times than in antiquity.

literal_meaning.id: Menurut Theoi berarti 'dari mata air' atau 'memancar keluar'; usulan lain mengaitkannya dengan kata Luwian untuk 'kilat'.
literal_meaning.en: According to Theoi it means 'of the spring' or 'sprung forth'; another proposal links it to a Luwian word for 'lightning'.

who.id: Pegasus adalah kuda bersayap abadi dari mitologi Yunani.
who.en: Pegasus is an immortal winged horse of Greek mythology.

origin.id: Ia dikisahkan lahir dari leher Medusa yang dipenggal Perseus.
origin.en: He is said to have sprung from the neck of Medusa after Perseus beheaded her.

role.id: Ia menjadi tunggangan Bellerophon melawan Chimaera dan kemudian pembawa petir Zeus.
role.en: He served as Bellerophon's mount against the Chimaera and later as bearer of Zeus's thunderbolts.

famous_for.id: Pegasus paling dikenal sebagai kuda bersayap yang menciptakan mata air dengan hentakan kukunya.
famous_for.en: Pegasus is best known as the winged horse who made springs with a stamp of his hoof.

did_you_know.id: Menurut Theoi, gagasan Pegasus sebagai kuda para Muse lebih terkenal di zaman modern daripada di zaman kuno, sebab bagi orang kuno hubungannya dengan para Muse hanya lewat Hippocrene.
did_you_know.en: According to Theoi, Pegasus as the horse of the Muses is better known in modern times than in antiquity, since for the ancients his only link to the Muses was Hippocrene.

description.id: Bellerophon menunggangi dan menerbangkan Pegasus; Pegasos juga terbang ke Olympos.
description.en: Bellerophon rode and flew Pegasus, and Pegasos flew on to Olympos.

description.id: Pegasos disebut kuda bersayap yang abadi.
description.en: Pegasos is described as an immortal winged horse.

description.id: Menurut Hesiod dalam Theogony, Pegasus membawakan petir dan kilat kepada Zeus kapan pun diperlukan.
description.en: According to Hesiod's Theogony, Pegasus brought Zeus his thunder and lightning whenever needed.

description.id: Pegasus dikreditkan menciptakan sejumlah mata air dengan hentakan kukunya, termasuk Hippocrene.
description.en: Pegasus is credited with creating a number of springs with a stamp of his hoof, including Hippocrene.

role.id: Pegasus lahir dari leher Medusa.
role.en: Pegasus is born from Medusa's neck.

summary.id: Ketika Perseus memenggal kepala Medusa, Pegasos dan Khrysaor melompat dari darah atau tubuhnya. Hesiod menyatakan Pegasos dinamai dari mata air Okeanos tempat ia lahir.
summary.en: When Perseus beheaded Medusa, Pegasos and Khrysaor sprang from her blood or body. Hesiod says Pegasos was named after the springs of Okeanos where he was born.

role.id: Pegasus membantu Bellerophon membunuh Chimaera.
role.en: Pegasus helps Bellerophon kill the Chimaera.

summary.id: Dengan bantuan Athena, Bellerophon menjinakkan Pegasus dan menunggangi serta menerbangkannya untuk membunuh Chimaera dengan tombaknya. Hesiod menyatakan Khimaira dibunuh oleh Pegasos dan Bellerophon.
summary.en: With Athena's help, Bellerophon tamed Pegasus and rode and flew him to kill the Chimaera with his spear. Hesiod states that Khimaira was killed by Pegasos and Bellerophon.

role.id: Pegasus melempar Bellerophon yang hendak terbang ke tempat para dewa.
role.en: Pegasus throws Bellerophon, who tried to fly to the gods.

summary.id: Karena menyangka bisa terbang cukup tinggi untuk bergabung dengan para dewa, Bellerophon dilempar Pegasus dan jatuh ke bumi, sedangkan Pegasus terus terbang ke Gunung Olympus. Sumber lain menyebut Zeus yang membuat kuda itu meronta, atau lalat pengganggu kiriman Zeus yang membuatnya murka.
summary.en: Thinking he could fly high enough to join the gods, Bellerophon was thrown by Pegasus and fell to earth, while Pegasus kept on flying to Mount Olympus. Other sources say Zeus made the horse buck, or that a gad-fly sent by Zeus enraged him.

role.id: Hentakan kuku Pegasus memunculkan mata air.
role.en: Pegasus's hoofstamp brings forth a spring.

summary.id: Pegasus dikreditkan menciptakan mata air Hippocrene di Gunung Helicon. Antoninus Liberalis menyebut ia menghentak puncak gunung itu atas kehendak Poseidon agar gunung tidak terus membengkak, sedangkan Pausanias menyebutnya dibuat oleh kuku kuda Bellerophon.
summary.en: Pegasus is credited with creating the Hippocrene spring on Mount Helicon. Antoninus Liberalis says he struck the mountain's summit by Poseidon's will to stop it swelling, while Pausanias says it was made by the hoof of Bellerophon's horse.

description.id: Tempat mata air Hippocrene, dekat hutan suci para Muse.
description.en: Site of the Hippocrene spring, close to the grove sacred to the Muses.

description.id: Tempat mata air lain yang dikaitkan dengan hentakan kuku Pegasus.
description.en: Site of another spring credited to Pegasus's hoofstamp.

description.id: Dalam sebagian kisah, tempat Bellerophon menemukan Pegasus, dekat Corinth.
description.en: In some accounts, where Bellerophon found Pegasus, near Corinth.

description.id: Tujuan Pegasus setelah Bellerophon jatuh.
description.en: Where Pegasus went after Bellerophon fell.

description.id: Pedimennya memuat penggambaran Pegasus yang terkenal dalam seni pahat.
description.en: Its pediment carries a famous sculptural depiction of Pegasus.

timeline.period: Greek epic C8th or C7th B.C.

description.id: Theoi menggolongkan Theogony Hesiod, yang memuat kisah kelahiran Pegasos, sebagai epos Yunani abad ke-8 atau ke-7 SM.
description.en: Theoi classes Hesiod's Theogony, with its account of Pegasos's birth, as Greek epic of the 8th or 7th century BCE.

description.id: Pegasus muncul pada tembikar Yunani, yang paling awal berupa tembikar Corinthian abad ke-7 SM.
description.en: Pegasus appears on Greek pottery, the earliest being Corinthian wares of the 7th century BCE.

title.en: Pediment of the Temple of Artemis on Corcyra

description.id: Penggambaran Pegasus yang terkenal dalam seni pahat.
description.en: A famous sculptural depiction of Pegasus.

description.id: Pegasus menjadi desain populer pada koin, khususnya dari Corinth sejak abad ke-6 SM.
description.en: Pegasus was a popular coin design, in particular from Corinth from the 6th century BCE.

description.id: Benvenuto Cellini memasukkan Pegasus pada koin yang dibuat untuk menghormati Kardinal Pietro Bembo; sejak itu Pegasus menjadi simbol Toskana.
description.en: Benvenuto Cellini included Pegasus on a coin made to honor Cardinal Pietro Bembo; Pegasus has been a symbol of Tuscany since.

note.id: Pegasus muncul setelah Medusa dipenggal.
note.en: Pegasus emerged after Medusa was beheaded.

note.id: Menurut sumber, Poseidon adalah ayah Pegasus.
note.en: According to the sources, Poseidon is Pegasus's father.

note.id: Lahir pada saat yang sama dan dengan cara yang sama.
note.en: Born at the same time and in the same way.

note.id: Pahlawan yang menjinakkan dan menunggangi Pegasus.
note.en: The hero who tamed and rode Pegasus.

note.id: Pegasus dan Bellerophon membunuh Chimaera.

note.en: Athena helped Bellerophon tame Pegasus.

note.id: Dalam satu tradisi Pegasus diserahkan kepada Eos.
note.en: In one tradition Pegasus was given to Eos.

description.en: A silhouette of Bellerophon on the winged Pegasus was adopted in 1941 as the upper-sleeve insignia of the United Kingdom's parachute troops.

traditional.id: Bagi orang kuno, hubungan Pegasus dengan para Muse hanya lewat Hippocrene yang muncul dari hentakan kukunya.
traditional.en: For the ancients, Pegasus's link to the Muses was only the Hippocrene well that his hoof called forth.

modern.id: Pegasus dianggap kuda para Muse, dan peran ini lebih terkenal di zaman modern daripada di zaman kuno.
modern.en: Pegasus is regarded as the horse of the Muses, a role more celebrated in modern times than in antiquity.

learning_questions.en: Why has Pegasus been used again and again in art and emblems from antiquity to modern times?

sources.title: Pegasus: The Winged Horse of Greek Mythology
sources.author: Mark Cartwright

sources.title: PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claims.quote: Pegasus (or Pegasos) is a winged-horse from Greek mythology which was fathered by Poseidon and was born from the severed neck of the gorgon Medusa, slain by Perseus.

statement.id: Pegasus adalah kuda bersayap mitologi Yunani, putra Poseidon yang muncul ketika Perseus memenggal Medusa.
statement.en: Pegasus is a winged horse of Greek mythology, fathered by Poseidon and born when Perseus beheaded Medusa.

claims.quote: PEGASOS (Pegasus) was an immortal, winged horse which sprang from the neck of the beheaded Gorgon Medousa (Medusa).

statement.id: Pegasus adalah kuda bersayap abadi yang muncul dari leher Medusa.
statement.en: Pegasus is an immortal winged horse that emerged from Medusa's neck.

claims.quote: Taming the horse with the help of Athena, Bellerophon rode (and flew) Pegasus and managed to kill the monstrous Chimaera with his spear.

statement.id: Bellerophon menjinakkan Pegasus dengan bantuan Athena dan menungganginya untuk mengalahkan Chimaera.
statement.en: With Athena's help, Bellerophon tamed Pegasus and rode him against the Chimaera.

claims.quote: However, becoming rather boastful and thinking he could fly high enough on his winged steed to take his place amongst the immortal gods, Bellerophon was thrown by Pegasus and fell unceremoniously back to earth.

statement.id: Pegasus menjatuhkan Bellerophon ketika sang pahlawan mencoba terbang ke tempat para dewa.
statement.en: Pegasus threw Bellerophon when the hero tried to fly to the gods.

claims.quote: According to Hesiod in his Theogony, Pegasus also brought Zeus his thunder and lightning whenever needed.

statement.id: Dalam Theogony karya Hesiod, Pegasus membawa petir untuk Zeus.
statement.en: In Hesiod's Theogony, Pegasus brought thunder and lightning to Zeus.

claims.quote: Pegasus is also credited with creating a number of springs with a stamp of his hoof. Most famous of these were the Hippocrene spring on Mt. Helicon

statement.id: Hentakan kaki Pegasus dipercaya menciptakan mata air Hippocrene di Gunung Helicon.
statement.en: Pegasus's hoofstamp was credited with creating the Hippocrene spring on Mount Helicon.

claims.quote: Pegasos was commemorated amongst the stars as the constellation of the same name.

statement.id: Pegasus dikenang sebagai rasi bintang yang memakai namanya.
statement.en: Pegasus was commemorated as the constellation of the same name.

claims.quote: Pegasus appeared on Greek pottery, the earliest being Corinthian wares from the 7th century BCE. Pegasus was also a popular design on coins, in particular from Corinth from the 6th century BCE.

statement.id: Pegasus muncul pada tembikar dan koin Yunani kuno.
statement.en: Pegasus appeared on ancient Greek pottery and coins.

claims.quote: At the same time and in the same way, Chryasor was also born.

statement.id: Pada saat yang sama dan dengan cara yang sama, Chrysaor (ditulis Chryasor dalam sumber) juga lahir.
statement.en: At the same time and in the same way, Chrysaor (spelled Chryasor in the source) was also born.

claims.quote: Poseidon gave Pegasus to his son Bellerophon who put Pegasus to good use in his famous battle with the Chimaera.

statement.id: Poseidon memberikan Pegasus kepada putranya, Bellerophon, yang memanfaatkannya dalam pertempuran terkenal melawan Chimaera.
statement.en: Poseidon gave Pegasus to his son Bellerophon, who put Pegasus to good use in his famous battle with the Chimaera.

claims.quote: To aid him in this task, Bellerophon was fortunate to have at his disposal Pegasus. In some accounts he found the horse at the fountain of Pirene near Corinth, and Hesiod suggests this fact explains the name Pegasus, derived from 'water'- pēgē.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian kisah Bellerophon menemukan kuda itu di mata air Pirene dekat Corinth, dan Hesiod menyiratkan hal ini menjelaskan nama Pegasus, yang diturunkan dari pēgē ('air').
statement.en: In some accounts Bellerophon found the horse at the fountain of Pirene near Corinth, and Hesiod suggests this explains the name Pegasus, derived from pēgē ('water').

claims.quote: Meanwhile, Pegasus kept on going and on reaching Mt. Olympus, he was given to Eos who was responsible for bringing Dawn across the sky each day.

statement.id: Pegasus terus terbang dan setibanya di Gunung Olympus ia diserahkan kepada Eos, yang bertugas membawa fajar melintasi langit setiap hari.
statement.en: Pegasus flew on and, on reaching Mt. Olympus, was given to Eos, who was responsible for bringing Dawn across the sky each day.

claims.quote: A famous representation in sculpture is from the pediment of the Temple of Artemis on Corcyra (c. 580 BCE).

statement.id: Salah satu penggambaran terkenal dalam seni pahat berasal dari pedimen Kuil Artemis di Corcyra (sekitar 580 SM).
statement.en: A famous sculptural representation comes from the pediment of the Temple of Artemis on Corcyra (c. 580 BCE).

claims.quote: The Bellerophon and Pegasus myth was also a popular subject in Roman art - especially engraved semi-precious stone cameos and floor mosaics - where the horse became symbolic of immortality.

statement.id: Mitos Bellerophon dan Pegasus juga populer dalam seni Romawi, terutama kamei batu semimulia dan mozaik lantai, tempat kuda itu menjadi lambang keabadian.
statement.en: The Bellerophon and Pegasus myth was also popular in Roman art, especially engraved semi-precious stone cameos and floor mosaics, where the horse became symbolic of immortality.

claims.quote: Pegasos' name means either "of the spring" from the Greek word ... "sprung forth" from the word ... The first alludes to the steed's connection with various springs, and the latter to its birth from the Gorgon's neck.

statement.id: Menurut Theoi, nama Pegasos berarti 'dari mata air' atau 'memancar keluar'; yang pertama merujuk pada kaitan kuda itu dengan berbagai mata air, yang kedua pada kelahirannya dari leher Gorgon.
statement.en: According to Theoi, Pegasos' name means either 'of the spring' or 'sprung forth'; the first alludes to the steed's link with various springs, the second to its birth from the Gorgon's neck.

claims.quote: Later the hero attempted to fly to heaven but Zeus caused the horse to buck throwing him back down to earth in disgrace. Pegasos winged his way on to Olympos where he became the thunderbolt-bearer of Zeus.

statement.id: Bellerophon kemudian mencoba terbang ke surga, tetapi Zeus membuat kuda itu meronta sehingga sang pahlawan terlempar ke bumi; Pegasos terbang ke Olympos dan menjadi pembawa petir Zeus.
statement.en: Later the hero tried to fly to heaven, but Zeus made the horse buck and throw him back to earth; Pegasos flew on to Olympos and became Zeus's thunderbolt-bearer.

claims.quote: Pegasos was commemorated amongst the stars as the constellation of the same name. Its rising marks the arrival of spring and, in Greece, of seasonal thunderstorms.

statement.id: Terbitnya rasi bintang Pegasus menandai datangnya musim semi dan, di Yunani, badai petir musiman.
statement.en: The rising of the Pegasus constellation marks the arrival of spring and, in Greece, of seasonal thunderstorms.

claims.quote: According to this view, which is apparently the most ancient, Pegasus was the thundering horse of Zeus; but later writers describe him as the horse of Eos

statement.id: Menurut pandangan yang tampaknya paling kuno, Pegasus adalah kuda petir milik Zeus, sedangkan penulis yang lebih belakangan menyebutnya kuda Eos.
statement.en: On the view that seems the most ancient, Pegasus was the thundering horse of Zeus, whereas later writers describe him as the horse of Eos.

claims.quote: The latter advised him to spend a night in the temple of Athena, and, as Bellerophon was sleeping, the goddess appeared to him in a dream, commanding him to sacrifice to Poseidon, and gave him a golden bridle.

statement.id: Menurut salah satu kisah, Athena menampakkan diri kepada Bellerophon dalam mimpi, memerintahkannya berkurban kepada Poseidon, dan memberinya kekang emas.
statement.en: In one account Athena appeared to Bellerophon in a dream, told him to sacrifice to Poseidon, and gave him a golden bridle.

claims.quote: According to some Athena herself tamed and bridled Pegasus, and surrendered him to Bellerophon

statement.id: Menurut sebagian kisah, Athena sendiri yang menjinakkan dan memasang kekang pada Pegasus lalu menyerahkannya kepada Bellerophon.
statement.en: According to some accounts, Athena herself tamed and bridled Pegasus and handed him over to Bellerophon.

claims.quote: After he had conquered the Chimaera ... he endeavoured to rise up to heaven with his winged horse, but fell down upon the earth, either from fear or from giddiness, or being thrown off by Pegasus, who was rendered furious by a gad-fly which Zeus had sent.

statement.id: Setelah menaklukkan Chimaera, ia berusaha naik ke surga dengan kuda bersayapnya tetapi jatuh ke bumi, entah karena takut atau pusing, entah karena dilempar Pegasus yang dibuat murka oleh seekor lalat pengganggu kiriman Zeus.
statement.en: After conquering the Chimaera, he tried to rise to heaven on his winged horse but fell to earth, whether from fear or giddiness or because Pegasus, enraged by a gad-fly Zeus had sent, threw him.

claims.quote: Pegasus lastly was also regarded as the horse of the Muses, and in this capacity he is more celebrated in modern times than he ever was in antiquity ; for with the ancients he had no connection with the Muses, except that by his hoof he called forth the inspiring well Hippocrene.

statement.id: Pegasus belakangan juga dianggap kuda para Muse; dalam peran ini ia lebih terkenal di zaman modern daripada di masa kuno, sebab bagi orang kuno hubungannya dengan para Muse hanya lewat hentakan kukunya yang memunculkan mata air Hippocrene.
statement.en: Pegasus was also later regarded as the horse of the Muses; in this role he is more celebrated in modern times than in antiquity, since for the ancients his only link to the Muses was that his hoof called forth the Hippocrene well.

claims.quote: But when Perseus had cut off the head of Medousa (Medusa) there sprang from her blood stout-hearted Khrysaor (Chrysaor) and the horse Pegasos so named from the springs (pegai) of Okeanos (Oceanus), where he was born.
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: The Birth of Pegasus

statement.id: Hesiod, Theogony: setelah Perseus memenggal kepala Medusa, Khrysaor dan kuda Pegasos melompat dari darahnya; Pegasos dinamai dari mata air (pegai) Okeanos tempat ia lahir.
statement.en: Hesiod, Theogony: when Perseus cut off Medusa's head, Khrysaor and the horse Pegasos sprang from her blood; Pegasos was named after the springs (pegai) of Okeanos where he was born.

claims.quote: Hesiod, Theogony 280 ff (trans. Evelyn-White) (Greek epic C8th or C7th B.C.)
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: The Birth of Pegasus

statement.id: Theoi menggolongkan Theogony karya Hesiod, yang memuat kisah kelahiran Pegasos, sebagai epos Yunani abad ke-8 atau ke-7 SM.
statement.en: Theoi classes Hesiod's Theogony, which contains the account of Pegasos's birth, as Greek epic of the 8th or 7th century BCE.

claims.quote: [1.1] POSEIDON & MEDOUSA (Hesiod Theogony 278, Apollodorus 2.32 & 2.42, Hyginus Fabulae 151 & Astronomica 2.18, Ovid Metamorphoses 4.781 & 6.119)

statement.id: Theoi mencatat Poseidon dan Medousa sebagai orang tua Pegasos menurut Hesiod, Apollodorus, Hyginus, dan Ovid.
statement.en: Theoi lists Poseidon and Medousa as Pegasos's parents according to Hesiod, Apollodorus, Hyginus, and Ovid.

claims.quote: [1.2] MEDOUSA (Pindar Olympian Ode, Nonnus Dionysiaca 24.270)

statement.id: Theoi juga mencatat tradisi (Pindar, Nonnus) yang hanya menyebut Medousa sebagai orang tua Pegasos.
statement.en: Theoi also records a tradition (Pindar, Nonnus) naming only Medousa as Pegasos's parent.

claims.quote: his father [Poseidon] gave him Pegasos who would bear him most swiftly on his wings, and flew unwearying everywhere over the earth
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: Pegasus, Bellerophon & the Chimera

statement.id: Hesiod (Catalogues of Women): ayah Bellerophon, Poseidon, memberinya Pegasos yang membawanya secepat kilat dengan sayapnya dan terbang tak kenal lelah ke mana-mana di bumi.
statement.en: Hesiod (Catalogues of Women): Bellerophon's father Poseidon gave him Pegasos, who bore him swiftly on his wings and flew unwearying everywhere over the earth.

claims.quote: But Khimaira (Chimera) was killed by Pegasos and gallant Bellerophon.
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: Pegasus, Bellerophon & the Chimera

statement.id: Hesiod, Theogony: Khimaira dibunuh oleh Pegasos dan Bellerophon yang gagah berani.
statement.en: Hesiod, Theogony: Khimaira (Chimera) was killed by Pegasos and gallant Bellerophon.

claims.quote: seeking to yoke the snake-haired Gorgo's offspring, Pegasos. Till Pallas [Athena], goddess maid, brought him the bridle and golden headband
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: Pegasus, Bellerophon & the Chimera

statement.id: Pindar: Bellerophon lama berusaha mengekang Pegasos, anak Gorgo berambut ular, sampai Pallas (Athena) membawakan kekang dan ikat kepala emas.
statement.en: Pindar: Bellerophon long strove to yoke Pegasos, the snake-haired Gorgo's offspring, until Pallas (Athena) brought him the bridle and golden headband.

claims.quote: When the Mousai (Muses) sang, heaven, the stars, the sea and rivers stood still, while Mount Helikon (Helicon), beguiled by the pleasure of it all, swelled skyward till, by the will of Poseidon, Pegasos checked it by striking the summit with his hoof.
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: Pegasus & the Spring of Hippocrene

statement.id: Antoninus Liberalis: Gunung Helikon, terpikat kenikmatan nyanyian para Muse, membengkak ke langit sampai Pegasos, atas kehendak Poseidon, menghentikannya dengan menghentak puncaknya.
statement.en: Antoninus Liberalis: Mount Helikon, beguiled by the pleasure of the Muses' song, swelled skyward until Pegasos, by Poseidon's will, checked it by striking the summit with his hoof.

short_description.id: Asclepius adalah dewa pengobatan Yunani, putra Apollo, yang menyembuhkan orang sakit dan bahkan menghidupkan orang mati sebelum dibunuh Zeus; ia dikenali lewat tongkat berlilit ular.
short_description.en: Asclepius is the Greek god of medicine, son of Apollo, who healed the sick and even revived the dead before Zeus killed him; he is recognized by his snake-entwined staff.

long_description.id: Asclepius (Asklepios, juga disebut Aesculapius) adalah dewa pengobatan Yunani yang juga dianggap memiliki daya ramal. Dalam mitos ia putra Apollo; ibunya paling sering disebut Koronis, meski ada versi dengan Arsinoe sebagai ibunya. Ia dibesarkan dan diajar centaur Chiron dan, menurut sumber lain, menerima rahasia pengobatan dari ayahnya. Namanya dikatakan berarti "membelah" karena Apollo membedah rahim ibunya untuk mengambil bayi itu. Satu sumber mencatat bahwa dalam puisi Homeros ia tampaknya hanya manusia, bukan dewa.
long_description.en: Asclepius (Asklepios, also called Aesculapius) is the Greek god of medicine, also credited with powers of prophecy. In myth he is the son of Apollo; his mother is most often named Koronis, though some versions give Arsinoe. He was raised and taught by the centaur Chiron and, according to another source, received the secrets of medicine from his father. His name is said to mean "to cut open" because Apollo cut the child from his mother's womb. One source notes that in the Homeric poems he appears to be merely a human being, not a god.

long_description.id: Keterampilan Asclepius begitu tinggi sehingga ia dapat menghidupkan kembali orang mati. Menurut Apollodorus, ia menerima darah Gorgon dari Athena: sisi kiri untuk membinasakan dan sisi kanan untuk menyelamatkan. Zeus membunuhnya dengan petir karena menganggapnya ancaman bagi pemisahan manusia dan dewa, takut manusia menjadi abadi atau saling menolong, atau, menurut sebagian, karena Pluto mengeluh jumlah orang mati berkurang. Apollo yang murka membunuh para Kiklops dan sendiri dihukum melayani Admetos. Asclepius kemudian didewakan dan menjadi rasi Ophiochus.
long_description.en: Asclepius's skill was so great that he could revive the dead. According to Apollodorus he received the Gorgon's blood from Athena: the left side to destroy and the right side to preserve. Zeus killed him with a thunderbolt, seeing him as a threat to the division between humans and gods, fearing men would become immortal or help one another, or, according to some, because Pluto complained that the number of the dead was shrinking. An angry Apollo slew the Cyclopes and was himself punished by serving Admetos. Asclepius was then deified and became the constellation Ophiochus.

long_description.id: Kuil-kuilnya didirikan di banyak bagian Yunani, dekat mata air penyembuh atau di gunung tinggi. Pusat pemujaannya yang paling terkenal adalah Epidaurus, tempat pasien yang telah menjalani ritus penyucian tidur semalam menunggu mimpi tempat sang dewa menunjukkan obat. Orang yang sembuh mempersembahkan kurban, terutama ayam jantan, dan menggantung lempeng nazar; pasien yang bersyukur juga meninggalkan persembahan yang kadang menggambarkan bagian tubuh yang sembuh. Tempat suci itu dikatakan seperti rumah sakit, dan hutan di sekitarnya melarang kematian dan kelahiran. Kultusnya menyebar ke kota Athena, Pergamon, dan Roma, dan Epidaurus ditutup pada 426 M.
long_description.en: Sanctuaries to him rose across much of Greece, typically beside healing springs or on lofty mountains. His most famous centre was Epidaurus, where patients who had undergone purification rituals slept overnight awaiting dreams in which the god offered remedies. Those who recovered offered sacrifice, especially a cock, and hung up votive tablets; thankful patients also left offerings, sometimes depicting the body part that was cured. The sanctuaries are likened to hospitals, and the grove around Epidaurus forbade death and birth. His cult spread to Athens, Pergamon and Rome, and the Epidaurus sanctuary closed in 426 CE.

long_description.id: Dalam seni, Asclepius digambarkan berjanggut, berjubah himation sederhana, dan memegang tongkat dengan ular suci melilitnya, yang kini menjadi simbol kedokteran. Di Epidaurus, patungnya digambarkan duduk di singgasana dengan tangan bertumpu pada kepala ular dan seekor anjing di sisinya. Ia sering ditemani Hygeia atau Telesphorus, dan kadang ada anjing di kakinya. Ular melambangkan regenerasi dan pembaruan. Keturunannya, Asclepiad, menurunkan ilmu pengobatan, dan dokter paling terkenal di antara mereka adalah Hippocrates.
long_description.en: In art Asclepius is shown bearded, wearing a simple himation, and holding a staff coiled by a sacred snake, which has become the modern symbol of medicine. At Epidaurus his statue showed him enthroned with a hand resting on the head of a serpent and a dog by his side. He is often accompanied by Hygeia or Telesphorus, and sometimes has a dog at his feet. Snakes symbolise regeneration and renovation. His descendants, the Asclepiads, carried on the art of medicine, the most famous of them being Hippocrates.

cultural_context.id: Asclepius adalah dewa pelindung dan leluhur yang dipercaya dari serikat dokter kuno, Asklepiades. Pemujaan Asclepius menyatukan agama dan pengobatan: kuilnya didatangi banyak orang sakit sehingga dapat dibandingkan dengan rumah sakit modern, dan pengetahuan pengobatan dianggap rahasia suci yang diwariskan dalam keluarga Asclepiadae.
cultural_context.en: Asclepius was the patron god and reputed ancestor of the ancient guild of doctors, the Asklepiades. The worship of Asclepius joined religion and medicine: his temples were frequented by many sick people and may be compared to modern hospitals, and medical knowledge was regarded as a sacred secret passed down in the families of the Asclepiadae.

description.en: His ability to raise the dead was seen as a crime against the natural order and a threat to the division between humans and gods, so Zeus killed him with a thunderbolt.

description.id: Pemujaannya dibawa ke Roma pada 293 SM atas perintah kitab Sibylline untuk menolak wabah; sang dewa dibawa dari Epidaurus sebagai ular dan diberi kuil di pulau di Sungai Tiber.

role.id: Putra Apollo yang diselamatkan dari pembakaran ibunya.

summary.id: Dalam satu versi ibunya meninggal saat bersalin dan Apollo membedah rahimnya di atas pembakaran untuk mengambil bayi itu; dari sini ia dinamai "membelah". Versi lain: Koronis meninggalkan bayinya dekat Epidaurus untuk dijaga kambing dan anjing, atau Koronis dibunuh Apollo karena tidak setia, atau ibunya adalah Arsinoe.
summary.en: In one version his mother died in labour and Apollo cut him from her womb on the pyre, hence the name "to cut open". Other versions: Koronis abandoned the baby near Epidaurus to be looked after by a goat and a dog, or Koronis was killed by Apollo for being unfaithful, or his mother was Arsinoe.

role.id: Penyembuh yang menghidupkan orang mati dan dibunuh Zeus.

summary.en: Asclepius received the Gorgon's blood from Athena and could revive the dead. Zeus, afraid men would learn medicine from him, struck him with a thunderbolt; an angry Apollo slew the Cyclopes, and Zeus punished Apollo by making him serve Admetos for a year.

summary.en: Roman tradition holds that in 293 BCE the sacred snake was carried from Epidaurus to the Tiber Island as a cure for a plague; the god came as a snake and was assigned a temple on the island.

description.id: Pusat pemujaan utama Asclepius di Yunani dan pusat penyembuhan penting, tempat festival Asklepieia diadakan tiap empat atau lima tahun menurut sumber; tempat suci itu dikenal sebagai Asklepieion karena ia dipercaya lahir di Gunung Titthion di dekatnya.

statement.id: Asclepius digambarkan berjanggut dengan tongkat berlilit ular, lambang pengobatan modern.
statement.en: Asclepius is depicted bearded with a snake-entwined staff, a modern medical symbol.

claims.quote: The god was fetched from Epidaurus in the form of a snake and a temple assigned him on the island in the Tiber

statement.id: Kultus Asclepius dibawa ke Roma dalam wujud ular dan diberi kuil di Pulau Tiber.
statement.en: His cult was brought to Rome in snake form and given a temple on Tiber Island.

claims.quote: The god had several sanctuaries across Greece; the most famous was at Epidaurus which became an important centre of healing in both ancient Greek and Roman times

statement.id: Epidaurus adalah pusat penyembuhan penting bagi Yunani dan Romawi kuno.
statement.en: Epidaurus was an important healing centre in Greek and Roman times.

claims.quote: ASKLEPIOS (Asclepius) was the god of medicine. He was also the patron god, and reputed ancestor, of the Asklepiades (Asclepiades), the ancient guild of doctors.

statement.id: Asklepios adalah dewa pengobatan, sekaligus dewa pelindung dan leluhur yang dipercaya dari Asklepiades, serikat dokter kuno.
statement.en: Asklepios was the god of medicine and also the patron god and reputed ancestor of the Asklepiades, the ancient guild of doctors.

claims.quote: His mother died in labour and when she was laid out on the pyre, Apollon cut the unborn child from her womb. From this Asklepios received his name which means "to cut open."

statement.id: Ibunya meninggal saat bersalin dan ketika jenazahnya diletakkan di pembakaran, Apollo membedah rahimnya untuk mengambil bayi itu; dari sini Asklepios menerima namanya yang berarti "membelah".
statement.en: His mother died in labour and when she was laid on the pyre Apollo cut the unborn child from her womb; from this Asklepios received his name, which means "to cut open".

claims.quote: He grew so skilled in the craft that he was able to restore the dead to life. This was a crime against the natural order and so Zeus destroyed him with a thunderbolt.

statement.id: Ia begitu terampil sehingga mampu menghidupkan orang mati; ini kejahatan terhadap tatanan alam sehingga Zeus menghancurkannya dengan petir.
statement.en: He grew so skilled that he could restore the dead to life; this was a crime against the natural order, so Zeus destroyed him with a thunderbolt.

claims.quote: After his death Asklepios was placed amongst the stars as the constellation Ophiochus ("the Serpent Holder").

statement.id: Setelah kematiannya Asklepios ditempatkan di antara bintang sebagai rasi Ophiochus ("Pemegang Ular").
statement.en: After his death Asklepios was placed among the stars as the constellation Ophiochus ("the Serpent Holder").

claims.quote: he had received from Athena the blood that had coursed though the Gorgon's veins, the left-side portion of which he used to destroy people, but that on the right he used for their preservation, which is how he could revive those who had died.

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Apollodorus, ia menerima dari Athena darah dari pembuluh Gorgon: bagian sisi kiri dipakai untuk membinasakan orang, sisi kanan untuk menyelamatkan, sehingga ia dapat menghidupkan kembali orang yang mati.
statement.en: According to Apollodorus' summary, he received from Athena the blood from the Gorgon's veins: the left side he used to destroy people, the right to preserve them, which is how he could revive the dead.

claims.quote: Zeus was afraid that men might learn the art of medicine from Asklepios and help each other out, so he hit him with a thunderbolt. This angered Apollon, who slew the Kyklopes (Cyclopes), for they designed the thunderbolt for Zeus.

statement.id: Zeus takut manusia akan belajar ilmu pengobatan dari Asklepios dan saling menolong, maka ia menyambarnya dengan petir; Apollo yang murka membunuh para Kiklops yang merancang petir itu bagi Zeus.
statement.en: Zeus was afraid men might learn medicine from Asklepios and help each other, so he struck him with a thunderbolt; this angered Apollo, who slew the Cyclopes who designed the thunderbolt for Zeus.

claims.quote: These temples were not only places of worship, but were frequented by great numbers of sick persons, and may therefore be compared to modern hospitals.
claims.locator: Asklepios (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Kuil-kuil itu bukan hanya tempat ibadah tetapi juga didatangi banyak orang sakit sehingga dapat dibandingkan dengan rumah sakit modern.
statement.en: These temples were not only places of worship but were frequented by great numbers of sick persons and may therefore be compared to modern hospitals.

claims.quote: The principal seat of his worship in Greece was Epidaurus, where he had a temple surrounded with an extensive grove, within which no one was allowed to die, and no woman to give birth to a child.
claims.locator: Asklepios (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Pusat utama pemujaannya di Yunani adalah Epidaurus, dengan kuil yang dikelilingi hutan luas; di dalamnya tak seorang pun boleh meninggal dan tak seorang perempuan pun boleh melahirkan.
statement.en: The principal seat of his worship in Greece was Epidaurus, where his temple was surrounded by an extensive grove within which no one was allowed to die and no woman to give birth.

claims.quote: Serpents were everywhere connected with the worship of Aesculapius, probably because they were a symbol of prudence and renovation, and were believed to have the power of discovering herbs of wondrous powers
claims.locator: Asklepios (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Ular terkait dengan pemujaan Aesculapius di mana-mana, mungkin karena melambangkan kebijaksanaan dan pembaruan serta dipercaya mampu menemukan ramuan berkhasiat ajaib.
statement.en: Serpents were connected with the worship of Aesculapius everywhere, probably as a symbol of prudence and renovation, and were believed able to discover herbs of wondrous powers.

claims.quote: He was seated on a throne, holding in one hand a staff, and with the other resting upon the head of a dragon (serpent), and by his side lay a dog.
claims.locator: Asklepios (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Di Epidaurus ia digambarkan duduk di singgasana, satu tangan memegang tongkat dan tangan lain bertumpu pada kepala naga (ular), dengan seekor anjing di sisinya.
statement.en: At Epidaurus he was shown seated on a throne, holding a staff in one hand and resting the other on the head of a dragon (serpent), with a dog by his side.

claims.quote: The knowledge of medicine was regarded as a sacred secret, which was transmitted from father to son in the families of the Asclepiadae
claims.locator: Asklepios (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Pengetahuan pengobatan dianggap rahasia suci yang diwariskan dari ayah ke anak dalam keluarga Asclepiadae.
statement.en: Medical knowledge was regarded as a sacred secret transmitted from father to son in the families of the Asclepiadae.

claims.quote: In the Homeric poems Aesculapius does not appear to be considered as a divinity, but merely as a human being
claims.locator: Asklepios (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Dalam puisi-puisi Homeros, Aesculapius tampaknya tidak dianggap dewa, melainkan sekadar manusia.
statement.en: In the Homeric poems Aesculapius does not appear to be considered a divinity, but merely a human being.

claims.quote: Asklepios was depicted as a kindly, bearded man holding a serpent-entwined staff.

statement.id: Asklepios digambarkan sebagai lelaki ramah berjanggut yang memegang tongkat berlilit ular.
statement.en: Asklepios was depicted as a kindly, bearded man holding a serpent-entwined staff.

claims.quote: I begin to sing of Asclepius, son of Apollo and healer of sicknesses.

statement.id: Himne Homerik XVI menyanyikan Asclepius, putra Apollo dan penyembuh penyakit.
statement.en: Homeric Hymn XVI sings of Asclepius, son of Apollo and healer of sicknesses.

claims.quote: In the Dotian plain fair Coronis, daughter of King Phlegyas, bare him, a great joy to men, a soother of cruel pangs.

statement.id: Menurut Himne itu, Koronis, putri Raja Phlegyas, melahirkannya di dataran Dotion; ia sukacita besar bagi manusia dan penenang rasa sakit yang kejam.
statement.en: According to the Hymn, Coronis, daughter of King Phlegyas, bore him in the Dotian plain, a great joy to men and a soother of cruel pangs.

claims.quote: All who were healed offered sacrifice—especially a cock—and hung up votive tablets, on which were recorded their names, their diseases and the manner in which they had been cured.

statement.id: Semua yang sembuh mempersembahkan kurban, terutama ayam jantan, dan menggantungkan lempeng nazar yang mencatat nama, penyakit, dan cara penyembuhan mereka.
statement.en: All who were healed offered sacrifice, especially a cock, and hung up votive tablets recording their names, their diseases and how they had been cured.

claims.quote: the legendary Greek god of medicine, the son of Apollo and the nymph Coronis. Tricca in Thessaly and Epidaurus in Argolis disputed the honour of his birthplace, but an oracle declared in favour of Epidaurus.

statement.id: Aesculapius adalah dewa pengobatan Yunani legendaris, putra Apollo dan nimfa Koronis; Tricca di Thessalia dan Epidaurus di Argolis memperebutkan kehormatan sebagai tempat kelahirannya, tetapi orakel memutuskan Epidaurus.
statement.en: Aesculapius was the legendary Greek god of medicine, son of Apollo and the nymph Coronis; Tricca in Thessaly and Epidaurus in Argolis disputed the honour of his birthplace, but an oracle declared for Epidaurus.

claims.quote: His skill in curing disease and restoring the dead to life aroused the anger of Zeus, who, being afraid that he might render all men immortal, slew him with a thunderbolt

statement.id: Keahliannya menyembuhkan penyakit dan menghidupkan orang mati membangkitkan murka Zeus, yang takut ia akan membuat semua manusia abadi, lalu membunuhnya dengan petir.
statement.en: His skill in curing disease and restoring the dead to life aroused Zeus's anger; fearing he might make all men immortal, Zeus slew him with a thunderbolt.

claims.quote: He is commonly represented standing, dressed in a long cloak, with bare breast; his usual attribute is a club-like staff with a serpent (the symbol of renovation) coiled round it. He is often accompanied by Telesphorus, the boy genius of healing, and his daughter Hygieia, the goddess of health.

statement.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan berdiri berjubah panjang berdada terbuka dengan atribut tongkat bak gada berlilit ular (lambang pembaruan); ia sering ditemani Telesphorus, anak jenius penyembuhan, dan putrinya Hygieia, dewi kesehatan.
statement.en: He is commonly shown standing in a long cloak with bare breast, with a club-like staff coiled by a serpent (symbol of renovation) as his usual attribute; he is often accompanied by Telesphorus, the boy genius of healing, and his daughter Hygieia, goddess of health.

claims.quote: His worship was introduced into Rome by order of the Sibylline books (293 B.C.), to avert a pestilence.

statement.id: Pemujaannya dibawa ke Roma atas perintah kitab Sibylline (293 SM) untuk menolak wabah.
statement.en: His worship was introduced into Rome by order of the Sibylline books (293 B.C.) to avert a pestilence.

claims.quote: Temples were erected to Aesculapius in many parts of Greece, near healing springs or on high mountains.

statement.id: Kuil-kuil untuk Aesculapius didirikan di banyak bagian Yunani, dekat mata air penyembuh atau di gunung-gunung tinggi.
statement.en: Temples to Aesculapius were erected in many parts of Greece, near healing springs or on high mountains.

claims.quote: The practice of sleeping (incubatio) in these sanctuaries was very common, it being supposed that the god effected cures or prescribed remedies to the sick in dreams.

statement.id: Praktik tidur (incubatio) di tempat suci itu sangat umum, karena dianggap sang dewa menyembuhkan atau meresepkan obat bagi orang sakit lewat mimpi.
statement.en: The practice of sleeping (incubatio) in these sanctuaries was very common, it being supposed that the god effected cures or prescribed remedies to the sick in dreams.

claims.quote: The motherless Asclepius was then brought up by his father who gave him the gift of healing and the secrets of medicine using plants and herbs.

statement.id: Asclepius yang kehilangan ibu dibesarkan ayahnya yang memberinya karunia penyembuhan dan rahasia pengobatan dengan tumbuhan dan ramuan.
statement.en: The motherless Asclepius was brought up by his father, who gave him the gift of healing and the secrets of medicine using plants and herbs.

claims.quote: Asclepius had many children - two sons: Machaon and Podaleirios, and four daughters: Iaso, Panacea, Aceso, and Aglaia.

statement.id: Asclepius punya banyak anak: dua putra, Machaon dan Podaleirios, serta empat putri, Iaso, Panacea, Aceso, dan Aglaia.
statement.en: Asclepius had many children: two sons, Machaon and Podaleirios, and four daughters, Iaso, Panacea, Aceso and Aglaia.

claims.quote: This was because the father of the gods saw Asclepius and his art of healing as a threat to the eternal division between humanity and the gods, especially following rumours that Asclepius' healing powers were so formidable that he could even raise the dead

statement.id: Ayah para dewa memandang Asclepius dan seni penyembuhannya sebagai ancaman bagi pemisahan abadi antara manusia dan dewa, terlebih setelah beredar kabar bahwa daya penyembuhannya begitu hebat hingga dapat membangkitkan orang mati.
statement.en: The father of the gods saw Asclepius and his healing art as a threat to the eternal division between humanity and the gods, especially after rumours that his healing powers were so formidable he could even raise the dead.

claims.quote: In some accounts, Koronis abandoned her child near Epidaurus in shame for his illegitimacy and left the baby to be looked after by a goat and a dog. However, in a different version of the story Koronis was killed by Apollo for being unfaithful, whilst, in yet another version, the Messenian Arsinoe was the unfortunate mother of Asclepius.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian versi Koronis meninggalkan bayinya dekat Epidaurus dan bayi itu dijaga seekor kambing dan anjing; versi lain menyebut Koronis dibunuh Apollo karena tidak setia; versi lain lagi menyebut Arsinoe dari Messenia sebagai ibunya.
statement.en: In some accounts Koronis abandoned her child near Epidaurus and the baby was looked after by a goat and a dog; in another Koronis was killed by Apollo for being unfaithful; in yet another the Messenian Arsinoe was his mother.

claims.quote: Epidaurus was also the site of the pan-Hellenic Asklepieia festival, founded in the 5th century BCE and held every four years to celebrate theatre, sport, and music in honour of Asclepius.

statement.id: Epidaurus juga tempat festival Asklepieia se-Yunani yang didirikan pada abad ke-5 SM dan diadakan setiap empat tahun untuk merayakan teater, olahraga, dan musik demi menghormati Asclepius.
statement.en: Epidaurus was also the site of the pan-Hellenic Asklepieia festival, founded in the 5th century BCE and held every four years to celebrate theatre, sport and music in honour of Asclepius.

claims.quote: Another important sanctuary in Asclepius' name was in Athens, situated just below the Acropolis on the western slope. Tradition said that a priest named Telemachos brought the god to the site in the form of a sacred snake in 419 BCE.

statement.id: Tempat suci penting lain untuk Asclepius ada di kota Athena, di lereng barat tepat di bawah Akropolis; menurut tradisi, seorang imam bernama Telemachos membawa sang dewa ke sana dalam wujud ular suci pada 419 SM.
statement.en: Another important sanctuary of Asclepius was in Athens, just below the Acropolis on the western slope; tradition said a priest named Telemachos brought the god there in the form of a sacred snake in 419 BCE.

claims.quote: Finally, in 293 BCE the Romans were said to have taken the sacred snake from Epidaurus to the Tiber Island in order to cure a plague

statement.id: Pada 293 SM orang Romawi konon membawa ular suci dari Epidaurus ke Pulau Tiber untuk menyembuhkan wabah.
statement.en: In 293 BCE the Romans were said to have taken the sacred snake from Epidaurus to the Tiber Island in order to cure a plague.

claims.quote: The sanctuary finally closed in 426 CE when Roman emperor Theodosius II decreed the closure of all pagan sites in Greece.

statement.id: Tempat suci itu akhirnya ditutup pada 426 M ketika Kaisar Romawi Theodosius II memerintahkan penutupan semua situs pagan di Yunani.
statement.en: The sanctuary finally closed in 426 CE when the Roman emperor Theodosius II decreed the closure of all pagan sites in Greece.

claims.quote: The descendants of Asclepius, who continued in the art of medicine and healing, were known as the Asclepiads. Machaon, for example, helped Menelaos when he was wounded in the Trojan War, but the most famous doctor of the family was undoubtedly Hippocrates.

statement.id: Keturunan Asclepius yang melanjutkan seni pengobatan disebut Asclepiad; Machaon membantu Menelaos yang terluka dalam Perang Troya, tetapi dokter paling terkenal di keluarga itu tak diragukan lagi Hippocrates.
statement.en: Asclepius's descendants who continued in medicine were known as the Asclepiads; Machaon helped the wounded Menelaos in the Trojan War, but the most famous doctor of the family was undoubtedly Hippocrates.

claims.quote: He is sometimes accompanied by Hygeia and occasionally has a dog at his feet, as these animals were sacred at some of the god's sanctuaries.

statement.id: Ia kadang ditemani Hygeia dan sesekali ada anjing di kakinya, karena hewan-hewan itu dianggap suci di beberapa tempat sucinya.
statement.en: He is sometimes accompanied by Hygeia and occasionally has a dog at his feet, as these animals were sacred at some of his sanctuaries.

claims.quote: Apollo protested against his son's treatment but was himself punished by Zeus for impiety and made to serve Admetos, the king of Thessaly, for one year.

statement.id: Apollo memprotes perlakuan terhadap putranya tetapi dihukum Zeus karena ketidaksalehan dan dipaksa melayani Admetos, raja Thessalia, selama satu tahun.
statement.en: Apollo protested against his son's treatment but was himself punished by Zeus for impiety and made to serve Admetos, king of Thessaly, for one year.

claims.quote: Thankful patients often left votive offerings at the site, sometimes depicting the body part which had been cured.

statement.id: Pasien yang bersyukur sering meninggalkan persembahan nazar di tempat itu, kadang menggambarkan bagian tubuh yang sembuh.
statement.en: Thankful patients often left votive offerings at the site, sometimes depicting the body part that had been cured.

claims.quote: These were associated with Asclepius and symbolised regeneration, as snakes were thought to live both below and above ground and were also connected to prophetic powers as they knew the hidden secrets below ground.

statement.id: Ular dikaitkan dengan Asclepius dan melambangkan regenerasi karena dianggap hidup di bawah dan di atas tanah, dan juga dikaitkan dengan daya ramal karena mengetahui rahasia tersembunyi di bawah tanah.
statement.en: Snakes were associated with Asclepius and symbolised regeneration, as they were thought to live both below and above ground, and were connected to prophetic powers as they knew the hidden secrets below ground.

claims.quote: In some traditions he was married to Hygeia, also a goddess of health; in another version she was his daughter and Asclepius married Epione.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa tradisi ia menikah dengan Hygeia, juga dewi kesehatan; dalam versi lain Hygeia adalah putrinya dan Asclepius menikahi Epione.
statement.en: In some traditions he was married to Hygeia, also a goddess of health; in another version she was his daughter and Asclepius married Epione.

claims.quote: The cult of Asclepius was also transferred to Pergamon sometime in the 4th century BCE, possibly by a healed patient at Epidaurus named Archias.

statement.id: Kultus Asclepius juga dipindahkan ke Pergamon pada suatu waktu di abad ke-4 SM, mungkin oleh pasien sembuh di Epidaurus bernama Archias.
statement.en: The cult of Asclepius was also transferred to Pergamon sometime in the 4th century BCE, possibly by a healed patient at Epidaurus named Archias.

claims.quote: The serpent, the perpetual symbol of Aesculapius, has given rise to the opinion, that the worship was derived from Egypt, and that Aesculapius was identical with the serpent Cnuph worshipped in Egypt, or with the Phoenician Esmun.
claims.locator: Asklepios (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Ular, lambang abadi Aesculapius, melahirkan pendapat bahwa pemujaannya berasal dari Mesir dan bahwa Aesculapius identik dengan ular Cnuph yang dipuja di Mesir atau dengan Esmun dari Fenisia.
statement.en: The serpent, Aesculapius's perpetual symbol, has given rise to the opinion that his worship was derived from Egypt and that he was identical with the serpent Cnuph worshipped in Egypt or the Phoenician Esmun.

claims.quote: or, according to others, because Pluto had complained of Aesculapius diminishing the number of the dead too much.
claims.locator: Asklepios (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut sebagian lain, penyebabnya adalah Pluto mengeluh bahwa Aesculapius terlalu banyak mengurangi jumlah orang mati.
statement.en: According to others, the cause was that Pluto had complained that Aesculapius diminished the number of the dead too much.

claims.quote: Asklepios' apotheosis into godhood occurred at the same time. He was sometimes identified with Homer's Paion (Paeon), the physician of the gods.

statement.id: Apoteosis Asklepios menjadi dewa terjadi pada saat yang sama; ia kadang diidentifikasi dengan Paion (Paeon) dalam Homeros, tabib para dewa.
statement.en: Asklepios' apotheosis into godhood occurred at the same time; he was sometimes identified with Homer's Paion (Paeon), the physician of the gods.

claims.quote: Here was the god’s most famous shrine, and games were celebrated in his honour every five years, accompanied by solemn processions.

statement.id: Di sinilah tempat suci sang dewa yang paling terkenal, dan pertandingan diadakan untuk menghormatinya setiap lima tahun disertai prosesi khidmat.
statement.en: Here was the god's most famous shrine, and games were celebrated in his honour every five years, accompanied by solemn processions.

claims.quote: known as the Asklepieion, because he was believed to have been born on the nearby Mt. Titthion.

statement.id: Epidaurus dikenal sebagai Asklepieion karena ia dipercaya lahir di Gunung Titthion di dekatnya.
statement.en: The sanctuary at Epidaurus was known as the Asklepieion because he was believed to have been born on the nearby Mt. Titthion.

summary.id: Koronis, putri Phlegyas, ibunya.
summary.en: Koronis, daughter of Phlegyas, is his mother.

summary.id: Arsinoe dari Messenia adalah ibunya.
summary.en: The Messenian Arsinoe is his mother.

summary.id: Tricca di Thessalia dan Epidaurus berselisih; orakel memutuskan Epidaurus.
summary.en: Tricca in Thessaly and Epidaurus disputed it; an oracle declared for Epidaurus.

summary.id: Ia dipercaya lahir di Gunung Titthion di dekat Epidaurus.
summary.en: He was believed to have been born on the nearby Mt. Titthion at Epidaurus.

summary.id: Zeus takut ia membuat semua manusia abadi.
summary.en: Zeus feared he would make all men immortal.

summary.id: Zeus menganggapnya ancaman bagi pemisahan manusia dan dewa.
summary.en: Zeus saw him as a threat to the division between humans and gods.

summary.id: Pluto mengeluh jumlah orang mati berkurang.
summary.en: Pluto complained the number of the dead was shrinking.

summary.id: Hygeia istri Asclepius.
summary.en: Hygeia is Asclepius's wife.

summary.id: Hygeia putri Asclepius, dan ia menikahi Epione.
summary.en: Hygeia is his daughter and he married Epione.

summary.id: Setiap empat tahun.
summary.en: Every four years.

summary.id: Setiap lima tahun, disertai prosesi khidmat.
summary.en: Every five years, accompanied by solemn processions.

summary.id: Ular simbolnya melahirkan pendapat bahwa pemujaannya berasal dari Mesir.
summary.en: His serpent symbol gave rise to the opinion that his worship derived from Egypt.

summary.id: Dalam Homeros ia tampaknya hanya manusia, bukan dewa.
summary.en: In Homer he appears to be merely a human being, not a god.

short_description.id: Odin adalah dewa utama dalam mitologi Nordik yang digambarkan bijak dan bermata satu, dan terkait dengan perang, puisi, orang mati, rune, dan sihir.
short_description.en: Odin is the main god of Norse mythology, depicted as wise and one-eyed and associated with war, poetry, the dead, runes, and magic.

long_description.id: Odin adalah dewa utama dalam mitologi Nordik. Ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua yang sangat bijak dan bermata satu, dikenali dari topi dan jubahnya, janggut panjang, serta tombak Gungnir. Menurut sumber, ia tinggal di Asgard, benteng para dewa. Cincin Draupnir dan kuda berkaki delapan Sleipnir juga termasuk atributnya, dan dua gagaknya, Huginn dan Muninn, terbang berkeliling dunia mengumpulkan kabar lalu membisikkannya ke telinganya.
long_description.en: Odin is the main god of Norse mythology. He is depicted as an immensely wise, one-eyed old man, recognised by his hat and cloak, long beard, and spear Gungnir. According to the sources he resides in Asgard, the stronghold of the gods. The ring Draupnir and the eight-legged horse Sleipnir are also among his attributes, and his two ravens, Huginn and Muninn, fly around the world gathering news and whisper it into his ear.

long_description.id: Ranah Odin mencakup puisi, orang mati, rune, dan sihir, serta perang: dalam sumber Jermanik selatan dan barat, Odin yang menentukan apakah pertempuran atau prajurit tertentu menang. Para Valkyrie membawa prajurit yang gugur ke Valhalla; mereka dikenal sebagai Einherjar dan menjadi pasukan Odin melawan kekuatan dunia bawah saat Ragnarök. Odin juga digambarkan sebagai pemimpin Wild Hunt, pasukan orang mati yang menunggang badai. Sihirnya membuatnya sering dipandang sebagai syaman, dan ia juga memiliki fungsi sebagai dewa penyembuhan, dan ia memakai sihir untuk melihat sekilas masa depan.
long_description.en: Odin's domain covers poetry, the dead, runes, and magic, as well as war: in southern and western Germanic sources it is Odin who decides whether battles or individual warriors are victorious. The Valkyries bring slain fighters to Valhalla; these fighters, known as the Einherjar, become Odin's strike-force against the powers of the Underworld at Ragnarök. Odin is also portrayed as the leader of the Wild Hunt, an army of the dead who ride on the storms. His magic often leads him to be seen as a shaman and a god of healing, and he uses magic to catch glimpses of the future.

long_description.id: Kisah-kisah Odin banyak berkisah tentang pencarian pengetahuan. Menurut Edda Prosa, ia baru boleh minum dari sumur Mimer setelah meninggalkan salah satu matanya sebagai jaminan. Ia juga menggantung sembilan malam di Yggdrasil dengan luka tombak sebelum rune terungkap kepadanya, dan mencuri mead para skald lalu kabur dalam wujud elang. Dalam kisah penciptaan, Odin dan saudara-saudaranya Vili dan Vé membunuh raksasa purba Ymir dan membentuk bumi, langit, gunung, dan laut dari tubuhnya.
long_description.en: Many of Odin's stories concern the search for knowledge. According to the Prose Edda, he was allowed to drink from Mimer's well only after leaving one of his eyes there as a pledge. He also hangs for nine nights on Yggdrasil with a spear wound before the runes are revealed to him, and he steals the mead of the skalds and escapes in the shape of an eagle. In the creation story, Odin and his brothers Vili and Vé slay the proto-giant Ymir and make the earth, sky, mountains, and sea from his body.

long_description.id: Pada Ragnarök, Odin maju paling depan dengan helm emas, zirah gemerlap, dan tombak Gungner melawan serigala Fenris, dan ia terbunuh oleh Fenrir. Para pemuja utamanya sebagian besar kalangan elite, yaitu raja, kepala suku, dan penyair, serta prajurit. Adam dari Bremen menulis pada 1070 M bahwa di kuil Uppsala kuno persembahan untuk Odin dibuat pada masa perang. Kisah Odin dikenal antara lain dari Edda dan saga Islandia yang ditulis pada Abad Pertengahan.
long_description.en: At Ragnarök, Odin rides first with his golden helmet, resplendent byrnie, and spear Gungner against the Fenris-wolf, and he is killed by Fenrir. His main worshippers were mostly the elite, namely kings, chieftains, and poets, along with warriors. Adam of Bremen wrote in 1070 CE that at the Old Uppsala temple sacrifices were made to Odin in times of war. The tales of Odin are known from Edda writings and Icelandic sagas recorded in the Middle Ages.

cultural_context.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, para pemuja utama Odin sebagian besar adalah kalangan elite, yaitu raja, kepala suku, dan penyair, serta juga prajurit.
cultural_context.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Odin's main worshippers mostly belonged to the elite, namely kings, chieftains, and poets, and also included warriors.

literal_meaning.id: "penguasa kegilaan" atau "pemimpin orang yang kerasukan"
literal_meaning.en: "lord of frenzy" or "leader of the possessed"

who.id: Odin adalah dewa utama mitologi Nordik, lelaki tua bijak bermata satu.
who.en: Odin is the main god of Norse mythology, an immensely wise one-eyed old man.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari mitologi Nordik, dan juga dikenal dalam mitologi Jermanik sebagai Woden, Wodan, atau Wuotan.
origin.en: He comes from Norse mythology and is also known in Germanic mythology as Woden, Wodan, or Wuotan.

role.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan puisi, orang mati, rune, dan sihir, serta mengumpulkan prajurit gugur di Valhalla.
role.en: He is associated with poetry, the dead, runes, and magic, and gathers slain warriors in Valhalla.

famous_for.id: Odin terkenal karena kebijaksanaannya, mata yang dikorbankan demi pengetahuan, dan dua gagaknya, Huginn dan Muninn.
famous_for.en: Odin is known for his wisdom, the eye given up for knowledge, and his two ravens Huginn and Muninn.

did_you_know.id: Nama hari Wednesday dalam bahasa Inggris modern berasal dari "hari Woden", yaitu nama Odin dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno.
did_you_know.en: The modern English weekday name Wednesday traces back to "day of Woden", Woden being Odin's Old English name.

description.id: Odin disebut sebagai dewa sihir, dan sihirnya membuatnya sering dipandang sebagai syaman.
description.en: Odin is called the god of magic, and his magic often leads him to be seen as a shaman.

description.id: Odin terutama memakai sihir untuk melihat sekilas masa depan, dan digambarkan jatuh ke dalam trans serta mendapat penglihatan.
description.en: Odin mainly used magic to catch glimpses of the future, and is described as falling into trances and having visions.

description.id: Odin dipandang sebagai dewa penyembuhan.
description.en: Odin has a function as a god of healing.

description.id: Dalam kisah mead puisi, Odin berubah menjadi elang untuk melarikan diri.
description.en: In the story of the mead of poetry, Odin shape-shifts into an eagle to escape.

description.id: Dalam sumber Jermanik selatan dan barat, Odin yang menentukan apakah pertempuran atau prajurit tertentu menang.
description.en: In southern and western Germanic sources, Odin decides whether battles or individual warriors are victorious.

description.id: Tombak Gungnir adalah atribut utamanya, dan Odin maju dengan tombak itu melawan serigala Fenris pada Ragnarök. Cincin Draupnir meneteskan delapan cincin baru setiap sembilan malam.
description.en: The spear Gungnir is a main attribute, and Odin advances with it against the Fenris-wolf at Ragnarök. The ring Draupnir drips eight new rings every nine nights.

description.id: Pengetahuan Odin disebut berasal dari kepala Mímir atau dari minum air sumur Mímir, dan menurut Edda Prosa ia menyerahkan salah satu matanya sebagai jaminan.
description.en: Odin's knowledge is said to come from Mímir's head or from drinking from Mímir's well, and according to the Prose Edda he left one eye as a pledge.

tradition.id: Mitologi Jermanik (Inggris Kuno, Franka Kuno, Jerman Kuno Tinggi)
tradition.en: Germanic mythology (Old English, Old Franconian, Old High German)

description.id: Odin juga ada dalam mitologi Jermanik sebagai Woden (Inggris Kuno), Wodan (Franka Kuno), serta Wutan atau Wuotan (Jerman Kuno Tinggi).
description.en: Odin also exists in Germanic mythology as Woden (Old English), Wodan (Old Franconian), and Wutan or Wuotan (Old High German).

role.id: Pencari pengetahuan yang menyerahkan matanya
role.en: Seeker of knowledge who gives up an eye

summary.id: Menurut Edda Prosa, Alfather datang ke sumur Mimer untuk minum, tetapi baru mendapatkannya setelah meninggalkan salah satu matanya sebagai jaminan. World History Encyclopedia menyebut pengetahuan Odin berasal dari kepala Mímir atau dari minum air sumur Mímir.
summary.en: According to the Prose Edda, Alfather came to Mimer's well to drink but received a drink only after leaving one of his eyes as a pledge. World History Encyclopedia says Odin's knowledge comes from Mímir's head or from drinking from Mímir's well.

role.id: Orang yang berkorban
role.en: The one who sacrifices himself

summary.id: Selama sembilan malam Odin tergantung pada sebuah dahan Yggdrasil, pohon dunia, dengan luka tombak yang hampir merenggut nyawanya; baru setelah itu rune tersingkap baginya.
summary.en: For nine nights Odin dangles from a bough of the World Tree Yggdrasil, wounded by a spear and close to death, and only afterwards are the runes revealed to him.

role.id: Pencuri mead
role.en: The thief of the mead

summary.id: Menurut Snorri, kemahiran puisi Odin berasal dari pencurian mead para skald setelah ia tidur tiga malam dengan raksasa perempuan Gunnlǫð. Ia diizinkan tiga tegukan, menghabiskan semua wadah, lalu berubah menjadi elang dan kabur.
summary.en: According to Snorri, Odin's poetic skill comes from stealing the mead of the skalds after sleeping for three nights with the giantess Gunnlǫð. He is allowed three sips, drains the containers, then shape-shifts into an eagle and flees.

role.id: Pencipta bersama saudara-saudaranya
role.en: Creator together with his brothers

summary.id: Borr dan Bestla menjadi orang tua Odin dan saudara-saudaranya, yang biasanya bernama Vili dan Vé. Mereka membunuh raksasa purba Ymir dan membentuk bumi dari dagingnya, langit dari tengkoraknya, gunung dari tulangnya, dan laut dari darahnya.
summary.en: Borr and Bestla sired Odin and his brothers, usually named Vili and Vé. They slew the proto-giant Ymir and made the earth from his flesh, the sky from his skull, the mountains from his bones, and the sea from his blood.

title.en: The contests of knowledge in Vafþrúðnismál and Grímnismál

role.id: Peserta adu kecerdasan dan penyamar
role.en: Contestant in the battle of wits and the disguised wanderer

summary.id: Dalam Vafþrúðnismál Odin memulai adu kecerdasan dengan raksasa Vafþrúðnir dan mengalahkannya. Dalam Grímnismál Odin yang menyamar disiksa dan akhirnya membuka pengetahuannya kepada Raja Geirroðr.
summary.en: In Vafþrúðnismál Odin starts a battle of wits with the giant Vafþrúðnir and beats him. In Grímnismál a disguised Odin is tortured and ends up revealing his knowledge to King Geirroðr.

role.id: Pemimpin einherjar yang gugur
role.en: Leader of the einherjar who falls

summary.id: Dalam Edda Prosa Odin maju paling depan dengan helm emas, zirah gemerlap, dan tombak Gungner melawan serigala Fenris. Pada masa depan mitos itu, ia memimpin einherjar dan terbunuh oleh Fenrir.
summary.en: In the Prose Edda Odin rides first with a golden helmet, resplendent byrnie, and the spear Gungner against the Fenris-wolf. In the mythic future he leads the einherjar and is killed by Fenrir.

description.en: The stronghold and home of the gods, where Odin resides.

description.id: "Aula orang gugur", tempat Odin mengumpulkan prajurit yang tewas.
description.en: The 'hall of the slain', where Odin gathers slain warriors.

description.id: Sumur tempat Odin meninggalkan salah satu matanya sebagai jaminan.
description.en: The well where Odin left one of his eyes as a pledge.

description.id: Kuil pagan besar di Swedia; menurut Adam dari Bremen, persembahan untuk Odin dibuat di sana pada masa perang.
description.en: A great pagan temple in Sweden; according to Adam of Bremen, sacrifices were made there to Odin in times of war.

description.id: Ukiran batu Swedia menampilkan sosok dewa bertombak yang mungkin dikaitkan dengan Odin.
description.en: Swedish rock carvings depict figures of a god holding a spear who might be linked to Odin.

description.id: Paling lambat sekitar 500 M, Odin jelas muncul pada berbagai hiasan bersama burung dan prajurit.
description.en: By at least 500 CE, Odin clearly appears on a range of ornaments alongside birds and warriors.

description.id: Adam dari Bremen menulis tentang kunjungannya ke kuil Uppsala kuno, tempat patung Odin berdiri di sisi patung Thor.
description.en: Adam of Bremen wrote of his visit to the Old Uppsala temple, where a statue of Odin stood beside that of Thor.

description.id: Kisah Odin dikenal antara lain dari Edda Snorri, puisi Edda lain, dan saga Islandia yang ditulis pada Abad Pertengahan.
description.en: The stories of Odin are known from Snorri's Edda, other Edda poems, and Icelandic sagas written down in the Middle Ages.
