statement.en: Persephone is named as Hades's wife whom he brought to the underworld.

claims.quote: Hades was the only god not to reside on Mount Olympus, dwelling instead in a dark palace beneath the earth.

statement.id: Hades digambarkan tinggal di istana gelap di bawah bumi, bukan di Olympus.
statement.en: Hades is described as dwelling in a dark palace beneath the earth rather than on Olympus.

claims.quote: Haides was devoured by Kronos (Cronus) as soon as he was born, along with four of his siblings. Zeus later caused the Titan to disgorge them, and together they drove the Titan gods from heaven and locked them away in the pit of Tartaros.

statement.id: Menurut Theoi, Haides ditelan Kronos begitu lahir bersama empat saudaranya; Zeus kemudian membuat sang Titan memuntahkan mereka, dan bersama-sama mereka mengusir para dewa Titan dari langit dan mengurung mereka di jurang Tartaros.
statement.en: According to Theoi, Haides was devoured by Kronos as soon as he was born along with four siblings; Zeus later made the Titan disgorge them, and together they drove the Titan gods from heaven and locked them in the pit of Tartaros.

claims.quote: I [Poseidon] when the lots were shaken drew the grey sea to live in forever; Aides drew the lot of the mists and the darkness, and Zeus was allotted the wide sky, in the cloud and the bright air.
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Homer Iliad 15.187 ff (trans. Lattimore)

statement.id: Dalam Iliad (terjemahan Lattimore), Poseidon berkata bahwa ketika undi dikocok ia mendapat laut kelabu, Aides mendapat undi kabut dan kegelapan, dan Zeus mendapat langit luas.
statement.en: In the Iliad (Lattimore's translation), Poseidon says that when the lots were shaken he drew the grey sea, Aides drew the lot of the mists and the darkness, and Zeus was allotted the wide sky.

claims.quote: strong Haides (Hades), pitiless in heart, who dwells under the earth
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Hesiod Theogony 453 ff (trans. Evelyn-White)

statement.id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos, Haides digambarkan kuat, tanpa belas kasih di hatinya, dan berdiam di bawah bumi.
statement.en: In Hesiod's Theogony Haides is described as strong, pitiless in heart, and dwelling under the earth.

claims.quote: Haides desired a bride and petitioned his brother Zeus to grant him one of his daughters. The god offered him Persephone, the daughter of Demeter. However, knowing that the goddess would resist the marriage, he assented to the forceful abduction of the girl.

statement.id: Haides menginginkan pengantin dan memohon kepada saudaranya Zeus agar memberinya salah satu putrinya; Zeus menawarkan Persephone, putri Demeter, dan karena tahu Demeter akan menolak, ia menyetujui penculikan paksa gadis itu.
statement.en: Haides desired a bride and asked his brother Zeus for one of his daughters; Zeus offered Persephone, daughter of Demeter, and, knowing Demeter would resist, assented to the forceful abduction of the girl.

claims.quote: When Demeter learned of this, she was furious and caused a great dearth to fall upon the earth until her daughter was returned. Zeus was forced to concede lest mankind perish, and the girl was fetched forth from the underworld. However, since she had tasted of the pomegranate seed, she was forced to return to him for a portion of each year.

statement.id: Demeter murka dan menimpakan paceklik besar ke bumi sampai putrinya dikembalikan; Zeus terpaksa mengalah dan gadis itu dijemput dari dunia bawah, tetapi karena telah mencicipi biji delima ia harus kembali kepada Haides selama sebagian tiap tahun.
statement.en: Demeter was furious and brought a great dearth upon the earth until her daughter was returned; Zeus was forced to concede and the girl was fetched from the underworld, but since she had tasted the pomegranate seed she had to return to Haides for a portion of each year.

claims.quote: Haides was depicted as a dark-bearded, regal god. He was depicted as either Aidoneus, enthroned in the underworld, holding a bird-tipped sceptre, or as Plouton (Pluton), the giver of wealth, pouring fertility from a cornucopia.

statement.id: Haides digambarkan sebagai dewa berjanggut gelap yang agung, entah sebagai Aidoneus yang bertakhta di dunia bawah dengan tongkat berujung burung, atau sebagai Plouton, pemberi kekayaan, yang mencurahkan kesuburan dari cornucopia.
statement.en: Haides was depicted as a dark-bearded, regal god, either as Aidoneus enthroned in the underworld holding a bird-tipped sceptre, or as Plouton, the giver of wealth, pouring fertility from a cornucopia.

claims.quote: The Romans named him Dis, or Pluto, the Latin form of his Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches."

statement.id: Bangsa Romawi menamainya Dis atau Pluto, bentuk Latin dari gelar Yunaninya Plouton, "Penguasa Kekayaan".
statement.en: The Romans named him Dis, or Pluto, the Latin form of his Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches."

claims.quote: He possessed a helmet which rendered the wearer invisible (Il. v. 845), and later traditions stated that this helmet was given him as a present by the Cyclopes after their delivery from Tartarus.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Haides memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat, dan tradisi kemudian menyebut helm itu hadiah dari para Kiklops setelah mereka dibebaskan dari Tartarus.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Hades possessed a helmet that rendered the wearer invisible, and later traditions said it was a gift from the Cyclopes after their delivery from Tartarus.

claims.quote: He kept the gates of the lower world closed (whence he is called ... that no shade might be able to escape or return to the region of light.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Haides menjaga gerbang dunia bawah tetap tertutup agar tak ada arwah yang dapat lolos atau kembali ke wilayah cahaya.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Hades kept the gates of the lower world closed so that no shade could escape or return to the region of light.

claims.quote: His character is described as fierce and inexorable, whence of all the gods he was most hated by mortals.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, wataknya digambarkan garang dan tak kenal ampun sehingga di antara semua dewa ia paling dibenci manusia.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, his character is described as fierce and inexorable, so that of all the gods he was most hated by mortals.

claims.quote: In Elis he had a sacred enclosure and a temple, which was opened only once in every year
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Di Elis Haides memiliki pelataran suci dan sebuah kuil yang hanya dibuka sekali setiap tahun.
statement.en: In Elis Hades had a sacred enclosure and a temple that was opened only once every year.

claims.quote: Plato (Cratyl. p. 403) observes that people preferred calling him Pluton (the giver of wealth) to pronouncing the dreaded name of Hades or Aides.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Plato mencatat bahwa orang lebih suka menyebutnya Pluton (pemberi kekayaan) daripada mengucapkan nama Hades atau Aides yang ditakuti.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Plato observes that people preferred calling him Pluton (the giver of wealth) to pronouncing the dreaded name of Hades or Aides.

claims.quote: The etymology of Hades is uncertain: some derive it from a-idein, whence it would signify "the god who makes invisible,"
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, asal-usul kata Hades tidak pasti; sebagian menurunkannya dari a-idein sehingga berarti "dewa yang membuat tak terlihat".
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, the etymology of Hades is uncertain; some derive it from a-idein, so that it would signify "the god who makes invisible".

claims.quote: In Homer Aides is invariably the name of the god; but in later times it was transferred to his house, his abode or kingdom, so that it became a name for the lower world itself.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, dalam Homeros Aides selalu nama sang dewa, tetapi kemudian dialihkan ke rumah, tempat tinggal, atau kerajaannya sehingga menjadi nama dunia bawah itu sendiri.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, in Homer Aides is always the name of the god, but later it was transferred to his house, abode or kingdom and became a name for the lower world itself.

claims.quote: The three goddesses of earthly wrath were sometimes represented as daughters of Haides. The usual account, however, describes them as earth-born.
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Offspring of Hades

statement.id: Menurut Theoi, tiga dewi murka bumi kadang digambarkan sebagai putri Haides, tetapi kisah yang lazim menyebut mereka lahir dari bumi.
statement.en: According to Theoi, the three goddesses of earthly wrath were sometimes represented as daughters of Haides, but the usual account describes them as earth-born.

claims.quote: In return the Kyklopes (Cyclopes) gave Zeus thunder, lightning, and a thunderbolt, as well as a helmet for Plouton (Pluton) [Haides] and a trident for Poseidon.
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Pseudo-Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 1.6-7 (trans. Aldrich)

statement.id: Dalam Bibliotheca Pseudo-Apollodoros, para Kiklops memberi Zeus guntur dan petir, serta helm untuk Plouton (Haides) dan trisula untuk Poseidon.
statement.en: In Pseudo-Apollodorus's Bibliotheca the Kyklopes gave Zeus thunder, lightning and a thunderbolt, as well as a helmet for Plouton (Haides) and a trident for Poseidon.

claims.quote: Haides trembled where he rules over the dead below.
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Hesiod Theogony 820 ff (trans. Evelyn-White)

statement.id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos, Haides gemetar di tempat ia memerintah orang mati di bawah ketika Zeus bertarung melawan Typhoeus.
statement.en: In Hesiod's Theogony, Haides trembled where he rules over the dead below as Zeus battled Typhoeus.

claims.quote: Perhaps the most feared of the gods, he is described by both Homer and Hesiod as 'pitiless', 'loathsome', and 'monstrous' Hades.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Hades mungkin dewa yang paling ditakuti dan oleh Homeros maupun Hesiodos disebut 'tanpa belas kasih', 'menjijikkan', dan 'mengerikan'.
statement.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Hades was perhaps the most feared of the gods and is described by both Homer and Hesiod as 'pitiless', 'loathsome', and 'monstrous'.

claims.quote: Indeed, even to speak his name was avoided; instead epithets were used such as Eubuleus (giving good advice).

statement.id: Bahkan menyebut namanya dihindari; sebagai gantinya dipakai gelar seperti Eubuleus (pemberi nasihat baik).
statement.en: Even speaking his name was avoided; epithets such as Eubuleus (giving good advice) were used instead.

claims.quote: There are also accounts of sacrificial practices made in honour of Hades, carried out at night and where the blood of victims was left to seep down into the earth to reach the underworld god.

statement.id: Ada pula catatan tentang praktik kurban untuk Hades yang dilakukan malam hari dengan darah korban dibiarkan meresap ke tanah agar sampai ke dewa dunia bawah.
statement.en: There are also accounts of sacrificial practices in honour of Hades, carried out at night, with the victims' blood left to seep into the earth to reach the underworld god.

claims.quote: The god also had a helmet made by Hephaistos which rendered the wearer invisible, and it was this helmet that was used by Athena when she fought Ares in Homer's account of the Trojan War in the Iliad and by Perseus in his quest for the head of Medusa.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Hades memiliki helm buatan Hephaistos yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat; helm itu dipakai Athena saat melawan Ares dalam Iliad dan oleh Perseus dalam perburuan kepala Medusa.
statement.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Hades had a helmet made by Hephaistos that rendered the wearer invisible; it was used by Athena when she fought Ares in the Iliad and by Perseus in his quest for Medusa's head.

claims.quote: In mythology, Hades fell in love with Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter, and abducted her to live with him.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi, Hades jatuh cinta pada Persephone, putri Zeus dan Demeter, dan menculiknya untuk tinggal bersamanya.
statement.en: In mythology, Hades fell in love with Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter, and abducted her to live with him.

claims.quote: However, Hades tricked the girl into eating a pomegranate seed and therefore she could only return to the living for half of the year. This myth was symbolic perhaps of the cycle of life and death, planting and harvest.

statement.id: Hades menipu gadis itu agar memakan biji delima sehingga ia hanya dapat kembali kepada yang hidup selama setengah tahun; mitos ini mungkin melambangkan siklus hidup dan mati, penanaman dan panen.
statement.en: Hades tricked the girl into eating a pomegranate seed so that she could only return to the living for half of the year; the myth was perhaps symbolic of the cycle of life and death, planting and harvest.

claims.quote: When Hermes discovered this, he demanded Persephone be returned to Demeter and it was decided that if she had not eaten any food from Hades, she could return to the upper world.

statement.id: Ketika Hermes mengetahuinya, ia menuntut Persephone dikembalikan kepada Demeter dan diputuskan bahwa jika ia belum makan apa pun dari Hades, ia boleh kembali ke dunia atas.
statement.en: When Hermes discovered this he demanded that Persephone be returned to Demeter, and it was decided that if she had not eaten any food from Hades she could return to the upper world.

claims.quote: In Archaic and Classical Greek art, Hades is most often represented as a more mature man, bearded and holding a sceptre, a two-pronged spear, a libation vase, or a cornucopia - symbolic of the mineral and vegetable wealth which comes from the ground.

statement.id: Dalam seni Yunani Arkais dan Klasik, Hades paling sering digambarkan sebagai pria dewasa berjanggut yang memegang tongkat, tombak bermata dua, bejana libasi, atau cornucopia, lambang kekayaan mineral dan nabati dari tanah.
statement.en: In Archaic and Classical Greek art Hades is most often a mature bearded man holding a sceptre, a two-pronged spear, a libation vase, or a cornucopia, symbolic of the mineral and vegetable wealth that comes from the ground.

claims.quote: On occasion he is seated on an ebony throne or rides a chariot pulled by black horses, often with Persephone at his side.

statement.id: Kadang ia digambarkan duduk di singgasana eboni atau menunggang kereta yang ditarik kuda hitam, sering dengan Persephone di sisinya.
statement.en: On occasion he is shown seated on an ebony throne or riding a chariot pulled by black horses, often with Persephone at his side.

claims.quote: The god Hermes was believed to lead souls to the river Styx in the underworld, at which point the aged boatman Charon ferried them to the gates of Hades where Kerberos - the ferocious three-headed dog (or fifty-headed according to Hesiod) with serpents coming out of its body - stood guard to keep souls in rather than to keep others out.

statement.id: Hermes dipercaya menuntun jiwa ke Sungai Styx di dunia bawah, tempat juru perahu tua Charon menyeberangkan mereka ke gerbang Hades, yang dijaga Kerberos, anjing ganas berkepala tiga (atau lima puluh menurut Hesiodos) yang menjaga agar jiwa tetap di dalam.
statement.en: Hermes was believed to lead souls to the river Styx, where the aged boatman Charon ferried them to the gates of Hades, guarded by Kerberos, a ferocious three-headed dog (fifty-headed according to Hesiod) who kept souls in rather than others out.

claims.quote: It was for payment to Charon that bereaved family members put a coin in the mouth of the deceased (for Greeks the traditional coin was the low-value obol). The unburied or those without the means to pay the boatman were condemned to wander the Earth as ghosts.

statement.id: Untuk membayar Charon, keluarga yang berduka menaruh koin di mulut jenazah (bagi orang Yunani koin tradisionalnya obol bernilai rendah); orang yang tak dikubur atau tak mampu membayar dihukum mengembara di bumi sebagai hantu.
statement.en: To pay Charon, bereaved families put a coin in the mouth of the deceased (the traditional Greek coin was the low-value obol); the unburied or those unable to pay were condemned to wander the Earth as ghosts.

claims.quote: Traditionally, the three judges of souls were Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos, themselves noted for their honourable lives.

statement.id: Secara tradisional, tiga hakim jiwa adalah Minos, Rhadamanthys, dan Aiakos, yang terkenal karena hidup terhormat.
statement.en: Traditionally the three judges of souls were Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos, themselves noted for their honourable lives.

claims.quote: Souls judged to have led especially good lives were first taken to drink the waters of the River Lethe which made them forget all bad things, and then they were taken to the idyllic Elysian Fields.

statement.id: Jiwa yang dinilai hidup sangat baik lebih dulu diajak minum air Sungai Lethe yang membuat mereka melupakan semua hal buruk, lalu dibawa ke Padang Elysium yang indah.
statement.en: Souls judged to have led especially good lives were first taken to drink the waters of the River Lethe, which made them forget all bad things, and then to the idyllic Elysian Fields.

claims.quote: Those souls judged to have led bad lives were put in the hands of the Furies and taken to Tartarus, the lowest level of Hades, to receive punishment for their misdeeds.

statement.id: Jiwa yang dinilai hidup buruk diserahkan kepada para Furia dan dibawa ke Tartarus, tingkat terendah Hades, untuk menerima hukuman atas perbuatan mereka.
statement.en: Souls judged to have led bad lives were put in the hands of the Furies and taken to Tartarus, the lowest level of Hades, to be punished for their misdeeds.

claims.quote: Although a fearful place to the living, Hades was visited by several heroes in the course of their various adventures, including Hercules to capture Kerberos in the last of his twelve labours, by Odysseus to seek the advice of wise Tiresias, by Orpheus to find Eurydice, and by Theseus and Peirithoos to capture Persephone so that she might marry the latter.

statement.id: Meski menakutkan bagi yang hidup, Hades dikunjungi beberapa pahlawan: Hercules untuk menangkap Kerberos pada pekerjaan kedua belasnya, Odiseus untuk meminta nasihat Tiresias, Orpheus untuk mencari Eurydice, dan Theseus serta Peirithoos untuk menculik Persephone agar dinikahi Peirithoos.
statement.en: Though fearful to the living, Hades was visited by several heroes: Hercules to capture Kerberos in his last labour, Odysseus to seek Tiresias's advice, Orpheus to find Eurydice, and Theseus and Peirithoos to capture Persephone so that Peirithoos might marry her.

claims.quote: These last two heroes were, however, less fortunate than the others in that Hades imprisoned them in two thrones (or tied to two rocks in other accounts) and only Theseus would later escape from the underworld when Hercules released him.

statement.id: Kedua pahlawan terakhir itu kurang beruntung karena Hades memenjarakan mereka di dua singgasana (atau mengikat mereka pada dua batu menurut kisah lain), dan hanya Theseus yang kemudian lolos ketika Hercules membebaskannya.
statement.en: The last two heroes were less fortunate: Hades imprisoned them in two thrones (or tied them to two rocks in other accounts), and only Theseus later escaped when Hercules released him.

claims.quote: Following the overthrow of first the Titans and then the Giants by the Olympian gods, Hades drew lots with his brothers Zeus and Poseidon to decide which part of the world each would rule.

statement.id: Setelah para dewa Olimpus menggulingkan Titan lalu Raksasa, Hades mengundi dengan saudara-saudaranya, Zeus dan Poseidon, untuk menentukan bagian dunia yang akan diperintah masing-masing.
statement.en: After the Olympian gods overthrew first the Titans and then the Giants, Hades drew lots with his brothers Zeus and Poseidon to decide which part of the world each would rule.

claims.quote: The origin of Hades's name is uncertain but has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one" since antiquity.

statement.id: Asal-usul nama Hades tidak pasti, tetapi sejak zaman kuno umumnya dianggap berarti "yang tak terlihat".
statement.en: The origin of Hades's name is uncertain but has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one" since antiquity.

claims.quote: Roman-era mythographers eventually equated the Etruscan god Aita, and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus, with Hades, and merged all these figures into Pluto, a Latinisation of Plouton

statement.id: Para mitograf zaman Romawi akhirnya menyamakan dewa Etruria Aita serta dewa Romawi Dis Pater dan Orcus dengan Hades dan menggabungkan semuanya menjadi Pluto, Latinisasi dari Plouton.
statement.en: Roman-era mythographers eventually equated the Etruscan god Aita and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus with Hades, merging them all into Pluto, a Latinisation of Plouton.

claims.quote: Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

statement.id: Hades adalah putra sulung Kronos dan Rhea, meski itu juga membuatnya putra terakhir yang dimuntahkan ayahnya.
statement.en: Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

claims.quote: Martin Litchfield West argues instead for an original meaning of "the one who presides over meeting up" from the universality of death.

statement.id: Martin Litchfield West mengusulkan makna asli "yang memimpin pertemuan" yang berasal dari universalitas kematian.
statement.en: Martin Litchfield West instead argues for an original meaning of "the one who presides over meeting up", from the universality of death.

claims.quote: Hence he is called the infernal Zeus (Zeus katachthonios), or the king of the shades
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, karena itu ia disebut Zeus dunia bawah (Zeus katachthonios) atau raja para arwah.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, he is hence called the infernal Zeus (Zeus katachthonios) or the king of the shades.

summary.en: World History Encyclopedia: the helmet was made by Hephaistos.

short_description.id: Hephaestus adalah dewa Olimpus dalam mitologi Yunani untuk api, pandai besi, dan kerajinan, yang menempa senjata, perhiasan, dan alat ajaib bagi para dewa.
short_description.en: Hephaestus is an Olympian god in Greek mythology of fire, smiths, and crafts, who forged weapons, jewellery, and marvellous devices for the gods.

long_description.id: Hephaestus adalah dewa Olimpus untuk api, pandai besi, pengrajin, pengerjaan logam, pemahatan batu, dan seni patung. Ia adalah dewa api, terutama sebagai kekuatan alam di daerah vulkanik dan sebagai sarana dalam seni dan kerajinan. Dalam seni ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki berjanggut yang memegang palu dan penjepit, sering memakai topi pekerja dan menunggang bagal. Bengkelnya digambarkan berada di bawah gunung berapi seperti Gunung Etna; dalam Iliad ia memiliki rumah dari perunggu yang bertabur bintang.
long_description.en: Hephaestus is an Olympian god whose domains include fire, smiths, craftsmen, metalwork, stonemasonry, and sculpture. He is the god of fire, especially as a power of nature in volcanic districts and as a means in arts and crafts. In art he is a bearded man holding a hammer and tongs, often wearing a workman's hat and riding a mule. His workshop is described as lying beneath volcanoes such as Mount Etna; in the Iliad he has a house of bronze decked with stars.

long_description.id: Para dewa Olimpus menerima buah karyanya: rumah, zirah, dan alat cerdik. Ia dikreditkan membuat tongkat kerajaan dan aegis Zeus serta helm Hermes, dan membentuk Pandora dari tanah liat. Ia juga membuat automaton, antara lain pelayan emas yang bisa berbicara, tripod berroda yang bergerak sendiri, dan Talos dari perunggu. Dalam Iliad, ia menempa perisai bagi Achilles dari perunggu, timah, emas, dan perak, dihias dengan bumi, langit, laut, matahari, dan bulan.
long_description.en: The Olympian gods received the fruits of his craft: houses, armour, and ingenious devices. He is credited with making the sceptre and aegis of Zeus and the helmet of Hermes, and with shaping Pandora from clay. He also made automatons, including gold maids who could speak, self-moving wheeled tripods, and bronze Talos. In the Iliad he forges a shield for Achilles from bronze, tin, gold, and silver, decorated with the earth, the heavens, the sea, the sun, and the moon.

long_description.id: Tradisi Homeros menyebut Hephaestus putra Zeus dan Hera, sedangkan tradisi lain menyebut Hera melahirkannya tanpa ayah. Ia dibuang dari Olimpus, menurut satu versi oleh Hera saat lahir dan menurut versi lain oleh Zeus, lalu mendarat di Lemnos dan dirawat Thetis dan Eurynome. Ia kemudian menjebak Hera dalam singgasana terkutuk; Dionysos membujuknya kembali ke Olimpus. Ia menikahi Aphrodite, yang kemudian terperangkap bersama Ares dalam jaring emas.
long_description.en: Homeric tradition names Hephaestus as the son of Zeus and Hera, while other traditions say Hera bore him without a father. He was cast out of Olympus, by Hera at birth in one version and by Zeus in another, landed on Lemnos, and was cared for by Thetis and Eurynome. He later trapped Hera in a cursed throne; Dionysos led him back to Olympus. He married Aphrodite, who was later trapped with Ares in a golden net.

long_description.id: Ia dipuja terutama di Athena dan Lemnos. Di Athena ia berbagi kuil dan festival dengan Athena, termasuk festival Chalkeia para pandai besi, sedangkan di Lemnos kota Hephaistia memiliki tempat suci untuknya. Ia dipercaya menyembuhkan lewat tanah Lemnos, dan bangsa Romawi menyamakannya dengan Vulcan.
long_description.en: He was worshipped especially at Athens and Lemnos. At Athens he shared a temple and festivals with Athena, including the Chalkeia festival of the blacksmiths, while on Lemnos the city of Hephaistia had a sanctuary for him. Lemnian earth was believed to heal, and the Romans equated him with Vulcan.

cultural_context.id: Hephaestus dan Athena dipercaya mengajarkan manusia kerajinan yang memperindah hidup, sehingga manusia yang dulu tinggal di gua kini hidup damai di rumah sendiri menurut Himne Homerik 20. Kepincangannya mungkin cerminan kerasnya kondisi kerja pandai besi, menurut satu penafsiran, dan orang Yunani sering menaruh patung kecil mirip kurcaci sang dewa di dekat perapian. Asal-usulnya tidak jelas; ia mungkin berasal dari gagasan bahwa raja-raja awal juga harus menguasai kerajinan.
cultural_context.en: Hephaestus and Athena were believed to have taught men the crafts that embellish life, so that, according to Homeric Hymn 20, people now live peacefully in their own houses. His lameness may reflect the harsh working conditions of a blacksmith, according to one interpretation, and the Greeks often placed small dwarf-like statues of him near the hearth. His origins are obscure; he may derive from the idea that early kings should also master crafts.

who.id: Hephaestus adalah dewa Olimpus untuk api, pandai besi, dan kerajinan.
who.en: Hephaestus is the Olympian god of fire, smiths, and crafts.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari mitologi Yunani dan dipuja terutama di Athena dan Lemnos.
origin.en: He comes from Greek mythology and was worshipped especially at Athens and Lemnos.

role.id: Ia adalah pandai besi cemerlang bagi para dewa Olimpus.
role.en: He is the brilliant blacksmith of the Olympian gods.

famous_for.id: Ia paling dikenal sebagai pandai besi ilahi yang pincang, pembuat zirah Achilles dan jebakan bagi Hera dan Aphrodite.
famous_for.en: He is best known as the lame divine smith, maker of Achilles' armour and of traps for Hera and Aphrodite.

did_you_know.id: Dalam Iliad, Hephaestus ditopang pelayan perempuan dari emas yang punya pengertian, bicara, dan tenaga, serta membuat tripod berroda emas yang bergerak sendiri ke pertemuan para dewa.
did_you_know.en: In the Iliad, Hephaestus is supported by golden handmaidens who have understanding, speech, and strength, and makes golden-wheeled tripods that move by themselves into the gathering of the gods.

description.id: Ia menempa perisai bagi Achilles dari perunggu, timah, emas, dan perak, membuat tongkat kerajaan dan aegis Zeus serta helm Hermes, dan menyediakan zirah dan alat bagi para dewa.
description.en: He forges a shield for Achilles from bronze, tin, gold, and silver, makes the sceptre and aegis of Zeus and the helmet of Hermes, and provides armour and devices for the gods.

description.id: Ia membuat pelayan emas yang dapat berbicara dan cerdas, Talos dari perunggu, anjing penjaga, serta tripod yang bergerak sendiri.
description.en: He made gold maids who could speak and were intelligent, bronze Talos, watchdogs, and tripods that move by themselves.

description.id: Dalam Perang Troya ia mengalahkan dewa sungai Xanthos dengan api.
description.en: In the Trojan War he defeated the river god Xanthos with fire.

description.id: Ia menjebak Hera dalam singgasana terkutuk dan menjerat Aphrodite dan Ares dalam jaring rantai tak terlihat.
description.en: He trapped Hera in a cursed throne and ensnared Aphrodite and Ares in an invisible net of chains.

description.id: Tanah Lemnos dari tempat Hephaestus jatuh dipercaya menyembuhkan kegilaan, gigitan ular, dan pendarahan.
description.en: Lemnian earth from the spot where Hephaestus fell was believed to cure madness, snake bites, and haemorrhage.

description.id: Hephaestus berkaki pincang dan digambarkan sebagai satu-satunya dewa yang kurang sempurna; Homeros dan Hesiod menyebutnya "si pincang".
description.en: Hephaestus has a lame foot and is described as the only less-than-perfect god; Homer and Hesiod call him "the lame one".

title.en: The fall of Hephaestus from Olympus

role.id: Dewa yang dibuang dan dirawat dewi laut.
role.en: The god cast out and cared for by sea goddesses.

summary.id: Hephaestus dibuang dari Olimpus oleh Hera (atau Zeus menurut kisah lain), mendarat di Lemnos, dan dirawat Thetis dan Eurynome selama sembilan tahun di sebuah gua, tempat ia membuat berbagai perhiasan.
summary.en: Hephaestus was cast out of Olympus by Hera (or Zeus in other accounts), landed on Lemnos, and was cared for by Thetis and Eurynome for nine years in a grotto, where he made a variety of ornaments.

title.id: Singgasana Hera dan kembalinya ke Olimpus
title.en: Hera's throne and his return to Olympus

role.id: Pembuat singgasana yang menjerat ibunya.
role.en: The maker of the throne that trapped his mother.

summary.id: Hephaistos menjebak Hera dalam rantai tak terlihat pada singgasana buatannya. Dionysos menuntunnya yang mabuk anggur kembali ke Olimpus untuk membebaskan Hera, dan pernikahan dengan Aphrodite menjadi harga pembebasan.
summary.en: Hephaistos captured Hera in the invisible chains of a throne he built. Dionysos led him, under the influence of wine, back to Olympus to free Hera, and the wedding to Aphrodite was the price of release.

title.id: Jaring emas bagi Aphrodite dan Ares
title.en: The golden net for Aphrodite and Ares

role.id: Suami yang menjerat pasangan selingkuh dengan jaring buatannya.
role.en: The husband who ensnares the adulterous pair with his crafted net.

summary.id: Aphrodite dan Ares terperangkap dalam jaring emas buatan Hephaistos di ranjangnya; ia memanggil semua dewa Olimpus untuk menyaksikannya.
summary.en: Aphrodite and Ares were trapped in a golden net made by Hephaistos around his bed; he called all the Olympian gods to witness the spectacle.

role.id: Pandai besi yang membuatkan zirah atas permintaan Thetis.
role.en: The smith who makes the armour at Thetis's request.

summary.id: Atas permintaan Thetis, ibu Achilles, Hephaestus menyalakan dua puluh alat tiupnya dan menempa perisai besar dari perunggu, timah, emas, dan perak, dihias dengan bumi, langit, laut, matahari, dan bulan.
summary.en: At the request of Thetis, Achilles' mother, Hephaestus set his twenty bellows to work and forged a great shield from bronze, tin, gold, and silver, decorated with the earth, the heavens, the sea, the sun, and the moon.

role.id: Pembuat kalung yang membawa nasib buruk.
role.en: The maker of the ill-fated necklace.

summary.id: Hephaistos membuat kalung terkutuk Harmonia yang menjerumuskan keturunannya ke dalam rangkaian tragedi.
summary.en: Hephaistos made a necklace for Harmonia that was cursed; it doomed her descendants to a cycle of tragedy.

role.id: Pembuat perempuan pertama.
role.en: The maker of the first woman.

summary.id: Atas perintah Zeus, Hephaistos membuat Pandora, perempuan pertama, dari tanah liat.
summary.en: At the command of Zeus, Hephaistos crafted Pandora, the first woman, from clay.

role.id: Bidan yang membelah kepala Zeus.
role.en: The midwife who splits Zeus's head.

summary.id: Hephaistos membelah kepala Zeus dengan kapaknya agar Athena dapat lahir dari sana.
summary.en: Hephaistos split Zeus' head with his axe so that Athena might be born from there.

description.id: Pulau tempat Hephaestus mendarat setelah dilempar dari Olimpus dan tempat kota Hephaistia dengan tempat suci untuknya.
description.en: The island where Hephaestus landed after being thrown from Olympus, and the site of the city of Hephaistia with a sanctuary for him.

description.id: Kota dengan kuil bersama Hephaestus dan Athena serta festival Chalkeia para pandai besi.
description.en: The city with a temple shared by Hephaestus and Athena and the Chalkeia festival of the blacksmiths.

description.id: Gunung berapi di Sisilia yang dikaitkan dengan bengkel Hephaistos di bawahnya.
description.en: A volcano on Sicily associated with Hephaistos's workshop beneath it.

description.id: Tempat istana Hephaestus yang berisi bengkel, landasan, dan dua puluh alat tiup.
description.en: The place of Hephaestus's palace, containing his workshop, anvil, and twenty bellows.

title.en: Building of the Doric temple at Athens

description.id: Kuil Doric yang didedikasikan bersama bagi Hephaistos dan Athena dibangun sekitar 449 SM.
description.en: The Doric temple jointly dedicated to Hephaistos and Athena was built c. 449 BCE.

note.id: Ibu Hephaestus; ia dilempar dari Olimpus oleh ibunya dan menjebaknya dalam singgasana.
note.en: Hephaestus's mother; he was cast from Olympus by her and trapped her in a throne.

note.en: Hephaestus's father in the Homeric version; in another version there is no father.

note.en: Hephaestus's wife according to the Odyssey and other tellings; she was trapped with Ares in the net.

note.en: Hephaestus's wife in the Iliad.

note.en: Hephaestus's wife in Hesiod's Theogony.

note.en: Trapped with Aphrodite in Hephaistos's net.

note.en: Shares a temple and festivals at Athens and taught crafts to men.

note.id: Keturunan Hephaistos yang membunuh orang asing dengan gada besi.
note.en: Offspring of Hephaistos who killed strangers with an iron club.

claims.quote: is the Greek god of artisans, blacksmiths, carpenters, craftsmen, fire, metallurgy, metalworking, sculpture, and volcanoes.

statement.id: Hephaestus adalah dewa Yunani bagi api dan kerajinan logam.
statement.en: Hephaestus is a Greek god of fire and metal crafts.

claims.quote: He was depicted as a bearded man holding a hammer and tongs--the tools of a smith--and sometimes riding a donkey.

statement.id: Hephaestus digambarkan sebagai lelaki berjanggut dengan palu dan penjepit logam.
statement.en: Hephaestus is shown as a bearded man with hammer and tongs.

claims.quote: The crafting of the armour of Akhilleus (Achilles) at the request of the hero's mother Thetis.

statement.id: Hephaestus membuat zirah Achilles atas permintaan Thetis.
statement.en: Hephaestus made armor for Achilles at Thetis's request.

claims.quote: the god of fire, was, according to the Homeric account, the son of Zeus and Hera.

statement.id: Versi Homer menyebut Hephaestus putra Zeus dan Hera.
statement.en: In a Homeric version Hephaestus is a son of Zeus and Hera.

claims.quote: Later traditions state that he had no father, and that Hera gave birth to him independent of Zeus

statement.id: Versi lain menyatakan Hera melahirkan Hephaestus tanpa ayah.
statement.en: Other traditions say Hera bore Hephaestus without a father.

claims.quote: The capture of Hera in a cursed throne and his return to Olympos.

statement.id: Hephaestus menjebak Hera dalam singgasana terkutuk.
statement.en: Hephaestus trapped Hera in a cursed throne.

claims.quote: In Rome, he was equated with Vulcan.

statement.id: Bangsa Romawi menyamakan Hephaestus dengan Vulcan.
statement.en: Romans equated Hephaestus with Vulcan.

claims.quote: Hephaistos was particularly worshipped at Athens and Lemnos in the northeast Aegean.

statement.id: Hephaestus terutama dipuja di Athena dan Lemnos.
statement.en: Hephaestus was especially worshipped at Athens and Lemnos.

claims.quote: He was the brilliant blacksmith of the Olympian gods, for whom he fashioned magnificent houses, armour, and ingenious devices.

statement.id: Hephaestus menempa berbagai benda untuk dewa Olimpus.
statement.en: Hephaestus forged objects for Olympian gods.

claims.quote: HEPHAISTOS (Hephaestus) was the Olympian god of fire, smiths, craftsmen, metalworking, stonemasonry and sculpture.

statement.id: Hephaistos adalah dewa Olimpus untuk api, pandai besi, pengrajin, pengerjaan logam, pemahatan batu, dan seni patung.
statement.en: Hephaistos was the Olympian god of fire, smiths, craftsmen, metalworking, stonemasonry and sculpture.

claims.quote: Hephaestus is the god of fire, especially in so far as it manifests itself as a power of physical nature in volcanic districts, and in so far as it is the indispensable means in arts and manufactures

statement.id: Hephaestus adalah dewa api, terutama sebagai kekuatan alam di daerah vulkanik dan sebagai sarana yang tak tergantikan dalam seni dan kerajinan.
statement.en: Hephaestus is the god of fire, especially as a power of nature in volcanic districts and as the indispensable means in arts and manufactures.

claims.quote: His fall from Olympos in which he was cast away by Hera at birth.

statement.id: Salah satu kisah terkenalnya adalah jatuhnya dari Olimpus ketika Hera membuangnya saat lahir.
statement.en: One of his famous myths is his fall from Olympos, in which he was cast away by Hera at birth.

claims.quote: The adultery of his wife Aphrodite who was trapped with Ares in a golden net.

statement.id: Kisah perselingkuhan istrinya, Aphrodite, yang terperangkap bersama Ares dalam jaring emas.
statement.en: The story of the adultery of his wife Aphrodite, who was trapped with Ares in a golden net.

claims.quote: The crafting of Pandora, the first woman, at the command of Zeus.

statement.id: Hephaistos membuat Pandora, perempuan pertama, atas perintah Zeus.
statement.en: Hephaistos crafted Pandora, the first woman, at the command of Zeus.

claims.quote: The crafting of the cursed necklace of Harmonia which doomed her descendants to a cycle of tragedy.

statement.id: Ia membuat kalung terkutuk Harmonia yang menjerumuskan keturunannya ke dalam rangkaian tragedi.
statement.en: He crafted the cursed necklace of Harmonia which doomed her descendants to a cycle of tragedy.

claims.quote: The Trojan War in which he fought the river-god Skamandros (Scamander) with fire.

statement.id: Dalam Perang Troya ia melawan dewa sungai Skamandros (Scamander) dengan api.
statement.en: In the Trojan War he fought the river-god Skamandros (Scamander) with fire.

claims.quote: he seized him by the leg, and hulled him down from Olympus. Hephaestus was a whole day falling, but in the evening he came down in the island of Lemnos, where he was kindly received by the Sintians.

statement.id: Zeus menyambar kakinya dan melemparkannya dari Olimpus; Hephaestus jatuh sehari penuh dan mendarat di pulau Lemnos, tempat suku Sintian menyambutnya dengan ramah.
statement.en: Zeus seized him by the leg and hurled him down from Olympus; Hephaestus was a whole day falling and came down on the island of Lemnos, where he was kindly received by the Sintians.

claims.quote: But the marine divinities, Thetis and Eurynome, received him, and he dwelt with them for nine years in a grotto, surrounded by Oceanus, making for them a variety of ornaments.

statement.id: Dewi laut Thetis dan Eurynome menerimanya, dan ia tinggal bersama mereka selama sembilan tahun di sebuah gua, dikelilingi Oceanus, membuatkan berbagai perhiasan bagi mereka.
statement.en: The marine divinities Thetis and Eurynome received him, and he dwelt with them for nine years in a grotto, surrounded by Oceanus, making them a variety of ornaments.

claims.quote: In Olympus, Hephaestus had his own palace, imperishable and shining like stars: it contained his workshop, with the anvil, and twenty bellows, which worked spontaneously at his bidding.

statement.id: Di Olimpus, Hephaestus memiliki istana sendiri yang abadi dan berkilau seperti bintang, berisi bengkel dengan landasan dan dua puluh alat tiup yang bekerja sendiri atas perintahnya.
statement.en: In Olympus, Hephaestus had his own palace, imperishable and shining like stars, containing his workshop with the anvil and twenty bellows which worked spontaneously at his bidding.

claims.quote: In later accounts, the Cyclopes, Brontes, Steropes, Pyracmon, and others, are his workmen and servants, and his workshop is no longer represented as in Olympus, but in the interior of some volcanic isle.

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang lebih belakangan, para Cyclops (Brontes, Steropes, Pyracmon, dan lainnya) adalah pekerja dan pelayannya, dan bengkelnya tidak lagi di Olimpus melainkan di dalam sebuah pulau vulkanik.
statement.en: In later accounts the Cyclopes (Brontes, Steropes, Pyracmon, and others) are his workmen and servants, and his workshop is no longer in Olympus but in the interior of some volcanic isle.

claims.quote: The wife of Hephaestus also lived in his palace: in the Iliad she is called a Charis, in the Odyssey Aphrodite ... and in Hesiod's Theogony (945) she is named Aglaia.

statement.id: Istri Hephaestus tinggal di istananya: dalam Iliad ia disebut seorang Charis, dalam Odyssey Aphrodite, dan dalam Theogony karya Hesiod ia bernama Aglaia.
statement.en: The wife of Hephaestus also lived in his palace: in the Iliad she is called a Charis, in the Odyssey Aphrodite, and in Hesiod's Theogony she is named Aglaia.

claims.quote: Later writers describe his lameness as the consequence of his second fall, while Homer makes him lame and weak from his birth.

statement.id: Penulis yang lebih belakangan menggambarkan kepincangannya sebagai akibat jatuhnya yang kedua, sedangkan Homeros menjadikannya lumpuh dan lemah sejak lahir.
statement.en: Later writers describe his lameness as the consequence of his second fall, while Homer makes him lame and weak from his birth.

claims.quote: Lemnian earth (terra Lemnia) from the spot on which Hephaestus had fallen was believed to cure madness, the bites of snakes, and haemorrhage

statement.id: Tanah Lemnos dari tempat Hephaestus jatuh dipercaya dapat menyembuhkan kegilaan, gigitan ular, dan pendarahan.
statement.en: Lemnian earth from the spot where Hephaestus had fallen was believed to cure madness, the bites of snakes, and haemorrhage.

claims.quote: for, like her, he give skill to mortal artists, and, conjointly with her, he was believed to have taught men the arts which embellish and adorn life.

statement.id: Bersama Athena, Hephaestus dipercaya memberi keterampilan kepada seniman fana dan mengajarkan manusia seni-seni yang memperindah kehidupan.
statement.en: Like Athena, he gives skill to mortal artists and, together with her, was believed to have taught men the arts which embellish and adorn life.

claims.quote: With bright-eyed Athene he taught men glorious crafts throughout the world ... But now that they have learned crafts through Hephaistos the famed worker (klytotekhnes), easily they live a peaceful life in their own houses the whole year round.

statement.id: Menurut Himne Homerik 20, bersama Athene ia mengajarkan manusia kerajinan yang mulia; kini setelah belajar dari Hephaistos, manusia hidup damai di rumah sendiri sepanjang tahun.
statement.en: According to Homeric Hymn 20, with Athene he taught men glorious crafts throughout the world; now that they have learned crafts through Hephaistos, they live a peaceful life in their own houses the whole year round.

claims.quote: During the best period of Grecian art, he was represented as a vigorous man with a beard, and is characterised by his hammer or some other instrument, his oval cap, and the chiton, which leaves the right shoulder and arm uncovered.

statement.id: Pada masa terbaik seni Yunani, ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki kekar berjanggut, dengan palu atau alat lain, topi oval, dan chiton yang membuka bahu dan lengan kanan.
statement.en: During the best period of Greek art he was represented as a vigorous bearded man, characterised by his hammer or some other instrument, his oval cap, and the chiton leaving the right shoulder and arm uncovered.

claims.quote: The Greeks frequently placed small dwarf-like statues of the god near the hearth

statement.id: Orang Yunani sering menaruh patung kecil mirip kurcaci sang dewa di dekat perapian.
statement.en: The Greeks frequently placed small dwarf-like statues of the god near the hearth.

claims.quote: As an ingenious craftsman, Hephaistos is credited with making the sceptre and aegis of Zeus, the helmet of Hermes, secret locking doors for Hera's chambers, and even the lovely first woman, Pandora, who he sculpted out of clay.

statement.en: Hephaistos is credited with making the sceptre and aegis of Zeus, the helmet of Hermes, secret locking doors for Hera's chambers, and Pandora, the first woman, whom he sculpted out of clay.

claims.quote: He also manufactured automatons - gold maids who could speak and were intelligent - for himself, bronze Talos as a gift for King Minos of Crete, and watchdogs for Alcinous, king of Phaeacia.

statement.en: He also manufactured automatons: gold maids who could speak and were intelligent for himself, bronze Talos as a gift for King Minos of Crete, and watchdogs for Alcinous, king of Phaeacia.

claims.quote: Hephaistos had his workshop beneath volcanos such as Mount Etna on Sicily.

statement.id: Hephaistos memiliki bengkel di bawah gunung berapi seperti Gunung Etna di Sisilia.
statement.en: Hephaistos had his workshop beneath volcanoes such as Mount Etna on Sicily.

claims.quote: The god had a lame foot and so he was unique as the only less-than-perfect god.

statement.id: Sang dewa berkaki pincang sehingga unik sebagai satu-satunya dewa yang kurang sempurna.
statement.en: The god had a lame foot and so was unique as the only less-than-perfect god.

claims.quote: he is said to have been thrown from the heavens by his mother (or in other accounts by Zeus) because of his ugliness and on landing on the island of Lemnos, the god was crippled.

statement.id: Ia dikatakan dilempar dari langit oleh ibunya (atau menurut kisah lain oleh Zeus) karena kejelekannya, dan setelah mendarat di pulau Lemnos, sang dewa menjadi pincang.
statement.en: He is said to have been thrown from the heavens by his mother (or in other accounts by Zeus) because of his ugliness, and on landing on the island of Lemnos the god was crippled.

claims.quote: Hephaistos married the goddess Aphrodite. The unlikely union occurred as a result of Hephaistos capturing his mother Hera in the invisible chains of a throne he had built, and the wedding was the price of release.

statement.id: Hephaistos menikahi Aphrodite; persatuan itu terjadi karena ia menjebak ibunya, Hera, dalam rantai tak terlihat pada singgasana buatannya, dan pernikahan itu menjadi harga pembebasan.
statement.en: Hephaistos married Aphrodite; the union occurred because he captured his mother Hera in the invisible chains of a throne he had built, and the wedding was the price of release.

claims.quote: The scene is a popular one in Greek art and usually depicts Dionysos leading Hephaistos, under the influence of wine, back to Olympus to free the entrapped Hera.

statement.id: Adegan itu populer dalam seni Yunani dan biasanya menggambarkan Dionysos menuntun Hephaistos yang mabuk anggur kembali ke Olimpus untuk membebaskan Hera yang terjerat.
statement.en: The scene is popular in Greek art and usually shows Dionysos leading Hephaistos, under the influence of wine, back to Olympus to free the entrapped Hera.

claims.quote: The god even acted as midwife at the birth of Athena, splitting Zeus' head with his axe so that the goddess might be born from there.

statement.id: Sang dewa bahkan menjadi bidan saat kelahiran Athena dengan membelah kepala Zeus dengan kapaknya agar sang dewi lahir dari sana.
statement.en: The god even acted as midwife at the birth of Athena, splitting Zeus' head with his axe so that the goddess might be born from there.

claims.quote: Supporting the Achaeans in the Trojan War, he memorably fights and defeats the river god Xanthos with fire and produces magnificent armour and a shield of bronze, gold, silver, and tin for Achilles

statement.id: Mendukung bangsa Akhaia dalam Perang Troya, ia mengalahkan dewa sungai Xanthos dengan api dan membuat perisai dari perunggu, emas, perak, dan timah bagi Achilles.
statement.en: Supporting the Achaeans in the Trojan War, he fights and defeats the river god Xanthos with fire and produces a shield of bronze, gold, silver, and tin for Achilles.

claims.quote: Hephaistos' most notable offspring in Greek mythology were Erechtheus, the first king of Athens, and Periphetes, who lived near Epidaurus and famously killed passing strangers with an iron club.

statement.id: Keturunan Hephaistos yang paling terkenal dalam mitologi Yunani adalah Erechtheus, raja pertama Athena, dan Periphetes, yang tinggal dekat Epidaurus dan terkenal membunuh orang asing yang lewat dengan gada besi.
statement.en: Hephaistos' most notable offspring in Greek mythology were Erechtheus, the first king of Athens, and Periphetes, who lived near Epidaurus and famously killed passing strangers with an iron club.

claims.quote: The Doric temple built c. 449 BCE and sometimes known as the Hephaisteion or Thesium

statement.id: Kuil Doric yang dibangun sekitar 449 SM, kadang disebut Hephaisteion atau Thesium, didedikasikan bersama bagi sang dewa dan Athena di Athena.
statement.en: The Doric temple built c. 449 BCE, sometimes known as the Hephaisteion or Thesium, was jointly dedicated to the god and Athena in Athens.

claims.quote: blacksmiths would march through the city carrying their tools during the annual Chalkeia festival which honoured the pair of gods.

statement.id: Menurut Sophocles, para pandai besi berarak melewati kota membawa perkakas mereka pada festival tahunan Chalkeia yang menghormati sepasang dewa itu.
statement.en: According to Sophocles, blacksmiths would march through the city carrying their tools during the annual Chalkeia festival which honoured the pair of gods.

claims.quote: Hephaistos gave his name to the city of Hephaistia, which had a sanctuary dedicated to him.

statement.id: Di Lemnos, Hephaistos memberi namanya kepada kota Hephaistia, yang memiliki tempat suci untuknya.
statement.en: On Lemnos, Hephaistos gave his name to the city of Hephaistia, which had a sanctuary dedicated to him.

claims.quote: In ancient Greek art, Hephaistos is often depicted wearing a pilos or workman's hat and an exomis or workman's tunic. He also often holds tongs, an axe, hammer, saw, or chisel, and is frequently seen riding a mule side-saddle.
claims.locator: How Was Hephaistos Represented in Art?

statement.id: Dalam seni Yunani kuno, Hephaistos sering digambarkan memakai pilos (topi pekerja) dan exomis (tunik pekerja), memegang penjepit, kapak, palu, gergaji, atau pahat, dan sering menunggang bagal dengan duduk menyamping.
statement.en: In ancient Greek art, Hephaistos is often depicted wearing a pilos or workman's hat and an exomis or workman's tunic, holding tongs, an axe, hammer, saw, or chisel, and frequently riding a mule side-saddle.

claims.quote: The origins of Hephaistos are obscure but he probably derives from the common idea that early kings should also be masters at certain crafts, especially metalwork, and perhaps, too, magic (which would have included the manipulation of fire).

statement.id: Asal-usul Hephaistos tidak jelas, tetapi ia mungkin berasal dari gagasan umum bahwa raja-raja awal juga harus menguasai kerajinan tertentu, terutama pengerjaan logam, dan mungkin sihir (yang mencakup pengolahan api).
statement.en: The origins of Hephaistos are obscure, but he probably derives from the common idea that early kings should also be masters of certain crafts, especially metalwork, and perhaps magic (which would have included the manipulation of fire).

claims.quote: Both Homer and Hesiod describe Hephaistos as 'the cripple-foot god' and 'the lame one'.

statement.id: Homeros dan Hesiod sama-sama menyebut Hephaistos "dewa berkaki pincang" dan "si pincang".
statement.en: Both Homer and Hesiod describe Hephaistos as "the cripple-foot god" and "the lame one".

claims.quote: The god's physical problems may have been a reflection in myth of the reality of a blacksmith's harsh working conditions where repeated hammering and toxic fumes can take their toll on both mind and body.

statement.id: Masalah fisik sang dewa mungkin merupakan cerminan dalam mitos dari kerasnya kondisi kerja pandai besi, tempat pemukulan berulang dan asap beracun dapat merusak pikiran dan tubuh.
statement.en: The god's physical problems may have been a reflection in myth of the reality of a blacksmith's harsh working conditions, where repeated hammering and toxic fumes can take their toll on both mind and body.

claims.quote: came unto the house of Hephaestus, imperishable, decked with stars, preeminent among the houses of immortals, wrought all of bronze, that the crook-foot god himself had built him.

statement.id: Dalam Iliad, rumah Hephaestus abadi, bertabur bintang, dan seluruhnya dari perunggu, dibangun sendiri oleh dewa berkaki bengkok itu.
statement.en: In the Iliad, the house of Hephaestus is imperishable, decked with stars, and wrought all of bronze, built by the crook-foot god himself.

claims.quote: he was fashioning tripods, twenty in all, to stand around the wall of his well-builded hall, and golden wheels had he set beneath the base of each that of themselves they might enter the gathering of the gods at his wish and again return to his house, a wonder to behold.

statement.id: Dalam Iliad, Hephaestus membuat dua puluh tripod untuk dinding aulanya, masing-masing berroda emas sehingga dapat masuk sendiri ke pertemuan para dewa atas kehendaknya lalu kembali ke rumahnya.
statement.en: In the Iliad, Hephaestus was fashioning twenty tripods for the wall of his hall, each set on golden wheels so that of themselves they might enter the gathering of the gods at his wish and return to his house.

claims.quote: there moved swiftly to support their lord handmaidens wrought of gold in the semblance of living maids. In them is understanding in their hearts, and in them speech and strength

statement.id: Dalam Iliad, pelayan perempuan dari emas yang menyerupai gadis hidup bergerak menopang tuan mereka; mereka punya pengertian di hati serta bicara dan tenaga.
statement.en: In the Iliad, handmaidens wrought of gold in the semblance of living maids moved to support their lord; in them is understanding in their hearts, and speech and strength.

claims.quote: even she that saved me when pain was come upon me after I had fallen afar through the will of my shameless mother, that was fain to hide me away by reason of my lameness.

statement.id: Dalam Iliad, Hephaestus berkata Thetis menyelamatkannya setelah ia jatuh jauh atas kehendak ibunya yang tak tahu malu, yang ingin menyembunyikannya karena kepincangannya.
statement.en: In the Iliad, Hephaestus says Thetis saved him after he had fallen afar through the will of his shameless mother, who was fain to hide him away by reason of his lameness.

claims.quote: And the bellows, twenty in all, blew upon the melting-vats, sending forth a ready blast of every force, now to further him as he laboured hard, and again in whatsoever way Hephaestus might wish and his work go on.

statement.id: Dalam Iliad, dua puluh alat tiup meniupkan hembusan ke bejana peleburan, melayani Hephaestus sesuai kehendaknya selagi ia bekerja.
statement.en: In the Iliad, the twenty bellows blew upon the melting-vats, sending forth a ready blast, serving Hephaestus as he wished while his work went on.

claims.quote: First fashioned he a shield, great and sturdy, adorning it cunningly in every part, and round about it set a bright rim, threefold and glittering, and therefrom made fast a silver baldric. Five were the layers of the shield itself; and on it he wrought many curious devices with cunning skill.

statement.id: Dalam Iliad, Hephaestus pertama-tama membuat perisai besar dan kokoh yang dihias dengan cerdik di setiap bagiannya, dengan lima lapisan dan banyak hiasan yang unik.
statement.en: In the Iliad, Hephaestus first fashioned a great and sturdy shield adorned cunningly in every part, with five layers and many curious devices.

claims.quote: Therein he wrought the earth, therein the heavens therein the sea, and the unwearied sun, and the moon at the full

statement.id: Dalam Iliad, pada perisai itu Hephaestus menempa bumi, langit, laut, matahari yang tak kenal lelah, dan bulan purnama.
statement.en: In the Iliad, on the shield Hephaestus wrought the earth, the heavens, the sea, the unwearied sun, and the moon at the full.

short_description.id: Diana adalah dewi Romawi perburuan, bulan, dan kelahiran, pelindung hewan liar yang bersenjata busur dan disamakan dengan Artemis Yunani.
short_description.en: Diana is a Roman goddess of the hunt, the moon, and childbirth, patron of wild beasts, armed with a bow and identified with Greek Artemis.

long_description.id: Diana paling dikenal sebagai dewi perburuan Romawi, dengan rusa sebagai hewan suci. Ia juga dikaitkan dengan bulan, kesuburan, kelahiran, dan hewan liar, dan Britannica 1911 menambahkan bahwa ia menguasai hutan, dataran, air, dan perang. Dalam silsilah Romawi, ia putri Jupiter dan Latona serta saudari Apollo; tradisi Yunani menyamakannya dengan Artemis.
long_description.en: Diana is best known as the Roman hunt goddess, with the deer as her sacred animal. She is also linked to the moon, fertility, childbirth, and wild animals, and the 1911 Britannica adds that she presided over wood, plain, water, and war. Roman genealogy makes her the daughter of Jupiter and Latona and sister of Apollo, while Greek tradition identifies her with Artemis.

long_description.id: Ada dua gambaran asal-usulnya. Britannica 1911 menyebutnya dewi Italia kuno yang berdiri sendiri, karena namanya bentuk feminin dari Janus (Dianus), yang baru kemudian disamakan dengan Artemis. Sebagai dewi kelahiran ia dikenal dengan nama Lucina, dan sebagai dewi bulan ia disamakan dengan Hecate serta dipanggil "berwujud tiga".
long_description.en: Two pictures of her origin exist. The 1911 Britannica calls her an old, independent Italian goddess, since her name is the feminine form of Janus (Dianus), only later identified with Artemis. As goddess of childbirth she was known as Lucina, and as moon-goddess she was identified with Hecate and invoked as "three-formed".

long_description.id: Seni Romawi sering menggambarkan Diana dengan busur dan tabung panah, dan menurut sebagian besar riwayat keterampilannya setara dengan Apollo. Kisah-kisahnya mencakup Actaeon yang berubah menjadi rusa, Niobe, Endymion, Orion, dan Iphigenia; dalam banyak kisah itu ia digambarkan murka atau bersedih.
long_description.en: Roman art often portrays Diana with a bow and quiver, and according to most accounts her skill equaled Apollo's. Her stories include Actaeon transformed into a stag, Niobe, Endymion, Orion, and Iphigenia; in many of them she is shown angry or grieving.

long_description.id: Tempatnya yang paling termasyhur adalah hutan kecil di Aricia dekat Danau Nemi, tempat ia dipuja bersama Virbius dan dilayani pendeta yang disebut Rex Nemorensis. Di Roma, pemujaannya dibawa kaum plebeian Latin sehingga ia dianggap pelindung kelas bawah dan budak, dengan kuil terpenting di Aventine dan pesta pada idus Agustus.
long_description.en: Her most celebrated shrine was the grove at Aricia by Lake Nemi, where she was worshipped with Virbius and served by a priest called Rex Nemorensis. At Rome her cult was brought by Latin plebeians, so she was regarded as protectress of the lower classes and slaves, with her chief temple on the Aventine and a festival on the ides of August.

cultural_context.id: Karena pemujaannya dibawa ke Roma oleh kaum plebeian Latin, Diana dipandang sebagai pelindung kelas bawah dan terutama budak; pada hari penahbisan kuilnya di Aventine para budak berlibur.
cultural_context.en: Because her worship was brought to Rome by Latin plebeians, Diana was regarded as protectress of the lower classes and especially of slaves; on the dedication day of her Aventine temple the slaves kept holiday.

literal_meaning.id: bentuk feminin dari Janus (Dianus)
literal_meaning.en: the feminine form of Janus (Dianus)

who.id: Diana adalah dewi Romawi perburuan, bulan, dan kelahiran.
who.en: Diana is a Roman goddess of the hunt, the moon, and childbirth.

origin.id: Ia dewi Italia kuno yang kemudian disamakan dengan Artemis Yunani.
origin.en: She is an old Italian goddess later identified with the Greek Artemis.

role.id: Ia menjadi pelindung hewan liar, penolong dalam persalinan, dan pelindung kelas bawah di Roma.
role.en: She serves as patron of wild beasts, helper in childbirth, and protectress of the lower classes at Rome.

famous_for.id: Diana paling dikenal sebagai dewi perburuan dan karena kisah Actaeon.
famous_for.en: Diana is best known as the goddess of the hunt and for the story of Actaeon.

did_you_know.id: Pendeta Diana di Aricia, yang disebut Rex Nemorensis, adalah budak pelarian yang harus membunuh pendahulunya dalam duel untuk memenuhi syarat jabatan.
did_you_know.en: Diana's priest at Aricia, called Rex Nemorensis, was a runaway slave obliged to slay his predecessor in single combat to qualify for office.

description.id: Seni Romawi menggambarkannya bersenjata busur dan tabung panah, dan keterampilannya memanah setara dengan Apollo menurut sebagian besar riwayat.
description.en: Roman art depicts her armed with a bow and quiver, and her skill with the bow equaled Apollo's according to most accounts.

description.id: Dalam kisah-kisah itu Diana mengubah Actaeon menjadi rusa jantan dan mengubah para nimfa menjadi merpati.
description.en: In these stories Diana transforms Actaeon into a stag and turns the nymphs into pigeons.

description.id: Dalam kisah Perang Troya, ia menenangkan perairan sehingga kapal-kapal Yunani tidak dapat berlayar.
description.en: In the Trojan War story she stilled the waters so that the Greek ships could not sail.

description.id: Ketika Iphigenia hendak dikurbankan, Diana menggantikannya dengan seekor rusa.
description.en: When Iphigenia was about to be sacrificed, Diana replaced her with a deer.

description.id: Dalam kisah Endymion, Diana membuat pemuda itu tertidur abadi.
description.en: In the Endymion story Diana caused the youth to fall into an eternal sleep.

description.id: Bentuk pemujaan di hutan kecil Aricia, tempat Diana dipuja bersama Virbius dan dilayani Rex Nemorensis.
description.en: The cult form in the grove at Aricia, where Diana was worshipped with Virbius and served by the Rex Nemorensis.

description.id: Bentuk pemujaan Diana di lereng Gunung Tifata dengan nama Tifatina.
description.en: The cult of Diana on the slopes of Mount Tifata under the name Tifatina.

description.id: Diana sebagai Noctiluca memiliki tempat suci di Palatine yang diterangi sepanjang malam.
description.en: Diana as Noctiluca had a sanctuary on the Palatine kept lit throughout the night.

description.id: Sebagai dewi kelahiran, Diana dikenal dengan nama Lucina, seperti Juno.
description.en: As goddess of childbirth Diana was known as Lucina, like Juno.

role.id: Diana mengubah Actaeon menjadi rusa jantan setelah ia melihatnya mandi.
role.en: Diana transforms Actaeon into a stag after he sees her bathing.

summary.id: Menurut Ovid, Actaeon tanpa sengaja memasuki lembah keramat Diana ketika sang dewi mandi bersama para nimfa. Diana memercikkan air ke wajahnya dan memasang tanduk rusa pada dahinya; ia kemudian dicabik anjing-anjingnya sendiri, dan kemurkaan Diana baru reda setelah itu.
summary.en: In Ovid, Actaeon wandered into Diana's sacred valley while she bathed with her nymphs. Diana dashed water on his face and fixed a stag's horns on his brows; he was then torn by his own hounds, and her fury abated only after that.

role.id: Diana dan Apollo membunuh anak-anak Niobe atas perintah ibu mereka.
role.en: Diana and Apollo kill Niobe's children at their mother's command.

summary.id: Dalam kemarahannya, Latona memerintahkan Apollo dan Diana membinasakan seluruh 14 anak Niobe.
summary.en: In her rage, Latona ordered Apollo and Diana to slay all 14 of Niobe's offspring.

role.id: Diana membuat Endymion tertidur abadi.
role.en: Diana makes Endymion sleep eternally.

summary.id: Diana, yang memilih tetap perawan, membuat Endymion tertidur abadi karena takut kecantikannya rusak oleh kerja keras dan cuaca.
summary.en: Diana, who chose to remain a virgin, caused Endymion to fall into an eternal sleep, fearing his beauty might be marred by toil and exposure.

role.id: Diana menolong para nimfa dan berduka atas Orion.
role.en: Diana helps the nymphs and grieves for Orion.

summary.id: Diana mengubah para nimfa yang meminta bantuan menjadi merpati; dalam kisah lain ia mengenai Orion tanpa sadar dan dalam dukanya mengubah Orion dan Sirius menjadi rasi bintang.
summary.en: Diana turned the nymphs who asked for help into pigeons; in another tale she unknowingly hit Orion and in her grief turned Orion and Sirius into a constellation.

role.id: Diana menahan kapal Yunani lalu menyelamatkan Iphigenia.
role.en: Diana holds back the Greek ships and then saves Iphigenia.

summary.id: Diana menenangkan perairan sehingga kapal Yunani tidak dapat berlayar; ketika Iphigenia akan dikurbankan, ia menggantikannya dengan seekor rusa dan Iphigenia menjadi pendeta di kuilnya.
summary.en: Diana stilled the waters so the Greek ships could not sail; when Iphigenia was to be sacrificed she substituted a deer and Iphigenia became a priestess at her temple.
