text.id: namanya berasal dari masa Mikenai; tokoh Dua Belas Dewa Olimpus dalam tradisi arkais
text.en: name of Mycenaean origin; one of the Twelve Olympians in the archaic tradition

short_description.id: Ares adalah dewa perang dan keberanian Yunani, putra Zeus dan Hera, yang mewakili sisi perang yang brutal dan sering dikalahkan dalam mitos.
short_description.en: Ares is the Greek god of war and courage, son of Zeus and Hera, who stands for the brutal side of war and is often defeated in myth.

long_description.id: Ares adalah dewa perang dan keberanian Yunani, salah satu dari Dua Belas Dewa Olimpus dan putra Zeus dan Hera. Ia mewujudkan keberanian fisik yang diperlukan untuk menang perang, tetapi juga dapat melambangkan kebrutalan dan nafsu darah, berbeda dengan saudarinya Athena yang berfungsi pada strategi. Banyak orang Yunani bersikap mendua terhadapnya, dan salah satu sumber menyebutnya mungkin dewa Olimpus yang paling tidak populer.
long_description.en: Ares is the Greek god of war and courage, one of the Twelve Olympians and a son of Zeus and Hera. He embodies the physical valor needed for success in war but can also personify brutality and bloodlust, in contrast to his sister Athena, whose functions lie in strategy. Many Greeks were ambivalent toward him, and one source calls him perhaps the most unpopular Olympian.

long_description.id: Dalam seni Yunani kuno ia digambarkan sebagai prajurit dewasa berjanggut atau pemuda tanpa janggut dengan ketopong dan tombak, dengan zirah, perisai, dan kadang pedang. Ketopong adalah atribut utamanya, dan ia sulit dibedakan dari prajurit lain dalam seni. Hewan sucinya adalah ular, dan Naga Kolkhis penjaga Bulu Domba Emas disebut sebagai hewan Ares; ia juga dikaitkan dengan burung nasar dan beberapa burung hantu. Kisah-kisah paling terkenal tentangnya sering menampilkannya dikalahkan atau dipermalukan.
long_description.en: In ancient Greek art he is depicted as a mature bearded warrior or a beardless youth with helmet and spear, with armor, shield, and sometimes a sword. The helm is his main attribute, and he is hard to tell apart from other warriors in art. His sacred animal is the serpent, the Colchian Dragon guarding the Golden Fleece is named among his animals, and he is also associated with vultures and a few species of owl. The most famous stories about him often show him defeated or humiliated.

long_description.id: Hephaistos menjebak Ares dan Aphrodite dalam jaring emas; dari Aphrodite Ares memiliki Deimos, Phobos, dan Harmonia. Dalam Iliad ia memihak Troya, dilukai Diomedes yang dibantu Athena, dan meraung sekeras sembilan atau sepuluh ribu prajurit. Dalam kisah lain raksasa kembar mengurungnya dalam bejana perunggu sampai Hermes membebaskannya, dan Hercules, yang dilindungi Athena, melukainya dalam kisah Kyknos. Ia pernah diadili di Areiopagos di Athena atas pembunuhan Halirrhothius dan dibebaskan.
long_description.en: Hephaistos trapped Ares and Aphrodite in a golden net; by Aphrodite Ares had Deimos, Phobos, and Harmonia. In the Iliad he sides with Troy, is wounded by Diomedes helped by Athena, and bellows as loudly as nine or ten thousand warriors. In other tales twin giants confine him in a bronze jar until Hermes frees him, and Hercules, protected by Athena, wounds him in the Kyknos story. He was tried at the Areopagus in Athens for killing Halirrhothius and acquitted.

long_description.id: Orang Romawi mengidentifikasi Mars dengan Ares; Mars diberi kedudukan lebih penting sebagai pelindung leluhur bangsa Romawi dan disebut ayah Romulus dan Remus. Ares dipuja di Thrakia dan Asia Kecil, tempat ia menjadi dewa orakel di beberapa daerah, dan beberapa kota mengikat arcanya sebagai pelindung. Di Sparta ia diberi sapi atau ayam jantan sebagai kurban setelah pertempuran. Kultusnya di Aksum disebut lewat Maḥrem, yang dalam prasasti Yunani disebut Ares.
long_description.en: The Romans identified Mars with Ares; Mars was given a more important place as ancestral protector of the Roman people and is named father of Romulus and Remus. Ares was worshipped in Thrace and Asia Minor, where he was an oracular deity in some regions, and some cities bound his statue as their protector. In Sparta he received an ox or a rooster as sacrifice after battle. In Aksum Maḥrem was invoked as Ares in Greek inscriptions.

cultural_context.id: Banyak orang Yunani bersikap mendua terhadap Ares: ia mewujudkan keberanian fisik yang diperlukan untuk menang perang, tetapi juga kebrutalan dan nafsu darah. Keterkaitan dengannya memberi tempat dan benda sifat buas atau militeristik. Pemujaannya di Yunani tidak lazim, kuilnya biasanya dibangun di luar kota, dan beberapa kota mengikat arcanya sebagai pelindung.
cultural_context.en: Many Greeks were ambivalent toward Ares: he embodies the physical valor needed in war but also brutality and bloodlust. An association with him gives places and objects a savage or militarized quality. His worship in Greece was not common, his temples were usually built outside the towns, and some cities bound his statue as their protector.

literal_meaning.id: dihubungkan dengan ἀρή, "bencana, kehancuran, kutukan"
literal_meaning.en: traditionally connected with ἀρή, "bane, ruin, curse, imprecation"

who.id: Ares adalah dewa perang dan keberanian Yunani, salah satu dari Dua Belas Dewa Olimpus dan putra Zeus dan Hera.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari tradisi Yunani; namanya menunjukkan asal-usul Mikenai, dan sebagian orang menganggap ia berasal dari dewa Thrakia.
origin.en: He comes from Greek tradition; his name shows Mycenaean origins, and some think he originated as a Thracian deity.

famous_for.en: He is famous for his affair with Aphrodite exposed by Hephaistos's golden net and for being often defeated or humiliated in myth.

did_you_know.id: Areiopagos di Athena disebut sebagai "bukit Ares" dan konon tempat Ares diadili atas pembunuhan Halirrhothius.
did_you_know.en: The Areopagus in Athens is called the "mount of Ares" and was supposedly where Ares was tried for killing Halirrhothius.

role.en: Aphrodite's lover caught in the trap

summary.id: Ares berselingkuh dengan Aphrodite, tetapi suaminya Hephaistos menjebak keduanya dalam jaring emas dan mempermalukan mereka dengan memanggil para dewa lain menjadi saksi. Dalam Buku 8 Odyssey kisah ini diceritakan cukup rinci, dan hukuman bagi Ares adalah pengusiran sementara dari Gunung Olimpus.
summary.en: Ares was Aphrodite's lover, but her husband Hephaistos caught the two of them in a golden net and shamed them before the other gods, whom he summoned as witnesses. The tale is told in some detail in Book 8 of the Odyssey, and Ares' punishment was temporary banishment from Mount Olympus.

title.en: Ares imprisoned in a bronze jar

role.id: Dewa yang ditawan raksasa
role.en: The god taken captive by giants

summary.id: Raksasa kembar Otus dan Ephialtes mengurung Ares dalam bejana perunggu sampai Hermes membebaskannya. Iliad menyebut ia terikat tiga belas bulan, sedangkan sumber lain menyebut satu tahun.
summary.en: The twin giants Otus and Ephialtes confined Ares in a bronze jar until Hermes freed him. The Iliad says he lay bound for thirteen months, while another source says one year.

role.id: Pembunuh yang cemburu
role.en: The jealous killer

summary.id: Ketika Aphrodite jatuh cinta pada Adonis, Ares cemburu, menjelma babi hutan, dan membunuh pemuda itu saat berburu.
summary.en: When Aphrodite fell in love with Adonis, Ares grew jealous, transformed himself into a boar, and killed the youth while he was hunting.

role.id: Ayah yang mengubah bentuk anaknya
role.en: The father who transformed his daughter

summary.id: Ares mengubah putrinya Harmonia dan suaminya Kadmos dari Thebai menjadi ular dan membawa mereka ke Pulau-Pulau Orang Terberkati.
summary.en: Ares transformed his daughter Harmonia and her husband Kadmos of Thebes into serpents and had them carried to the Islands of the Blessed.

title.en: The trial of Ares at the Areiopagos

role.id: Terdakwa yang dibebaskan
role.en: The defendant who was acquitted

summary.id: Ares membunuh Hallirhothios, putra Poseidon, untuk membalas pemerkosaan putrinya Alkippe. Ia diadili di Areiopagos di Athena dan dibebaskan dari tuduhan pembunuhan.
summary.en: Ares killed Hallirhothios, son of Poseidon, in revenge for the rape of his daughter Alkippe. The Areiopagos court in Athens tried him and cleared him of murder.

title.en: The battle with Herakles over Kyknos

role.id: Ayah yang membela putranya dan kalah
role.en: The father who defended his son and lost

summary.id: Kyknos, putra Ares, menghadang peziarah menuju Delphi sehingga Apollo mengirim Hercules. Hercules membunuh Kyknos, Ares yang murka melawannya, tetapi dilukai sang pahlawan dan terpaksa kembali ke Olimpos.
summary.en: Kyknos, a son of Ares, waylaid pilgrims on their way to Delphi, so Apollo sent Hercules. Hercules killed Kyknos, and a furious Ares fought him but was wounded by the hero and forced back to Olympos.

role.id: Sekutu Troya yang dilukai Diomedes
role.en: Trojan ally wounded by Diomedes

summary.id: Dalam Iliad Ares mendukung bangsa Troya. Diomedes, dibantu Athena, melukainya dengan tombak sehingga ia meraung sekeras sembilan atau sepuluh ribu prajurit dan terbang kembali ke Olimpos. Dalam kisah lain Athena menjatuhkannya dengan batu besar, dan Zeus mengabaikan keluhannya tetapi menyuruh Paieon menyembuhkannya.
summary.en: In the Iliad Ares supports the Trojans. Diomedes, helped by Athene, wounds him with a spear so that he bellows as loudly as nine or ten thousand warriors and flies back to Olympos. Elsewhere Athena knocks him down with a large rock, and Zeus ignores his complaints but has Paieon heal him.

description.id: Singkapan batu alami di Athena yang agak jauh dari Akropolis; konon tempat Ares diadili dan dibebaskan atas pembunuhan Halirrhothius.
description.en: A natural rock outcrop in Athens some distance from the Acropolis, supposedly where Ares was tried and acquitted for killing Halirrhothius.

description.id: Dianggap tempat kelahiran Ares dan tempat ia berlindung setelah ejekan atas perselingkuhannya; Ares juga punya kultus di sana.
description.en: Considered Ares's birthplace and refuge after the mockery of his affair; Ares also had a cult there.

description.id: Kultus Ares tercatat di 29 lokasi di sana sejak abad ke-5 SM hingga masa Kekaisaran Romawi.
description.en: Cults of Ares are attested at 29 sites there from the 5th century BC into the Roman Imperial era.

description.id: Nama Ares menunjukkan asal-usul Mikenai.
description.en: The name Ares shows Mycenaean origins.

title.id: Pertempuran dengan Hercules di vas Attika
title.en: The battle with Hercules on Attic vases

description.id: Mitos pertempuran Ares dengan Hercules menjadi subjek populer vas Attika.
description.en: The myth of Ares' battle with Hercules was a popular subject for Attic vases.

description.id: Kultus Ares di Asia Kecil selatan tercatat sejak masa ini.
description.en: Cults of Ares in southern Asia Minor are attested from this time.

note.id: Ibu Ares.
note.en: Ares's mother.

note.id: Kekasih Ares; keduanya terperangkap jaring emas dan memiliki tiga anak.
note.en: Ares's lover; the pair were caught in the golden net and had three children.

note.id: Suami Aphrodite yang menjebak Ares dan Aphrodite dalam jaring emas.
note.en: Aphrodite's husband, who trapped Ares and Aphrodite in the golden net.

note.id: Saudari Ares yang mewakili strategi perang; dalam Iliad ia menjatuhkan Ares dengan batu besar.
note.en: Ares's sister, who stands for strategy in war; in the Iliad she knocks him out with a large rock.

note.id: Saudari Ares.
note.en: Ares's sister.

note.id: Saudari Ares.
note.en: Ares's sister.

note.id: Saudari Ares yang menyulut perang.
note.en: Ares's sister, who calls forth war.

note.en: Child of Ares and Aphrodite.

note.en: Daughter of Ares and Aphrodite.

note.en: One of Ares's Amazon-queen daughters.

note.en: Ares's nearest counterpart in Roman religion; the Romans identified Mars with Ares.

traditional.en: In Greek mythology Ares is a cruel and blood-thirsty god.

modern.id: Dalam karya sastra Renaisans dan Neoklasik, ia digantikan Mars, lambang romantis keberanian jantan.
modern.en: In Renaissance and Neoclassical literary works he is replaced by Mars, a romantic emblem of manly valor.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa orang Yunani bersikap mendua terhadap Ares, padahal ia dewa perang?
learning_questions.en: Why were the Greeks ambivalent toward Ares even though he was a god of war?

learning_questions.id: Apa perbedaan Ares dan Athena dalam cara mereka mewakili perang?
learning_questions.en: How do Ares and Athena differ in the way they represent war?

learning_questions.id: Mengapa Ares begitu sering dikalahkan atau dipermalukan dalam mitos?
learning_questions.en: Why is Ares so often defeated or humiliated in myth?

sources.author: Homer, trans. A. T. Murray

claims.quote: is the Greek god of war and courage. He is one of the Twelve Olympians, and the son of Zeus and Hera.

statement.id: Ares adalah dewa perang dan keberanian Yunani, salah satu dewa Olimpus dan putra Zeus serta Hera.
statement.en: Ares is a Greek god of war and courage, an Olympian and son of Zeus and Hera.

claims.quote: ARES was the Olympian god of war, battlelust, courage and civil order.

statement.id: Ares adalah dewa Olimpus yang berkaitan dengan perang dan keberanian.
statement.en: Ares is an Olympian deity associated with war and courage.

claims.quote: In ancient Greek Archaic and Classical art, Ares is most often depicted wearing full armour and helmet and carrying a shield and spear.
claims.locator: How is Ares Represented in Art?

statement.id: Ares digambarkan memakai zirah dan ketopong serta membawa perisai dan tombak.
statement.en: Ancient art shows Ares armored with helmet, shield, and spear.

claims.quote: Ares had an adulterous affair with the goddess Aphrodite but her husband Hephaistos trapped the pair in a golden net

statement.id: Hephaistos menjebak Ares dan Aphrodite dalam jaring emas.
statement.en: Hephaistos trapped Ares and Aphrodite in a golden net.

claims.quote: They imprisoned the god in a bronze jar (or cauldron) for one year and he was only freed through the intervention of Hermes.

statement.id: Raksasa kembar mengurung Ares di bejana perunggu sampai Hermes membebaskannya.
statement.en: Twin giants confined Ares in a bronze vessel until Hermes freed him.

claims.quote: The Romans identified their god Mars with the Greek Ares.

statement.id: Orang Romawi menyamakan Mars dengan Ares.
statement.en: Romans identified Mars with Ares.

claims.quote: In ancient Greek art he was depicted as either a mature, bearded warrior armed for battle, or a nude, beardless youth with a helm and spear.

statement.id: Penggambaran kuno Ares dapat berupa prajurit dewasa berjanggut atau pemuda berketopong dan tombak.
statement.en: Ancient depictions show Ares as a bearded warrior or a helmeted youth with spear.

claims.quote: The etymology of the name Ares is traditionally connected with the Greek word ἀρή (arē), the Ionic form of the Doric ἀρά (ara), "bane, ruin, curse, imprecation".

statement.id: Etimologi nama Ares secara tradisional dikaitkan dengan kata Yunani ἀρή (arē), bentuk Ionia dari ἀρά (ara) Doria, yang berarti "bencana, kehancuran, kutukan".
statement.en: The etymology of the name Ares is traditionally connected with the Greek word ἀρή (arē), the Ionic form of Doric ἀρά (ara), "bane, ruin, curse, imprecation".

claims.quote: Although Ares's name shows his origins as Mycenaean, his reputation for savagery was thought by some to reflect his likely origins as a Thracian deity.

statement.id: Nama Ares menunjukkan asal-usul Mikenai, tetapi reputasinya yang buas oleh sebagian orang dianggap mencerminkan asalnya sebagai dewa Thrakia.
statement.en: Ares's name shows Mycenaean origins, but his reputation for savagery was thought by some to reflect his likely origins as a Thracian deity.

claims.quote: Many Greeks were ambivalent towards him. He embodies the physical valor necessary for success in war but can also personify sheer brutality and bloodlust, in contrast to his sister Athena, whose martial functions include military strategy and generalship.

statement.id: Banyak orang Yunani bersikap mendua terhadap Ares: ia mewujudkan keberanian fisik yang diperlukan untuk menang perang, tetapi juga dapat melambangkan kebrutalan dan nafsu darah, berbeda dengan saudarinya Athena yang berfungsi pada strategi dan kepemimpinan militer.
statement.en: Many Greeks were ambivalent toward Ares: he embodies the physical valor needed for success in war but can also personify sheer brutality and bloodlust, in contrast to his sister Athena, whose martial functions include strategy and generalship.

claims.quote: An association with Ares endows places, objects, and other deities with a savage, dangerous, or militarized quality.

statement.id: Keterkaitan dengan Ares memberi tempat, benda, dan dewa lain sifat buas, berbahaya, atau militeristik.
statement.en: An association with Ares endows places, objects, and other deities with a savage, dangerous, or militarized quality.

claims.quote: Although there are many literary allusions to Ares's love affairs and children, he has a limited role in Greek mythology. When he does appear, he is often humiliated.

statement.id: Meski banyak sindiran sastra tentang asmara dan anak-anak Ares, perannya dalam mitologi Yunani terbatas, dan bila muncul ia sering dipermalukan.
statement.en: Although there are many literary allusions to Ares's love affairs and children, he has a limited role in Greek mythology, and when he appears he is often humiliated.

claims.quote: Enyalios was sometimes identified with Ares and sometimes differentiated from him as another war god with separate cult, even in the same town

statement.id: Enyalios kadang disamakan dengan Ares dan kadang dibedakan sebagai dewa perang lain dengan kultus tersendiri, bahkan di kota yang sama.
statement.en: Enyalios was sometimes identified with Ares and sometimes differentiated from him as another war god with a separate cult, even in the same town.

claims.quote: There was an archaic Spartan statue of Ares in chains in the temple of Enyalios (sometimes regarded as the son of Ares, sometimes as Ares himself), which Pausanias claimed meant that the spirit of war and victory was to be kept in the city.

statement.id: Ada arca arkais Ares dalam belenggu di kuil Enyalios di Sparta, yang menurut Pausanias berarti semangat perang dan kemenangan harus ditahan di kota itu.
statement.en: There was an archaic Spartan statue of Ares in chains in the temple of Enyalios, which Pausanias claimed meant the spirit of war and victory was to be kept in the city.

claims.quote: Some cities in Greece and several in Asia Minor held annual festivals to bind and detain him as their protector. In parts of Asia Minor, he was an oracular deity.

statement.id: Beberapa kota di Yunani dan beberapa di Asia Kecil mengadakan festival tahunan untuk mengikat dan menahan Ares sebagai pelindung mereka; di sebagian Asia Kecil ia menjadi dewa orakel.
statement.en: Some cities in Greece and several in Asia Minor held annual festivals to bind and detain him as their protector, and in parts of Asia Minor he was an oracular deity.

claims.quote: Still further away from Greece, the Scythians were said to ritually kill one in a hundred prisoners of war as an offering to their equivalent of Ares.

statement.id: Lebih jauh dari Yunani, bangsa Skithia dikatakan membunuh satu dari setiap seratus tawanan perang secara ritual sebagai persembahan bagi padanan Ares mereka.
statement.en: Further from Greece, the Scythians were said to ritually kill one in a hundred prisoners of war as an offering to their equivalent of Ares.

claims.quote: The later belief that ancient Spartans had offered human sacrifice to Ares may owe more to mythical prehistory, misunderstandings, and reputation than to reality.

statement.id: Kepercayaan belakangan bahwa orang Sparta kuno mengurbankan manusia kepada Ares mungkin lebih berasal dari prasejarah mitis, salah paham, dan reputasi daripada kenyataan.
statement.en: The later belief that ancient Spartans offered human sacrifice to Ares may owe more to mythical prehistory, misunderstandings, and reputation than to reality.

claims.quote: In the Trojan War, Aphrodite, protector of Troy, persuades Ares to take the Trojans' side. The Trojans lose, while Ares's sister Athena helps the Greeks to victory.

statement.id: Dalam Perang Troya, Aphrodite, pelindung Troya, membujuk Ares memihak bangsa Troya; Troya kalah sementara Athena, saudari Ares, membantu bangsa Yunani menang.
statement.en: In the Trojan War, Aphrodite, protector of Troy, persuades Ares to take the Trojans' side; the Trojans lose while Athena, Ares's sister, helps the Greeks to victory.

claims.quote: Ares's nearest counterpart in Roman religion is Mars, who was given a more important and dignified place in ancient Roman religion as ancestral protector of the Roman people and state.

statement.id: Padanan terdekat Ares dalam agama Romawi adalah Mars, yang diberi kedudukan lebih penting dan terhormat sebagai pelindung leluhur bangsa dan negara Romawi.
statement.en: Ares's nearest counterpart in Roman religion is Mars, who was given a more important and dignified place as ancestral protector of the Roman people and state.

claims.quote: In Africa, Maḥrem, the principal god of the kings of Aksum prior to the 4th century AD, was invoked as Ares in Greek inscriptions.

statement.id: Di Afrika, Maḥrem, dewa utama para raja Aksum sebelum abad ke-4 M, disebut sebagai Ares dalam prasasti Yunani.
statement.en: In Africa, Maḥrem, the principal god of the kings of Aksum before the 4th century AD, was invoked as Ares in Greek inscriptions.

claims.quote: Thrace was considered to be Ares's birthplace and his refuge after the affair with Aphrodite was exposed to the general mockery of the other gods.

statement.id: Thrakia dianggap tempat kelahiran Ares dan tempat ia berlindung setelah perselingkuhannya dengan Aphrodite menjadi bahan ejekan para dewa lain.
statement.en: Thrace was considered Ares's birthplace and his refuge after the affair with Aphrodite was exposed to the mockery of the other gods.

claims.quote: Like most Greek deities, Ares was given animal sacrifice; in Sparta, after battle, he was given an ox for a victory by stratagem, or a rooster for victory through onslaught.

statement.id: Seperti kebanyakan dewa Yunani, Ares menerima kurban hewan; di Sparta, setelah pertempuran ia diberi seekor sapi untuk kemenangan lewat siasat atau seekor ayam jantan untuk kemenangan lewat serbuan.
statement.en: Like most Greek deities, Ares received animal sacrifice; in Sparta after battle he was given an ox for a victory by stratagem or a rooster for victory through onslaught.

claims.quote: In literary works of these eras, Ares is replaced by the Roman Mars, a romantic emblem of manly valor rather than the cruel and blood-thirsty god of Greek mythology.

statement.id: Dalam karya sastra masa Renaisans dan Neoklasik, Ares digantikan Mars dari Romawi, lambang romantis keberanian jantan, bukan dewa Yunani yang kejam dan haus darah.
statement.en: In Renaissance and Neoclassical literary works Ares is replaced by the Roman Mars, a romantic emblem of manly valor rather than the cruel and blood-thirsty god of Greek mythology.

claims.quote: His cults in southern Asia Minor are attested from the 5th century BC and well into the later Roman Imperial era, at 29 different sites, and on over 70 local coin issues.

statement.id: Kultus Ares di Asia Kecil selatan tercatat sejak abad ke-5 SM hingga masa Kekaisaran Romawi, di 29 lokasi dan lebih dari 70 penerbitan koin lokal.
statement.en: His cults in southern Asia Minor are attested from the 5th century BC well into the Roman Imperial era, at 29 sites and on over 70 local coin issues.

claims.quote: The Areopagus ("mount of Ares"), a natural rock outcrop in Athens, some distance from the Acropolis, was supposedly where Ares was tried and acquitted by the gods for his revenge-killing of Poseidon's son, Halirrhothius, who had raped Ares's daughter Alcippe.

statement.id: Areopagus ("bukit Ares"), singkapan batu alami di Athena yang agak jauh dari Akropolis, konon tempat Ares diadili dan dibebaskan para dewa atas pembunuhan balas dendamnya terhadap Halirrhothius, putra Poseidon, yang memerkosa Alcippe, putri Ares.
statement.en: The Areopagus ("mount of Ares"), a natural rock outcrop in Athens some distance from the Acropolis, was supposedly where Ares was tried and acquitted by the gods for the revenge-killing of Poseidon's son Halirrhothius, who had raped Ares's daughter Alcippe.

claims.quote: Ares' main attribute was a peaked warrior's helm. Even in domestic scenes, such as feasts of the gods, he was depicted either wearing or holding his helm. The god's other attributes included a shield, a spear and sometimes a sheathed sword.

statement.id: Atribut utama Ares adalah ketopong prajurit berpuncak, bahkan dalam adegan rumah tangga seperti pesta para dewa; atribut lainnya perisai, tombak, dan kadang pedang bersarung.
statement.en: Ares' main attribute was a peaked warrior's helm, even in domestic scenes such as feasts of the gods; his other attributes included a shield, a spear, and sometimes a sheathed sword.

claims.quote: Ares can be quite difficult to identify in ancient Greek art as there is little to distinguish him from other warrior figures.

statement.id: Ares cukup sulit dikenali dalam seni Yunani kuno karena hanya sedikit yang membedakannya dari tokoh prajurit lain.
statement.en: Ares can be quite difficult to identify in ancient Greek art because little distinguishes him from other warrior figures.

claims.quote: Ares' sacred animal was the serpent. He was also associated with certain birds, such as the vulture and a few species of owl, which ancient augury identified as portents of war, sedition and ill-fortune.

statement.id: Hewan suci Ares adalah ular; ia juga dikaitkan dengan burung tertentu seperti burung nasar dan beberapa jenis burung hantu, yang menurut augury kuno menjadi pertanda perang, hasutan, dan nasib buruk.
statement.en: Ares' sacred animal was the serpent; he was also associated with certain birds such as the vulture and a few species of owl, which ancient augury identified as portents of war, sedition, and ill-fortune.

claims.quote: The most famous of the god's animals in myth were the Colchian Dragon, a serpent set by Ares to guard the Golden Fleece, and the Ismenian Dragon, a giant snake which guarded his sacred spring near Thebes.

statement.id: Hewan Ares yang paling terkenal dalam mitos adalah Naga Kolkhis, ular yang ia tempatkan untuk menjaga Bulu Domba Emas, dan Naga Ismenia, ular raksasa penjaga mata air sucinya dekat Thebai.
statement.en: The most famous of the god's animals in myth were the Colchian Dragon, a serpent set by Ares to guard the Golden Fleece, and the Ismenian Dragon, a giant snake guarding his sacred spring near Thebes.

claims.quote: Ares was a son of Zeus and Hera, King and Queen of the Gods, and brother of the goddesses Eileithyia and Hebe.

statement.id: Ares adalah putra Zeus dan Hera, raja dan ratu para dewa, serta saudara dewi Eileithyia dan Hebe.
statement.en: Ares was a son of Zeus and Hera, King and Queen of the Gods, and brother of the goddesses Eileithyia and Hebe.

claims.quote: Ares had three children by the goddess Aphrodite named Deimos (Fear), Phobos (Terror), and Harmonia (Harmony).

statement.id: Ares memiliki tiga anak dengan Aphrodite: Deimos (Ketakutan), Phobos (Kengerian), dan Harmonia (Keselarasan).
statement.en: Ares had three children by Aphrodite named Deimos (Fear), Phobos (Terror), and Harmonia (Harmony).

claims.quote: When Aphrodite fell in love with the handsome youth Adonis, the god grew jealous, transformed himself into a boar, and gorged the boy to death as he was out hunting.

statement.id: Ketika Aphrodite jatuh cinta pada pemuda tampan Adonis, Ares cemburu, menjelma babi hutan, dan membunuh pemuda itu saat berburu.
statement.en: When Aphrodite fell in love with the handsome youth Adonis, Ares grew jealous, transformed himself into a boar, and gored the boy to death while he was hunting.

claims.quote: Ares transformed his daughter Harmonia and her husband Kadmos (Cadmus) of Thebes into serpents and had them carried away to the Islands of the Blessed.

statement.id: Ares mengubah putrinya Harmonia dan suaminya Kadmos dari Thebai menjadi ular dan membawa mereka ke Pulau-Pulau Orang Terberkati.
statement.en: Ares transformed his daughter Harmonia and her husband Kadmos of Thebes into serpents and had them carried away to the Islands of the Blessed.

claims.quote: The god slew Hallirhothios to avenge the rape of his daughter Alkippe. He was tried at the court of the Areiopagos in Athens but acquitted of murder.

statement.id: Ares membunuh Hallirhothios untuk membalas pemerkosaan putrinya, Alkippe; ia diadili di pengadilan Areiopagos di Athena tetapi dibebaskan dari tuduhan pembunuhan.
statement.en: Ares slew Hallirhothios to avenge the rape of his daughter Alkippe; he was tried at the court of the Areiopagos in Athens but acquitted of murder.

claims.quote: During the battle between Herakles and Ares' villianous Kyknos (Cycnus), the god intervened but was wounded by the hero and forced to flee back to Olympos.

statement.id: Dalam pertempuran antara Herakles dan Kyknos yang jahat, putra Ares, sang dewa ikut campur tetapi dilukai sang pahlawan dan terpaksa kembali ke Olimpos.
statement.en: In the battle between Herakles and Ares' villainous son Kyknos, the god intervened but was wounded by the hero and forced to flee back to Olympos.

claims.quote: Ares actively supported his Amazon-queen daughters in their many wars and battles. The most celebrated of these was Penthesileia who joined the Trojan War.

statement.id: Ares aktif mendukung putri-putrinya yang menjadi ratu Amazon dalam banyak perang; yang paling terkenal adalah Penthesileia yang ikut dalam Perang Troya.
statement.en: Ares actively supported his Amazon-queen daughters in their many wars and battles; the most celebrated was Penthesileia, who joined the Trojan War.

claims.quote: During the course of the Trojan War, Ares, who had sided with the Trojans, was wounded by the Greek hero Diomedes who drove a spear into his side, sending him flying back to Olympos bellowing in pain.

statement.id: Dalam Perang Troya, Ares yang memihak Troya dilukai pahlawan Yunani Diomedes yang menusukkan tombak ke sisinya, sehingga ia terbang kembali ke Olimpos sambil meraung kesakitan.
statement.en: During the Trojan War, Ares, who had sided with the Trojans, was wounded by the Greek hero Diomedes, who drove a spear into his side, sending him flying back to Olympos bellowing in pain.

claims.quote: Ares, on the other hand, is nothing but the personification of bold force and strength, and not so much the god of war as of its tumult, confusion, and horrors. His sister Eris calls forth war, Zeus directs its course, but Ares loves war for its own sake
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus ini, Ares hanyalah personifikasi kekuatan yang berani, dan lebih sebagai dewa kegaduhan, kekacauan, dan kengerian perang; Eris menyulut perang, Zeus mengarahkannya, tetapi Ares mencintai perang demi perang itu sendiri.
statement.en: According to this dictionary, Ares is nothing but the personification of bold force and strength, less the god of war than of its tumult, confusion, and horrors; Eris calls forth war, Zeus directs its course, but Ares loves war for its own sake.

claims.quote: The warlike character of the tribes of Thrace led to the belief, that the god's residence was in that country, and here and in Scythia were the principal seats of his worship.

statement.en: The warlike character of the Thracian tribes led to the belief that the god's residence was in that country, and there and in Scythia were the principal seats of his worship.

claims.quote: The temples of this god were usually built outside the towns, probably to suggest the idea that he was to prevent enemies from approaching them.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Kuil-kuil Ares biasanya dibangun di luar kota, mungkin untuk menyiratkan bahwa ia akan mencegah musuh mendekat.
statement.en: The temples of this god were usually built outside the towns, probably to suggest that he was to prevent enemies from approaching them.

claims.quote: deadly Ares the spoil-winner himself. He held a spear in his hands and was urging on the footmen: he was red with blood as if he were slaying living men, and he stood in his chariot.

statement.id: Dalam Perisai Herakles karya Hesiodos, Ares digambarkan memegang tombak, mendorong pasukan pejalan kaki, merah oleh darah, dan berdiri di keretanya.
statement.en: In Hesiod's Shield of Heracles, Ares is shown holding a spear, urging on the footmen, red with blood, and standing in his chariot.

claims.quote: Ares, exceeding in strength, chariot-rider, golden-helmed, doughty in heart, shield-bearer, Saviour of cities, harnessed in bronze, strong of arm, unwearying, mighty with the spear, O defender of Olympos
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes (Homeric Hymn 8 to Ares)

statement.id: Himne Homerik 8 menyapa Ares sebagai yang luar biasa kuat, penunggang kereta, berketopong emas, pembawa perisai, penyelamat kota, berbaju perunggu, dan perkasa dengan tombak.
statement.en: Homeric Hymn 8 addresses Ares as exceeding in strength, chariot-rider, golden-helmed, shield-bearer, saviour of cities, harnessed in bronze, and mighty with the spear.

claims.quote: Ares was the Greek god of war. He was perhaps the most unpopular of all the Olympian gods because of his quick temper, aggressiveness, and unquenchable thirst for conflict.

statement.id: Ares adalah dewa perang Yunani dan mungkin paling tidak populer di antara para dewa Olimpus karena emosinya yang cepat naik, agresivitasnya, dan hausnya yang tak terpuaskan akan pertikaian.
statement.en: Ares was the Greek god of war and perhaps the most unpopular of the Olympian gods because of his quick temper, aggressiveness, and unquenchable thirst for conflict.

claims.quote: Described by Hesiod in his Theogony as 'shield-piercing Ares' and 'city-sacking Ares,' the god represented the more brutal and bloody side of battle, which was in contrast to Athena who represented the more strategic elements of warfare.

statement.id: Dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos, Ares disebut "Ares penembus perisai" dan "Ares penjarah kota", mewakili sisi pertempuran yang lebih brutal dan berdarah, berbeda dengan Athena yang mewakili unsur strategis perang.
statement.en: Described by Hesiod in the Theogony as "shield-piercing Ares" and "city-sacking Ares", he represented the more brutal and bloody side of battle, in contrast to Athena, who represented its more strategic elements.

claims.quote: Ares' son Kyknos was infamous for waylaying pilgrims on their way to the oracle at Delphi, and so earned the displeasure of Apollo, who sent Hercules to deal with him. Hercules killed Kyknos, and a furious Ares engaged the hero in a fight. However, Hercules was protected from harm by Athena and even managed to wound Ares.

statement.id: Kyknos, putra Ares, terkenal menghadang peziarah menuju orakel Delphi sehingga Apollo mengirim Hercules; Hercules membunuh Kyknos, Ares yang murka melawannya, tetapi Hercules dilindungi Athena dan bahkan berhasil melukai Ares.
statement.en: Ares' son Kyknos waylaid pilgrims to the oracle at Delphi, so Apollo sent Hercules; Hercules killed Kyknos, a furious Ares fought him, but Hercules was protected by Athena and even managed to wound Ares.

claims.quote: In Homer's version of the Trojan War in the Iliad, Ares supports the Trojans, sometimes even leading them in battle along with Hector.

statement.id: Dalam versi Homeros tentang Perang Troya di Iliad, Ares mendukung bangsa Troya, bahkan kadang memimpin mereka berperang bersama Hektor.
statement.en: In Homer's version of the Trojan War in the Iliad, Ares supports the Trojans, sometimes even leading them in battle along with Hector.

claims.quote: Ares is roundly beaten by Athena who, supporting the Achaeans, knocks him out with a large rock.

statement.id: Ares dikalahkan telak oleh Athena, yang membela bangsa Akhaia dan menjatuhkannya dengan batu besar.
statement.en: Ares is roundly beaten by Athena, who, supporting the Achaeans, knocks him out with a large rock.

claims.quote: Fleeing back to Olympus, Zeus ignores the complaints of Ares but instructs Paieon to heal his wound.

statement.en: Fleeing back to Olympus, Ares' complaints are ignored by Zeus, who nonetheless instructs Paieon to heal his wound.

claims.quote: Ares was not commonly worshipped but there were cult sites with temples dedicated to the god on Crete (he is mentioned in Linear B tablets from Knossos) and at Argos, Athens, Erythrae, Geronthrae, Megalopolis, Tegea, Therapne, and Troezen. He also had a cult in Thrace

statement.en: Ares was not commonly worshipped, but there were cult sites with temples on Crete (he is mentioned in Linear B tablets from Knossos) and at Argos, Athens, Erythrae, Geronthrae, Megalopolis, Tegea, Therapne, and Troezen, and he also had a cult in Thrace.

statement.en: Ares is sometimes shown riding a chariot pulled by fire-breathing horses; the myth of his battle with Hercules was a popular subject for Attic vases in the 6th century BCE.

statement.en: In Roman mythology Mars was also the father of Romulus and Remus, the legendary founders of Rome, and the city therefore achieved a sacred status.

claims.quote: In stories from Greek mythology, Ares was usually to be found in the company of his other children with Aphrodite, Phobos (Fear) and Deimos (Terror), with his sister Eris (Strife), and with his charioteer Ennyo.

statement.en: In Greek myths Ares was usually found in the company of his children by Aphrodite, Phobos and Deimos, his sister Eris (Strife), and his charioteer Ennyo.

claims.quote: Hephaistos managed to entrap the lovers in an ingenious bed, and the tale is told in some detail in Book 8 of Homer's Odyssey. Once caught, the punishment for Ares' indiscretion was temporary banishment from Mount Olympus.

statement.id: Hephaistos berhasil menjebak sepasang kekasih itu dalam ranjang yang cerdik, kisah yang diceritakan cukup rinci dalam Buku 8 Odyssey; hukuman bagi Ares adalah pengusiran sementara dari Gunung Olimpus.
statement.en: Hephaistos managed to entrap the lovers in an ingenious bed, a tale told in some detail in Book 8 of Homer's Odyssey; Ares' punishment was temporary banishment from Mount Olympus.

claims.quote: Next Diomedes, good at the war-cry, drave at Ares with his spear of bronze, and Pallas Athene sped it mightily against his nethermost belly, where he was girded with his taslets. There did he thrust and smite him, rending the fair flesh, and forth he drew the spear again. Then brazen Ares bellowed

statement.id: Dalam Iliad, Diomedes menusukkan tombak perunggu ke Ares dan Athena mengarahkannya ke perut bagian bawah Ares, tempat ia mengenakan pelindung; setelah tombak ditarik, Ares meraung.
statement.en: In the Iliad, Diomedes drives his bronze spear at Ares and Athene speeds it against Ares' lower belly where he is girded with his taslets; when the spear is drawn out, Ares bellows.

claims.quote: loud as nine thousand warriors or ten thousand cry in battle, when they join in the strife of the War-god; and thereat trembling came upon Achaeans alike and Trojans, and fear gat hold of them; so mightily bellowed Ares insatiate of war.

statement.id: Raungan Ares dalam Iliad sekeras teriakan sembilan atau sepuluh ribu prajurit dalam pertempuran, sehingga bangsa Akhaia dan Troya sama-sama gemetar.
statement.en: In the Iliad Ares' bellow is as loud as nine or ten thousand warriors crying in battle, and trembling comes upon Achaeans and Trojans alike.

short_description.id: Atlas adalah Titan Yunani yang dihukum Zeus menopang langit di bahunya; ia juga dikenang sebagai pengajar astronomi dan pemberi nama pegunungan di Afrika Utara.
short_description.en: Atlas is a Greek Titan whom Zeus condemned to hold up the heavens on his shoulders; he is also remembered as a teacher of astronomy and the namesake of a mountain range in North Africa.

long_description.id: Atlas adalah Titan dalam mitologi Yunani, putra Iapetus dan Clymene atau Themis, serta kakak Prometheus. Menurut sumber-sumber kuno, ia dihukum Zeus karena memimpin para Titan melawan dewa-dewa Olimpus, dan hukumannya adalah menopang langit di bahunya. Ada pula tradisi yang menyebutnya menjaga tiang-tiang yang memisahkan langit dan bumi, dan Hesiod menempatkannya di tanah Hesperides.
long_description.en: Atlas is a Titan of Greek myth, son of Iapetus and Clymene or Themis, and elder brother of Prometheus. According to ancient sources, Zeus punished him for leading the Titans against the Olympian gods by making him hold up the heavens on his shoulders. Other traditions have him guard the pillars that keep sky and earth apart, and Hesiod places him in the land of the Hesperides.

long_description.id: Atlas juga dilukiskan sebagai sosok yang melambangkan ketahanan, mengetahui kedalaman semua laut, dan mengajarkan astronomi kepada manusia. Aeschylus menyebutnya unggul dalam kekuatan besar dan mengerang di bawah kubah langit. Pindar menulis bahwa ia masih bergulat dengan beban itu, sementara Zeus telah membebaskan para Titan.
long_description.en: Atlas is also portrayed as a figure who personified endurance, knew the depths of all the seas, and taught mankind astronomy. Aeschylus calls him pre-eminent in mighty strength, groaning beneath the vault of heaven. Pindar writes that he still struggles with the burden, while Zeus set the Titans free.

long_description.id: Kisah paling terkenal tentang Atlas melibatkan Hercules dan apel Hesperides. Hercules sementara memikul langit agar Atlas dapat mengambil apel, lalu menipunya agar memikul beban itu kembali. Dalam kisah lain, Perseus menggunakan kepala Medusa untuk mengubah Atlas, yang kurang ramah, menjadi gunung batu; tradisi yang lebih kemudian mengaitkannya dengan Pegunungan Atlas di Afrika Utara.
long_description.en: The most famous story about Atlas involves Hercules and the apples of the Hesperides. Hercules temporarily took the sky so Atlas could fetch the apples, then tricked him into taking the burden back. In another story, Perseus uses Medusa's head to turn the inhospitable Atlas into a stone mountain; later tradition links him with the Atlas Mountains of North Africa.

long_description.id: Seni Yunani menampilkan Atlas sejak abad ke-6 SM, dan Pausanias menggambarkannya pada peti Kypselos membawa apel Hesperides. Seni Helenistik serta Romawi sering menggambarkannya membungkuk menahan bola di bahunya. Nama Atlas juga diberikan kepada pegunungan, samudra, dan kumpulan peta besar, dan Plato menyebutnya raja pertama Atlantis.
long_description.en: Greek art shows Atlas from the 6th century BCE, and Pausanias describes him on the chest of Cypselus carrying the apples of the Hesperides. Hellenistic and Roman art often depicts him bent under a globe on his shoulders. His name was also given to a mountain range, an ocean and large collections of maps, and Plato calls him the first king of Atlantis.

cultural_context.id: Atlas melambangkan sifat ketahanan dan dikenal sebagai dewa yang mengajarkan astronomi, ilmu yang dipakai pelaut untuk navigasi dan petani untuk mengukur musim.
cultural_context.en: Atlas personified endurance and was known as the god who taught astronomy, a skill used by sailors for navigation and by farmers to measure the seasons.

literal_meaning.en: The name perhaps means 'suffering' or 'very enduring'.

claims.quote: In Greek mythology, the Titan Atlas was responsible for bearing the weight of the heavens on his shoulders, a burden given to him as punishment by Zeus.

statement.id: Atlas adalah Titan Yunani yang dihukum Zeus untuk menopang langit.
statement.en: Atlas is a Greek Titan punished by Zeus to hold up the heavens.

claims.quote: Atlas was the son of the Titans Iapetus and Clymene (or Themis) and the elder brother of Epimetheus, Menoetius, and Prometheus.

statement.id: Atlas adalah putra Iapetus dan Clymene atau Themis, serta saudara Prometheus.
statement.en: Atlas is a son of Iapetus and Clymene or Themis and brother of Prometheus.

claims.quote: Atlas was given the task of holding up the heavens as punishment from Zeus for leading the Titans in their battle with the Olympian Gods for control of the heavens.

statement.id: Atlas dihukum karena memimpin para Titan melawan dewa Olimpus.
statement.en: Atlas was punished for leading the Titans against the Olympian gods.

claims.quote: Hesiod in his Theogony also describes Atlas as holding up the heavens and locates him in the land of the Hesperides

statement.id: Hesiod menempatkan Atlas di tanah Hesperides sambil menopang langit.
statement.en: Hesiod locates Atlas in the land of the Hesperides holding up the heavens.

claims.quote: Following the advice of Prometheus, Hercules asked Atlas (in some versions the father of the Hesperides) to get him the apples while he, with the help of Athena, took the world onto his shoulders for a while

statement.id: Hercules meminta Atlas mengambil apel Hesperides dan sementara menggantikan bebannya.
statement.en: Hercules asked Atlas to fetch the Hesperides' apples while temporarily taking his burden.

claims.quote: However, the wily Hercules tricked the god into swapping places temporarily while the hero got himself some cushions to more easily bear the tremendous weight.

statement.id: Hercules menipu Atlas agar kembali menanggung bebannya.
statement.en: Hercules tricked Atlas into resuming his burden.

claims.quote: As punishment he was forced to guard the pillars of heaven or to hold up the sky itself.

statement.id: Ada tradisi yang menyebut Atlas menjaga tiang langit atau menopang langit.
statement.en: Traditions say Atlas guarded heaven's pillars or held up the sky.

claims.quote: It was here that, in punishment for his gross lack of hospitality, the Titan was transformed from a shepherd into a huge rock mountain by Perseus using the head of the Gorgon Medusa with her deadly stare.

statement.id: Dalam versi lain, Perseus mengubah Atlas menjadi gunung batu dengan kepala Medusa.
statement.en: In another account, Perseus turned Atlas into a mountain with Medusa's head.

claims.quote: In Hellenistic and Roman times, Atlas is frequently represented in his now familiar position with bent knees and back, straining to hold the globe on his shoulders.

statement.id: Seni Helenistik dan Romawi menggambarkan Atlas membungkuk menahan bola di bahunya.
statement.en: Hellenistic and Roman art depicts Atlas straining to hold a globe on his shoulders.

claims.quote: Atlas was the Titan god who bore the sky aloft. He personified the quality of endurance

statement.id: Atlas adalah dewa Titan yang menopang langit dan melambangkan sifat ketahanan.
statement.en: Atlas was the Titan god who bore the sky aloft and personified the quality of endurance.

claims.quote: Atlas was also the God who instructed mankind in the art of Astronomy, a tool which was used by sailors in navigation and farmers in measuring the Seasons.

statement.id: Atlas juga dikenal sebagai dewa yang mengajarkan manusia ilmu astronomi, yang dipakai pelaut untuk navigasi dan petani untuk mengukur musim.
statement.en: Atlas was also the god who instructed mankind in astronomy, used by sailors for navigation and by farmers to measure the seasons.

claims.quote: Atlas the baleful; he knows the depths of all the seas, and he, no other, guards (or holds) the tall pillars that keep the sky and earth apart.
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: Homer, Odyssey 1.52 ff

statement.id: Odyssey karya Homer menyebut Atlas mengetahui kedalaman semua laut dan menjaga (atau memegang) tiang-tiang tinggi yang memisahkan langit dan bumi.
statement.en: Homer's Odyssey says Atlas knows the depths of all the seas and guards (or holds) the tall pillars that keep sky and earth apart.

claims.quote: Atlas, pre-eminent in mighty strength, who moans as he supports the vault of heaven on his back.
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: Aeschylus, Prometheus Bound 407 ff

statement.id: Prometheus Bound karya Aeschylus menggambarkan Atlas sebagai yang unggul dalam kekuatan besar, mengerang sambil menopang kubah langit di punggungnya.
statement.en: Aeschylus's Prometheus Bound describes Atlas as pre-eminent in mighty strength, moaning as he supports the vault of heaven on his back.

claims.quote: Does not even now great Atlas struggle to bear up the weight of heaven, far from his fathers' land and his possessions? But almighty Zeus set free the Titanes (Titans)
claims.locator: Classical literature quotes: Pindar, Pythian Ode 4.290 ff

statement.id: Pindar menulis bahwa Atlas masih bergulat menopang beban langit jauh dari tanah ayahnya, tetapi Zeus yang mahakuasa membebaskan para Titan.
statement.en: Pindar writes that Atlas still struggles to bear the weight of heaven far from his fathers' land, but almighty Zeus set the Titans free.

claims.quote: Herakles agreed, but by a trick gave the sphere back to Atlas. On the advise of Prometheus he asked Atlas to take the sky while he put a cushion on his head.
claims.locator: Atlas & the labours of Heracles: Pseudo-Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 2.119-120

statement.id: Menurut Pseudo-Apollodorus, Herakles menyetujui tawaran Atlas lalu dengan tipu daya mengembalikan bola langit kepadanya, dengan alasan hendak meletakkan bantalan di kepala.
statement.en: According to Pseudo-Apollodorus, Heracles agreed but by a trick gave the sphere back to Atlas, asking him to take the sky while he put a cushion on his head.

claims.quote: These apples were not, as some maintain, in Libya, but rather were with Atlas among the Hyperboreans.
claims.locator: Atlas & the labours of Heracles: Pseudo-Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 2.114

statement.id: Pseudo-Apollodorus menyatakan apel emas itu bukan di Libya, melainkan bersama Atlas di antara bangsa Hyperborea.
statement.en: Pseudo-Apollodorus states the golden apples were not in Libya but with Atlas among the Hyperboreans.

claims.quote: Atlas too is supporting, just as the story has it, heaven and earth upon his shoulders; he is also carrying the apples of the Hesperides.
claims.locator: Atlas & the labours of Heracles: Pausanias, Description of Greece 5.18.4

statement.id: Pausanias menggambarkan Atlas pada peti Kypselos menopang langit dan bumi di bahunya sambil membawa apel Hesperides.
statement.en: Pausanias describes Atlas on the chest of Cypselus supporting heaven and earth on his shoulders while carrying the apples of the Hesperides.

claims.quote: Atlas, so huge, became a mountain; beard and hair were changed to forests, shoulders were cliffs, hands ridges
claims.locator: Atlas turned to stone by Perseus: Ovid, Metamorphoses 4.627 ff

statement.id: Dalam Metamorphoses karya Ovid, Atlas yang sangat besar berubah menjadi gunung: janggut dan rambutnya menjadi hutan, bahunya tebing, tangannya punggung bukit.
statement.en: In Ovid's Metamorphoses, the huge Atlas becomes a mountain: his beard and hair turn to forests, his shoulders to cliffs, his hands to ridges.

claims.quote: The daughters of Atlas were the star-nymphe Pleaides and Hyades, and his son, the beautiful youth Hyas.

statement.id: Putri-putri Atlas adalah Pleiades dan Hyades, nimfa bintang, dan putranya adalah pemuda tampan Hyas.
statement.en: Atlas's daughters were the star-nymphs the Pleiades and Hyades, and his son was the beautiful youth Hyas.

claims.quote: Atlas had worked out the science of astrology to a degree surpassing others and had ingeniously discovered the spherical arrangement of the stars, and for that reason was generally believed to be bearing the entire firmament upon his shoulders.
claims.locator: Rationalisation of the Atlas myth: Diodorus Siculus 4.26.2

statement.id: Diodorus Siculus memberi tafsir rasional: Atlas menguasai ilmu bintang dan menemukan susunan bola bintang, sehingga dipercaya memikul seluruh cakrawala di bahunya.
statement.en: Diodorus Siculus offers a rationalised reading: Atlas mastered the science of the stars and discovered their spherical arrangement, so he was believed to bear the whole firmament on his shoulders.

claims.quote: With a name perhaps conveying the meaning 'suffering' or 'very enduring,'

statement.id: Nama Atlas mungkin bermakna 'menderita' atau 'sangat tahan'.
statement.en: The name Atlas perhaps conveys the meaning 'suffering' or 'very enduring'.

claims.quote: Atlas was the father of the nymph Calypso and the seven Pleiades.

statement.id: Atlas adalah ayah nimfa Calypso dan tujuh Pleiades.
statement.en: Atlas was the father of the nymph Calypso and the seven Pleiades.

claims.quote: Later tradition, including Herodotus, associates the god with the Atlas Mountains in North Africa.

statement.id: Tradisi yang lebih kemudian, termasuk Herodotus, mengaitkan Atlas dengan Pegunungan Atlas di Afrika Utara.
statement.en: Later tradition, including Herodotus, associates Atlas with the Atlas Mountains in North Africa.

claims.quote: In Greek art, Atlas is, from the 6th century BCE, often featured in depictions of the labours of Hercules, most notably in a metope from the Temple of Zeus at Olympia (c. 460 BCE) where he stands in the gardens of the Hesperides.

statement.id: Dalam seni Yunani sejak abad ke-6 SM, Atlas sering muncul dalam penggambaran kerja keras Hercules, terutama pada metope Kuil Zeus di Olympia (sekitar 460 SM) tempat ia berdiri di taman Hesperides.
statement.en: In Greek art from the 6th century BCE, Atlas often appears in depictions of the labours of Hercules, most notably on a metope from the Temple of Zeus at Olympia (c. 460 BCE) where he stands in the gardens of the Hesperides.

claims.quote: For Plato, he was the eponymous first king of Atlantis, and this giant of a god also gave his name to a huge mountain range in Northern Africa, the great Atlantic Ocean and any large collection of maps.

statement.id: Bagi Plato, Atlas adalah raja pertama Atlantis; namanya juga dipakai untuk pegunungan besar di Afrika Utara, Samudra Atlantik, dan kumpulan peta besar.
statement.en: For Plato, Atlas was the eponymous first king of Atlantis; his name was also given to a huge mountain range in Northern Africa, the Atlantic Ocean and any large collection of maps.

claims.quote: This story may go back to the 5th century BCE.

statement.id: Kisah Atlas diubah menjadi gunung oleh Perseus mungkin berasal dari abad ke-5 SM.
statement.en: The story of Perseus turning Atlas into a mountain may go back to the 5th century BCE.

claims.quote: A surname of Atlas, describing him as the sufferer or bearer of heaven
claims.locator: Encyclopedia: Telamon (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Telamon adalah nama julukan Atlas yang menggambarkannya sebagai penderita atau pemikul langit.
statement.en: Telamon is a surname of Atlas describing him as the sufferer or bearer of heaven.

summary.id: Atlas menopang langit di bahunya sebagai hukuman Zeus.
summary.en: Atlas holds up the heavens on his shoulders as punishment from Zeus.

summary.id: Tradisi lain menyebutnya menjaga tiang langit (juga dalam Odyssey Homer).
summary.en: Other traditions say he guards the pillars of heaven (also in Homer's Odyssey).

summary.en: Hesiod locates Atlas in the land of the Hesperides.

summary.en: Pseudo-Apollodorus says the apples were with Atlas among the Hyperboreans, not in Libya.

text.id: Salah satu dewa Romawi tertua; dikaitkan dengan Juno Regina sejak abad ke-5 SM
text.en: One of the oldest Roman deities; associated with Juno Regina from the fifth century BCE

short_description.id: Juno adalah dewi Romawi pelindung negara dan seluruh segi kehidupan perempuan, istri sekaligus saudari Jupiter, yang dikenal lewat julukan seperti Regina, Lucina, Sospita, dan Moneta.
short_description.en: Juno is a Roman goddess who protected the state and every aspect of women's lives, wife and sister of Jupiter, known by epithets such as Regina, Lucina, Sospita and Moneta.

long_description.id: Juno adalah dewi utama Romawi yang melindungi negara secara keseluruhan sekaligus menjaga semua segi kehidupan perempuan, terutama perempuan yang menikah secara sah. Ia termasuk dewa Romawi tertua dan salah satu dari tiga dewa awal bersama Jupiter dan Minerva. Ia adalah istri dan saudari Jupiter, sering dipadankan dengan Hera dari Yunani; satu sumber menegaskan bahwa Juno dalam sastra Latin bukanlah dewi Romawi yang sejati karena pengaruh Yunani itu.
long_description.en: Juno was a principal Roman goddess who protected the nation as a whole and watched over every aspect of women's lives, especially legally married women. She was among the oldest Roman deities and one of the three original gods with Jupiter and Minerva. She was Jupiter's wife and sister and is often equated with the Greek Hera; one source stresses that the Juno of Latin literature is not the true Roman deity because of that Greek influence.

long_description.id: Juno punya banyak julukan yang menunjukkan perannya. Sebagai Juno Regina ia ratu dan pelindung negara dengan kuil di Aventine dan di Capitoline; sebagai Juno Lucina ia dewi kelahiran, dan di kuilnya semua simpul harus dilepas agar persalinan tidak terhambat. Sebagai Juno Sospita, dewa utama Lanuvium, ia pelindung perempuan dan negara yang digambarkan bersenjata dan berjubah kulit kambing. Sebagai Juno Moneta, kuilnya di Arx berdekatan dengan percetakan uang, dan kata "money" berasal dari namanya.
long_description.en: Juno had many epithets showing her roles. As Juno Regina she was queen and protector of the state, with temples on the Aventine and the Capitoline; as Juno Lucina she was goddess of childbirth, and at her temple all knots had to be untied so that delivery would not be hindered. As Juno Sospita, chief deity of Lanuvium, she protected women and the state and was pictured armed and wearing a goatskin. As Juno Moneta her temple on the Arx stood beside the mint, and the word "money" comes from her name.

long_description.id: Dalam seni, kehadiran merak menandai sosok Juno, dan merak disebut sebagai hewan sucinya. Angsa-angsanya dipelihara di Capitoline dan menurut legenda memperingatkan Roma saat bangsa Galia menyerbu pada 390 SM. Festival Matronalia pada 1 Maret dirayakan untuknya; para matron mempersembahkan sesaji dan suami memberi hadiah kepada istri. Asal festival itu diterangkan secara berbeda: sebagai ulang tahun Mars atau sebagai peringatan berakhirnya Perang Romawi-Sabin.
long_description.en: In art the presence of a peacock identifies Juno, and the peafowl is called her sacred animal. Her geese were kept on the Capitoline and, according to legend, warned Rome when the Gauls attacked in 390 BCE. The Matronalia on March 1 was celebrated for her; matrons made offerings and husbands gave presents to their wives. The festival's origin is explained differently: as the birthday of Mars or as the anniversary of the end of the Roman-Sabine War.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Aeneas karya Vergilius, Juno menjadi antagonis: ia mencintai Carthage, kota yang diramalkan akan dihancurkan Roma, dan berusaha menghalangi Aeneas, termasuk dengan badai di laut yang gagal ketika Neptunus ikut campur. Di Carthage ia diidentifikasi dengan dewi Tanit.
long_description.en: In Virgil's story of Aeneas, Juno is the antagonist: she loved Carthage, the city prophesied to be destroyed by Rome, and tried to block Aeneas, including with a storm at sea that failed when Neptune interfered. At Carthage she was identified with the goddess Tanit.

cultural_context.id: Juno menaungi seluruh kehidupan perempuan Romawi: sebagaimana setiap laki-laki punya genius, setiap perempuan punya Juno, dan perempuan memujanya pada semua saat penting dalam hidup. Ia juga dipandang sebagai pelindung ilahi komunitas.
cultural_context.en: Juno watched over the life of Roman women: just as every man had his genius, every woman had her Juno, and women worshipped her at all the critical moments of life. She is also regarded as the divine protectress of the community.

literal_meaning.id: Belum pasti: biasanya dianggap bentuk singkat Jovino dari akar div "bersinar"; ada pula usul dari iuven- "muda".
literal_meaning.en: Uncertain: usually taken as a shortened form of Jovino from a root div "shining"; another proposal derives it from iuven- "youth".

who.id: Juno adalah dewi Romawi pelindung negara dan kehidupan perempuan.
who.en: Juno is the Roman goddess who protected the state and women's lives.

origin.id: Ia termasuk dewa Romawi tertua, dipuja di Quirinal lalu Capitoline bersama Jupiter dan Minerva.
origin.en: She is among the oldest Roman deities, honored on the Quirinal and later the Capitoline with Jupiter and Minerva.

famous_for.en: She is known as Juno Regina, wife of Jupiter, and as the antagonist in the story of Aeneas.

did_you_know.en: The word "money" comes from Moneta, an epithet of Juno; her temple on the Arx stood next to the Roman mint.

note.en: Greek goddess often equated with Juno.

note.en: Juno's Etruscan counterpart.

note.id: Dewi yang diidentifikasi dengan Juno di Carthage.
note.en: The goddess identified with Juno at Carthage.

note.en: Worshipped with Juno and Jupiter on the Quirinal and in the Capitoline Triad.

note.en: Juno's son, the god of war.

note.en: Janus, god of passages and beginnings, is often named Iunonius after Juno.

note.en: In Virgil's story there is little love between Juno and Aeneas.
