statement.en: More specifically, Saraswati's son is the rishi (sage) Sarasvata, who, nourished by his mother's bountiful waters, withstood the Great Drought of Hindu mythology and survived as the definitive repository of the Vedas.

claims.quote: In Hindu art, Saraswati is usually depicted as a graceful youth with white skin. She most often wears a white sari (which symbolises purity) which has a blue border.

statement.id: Dalam seni Hindu, Saraswati biasanya digambarkan sebagai remaja anggun berkulit putih, paling sering berkain sari putih (lambang kesucian) bertepi biru.
statement.en: In Hindu art Saraswati is usually shown as a graceful youth with white skin, most often in a white sari (symbolizing purity) with a blue border.

claims.quote: As with many Hindu deities, Saraswati is often depicted with four arms, each holding a symbolic object. In the left hands she can carry a palm-leaf manuscript and ritual water vessel. In the upper right hand she holds a white lotus flower

statement.id: Seperti banyak dewa Hindu, Saraswati sering digambarkan berlengan empat, masing-masing memegang benda lambang; di tangan kiri ia dapat membawa manuskrip daun lontar dan bejana air ritual, dan di tangan kanan atas ia memegang teratai putih.
statement.en: Like many Hindu deities, Saraswati is often shown with four arms, each holding a symbolic object; in the left hands she can carry a palm-leaf manuscript and a ritual water vessel, and in the upper right hand she holds a white lotus.

claims.quote: Alternatively, she may be shown riding her vehicle (vahana), either a swan or goose.

statement.id: Ia juga dapat ditampilkan menunggang kendaraannya (wahana), yaitu angsa atau soang.
statement.en: She may also be shown riding her vehicle (vahana), either a swan or a goose.

claims.quote: Sarasvati is also worshipped as the goddess of learning in Jainism and by some Buddhist sects.

statement.id: Sarasvati juga dipuja sebagai dewi ilmu dalam Jainisme dan oleh beberapa sekte Buddha.
statement.en: Sarasvati is also worshipped as the goddess of learning in Jainism and by some Buddhist sects.

claims.quote: She with her might, like one who digs for lotus-stems, hath burst with her strong waves the ridges of the hills.

statement.id: Dalam himne Rigveda (terjemahan Griffith), Sarasvati dengan kekuatannya menjebol punggung bukit dengan ombaknya yang deras, seperti orang yang menggali batang teratai.
statement.en: In a Rigveda hymn (Griffith's translation), Sarasvati with her might bursts the ridges of the hills with her strong waves, like one who digs for lotus stems.

claims.quote: Thou hast discovered rivers for the tribes of men, and, rich in wealth! made poison flow away from them.

statement.id: Dalam himne Rigveda yang sama, Sarasvati dipuji karena menemukan sungai-sungai bagi suku-suku manusia dan, kaya akan harta, mengalirkan racun menjauh dari mereka.
statement.en: The same Rigveda hymn praises Sarasvati for discovering rivers for the tribes of men and, rich in wealth, making poison flow away from them.

claims.quote: Thou castest down, Sarasvati, those who scorned the Gods, the brood of every Brsaya skilled in magic arts.

statement.id: Dalam himne itu, Sarasvati dikatakan menjatuhkan mereka yang menghina para dewa, yaitu keturunan setiap Brsaya yang mahir ilmu sihir.
statement.en: In the hymn, Sarasvati is said to cast down those who scorned the Gods, the brood of every Brsaya skilled in magic arts.

claims.quote: Seven-sistered, sprung from threefold source, the Five Tribes' prosperer, she must be

statement.id: Dalam himne itu, Sarasvati disebut bersaudara tujuh, berasal dari tiga sumber, dan pemakmur Lima Suku.
statement.en: In the hymn, Sarasvati is called seven-sistered, sprung from a threefold source, and the prosperer of the Five Tribes.

claims.quote: Although one of the most important Hindu gods, Brahma is rarely actively worshipped. In mythology, this is explained as a result of a curse from Saraswati.

statement.id: Meski salah satu dewa Hindu terpenting, Brahma jarang dipuja secara aktif; dalam mitologi hal ini dijelaskan sebagai akibat kutukan Saraswati.
statement.en: Although one of the most important Hindu gods, Brahma is rarely actively worshipped; in mythology this is explained as the result of a curse from Saraswati.

summary.id: Dalam mitologi Hindu, Saraswati adalah istri Brahma.
summary.en: In Hindu mythology Saraswati is the wife of Brahma.

summary.id: Menurut sebagian tradisi, termasuk kaum Waisnawa Bengal, ia mula-mula istri Vishnu.
summary.en: According to some traditions, including the Bengal Vaisnavas, she was first the wife of Vishnu.

text.id: Periode Amarna, sekitar 1353-1336 SM
text.en: Amarna Period, c. 1353-1336 BCE

short_description.id: Aten adalah dewa matahari Mesir kuno berwujud cakram matahari dengan sinar berujung tangan, dipuja sebagai dewa utama pada masa Akhenaten.
short_description.en: Aten is an ancient Egyptian sun god shown as a sun disk with rays ending in hands, worshipped as the principal deity under Akhenaten.

long_description.id: Aten adalah dewa matahari Mesir kuno yang digambarkan sebagai cakram matahari, dengan sinar yang berujung tangan dan menawarkan kehidupan kepada raja serta perempuan terdekatnya. Kata aten sendiri berarti "cakram", dan pada mulanya Aten merupakan salah satu aspek Ra. Pada masa Amenhotep III ia dipuja luas, tetapi sumber berbeda menilai kedudukannya sebelum Akhenaten, sebagai dewa matahari yang lebih kecil atau sebagai dewa pencipta terkemuka.
long_description.en: Aten is an ancient Egyptian sun god shown as a sun disk, with rays ending in hands that offer life to the king and the women nearest to him. The word aten itself means "disc", and Aten was originally an aspect of Ra. He was widely worshipped under Amenhotep III, although sources differ on his standing before Akhenaten, calling him either a minor solar deity or a preeminent creator deity.

long_description.id: Pada masa Akhenaten, Aten disembah sebagai dewa utama dan Akhenaten mendirikan Amarna sebagai pusat keyakinannya. Pembaruan ini mengecualikan kultus dewa lain, dan himne masa Amarna berbeda secara radikal karena menyingkirkan dewa-dewa lain secara sistematis. Himne Agung kepada Aten menjadi sumber utama untuk memahami perubahan itu. Dalam himne itu Aten dipuji sebagai pemberi kehidupan yang menumbuhkan benih, menyingkirkan kegelapan, dan membuat musim serta banjir.
long_description.en: Under Akhenaten, Aten was worshipped as the principal deity and Akhenaten founded Amarna as a center for his beliefs. The reform excluded the cult of other deities, and the Amarna hymn is radically different in systematically excluding other gods. The Great Hymn to the Aten is the principal source for understanding the change. In that hymn Aten is praised as the giver of life who makes seed grow, removes the darkness, and makes the seasons and floods.

long_description.id: Kuil Aten di Amarna terbuka dan tidak beratap, dengan ruang luas serta altar persembahan. Dalam prasasti, Aten memelihara rakyat melalui Akhenaten, sehingga keluarga kerajaan menjadi perantara pemujaannya. Sarjana berbeda pendapat apakah agama ini monoteisme, monolatri, atau henoteisme.
long_description.en: The temples of Aten at Amarna were open and unroofed, with vast spaces and altars for offerings. In inscriptions Aten cares for the people through Akhenaten, making the royal family intermediaries for his worship. Scholars disagree on whether the religion was monotheism, monolatry, or henotheism.

long_description.id: Setelah Akhenaten wafat, Tutankhamun memindahkan ibu kota dari Akhetaten, membuka kembali kuil-kuil bagi dewa lain, dan mulai memulihkan praktik keagamaan terdahulu.
long_description.en: After Akhenaten died, Tutankhamun moved the capital away from Akhetaten, reopened the temples to other gods, and began restoring the earlier religious practices.

cultural_context.id: Dalam prasasti masa Amarna, Aten digambarkan memelihara rakyat melalui Akhenaten, sehingga keluarga kerajaan berperan sebagai perantara pemujaan Aten.
cultural_context.en: In Amarna-period inscriptions the Aten is shown caring for the people through Akhenaten, so that the royal family act as intermediaries for the Aten's worship.

description.id: Sinarnya berujung tangan yang menawarkan kehidupan, dan Himne Agung memujinya sebagai pemberi napas bagi semua ciptaannya. Menurut himne itu, makhluk hidup ketika ia bersinar dan mati ketika ia beristirahat.
description.en: His rays end in hands offering life, and the Great Hymn praises him as the one who gives breath to all he made. According to the hymn, beings live when he shines and die when he rests.

name.en: Creator and moulder of the earth

description.id: Atenisme menyebut Aten menciptakan semua negeri dan manusia, dan Himne Agung menyebutnya membentuk bumi sesuai kehendaknya seorang diri.
description.en: Atenism holds that Aten created all countries and people, and the Great Hymn says he moulds the earth to his wish alone.

description.id: Himne Agung menggambarkan Aten menyingkirkan kegelapan dan memberikan sinarnya saat fajar, sementara sinarnya mengikat negeri-negeri sampai batas ciptaannya.
description.en: The Great Hymn describes Aten removing the darkness and granting his rays at daybreak, while his rays bind the lands to the limit of his creation.

description.en: Under Amenhotep III Aten was depicted as a falcon-headed god like Ra, unlike the sun disk with hand-ended rays of the Amarna period.

title.en: The Great Hymn to the Aten

role.id: Aten adalah dewa yang dipuji dalam himne itu.
role.en: Aten is the god praised in the hymn.

summary.id: Himne ini memuji Aten yang terbit dari cakrawala, jauh namun sinarnya ada di bumi, menyingkirkan kegelapan, memberi kehidupan, dan menyediakan banjir bagi negeri-negeri. Prasastinya tertulis di dinding makam Ay di Amarna dan menjadi sumber utama tentang pembaruan agama masa Akhenaten.
summary.en: The hymn praises Aten rising from the horizon, distant yet with rays on earth, removing the darkness, giving life, and providing floods for the lands. Its inscription is on a wall of the courtier Ay at Amarna and is the principal source on the religious reform of Akhenaten's reign.

statement.id: Menurut Himne Agung, negeri terwujud oleh tindakan Aten; makhluk hidup ketika ia bersinar dan mati ketika ia beristirahat.
statement.en: According to the Great Hymn the land comes into being by Aten's action; beings live when he has shone and die when he rests.

claims.quote: It is inscribed in thirteen columns of hieroglyphs on the west wall of the courtier Ay at Amarna.
claims.locator: The Great Hymn to the Aten

statement.id: Himne Agung tertulis dalam tiga belas kolom hieroglif pada dinding barat makam pejabat istana Ay di Amarna.
statement.en: The Great Hymn is inscribed in thirteen columns of hieroglyphs on the west wall of the courtier Ay at Amarna.

claims.quote: Aten, also Aton, Atonu, or Itn ... was the focus of Atenism, the religious system formally established in ancient Egypt by the late Eighteenth Dynasty pharaoh Akhenaten.

statement.id: Aten, juga ditulis Aton, Atonu, atau Itn, menjadi pusat Atenisme, sistem keagamaan yang dibentuk secara resmi di Mesir kuno oleh firaun Akhenaten.
statement.en: Aten, also written Aton, Atonu, or Itn, was the focus of Atenism, the religious system formally established in ancient Egypt by the pharaoh Akhenaten.

claims.quote: The worship of Aten and the coinciding rule of Akhenaten are major identifying characteristics of a period within the Eighteenth Dynasty referred to as the Amarna Period (c. 1353 – 1336 BCE).

statement.id: Pemujaan Aten dan pemerintahan Akhenaten menjadi ciri utama masa dalam Dinasti Kedelapan Belas yang disebut Periode Amarna (sekitar 1353-1336 SM).
statement.en: The worship of Aten and Akhenaten's rule are major identifying features of the Eighteenth Dynasty period called the Amarna Period (c. 1353-1336 BCE).

claims.quote: The word Aten appears in the Old Kingdom as a noun meaning "disc" which referred to anything flat and circular; the sun was called the "disc of the day" where Ra was thought to reside.

statement.id: Kata Aten muncul pada masa Kerajaan Lama sebagai kata benda yang berarti "cakram", yaitu apa saja yang datar dan bundar; matahari disebut "cakram siang" tempat Ra diyakini bersemayam.
statement.en: The word Aten appears in the Old Kingdom as a noun meaning "disc", anything flat and circular; the sun was called the "disc of the day" where Ra was thought to reside.

claims.quote: The Aten was the disc of the sun and originally an aspect of Ra, the sun god in traditional ancient Egyptian religion.

statement.id: Aten adalah cakram matahari dan pada mulanya merupakan salah satu aspek Ra, dewa matahari dalam agama Mesir kuno tradisional.
statement.en: The Aten was the disc of the sun and originally an aspect of Ra, the sun god of traditional ancient Egyptian religion.

claims.quote: While Aten was the preeminent creator deity of a pantheon of ancient Egyptian gods under Amenhotep III, it was not until his successor that Aten would be the only god acknowledged via state worship.

statement.id: Pada masa Amenhotep III, Aten adalah dewa pencipta terkemuka dalam panteon Mesir; baru pada penerusnya Aten menjadi satu-satunya dewa dalam pemujaan negara.
statement.en: Under Amenhotep III Aten was the preeminent creator deity of a pantheon; only under his successor did Aten become the only god acknowledged in state worship.

claims.quote: Aten was extensively worshipped as a solar deity during the reign of Amenhotep III where it was depicted as a falcon-headed god like Ra.

statement.id: Pada masa Amenhotep III, Aten dipuja luas sebagai dewa matahari dan digambarkan berkepala elang seperti Ra.
statement.en: During the reign of Amenhotep III, Aten was widely worshipped as a solar deity and depicted as a falcon-headed god like Ra.

claims.quote: The Aten created all countries and people, and cares for every creature.

statement.id: Dalam Atenisme, Aten menciptakan semua negeri dan manusia serta memelihara setiap makhluk.
statement.en: In Atenism, the Aten created all countries and people and cares for every creature.

claims.quote: In inscriptions, like the Hymn to the Aten and the King, the Aten is depicted as caring for the people through Akhenaten, placing the royal family as intermediaries for the worship of the Aten.

statement.id: Dalam prasasti seperti Himne kepada Aten dan Raja, Aten digambarkan memelihara rakyat melalui Akhenaten, sehingga keluarga kerajaan menjadi perantara pemujaan Aten.
statement.en: In inscriptions such as the Hymn to the Aten and the King, the Aten is shown caring for the people through Akhenaten, making the royal family intermediaries for his worship.

claims.quote: Straying significantly from the tradition of ancient Egyptian temples being hidden and more enclosed the further one went into the site, temples of Aten were open and did not have roofs in order to allow the rays of the sun inside.

statement.id: Berbeda dari tradisi kuil Mesir yang tertutup, kuil Aten terbuka dan tidak beratap agar sinar matahari dapat masuk.
statement.en: Unlike the traditional enclosed Egyptian temple, temples of the Aten were open and unroofed so that the sun's rays could enter.

claims.quote: Not long after his death, one of Akhenaten's Eighteenth Dynasty successors, Tutankhamun, reopened the state temples to other Egyptian gods and re-positioned Amun as the pre-eminent solar deity.

statement.id: Tak lama setelah Akhenaten wafat, penerusnya Tutankhamun membuka kembali kuil-kuil negara bagi dewa-dewa Mesir lain dan menempatkan Amun sebagai dewa matahari utama.
statement.en: Not long after Akhenaten's death, his successor Tutankhamun reopened the state temples to other gods and re-positioned Amun as the pre-eminent solar deity.

claims.quote: Others see Akhenaten as a practitioner of an Aten monolatry, as he did not actively deny the existence of other gods; he simply refrained from worshipping any but the Aten. Other scholars call the religion henotheistic.

statement.id: Sebagian sarjana memandang Akhenaten menjalankan monolatri Aten karena ia tidak menyangkal dewa lain, hanya tidak memujanya; sarjana lain menyebut agama itu henoteistik.
statement.en: Some see Akhenaten as practising an Aten monolatry since he did not deny other gods but simply refrained from worshipping them; other scholars call the religion henotheistic.

claims.quote: instituted the first known monotheistic state religion in the world and, according to some, monotheism itself.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Akhenaten mendirikan agama negara monoteistik pertama yang diketahui di dunia dan, menurut sebagian orang, monoteisme itu sendiri.
statement.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Akhenaten instituted the first known monotheistic state religion in the world and, according to some, monotheism itself.

short_description.id: Cronus atau Kronos adalah Titan dalam mitologi Yunani, raja para Titan dan dewa waktu yang menggulingkan ayahnya, menelan anak-anaknya, lalu digulingkan Zeus.
short_description.en: Cronus or Kronos is a Titan of Greek mythology, king of the Titans and a god of time, who deposed his father, swallowed his children, and was overthrown by Zeus.

long_description.id: Cronus atau Kronos adalah Titan, putra bungsu Uranus dan Gaia. Menurut Hesiodos, ia anak yang terakhir lahir dan paling mengerikan, dan ia membenci ayahnya. Dengan sabit, ia menggulingkan Uranus dan menjadi raja pertama dunia; Theoi menyebutnya raja para Titan dan dewa waktu, terutama waktu sebagai kekuatan yang menghancurkan dan melahap segalanya. Ia biasanya digambarkan membawa harpe, arit, atau sabit.
long_description.en: Cronus or Kronos is a Titan, the youngest son of Uranus and Gaia. According to Hesiod, he was the last born and most terrible of the children, and he hated his father. With a sickle he deposed Uranus and became the world's first king; Theoi calls him king of the Titans and a god of time, especially time as a destructive, all-devouring force. He is usually depicted with a harpe, scythe, or sickle.

long_description.id: Pemerintahan Cronus dianggap Zaman Keemasan, masa tanpa penyakit, kelaparan, atau kesulitan, dan ia juga memerintah Kepulauan Orang Berbahagia. Ia menikahi Rhea dan mempunyai enam anak: Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, dan Zeus. Karena takut digulingkan anaknya, Cronus menelan setiap anak yang lahir; Hesiodos mencatat bahwa ia mengetahui takdir itu dari Bumi dan Langit.
long_description.en: Cronus's rule was regarded as the Golden Age, a time without disease, hunger, or hardship, and he also ruled the Isles of the Blessed. He married Rhea and had six children: Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, and Zeus. Fearing overthrow by his children, Cronus swallowed each child as it was born; Hesiod records that he learned this fate from Earth and Heaven.

long_description.id: Rhea menyelamatkan Zeus dengan menyembunyikannya di Kreta dan memberi Cronus batu terbungkus kain untuk ditelan. Zeus kemudian memaksa Cronus memuntahkan saudara-saudaranya; Hesiodos menyebut Cronus terperdaya saran Bumi, sedangkan sumber lain menyebut ramuan yang dibawa Zeus. Perang sepuluh tahun pun dimulai antara para Titan dari Gunung Othrys dan para dewa dari Gunung Olympus.
long_description.en: Rhea saved Zeus by hiding him on Crete and giving Cronus a swaddled stone to swallow. Zeus later forced Cronus to disgorge his siblings; Hesiod says Cronus was beguiled by Earth's suggestions, while another source describes a mixture Zeus brought him. A ten-year war then began between the Titans from Mount Othrys and the gods from Mount Olympus.

long_description.id: Nasib Cronus setelah kekalahan berbeda-beda menurut kisah: satu versi menyebutnya mengembara sendirian untuk mengukur keabadian, versi lain menyebut ia dikirim ke Tartarus, dan versi lain lagi menyebut Zeus membebaskannya dan menjadikannya raja Kepulauan Orang Berbahagia. Ia dipuja antara lain di Bukit Cronus di Olympia dan melalui festival Kronia, dan dikaitkan dengan Saturnus, Geb, Ēl, dan Kumarbi.
long_description.en: Accounts of Cronus's fate after defeat differ: one has him wander the world alone measuring out eternity, another has him sent to Tartarus, and another has Zeus free him and make him king of the Isles of the Blessed. He was worshipped at, among other places, the Hill of Cronus at Olympia and through the festival of the Kronia, and is linked with the Roman god Saturn, Geb, Ēl, and Kumarbi.

cultural_context.id: Cronus menerima persembahan di Bukit Cronus di Olympia, memiliki kuil di Gadir dan Athena, dan dihormati dalam festival Kronia. Cronus kemungkinan semula dewa panen, dan bulan panen di banyak daerah Yunani dinamai Cronion menurut namanya. Bangsa Romawi memadukannya dengan Saturnus dan memandangnya secara lebih positif.
cultural_context.en: Cronus received offerings at the Hill of Cronus in Olympia, had temples at Gadir and Athens, and was honoured in the Kronia festival. He was likely originally a harvest god, and the harvest month in many parts of Greece was named Cronion after him. The Romans conflated him with Saturn and took a more positive view of him.

statement.en: One version says Cronus was cursed to wander the world alone forever.

claims.quote: According to some, Kronos (Cronus), the former king of the Golden Age, was released by Zeus from Tartaros (Tartarus) and made king of the islands of the Blessed, where the heroes were sent to dwell in paradise after death.
claims.locator: Cronus King of the Islands of the Blessed

statement.id: Versi lain mengatakan Zeus membebaskan Cronus dari Tartarus dan menjadikannya penguasa Kepulauan Orang Berbahagia.
statement.en: Another version says Zeus freed Cronus from Tartarus and made him king of the Isles of the Blessed.

claims.quote: He is linked to the Roman god Saturn, the Egyptian god Geb, the Phoenician Ēl, and the Hittite/Hurrian god Kumarbi.

statement.id: Cronus dihubungkan dengan dewa Romawi Saturnus.
statement.en: Cronus is linked to the Roman god Saturn.

claims.quote: After them was born Cronos the wily, youngest and most terrible of her children, and he hated his lusty sire.

statement.id: Menurut Hesiodos, setelah para Titan lain lahir, lahirlah Cronos yang licik, anak bungsu dan paling mengerikan, dan ia membenci ayahnya yang penuh nafsu.
statement.en: According to Hesiod, after the other Titans came Cronos the wily, youngest and most terrible of her children, and he hated his lusty sire.

claims.quote: Then the son from his ambush stretched forth his left hand and in his right took the great long sickle with jagged teeth, and swiftly lopped off his own father's members and cast them away to fall behind him.

statement.id: Menurut Hesiodos, Cronos keluar dari persembunyiannya, mengambil sabit besar bergerigi dengan tangan kanan, dan dengan cepat memotong anggota tubuh ayahnya lalu membuangnya ke belakang.
statement.en: According to Hesiod, Cronos reached from his ambush, took the great jagged sickle in his right hand, swiftly lopped off his father's members, and cast them behind him.

claims.quote: For he learned from Earth and starry Heaven that he was destined to be overcome by his own son, strong though he was

statement.id: Menurut Hesiodos, Cronos mengetahui dari Bumi dan Langit berbintang bahwa ia ditakdirkan dikalahkan oleh putranya sendiri, sekuat apa pun dirinya.
statement.en: According to Hesiod, Cronos learned from Earth and starry Heaven that he was destined to be overcome by his own son, strong though he was.

claims.quote: great Cronos the wily was beguiled by the deep suggestions of Earth, and brought up again his offspring, vanquished by the arts and might of his own son, and he vomited up first the stone which he had swallowed last.

statement.id: Menurut Hesiodos, Cronos terperdaya oleh saran-saran licik Bumi, memuntahkan kembali anak-anaknya yang dikalahkan oleh siasat dan kekuatan putranya, dan lebih dulu memuntahkan batu yang ditelannya paling akhir.
statement.en: According to Hesiod, Cronos was beguiled by the deep suggestions of Earth and brought up his offspring, vanquished by the arts and might of his son, vomiting up first the stone he had swallowed last.

claims.quote: For the Titan gods and as many as sprang from Cronos had long been fighting together in stubborn war with heart-grieving toil, the lordly Titans from high Othyrs, but the gods, givers of good, whom rich-haired Rhea bare in union with Cronos, from Olympus.

statement.id: Menurut Hesiodos, para dewa Titan dan keturunan Cronos lama berperang sengit; para Titan dari Gunung Othyrs yang tinggi, para dewa yang dilahirkan Rhea dari Cronos dari Olympus.
statement.en: According to Hesiod, the Titan gods and those sprung from Cronos had long fought a stubborn war, the Titans from high Othyrs and the gods whom Rhea bore to Cronos from Olympus.

claims.quote: for he said that they strained and did presumptuously a fearful deed, and that vengeance for it would come afterwards.

statement.id: Menurut Hesiodos, Langit menyebut putra-putranya "Titan" dengan nada celaan karena mereka bertindak lancang dengan perbuatan mengerikan, dan ia berkata pembalasan akan datang kemudian.
statement.en: According to Hesiod, Heaven called his sons Titans in reproach because they presumptuously did a fearful deed, and said vengeance would come afterwards.

claims.quote: Cronus hid, holding the sickle and ready to carry out his mother's plan. As a lustful Uranus attempted to make love to Gaia, Chronus struck, slicing off his father's genitals.

statement.id: Cronus bersembunyi sambil memegang sabit; ketika Uranus hendak bercinta dengan Gaia, Cronus menyerang dan memotong alat kelamin ayahnya.
statement.en: Cronus hid holding the sickle; as Uranus tried to lie with Gaia, Cronus struck and sliced off his father's genitals.

claims.quote: Cronus imprisoned his father deep in Tartarus (the infernal region) along with the Cyclopes and Hecatonchires in caves.
claims.locator: Cronus as King of the World

statement.id: Cronus memenjarakan ayahnya jauh di Tartarus bersama para Cyclops dan Hecatonchires dalam gua-gua.
statement.en: Cronus imprisoned his father deep in Tartarus together with the Cyclopes and Hecatonchires in caves.

claims.quote: Cronus would not simply allow his children to overthrow him without a fight, and so began the Titanomachy, a ten-year-long battle between the Titans and the Olympian gods. The Titans fought from Mount Othrys, while the gods fought from Mount Olympus.

statement.id: Cronus tidak mau digulingkan anak-anaknya tanpa perlawanan, sehingga dimulailah Titanomakhia, pertempuran sepuluh tahun antara para Titan dari Gunung Othrys dan para dewa Olimpus dari Gunung Olympus.
statement.en: Cronus would not let his children overthrow him without a fight, so began the Titanomachy, a ten-year battle between the Titans from Mount Othrys and the Olympian gods from Mount Olympus.

claims.quote: One day, as Cronus lay with Philyra, he was interrupted by Rhea and, in a panic, turned himself into a stallion and fled. Philyra became pregnant and gave birth to the centaur Cheiron.

statement.id: Ketika Cronus bersama Philyra dan didatangi Rhea, ia panik, mengubah dirinya menjadi kuda jantan, lalu kabur; Philyra hamil dan melahirkan centaur Cheiron.
statement.en: When Rhea interrupted Cronus with Philyra, he panicked, turned himself into a stallion, and fled; Philyra became pregnant and gave birth to the centaur Cheiron.

claims.quote: Although there is no etymological link between Cronus and Chronus, the Stoics believed that the definition of a word was also the meaning of a myth.

statement.id: Walau tidak ada kaitan etimologis antara Cronus dan Chronus (waktu), kaum Stoik percaya bahwa arti sebuah kata juga merupakan makna sebuah mitos.
statement.en: Although there is no etymological link between Cronus and Chronus, the Stoics believed the definition of a word was also the meaning of a myth.

claims.quote: The Hill of Cronus was located above the sanctuary of Zeus in Olympia. It was sacred to Cronus, who received offerings there.

statement.id: Bukit Cronus terletak di atas tempat suci Zeus di Olympia; bukit itu suci bagi Cronus, yang menerima persembahan di sana.
statement.en: The Hill of Cronus lay above the sanctuary of Zeus in Olympia; it was sacred to Cronus, who received offerings there.

claims.quote: A festival called the Kronia was also believed to have been held in honour of Cronus. ... It was an agricultural festival held in Athens, Samos and Kolophon at the end of the year when slaves were temporarily freed.

statement.id: Festival Kronia diyakini diadakan untuk menghormati Cronus; itu festival pertanian di Athena, Samos, dan Kolophon pada akhir tahun ketika budak dibebaskan sementara.
statement.en: A festival called the Kronia was believed to have been held in honour of Cronus; it was an agricultural festival in Athens, Samos, and Kolophon at year's end when slaves were temporarily freed.

claims.quote: Some heroes chose not to die but were instead transported to the Isles of the Blessed at the end of the world, which Cronus also ruled.
claims.locator: Cronus as King of the World

statement.id: Sebagian pahlawan memilih tidak mati dan dipindahkan ke Kepulauan Orang Berbahagia di ujung dunia, yang juga diperintah Cronus.
statement.en: Some heroes chose not to die and were instead transported to the Isles of the Blessed at the end of the world, which Cronus also ruled.

claims.quote: Zeus took this mixture to Cronus, and as soon as he started drinking it, he threw up his children one by one.

statement.id: Zeus membawa ramuan itu kepada Cronus, dan begitu Cronus meminumnya, ia memuntahkan anak-anaknya satu per satu.
statement.en: Zeus took the mixture to Cronus, and as soon as he began drinking it, Cronus threw up his children one by one.

claims.quote: Cronus was usually depicted with a harpe, scythe, or sickle, which was the instrument he used to castrate and depose Uranus, his father.

statement.id: Cronus biasanya digambarkan membawa harpe, arit, atau sabit, alat yang ia pakai untuk mengebiri dan menggulingkan ayahnya, Uranus.
statement.en: Cronus was usually depicted with a harpe, scythe, or sickle, the instrument he used to castrate and depose his father Uranus.

claims.quote: Cronus was likely originally a harvest god, which is why in many regions of Greece the month of the harvest was named Cronion after him.

statement.id: Cronus kemungkinan semula dewa panen, sehingga di banyak daerah Yunani bulan panen dinamai Cronion menurut namanya.
statement.en: Cronus was likely originally a harvest god, which is why in many regions of Greece the month of the harvest was named Cronion after him.

claims.quote: observed that attempts to give the name Κρόνος a Greek etymology had failed. Recently, Janda (2010) offers a genuinely Indo-European etymology of "the cutter", from the root *(s)ker- "to cut"

statement.id: Upaya memberi nama Κρόνος etimologi Yunani dilaporkan gagal; Janda (2010) mengajukan etimologi Indo-Eropa "sang pemotong" dari akar *(s)ker- "memotong".
statement.en: Attempts to give the name Κρόνος a Greek etymology are reported to have failed; Janda (2010) offers an Indo-European etymology, "the cutter", from the root *(s)ker- "to cut".

claims.quote: the Romans took a more positive and innocuous view of the deity, by conflating their indigenous deity Saturn with Cronus.

statement.id: Bangsa Romawi memandang dewa ini secara lebih positif dan tidak berbahaya dengan memadukan dewa asli mereka, Saturnus, dengan Cronus.
statement.en: The Romans took a more positive and innocuous view of the deity by conflating their native deity Saturn with Cronus.

claims.quote: An alternate genealogy is presented by Plato, who wrote that Cronus, Phorcys, and Rhea were the children of Oceanus and Tethys.

statement.id: Plato menyajikan silsilah alternatif: Cronus, Phorcys, dan Rhea adalah anak Oceanus dan Tethys.
statement.en: Plato presents an alternate genealogy in which Cronus, Phorcys, and Rhea were children of Oceanus and Tethys.

claims.quote: During antiquity, Cronus was occasionally interpreted as Chronos, the personification of time.

statement.id: Pada zaman kuno, Cronus kadang ditafsirkan sebagai Chronos, personifikasi waktu.
statement.en: In antiquity, Cronus was occasionally interpreted as Chronos, the personification of time.

claims.quote: Kronos was essentially the same as Khronos (Chronos), the primordial god of time in the Orphic Theogonies.

statement.id: Theoi menyatakan Kronos pada dasarnya sama dengan Khronos (Chronos), dewa waktu purba dalam Teogoni Orfik.
statement.en: Theoi states that Kronos was essentially the same as Khronos (Chronos), the primordial god of time in the Orphic Theogonies.

claims.quote: At the instigation of his mother, Cronus unmanned his father for having thrown the Cyclopes, who were likewise his children by Ge, into Tartarus.

statement.id: Atas dorongan ibunya, Cronus mengebiri ayahnya karena ayahnya melemparkan para Cyclops, yang juga anak-anaknya dari Ge, ke Tartarus.
statement.en: At his mother's instigation, Cronus unmanned his father for having thrown the Cyclopes, also his children by Ge, into Tartarus.

claims.quote: Rhea managed to save the youngest, Zeus, by hiding him away on the island of Krete (Crete), and fed Kronos a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes.

statement.id: Rhea berhasil menyelamatkan si bungsu, Zeus, dengan menyembunyikannya di pulau Kreta, dan memberi Kronos batu terbungkus kain.
statement.en: Rhea managed to save the youngest, Zeus, by hiding him on the island of Crete, and fed Kronos a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes.

claims.quote: A temple dedicated to Cronus was located on the island of Gadir (modern-day Cádiz, Spain), founded by the Phoenicians. Another temple in Athens, built by Peisistratos, was dedicated to Cronus and Rhea.

statement.id: Sebuah kuil untuk Cronus berada di pulau Gadir (Cádiz modern, Spanyol), didirikan bangsa Fenisia; kuil lain di Athena, dibangun Peisistratos, didedikasikan untuk Cronus dan Rhea.
statement.en: A temple to Cronus stood on the island of Gadir (modern Cádiz, Spain), founded by the Phoenicians; another temple in Athens, built by Peisistratos, was dedicated to Cronus and Rhea.

claims.quote: Cronus' origin story is most famously told in Hesiod's (c. 700 BCE) Theogony.

statement.id: Kisah asal-usul Cronus paling terkenal dituturkan dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos (sekitar 700 SM).
statement.en: Cronus's origin story is most famously told in Hesiod's Theogony (c. 700 BCE).

claims.quote: In Athens, on the twelfth day of the Attic month of Hekatombaion, a festival called Kronia was held in honour of Cronus to celebrate the harvest

statement.id: Di Athena, pada hari ke-12 bulan Hekatombaion menurut penanggalan Attika, festival Kronia diadakan untuk menghormati Cronus dan merayakan panen.
statement.en: In Athens, on the twelfth day of the Attic month of Hekatombaion, the festival Kronia was held in honour of Cronus to celebrate the harvest.

claims.quote: Other sources state that the Kronia was a dark festival with human sacrifices being made to Cronus.

statement.id: Sumber lain menyatakan Kronia adalah festival kelam dengan persembahan manusia kepada Cronus.
statement.en: Other sources state the Kronia was a dark festival with human sacrifices made to Cronus.

claims.quote: In other traditions, Cronus was sent to Tartarus with the rest of his siblings. Other myths state that he was allowed to live out the rest of his days on the Isles of the Blessed.

statement.id: Dalam tradisi lain, Cronus dikirim ke Tartarus bersama saudara-saudaranya; mitos lain menyatakan ia dibiarkan menjalani sisa hidupnya di Kepulauan Orang Berbahagia.
statement.en: In other traditions Cronus was sent to Tartarus with his siblings; other myths say he was allowed to live out his days on the Isles of the Blessed.

claims.quote: In 2017, a star known as HD 240430 was given the nickname Kronus after it was observed eating the planets surrounding it.

statement.id: Pada 2017, bintang HD 240430 diberi julukan Kronus setelah teramati melahap planet-planet di sekelilingnya.
statement.en: In 2017, a star known as HD 240430 was nicknamed Kronus after it was observed eating the planets around it.

short_description.id: Demeter adalah dewi Olimpus dalam mitologi Yunani yang membawahi panen, pertanian, dan kesuburan tanah, dikenal lewat kisah putrinya Persephone dan Misteri Eleusis.
short_description.en: Demeter is an Olympian goddess in Greek mythology who presides over harvest, agriculture, and the fertility of the earth, known for the story of her daughter Persephone and the Eleusinian Mysteries.

long_description.id: Demeter adalah dewi Olimpus yang membawahi panen, pertanian, dan kesuburan tanah. Orang tuanya Kronos dan Rhea; saudaranya Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Hera, dan Hestia; dan ia ibu Persephone. Seni menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan dewasa bermahkota yang membawa bulir gandum atau obor, kadang duduk, berjalan, atau naik kereta yang ditarik kuda atau naga; lambangnya adalah berkas gandum dan cornucopia, dengan ular dan babi sebagai hewan sucinya. Ia kemungkinan penjelmaan kembali dewi-dewi ibu bumi setempat di Yunani Zaman Perunggu.
long_description.en: Demeter is an Olympian goddess who presides over harvest, agriculture, and the fertility of the earth. Kronos and Rhea are her parents; Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Hera, and Hestia are her siblings; and she is the mother of Persephone. Art shows her as a mature woman wearing a crown and bearing wheat or a torch, sometimes sitting, walking, or riding in a chariot drawn by horses or dragons; her symbols are the sheaf of grain and cornucopia, with the snake and pig as sacred animals. She was probably a reincarnation of local mother Earth goddesses of Bronze Age Greece.

long_description.id: Kisah utamanya adalah penculikan Persephone oleh Hades. Dalam Himne Homerik, Demeter menyembunyikan benih sehingga tanah tidak menumbuhkan apa pun dan manusia menghadapi tahun yang mengerikan. Ia baru memulihkan kesuburan bumi setelah Persephone dijanjikan tinggal bersamanya dua pertiga tahun. Sumber lain menyebut Persephone harus kembali kepada Hades selama sepertiga atau separuh tahun.
long_description.en: Her central story is the abduction of Persephone by Hades. In the Homeric Hymn, Demeter kept the seed hidden so that the ground produced nothing and mankind faced a dreadful year. She restored the earth's fertility only after it was agreed that Persephone would live with her for two parts of the year. Other accounts say Persephone had to return to Hades for one-third or one half of the year.

long_description.id: Demeter juga digambarkan memiliki kuasa lain. Ia mengutuk Erysichthon dengan rasa lapar yang tak terpuaskan karena menebang hutan sucinya, dan hampir membuat anak asuhannya di Eleusis tak mati dan tak menua sebelum rencananya digagalkan. Untuk menghindari Poseidon, ia berubah menjadi kuda betina. Himne Homerik juga menyatakan bahwa ia mengajarkan misterinya kepada Triptolemus, Polyxeinus, dan Diocles.
long_description.en: Demeter is also shown with other powers. She cursed Erysichthon with an unquenchable hunger for cutting down her holy grove, and nearly made her foster child at Eleusis deathless and unageing before her plan was thwarted. To escape Poseidon, she changed into a mare. The Homeric Hymn also says she taught her mysteries to Triptolemus, Polyxeinus, and Diocles.

long_description.id: Tempat suci di Eleusis didedikasikan bagi Demeter dan Persephone dan menjadi lokasi Misteri Eleusis. Sejak sekitar 600 SM, misteri itu menjadi upacara resmi dalam kalender Athena, dan misteri itu kemungkinan menjanjikan kehidupan akhirat yang lebih baik. Bangsa Romawi mengenal Demeter sebagai Ceres. Ia juga dipandang sebagai dewi pernikahan dan dipuja terutama oleh perempuan; kurban untuknya antara lain babi dan kue madu.
long_description.en: The sanctuary at Eleusis was dedicated to Demeter and Persephone and was the location of the Eleusinian Mysteries. From c. 600 BCE the mysteries became an official ceremony in the Athenian calendar, and they probably promised a better afterlife. The Romans knew Demeter as Ceres. She was also regarded as the goddess of marriage and was worshipped especially by women; sacrifices to her included pigs and honey-cakes.

cultural_context.id: Demeter dipuja dalam festival seperti Thesmophoria, festival musim gugur khusus perempuan di Attika. Kisahnya bersama Persephone mungkin melambangkan pergantian musim.
cultural_context.en: Demeter was honoured in festivals such as the Thesmophoria, an all-female autumn festival in Attica. Her story with Persephone was perhaps symbolic of the changing seasons.

literal_meaning.id: Dalam salah satu penjelasan kuno, "ibu bumi"; penjelasan lain menghubungkannya dengan kata Kreta untuk jelai.
literal_meaning.en: In one ancient explanation, "mother earth"; another connects it with the Cretan word for barley.

who.id: Demeter adalah dewi Olimpus yang membawahi panen, pertanian, dan kesuburan tanah.
who.en: Demeter is an Olympian goddess of harvest, agriculture, and the fertility of the earth.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari panteon Yunani kuno dan dipuja antara lain di Eleusis.
origin.en: She belongs to the ancient Greek pantheon and was worshipped at Eleusis among other places.

role.id: Ia menjamin kesuburan bumi dan melindungi pertanian serta tumbuhan.
role.en: She guaranteed the fertility of the earth and protected farming and vegetation.

famous_for.id: Ia paling dikenal karena kisah penculikan putrinya, Persephone, oleh Hades dan karena Misteri Eleusis.
famous_for.en: She is best known for the story of her daughter Persephone's abduction by Hades and for the Eleusinian Mysteries.

did_you_know.id: Dalam seni Arkais dan Klasik, obor di tangan Demeter melambangkan pencariannya akan putrinya yang hilang.
did_you_know.en: In Archaic and Classical art, the torch in Demeter's hand signifies her search for her lost daughter.

name.en: Withholding and restoring the earth's fertility

description.id: Dalam Himne Homerik, Demeter menyembunyikan benih sehingga tanah tidak menumbuhkan apa pun, lalu segera menumbuhkan buah ketika ia dibujuk.
description.en: In the Homeric Hymn, Demeter kept the seed hidden so the ground produced nothing, then straightway made fruit spring up once persuaded.

description.id: Sang dewi mengutuk Erysichthon dengan rasa lapar yang tak terpuaskan karena menebang hutan sucinya.
description.en: The goddess cursed Erysichthon with an unquenchable hunger for cutting down her holy grove.

description.id: Demeter berubah menjadi kuda betina untuk menghindari Poseidon, dan dalam Himne Homerik ia menanggalkan rupa perempuan tua sehingga kecantikan dan keharuman menyebar di sekelilingnya.
description.en: Demeter changed into a mare to escape Poseidon, and in the Homeric Hymn she shed the look of an old woman so that beauty and fragrance spread around her.

description.id: Demeter hampir membuat anak asuhannya tak mati dan tak menua, tetapi gagal karena diintip.
description.en: Demeter would have made her foster child deathless and unageing but was thwarted when she was spied upon.

title.id: Penculikan Persephone dan kelaparan di bumi
title.en: The abduction of Persephone and the dearth on earth

role.id: Ibu yang mencari putrinya dan menahan kesuburan bumi.
role.en: The mother who searches for her daughter and withholds the earth's fertility.

summary.id: Hades menculik Persephone. Demeter menyebabkan kekeringan agar para dewa membebaskannya; tanaman layu hingga Persephone dikembalikan, dengan syarat ia kembali kepada Hades selama sebagian tahun.
summary.en: Hades abducted Persephone. Demeter created a drought to convince the gods to release her; crops withered until Persephone was returned, on condition that she go back to Hades for part of the year.

title.id: Demeter dan anak asuhnya di Eleusis
title.en: Demeter and her foster child at Eleusis

role.id: Pengasuh yang menyamar dan hampir membuat anak itu tak mati.
role.en: The disguised nurse who nearly made the child deathless.

summary.id: Menyamar sebagai perempuan tua, Demeter merawat anak Metaneira, istri raja Eleusis. Ia hampir membuat anak itu tak mati dan tak menua, tetapi rencananya gagal karena Metaneira mengintip.
summary.en: Disguised as an old woman, Demeter cared for the son of Metaneira, wife of the king of Eleusis. She would have made him deathless and unageing, but Metaneira spied on her.

role.id: Dewi yang menghukum perusak hutan sucinya.
role.en: The goddess who punishes the destroyer of her holy grove.

summary.id: Erysichthon menebang hutan suci Demeter dan dikutuk dengan rasa lapar yang tak terpuaskan.
summary.en: Erysichthon cut down Demeter's holy grove and was cursed with an unquenchable hunger.

title.en: The teaching of agriculture and the mysteries

role.id: Dewi yang mengutus Triptolemos dan mengajarkan ritusnya.
role.en: The goddess who sends Triptolemos and teaches her rites.

summary.id: Demeter mengutus Triptolemos untuk mengajarkan pertanian dan, dalam Himne Homerik, mengajarkan misterinya kepada Triptolemus, Polyxeinus, dan Diocles.
summary.en: Demeter sent Triptolemos to instruct mankind in agriculture and, in the Homeric Hymn, taught her mysteries to Triptolemus, Polyxeinus, and Diocles.

description.id: Tempat suci Demeter dan Persephone serta lokasi Misteri Eleusis.
description.en: Sanctuary of Demeter and Persephone and location of the Eleusinian Mysteries.

description.id: Menurut kisah yang paling umum, tempat Persephone dibawa ke dunia bawah.
description.en: According to the common story, the place where Persephone was carried to the lower world.

description.id: Tempat tinggal Demeter menurut tabel ringkasan.
description.en: Demeter's home according to the summary table.

title.en: Eleusinian Mysteries become an official Athenian ceremony

description.id: Sejak sekitar 600 SM, Misteri Eleusis menjadi upacara resmi dalam kalender Athena.
description.en: From c. 600 BCE the Eleusinian Mysteries became an official ceremony in the Athenian calendar.

claims.quote: is the Olympian goddess of the harvest and agriculture, presiding over crops, grains, food, and the fertility of the earth.

statement.id: Demeter adalah dewi Olimpus yang membawahi panen, pertanian, dan kesuburan tanah.
statement.en: Demeter is an Olympian goddess of harvest, agriculture, and earth's fertility.

claims.quote: Demeter was depicted as a mature woman, often wearing a crown and bearing sheafs of wheat or a cornucopia (horn of plenty), and a torch.

statement.id: Demeter digambarkan sebagai perempuan dewasa yang membawa gandum atau obor.
statement.en: Demeter is shown as a mature woman bearing wheat or a torch.

claims.quote: The abduction of her daughter Persephone by Hades, and the great dearth she brought down upon the earth.

statement.id: Persephone adalah putri Demeter yang diculik Hades, diikuti masa kekurangan pangan.
statement.en: Persephone is Demeter's daughter abducted by Hades, followed by famine.

claims.quote: Once the temple was completed, Demeter withdrew from the world and lived inside it; at the same time, she created a great drought to convince the other gods to release Persephone from Hades.

statement.id: Demeter menyebabkan kekeringan untuk menuntut pembebasan Persephone.
statement.en: Demeter caused a drought to demand Persephone's release.

claims.quote: The sanctuary at Eleusis is dedicated to both the goddess and her daughter Persephone. This was the location of the famous Eleusinian Mysteries.

statement.id: Eleusis memiliki tempat suci Demeter dan Persephone serta ritual misteri mereka.
statement.en: Eleusis had a sanctuary for Demeter and Persephone and their mysteries.

claims.quote: To the Romans, the goddess remained popular and was known as Ceres.

statement.id: Bangsa Romawi mengenal Demeter sebagai Ceres.
statement.en: Romans knew Demeter as Ceres.

claims.quote: As the drought claimed ever more victims, crops withered

statement.id: Kekeringan dalam kisah Demeter membuat tanaman layu.
statement.en: The drought in Demeter's story withered crops.

claims.quote: Demeter was one of the oldest gods in the ancient Greek pantheon.

statement.id: Demeter adalah dewi dalam panteon Yunani kuno.
statement.en: Demeter is a deity in the ancient Greek pantheon.

claims.quote: that is, mother earth, while others consider Deo, which is synonymous with Demeter, as connected with dais and dainumi, and as derived from the Cretan word ... barley, so that Demeter would be the mother or giver of barley or of food generally.

statement.id: Sebagian orang menganggap nama Demeter sama dengan "gê mêtêr" (ibu bumi); yang lain menghubungkan "Deo" dengan kata Kreta untuk jelai, sehingga Demeter berarti ibu atau pemberi jelai atau makanan pada umumnya.
statement.en: Some consider the name Demeter the same as "gê mêtêr" (mother earth), while others link "Deo" to the Cretan word for barley, so that Demeter would be the mother or giver of barley or of food generally.

claims.quote: Demeter was the goddess of the earth (Eurip. Bacch. 276), and more especially of the earth as producing fruit, and consequently of agriculture

statement.id: Demeter adalah dewi bumi, terutama bumi yang menghasilkan buah, dan karena itu dewi pertanian.
statement.en: Demeter was the goddess of the earth, and more especially of the earth as producing fruit, and consequently of agriculture.

claims.quote: she accordingly was looked upon also as the goddess of marriage (Serv. ad Aen. iv. 58), and was worshipped especially by women.

statement.id: Anggapan bahwa Demeter menyuburkan bumi diperluas menjadi kesuburan pada umumnya; ia juga dipandang sebagai dewi pernikahan dan dipuja terutama oleh perempuan.
statement.en: Her role in the earth's fertility was extended to fertility in general; she was also regarded as the goddess of marriage and was worshipped especially by women.

claims.quote: dwelt upon earth among men, conferring presents and blessings wherever she was kindly received, and severely punishing those who repulsed her or did not receive her gifts with proper reverence.

statement.id: Dalam kisahnya, Demeter tinggal di antara manusia, memberi hadiah dan berkat kepada yang menyambutnya dengan baik, dan menghukum dengan keras mereka yang menolaknya atau tidak menerima pemberiannya dengan hormat.
statement.en: In her story, Demeter dwelt among men, conferring presents and blessings wherever she was kindly received and severely punishing those who repulsed her or did not receive her gifts with proper reverence.

claims.quote: She was represented sometimes in a sitting attitude, sometimes walking, and sometimes riding in a chariot drawn by horses or dragons, but always in full attire.

statement.id: Demeter digambarkan kadang duduk, kadang berjalan, dan kadang naik kereta yang ditarik kuda atau naga, selalu berpakaian lengkap.
statement.en: She was represented sometimes sitting, sometimes walking, and sometimes riding in a chariot drawn by horses or dragons, but always in full attire.

claims.quote: The sacrifices offered to her consisted of pigs, the symbol of fertility, bulls, cows, honey-cakes, and fruits.

statement.id: Kurban untuknya berupa babi sebagai lambang kesuburan, sapi jantan, sapi betina, kue madu, dan buah-buahan.
statement.en: Sacrifices offered to her consisted of pigs, the symbol of fertility, bulls, cows, honey-cakes, and fruits.

claims.quote: The spot where Persephone was believed to have been carried into the lower world is different in the different traditions; the common story places it in Sicily

statement.id: Tempat Persephone dipercaya dibawa ke dunia bawah berbeda-beda menurut tradisi; kisah yang paling umum menempatkannya di Sisilia.
statement.en: The spot where Persephone was believed to have been carried into the lower world differs between traditions; the common story places it in Sicily.

claims.quote: Home Mount Olympus Symbols Sheaf of grain, cornucopia Sacred Animals Snake, pig Sacred Plants Wheat, mint, poppy

statement.id: Tempat tinggalnya Gunung Olimpus; lambangnya berkas gandum dan cornucopia; hewan sucinya ular dan babi; tumbuhan sucinya gandum, mint, dan opium poppy.
statement.en: Her home is Mount Olympus; her symbols are the sheaf of grain and cornucopia; her sacred animals are the snake and pig; her sacred plants are wheat, mint, and poppy.

claims.quote: The punishment of Erysikhthon (Erysichthon) who was cursed with an unquenchable hunger by the goddess for cutting down her holy grove.

statement.id: Erysichthon dikutuk dengan rasa lapar yang tak terpuaskan oleh sang dewi karena menebang hutan sucinya.
statement.en: Erysichthon was cursed by the goddess with an unquenchable hunger for cutting down her holy grove.

claims.quote: The journeys of Triptolemos, a hero sent by the goddess to instruct mankind in agriculture.

statement.id: Triptolemos adalah pahlawan yang diutus sang dewi untuk mengajarkan pertanian kepada manusia.
statement.en: Triptolemos was a hero sent by the goddess to instruct mankind in agriculture.

claims.quote: Daughter of Kronos and Rhea, sister of Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Hera, and Hestia, Demeter was the mother of Persephone and Iacchus (both with Zeus) and Plutus, the god of wealth

statement.id: Demeter adalah putri Kronos dan Rhea, saudari Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Hera, dan Hestia, serta ibu Persephone dan Iacchus (keduanya dengan Zeus) dan Plutus, dewa kekayaan.
statement.en: Demeter was the daughter of Kronos and Rhea, sister of Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Hera, and Hestia, and mother of Persephone and Iacchus (both with Zeus) and Plutus, the god of wealth.

claims.quote: Demeter was also pursued by Poseidon, and to escape his attentions, she changed into a mare; however, Poseidon too changed into a horse and their resulting offspring was Arion, the winged horse ridden by Hercules.

statement.id: Untuk menghindari Poseidon, Demeter berubah menjadi kuda betina; Poseidon pun berubah menjadi kuda dan keturunan mereka adalah Arion, kuda bersayap yang ditunggangi Hercules.
statement.en: To escape Poseidon, Demeter changed into a mare; Poseidon too changed into a horse and their offspring was Arion, the winged horse ridden by Hercules.

claims.quote: It was here, disguised as an old woman, that the goddess cared for Demophon (or Triptolemus), the only son of Metaneira, the wife of Keleos (or Celeus), king of Eleusis.

statement.id: Di Eleusis, menyamar sebagai perempuan tua, sang dewi merawat Demophon (atau Triptolemus), putra tunggal Metaneira, istri Keleos (atau Celeus), raja Eleusis.
statement.en: At Eleusis, disguised as an old woman, the goddess cared for Demophon (or Triptolemus), the only son of Metaneira, wife of Keleos (or Celeus), king of Eleusis.

claims.quote: Finally, as a compromise, it was decided that Persephone would be released but that she would have to return to Hades for one-third of the year (or in other accounts one half).

statement.id: Sebagai kompromi, Persephone dibebaskan tetapi harus kembali kepada Hades selama sepertiga tahun (atau separuh tahun dalam kisah lain).
statement.en: As a compromise, Persephone would be released but had to return to Hades for one-third of the year (or one half in other accounts).

claims.quote: The story of Demeter and Persephone was perhaps symbolic of the changing seasons and the perennial change from life to death, to life once more, or, in other words, the changes from summer to winter and the return of life in spring.

statement.id: Kisah Demeter dan Persephone mungkin melambangkan pergantian musim dan siklus dari hidup ke kematian lalu hidup kembali, yakni dari musim panas ke musim dingin dan kembalinya kehidupan di musim semi.
statement.en: The story of Demeter and Persephone was perhaps symbolic of the changing seasons and the cycle from life to death to life once more, from summer to winter and the return of life in spring.

claims.quote: From c. 600 BCE the Eleusinian Mysteries became an official ceremony in the Athenian calendar

statement.id: Sejak sekitar 600 SM, Misteri Eleusis menjadi upacara resmi dalam kalender Athena.
statement.en: From c. 600 BCE the Eleusinian Mysteries became an official ceremony in the Athenian calendar.

claims.quote: Closely associated with fertility and agriculture, the mysteries probably brought worshippers good fortune and, perhaps most important for most participants, the promise of a better afterlife.

statement.id: Misteri yang erat kaitannya dengan kesuburan dan pertanian itu kemungkinan memberi peserta keberuntungan dan, yang terpenting bagi kebanyakan mereka, janji kehidupan akhirat yang lebih baik.
statement.en: Closely associated with fertility and agriculture, the mysteries probably brought worshippers good fortune and, most importantly for most participants, the promise of a better afterlife.

claims.quote: In Archaic and Classical art she is often seated, wears a crown of grain and holds a torch (signifying her search for her lost daughter) or a sceptre, a poppy (the flower that grows so abundantly in untended wheat fields) or simply stalks of grain.
claims.locator: How is Demeter Represented in Art?

statement.id: Dalam seni Arkais dan Klasik, Demeter sering duduk, bermahkota biji-bijian, dan memegang obor (tanda pencariannya akan putrinya), tongkat kerajaan, opium poppy, atau sekadar tangkai gandum.
statement.en: In Archaic and Classical art she is often seated, wears a crown of grain and holds a torch (signifying her search for her lost daughter) or a sceptre, a poppy, or simply stalks of grain.

claims.quote: The Thesmophoria, meanwhile, was an all-female autumn festival in Attica to honour Demeter.

statement.id: Thesmophoria adalah festival musim gugur khusus perempuan di Attika untuk menghormati Demeter.
statement.en: The Thesmophoria was an all-female autumn festival in Attica to honour Demeter.

claims.quote: Demeter was probably a reincarnation of local mother Earth goddesses worshipped in rural communities in Bronze Age Greece.

statement.id: Demeter kemungkinan merupakan penjelmaan kembali dewi-dewi ibu bumi setempat yang dipuja masyarakat pedesaan di Yunani Zaman Perunggu.
statement.en: Demeter was probably a reincarnation of local mother Earth goddesses worshipped in rural communities in Bronze Age Greece.

claims.quote: Then she caused a most dreadful and cruel year for mankind over the all-nourishing earth: the ground would not make the seed sprout, for rich-crowned Demeter kept it hid.

statement.id: Dalam Himne Homerik, Demeter menyebabkan tahun yang sangat mengerikan bagi manusia: tanah tidak menumbuhkan benih karena Demeter menyembunyikannya.
statement.en: In the Homeric Hymn, Demeter caused a most dreadful and cruel year for mankind: the ground would not make the seed sprout, for Demeter kept it hid.

claims.quote: And she would have made him deathless and unageing, had not well-girded Metaneira in her heedlessness kept watch by night from her sweet-smelling chamber and spied.

statement.id: Demeter hampir membuat anak asuhannya tak mati dan tak menua, tetapi gagal karena Metaneira mengintip pada malam hari.
statement.en: Demeter would have made the child in her care deathless and unageing, but Metaneira kept watch by night and spied.

claims.quote: did not refuse but straightway made fruit to spring up from the rich lands, so that the whole wide earth was laden with leaves and flowers.

statement.id: Setelah dibujuk, Demeter segera menumbuhkan buah dari tanah subur sehingga seluruh bumi dipenuhi daun dan bunga.
statement.en: Once persuaded, Demeter straightway made fruit spring up from the rich lands so that the whole wide earth was laden with leaves and flowers.

claims.quote: she showed the conduct of her rites and taught them all her mysteries, to Triptolemus and Polyxeinus and Diocles also

statement.id: Demeter menunjukkan tata cara ritusnya dan mengajarkan seluruh misterinya kepada Triptolemus, Polyxeinus, dan Diocles.
statement.en: Demeter showed the conduct of her rites and taught her mysteries to Triptolemus, Polyxeinus, and Diocles.

claims.quote: Lo! I am that Demeter who has share of honour and is the greatest help and cause of joy to the undying gods and mortal men.

statement.id: Demeter menyatakan dirinya mendapat bagian kehormatan dan menjadi penolong terbesar serta sebab sukacita bagi para dewa dan manusia.
statement.en: Demeter declares she has a share of honour and is the greatest help and cause of joy to the undying gods and mortal men.

claims.quote: the goddess changed her stature and her looks, thrusting old age away from her: beauty spread round about her and a lovely fragrance was wafted from her sweet-smelling robes

statement.id: Demeter mengubah perawakan dan rupanya, menyingkirkan ketuaan, sehingga keindahan menyebar di sekitarnya dan keharuman tercium dari jubahnya.
statement.en: The goddess changed her stature and her looks, thrusting old age away, so that beauty spread around her and a lovely fragrance was wafted from her robes.

claims.quote: the wide-pathed earth yawned there in the plain of Nysa, and the lord, Host of Many, with his immortal horses sprang out upon her

statement.id: Dalam Himne Homerik, bumi terbelah di dataran Nysa dan sang penguasa, Tuan Banyak Tamu (Host of Many), melompat keluar dengan kuda-kuda abadinya.
statement.en: In the Homeric Hymn, the earth yawned in the plain of Nysa and the lord, the Host of Many, sprang out with his immortal horses.

claims.quote: agreed that her daughter should go down for the third part of the circling year to darkness and gloom, but for the two parts should live with her mother and the other deathless gods.

statement.id: Zeus menyetujui bahwa putri Demeter turun ke kegelapan selama sepertiga tahun dan tinggal bersama ibunya dan dewa-dewa lain selama dua pertiga tahun.
statement.en: Zeus agreed that her daughter should go down to darkness for the third part of the circling year and live with her mother and the other gods for the two parts.

summary.id: Kisah yang paling umum menempatkannya di Sisilia, tetapi tempatnya berbeda-beda menurut tradisi.
summary.en: The common story places it in Sicily, but the place differs between traditions.

summary.en: The Homeric Hymn names the plain of Nysa.

text.id: Disebut dalam sastra Yunani sejak Theogony Hesiod (epos abad ke-8 atau ke-7 SM menurut Theoi) dan dipuja hingga masa Romawi
text.en: Named in Greek literature from Hesiod's Theogony (an epic of the 8th or 7th century BC according to Theoi) and worshipped into the Roman period

short_description.id: Hestia adalah dewi perawan perapian dan rumah dalam mitologi Yunani, putri sulung Cronus dan Rhea, yang menerima bagian pertama dari setiap kurban.
short_description.en: Hestia is the virgin Greek goddess of the hearth and home, eldest daughter of Cronus and Rhea, who received the first share of every sacrifice.

long_description.id: Hestia adalah dewi perawan perapian, rumah, dan keramahtamahan dalam kepercayaan Yunani. Dalam mitos ia putri sulung Cronus dan Rhea, ditelan ayahnya saat lahir lalu dimuntahkan kembali oleh Zeus. Sebagai pelindung keluarga dan komunitas politik, persembahan dibuat bagi Hestia di perapian setiap rumah dan di perapian umum kota. Bangsa Romawi mengenalnya sebagai Vesta.
long_description.en: Hestia is the virgin Greek goddess of the hearth, home, and hospitality. In myth she is the eldest daughter of Cronus and Rhea, swallowed by her father at birth and later disgorged by Zeus. As protector of the family and political community, offerings were made to Hestia at the hearth in every home and at a city's public hearth. The Romans knew her as Vesta.

long_description.id: Hestia menerima kurban lebih dulu daripada dewa lain, juga persembahan anggur pertama dan terakhir pada setiap pesta, dan biasanya disebut pertama dalam doa dan sumpah. Menurut mitos, Zeus memberinya kehormatan itu ketika ia bersumpah tetap perawan, meskipun Apollo, Poseidon, dan Priapus mendekatinya. Perapian melambangkan jantung dan jiwa rumah tangga, dan kaitannya dengan perapian menghubungkan Hestia dengan keramahtamahan serta perlindungan tamu. Di kota, ia terutama dikaitkan dengan prytaneion dan bouleuterion, pusat simbolis pemerintahan setempat.
long_description.en: Hestia received sacrifices before the other gods, as well as the first and last libations of wine at any feast, and was usually mentioned first in prayers and oaths. According to myth, Zeus gave her this honour when she swore to remain a virgin, despite the attentions of Apollo, Poseidon, and Priapus. The hearth symbolised the heart and soul of the household, and her link with the hearth tied Hestia to hospitality and the protection of guests. In the city her special place was the prytaneion and bouleuterion, the symbolic seat of local government.

long_description.id: Hestia tidak punya mitologi yang menonjol: ia digambarkan sebagai dewi senior yang menjauh dari urusan para dewa, dan ia satu-satunya yang tidak ikut serangan gagal para dewa Olimpus terhadap Zeus. Dalam sebagian daftar ia termasuk 12 dewa Olimpus, tetapi lebih umum tempatnya diisi Dionysos; dalam sebagian mitos ia sendiri menyerahkan tempat itu kepada Dionysos. Dalam seni ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda berkerudung dan berpakaian sederhana, sulit dibedakan dari dewi lain.
long_description.en: Hestia has no prominent mythology: she is presented as a senior goddess aloof from the affairs of the other gods, and alone among the goddesses she stayed out of the Olympians' unsuccessful assault on Zeus. Some lists count her among the 12 Olympians, though Dionysos more often fills that seat; some myths have her yield the seat to him herself. In art she is usually shown as a young woman, veiled and modestly dressed, and is hard to tell apart from other goddesses.

long_description.id: Pemujaan umum Hestia sangat marak di Attica, dengan kultus penting di Piraeus, Eleusis, Halimos, dan Krokonidai. Imam dan imam perempuan yang khusus mengabdi kepadanya tampak lazim sejak masa Helenistik, dan pada masa Romawi, ketika ia dikenal sebagai Vesta, ia terus dipuja, misalnya di Ephesus. Setiap kali koloni baru didirikan, nyala api dari perapian umum Hestia di kota induk dibawa ke permukiman baru.
long_description.en: Her public cult flourished above all in Attica, with notable cults at Piraeus, Eleusis, Halimos, and Krokonidai. Priests and priestesses specifically dedicated to her seem to have been common from the Hellenistic period, and in the Roman period, when she was known as Vesta, she continued to be worshipped, for example at Ephesus. Whenever a new colony was founded, a flame from Hestia's public hearth in the mother city was carried to the new settlement.

cultural_context.id: Perapian dipandang sebagai pusat suci kehidupan rumah tangga dan lambang jantung serta jiwa rumah tangga; Hestia dianggap pemberi kebahagiaan dan berkat rumah tangga, dan sumpah serta suaka pemohon dikaitkan dengan perapian. Kurban bagi Hestia berupa buah sulung, air, minyak, anggur, dan sapi berumur satu tahun, dan api perapiannya yang padam tidak boleh dinyalakan kembali dengan api biasa.
cultural_context.en: The hearth was seen as the sacred centre of domestic life and a symbol of the household's heart and soul; Hestia was regarded as the giver of domestic happiness and blessings, and oaths and the asylum of suppliants were tied to the hearth. Offerings to Hestia were first fruits, water, oil, wine, and one-year-old cows, and her hearth fire, if extinguished, could not be relit with ordinary fire.

literal_meaning.id: "perapian, tungku, altar"
literal_meaning.en: "hearth, fireplace, altar"

who.id: Hestia adalah dewi perawan perapian dan rumah dalam mitologi Yunani.
who.en: Hestia is the virgin goddess of the hearth and home in Greek mythology.

origin.id: Ia putri sulung Titan Cronus dan Rhea dalam mitologi Yunani; bangsa Romawi mengenalnya sebagai Vesta.
origin.en: She is the eldest daughter of Cronus and Rhea in Greek mythology; the Romans knew her as Vesta.

role.id: Ia menerima kurban pertama dan menjaga api perapian rumah, kota, dan altar.
role.en: She receives the first sacrifice and watches over the fire of the hearth in homes, cities, and altars.

famous_for.id: Hestia terkenal karena tetap perawan dan karena kehormatan menerima persembahan pertama dari Zeus.
famous_for.en: Hestia is known for remaining a virgin and for the honour of the first offering granted by Zeus.

did_you_know.id: Karena Hestia disebut pertama dalam doa dan sumpah, muncul ungkapan Yunani "mulai dari Hestia".
did_you_know.en: Because Hestia was named first in prayers and oaths, a Greek saying arose: 'to begin from Hestia.'

name.en: Domain: the hearth and the sacrificial flame

description.id: Hestia adalah personifikasi perapian dan dewi api kurban; Zeus menugaskannya memelihara api perapian Olimpus.
description.en: Hestia is the personification of the hearth and goddess of the sacrificial flame; Zeus assigned her to maintain the fires of the Olympian hearth.

description.id: Hestia juga memimpin pembuatan roti dan penyiapan hidangan keluarga, dan dikaitkan dengan keramahtamahan, perlindungan tamu, dan pembangunan rumah.
description.en: Hestia also presided over the baking of bread and the preparation of the family meal and is linked with hospitality, the protection of guests, and housebuilding.

description.id: Hestia menerima kurban sebelum dewa lain, anggur pertama dan terakhir pada pesta, dan disebut pertama dalam doa dan sumpah.
description.en: Hestia received sacrifices before the other gods, the first and last wine libations at feasts, and was mentioned first in prayers and oaths.

description.id: Lukisan vas Athena menampilkannya sebagai perempuan berkerudung yang kadang memegang dahan berbunga, dan patung klasik menampilkannya berkerudung dengan ketel sebagai atribut.
description.en: Athenian vase painting shows her as a veiled woman sometimes holding a flowered branch, and classical sculpture shows her veiled with a kettle as her attribute.

description.id: Nama bangsa Romawi untuk dewi ini; pada masa Romawi pemujaan Hestia berlanjut dengan nama Vesta.
description.en: The Romans' name for this goddess; in the Roman period worship of Hestia continued under the name Vesta.

description.id: Nama Hestia di tempat suci khususnya di prytaneum kota, lengkap dengan arca dan perapian suci.
description.en: Hestia's name at her special sanctuary in a town's prytaneum, with a statue and the sacred hearth.

title.en: Swallowed by Cronus and disgorged by Zeus

role.id: Anak sulung yang ditelan lebih dulu
role.en: The firstborn who was swallowed first

summary.id: Cronus, yang takut ditumbangkan anaknya, menelan Hestia dan saudara-saudaranya. Zeus kemudian memaksa sang Titan memuntahkan mereka; karena Hestia ditelan pertama dan dimuntahkan terakhir, ia disebut sekaligus yang tertua dan termuda.
summary.en: Cronus, fearing overthrow by his children, swallowed Hestia and her siblings. Zeus later forced the Titan to disgorge them; being swallowed first and disgorged last, Hestia was called both the eldest and the youngest.

title.id: Sumpah keperawanan dan kehormatan dari Zeus
title.en: The oath of virginity and Zeus's honour

role.id: Dewi yang menolak lamaran
role.en: The goddess who refuses suitors

summary.id: Ketika Apollon dan Poseidon melamarnya, Hestia menolak dan meminta Zeus membiarkannya tetap perawan. Zeus setuju, memberinya tempat di tengah rumah dan kehormatan menerima kurban pertama, dan ia mengambil tempat di perapian Zeus.
summary.en: When Apollon and Poseidon sought her hand, Hestia refused and asked Zeus to let her remain a virgin. Zeus agreed, gave her a place in the midst of the house and the honour of the first sacrifice, and she took her place at his hearth.

role.id: Dewi yang menyerahkan tempatnya
role.en: The goddess who gives up her place

summary.id: Dalam sebagian mitos Hestia melepaskan tempatnya di Gunung Olimpus dan bertukar dengan Dionysos, karena lebih suka menjauh dari urusan para dewa dan yakin disambut hangat di kota manusia mana pun.
summary.en: Some myths say Hestia stepped down from her seat on Mount Olympus in favour of Dionysos, choosing to stay out of divine affairs, confident that any human city would welcome her.

title.en: Not joining the attack on Zeus

role.id: Satu-satunya dewi yang tidak ikut
role.en: The only goddess who did not join

summary.id: Hestia adalah satu-satunya dewi yang tidak ikut para dewa Olimpus dalam serangan gagal mereka terhadap Zeus.
summary.en: Hestia was the only goddess who did not join the Olympians in their failed attack on Zeus.

title.id: Priapus dan Vesta dalam Fasti Ovidius
title.en: Priapus and Vesta in Ovid's Fasti

role.id: Dewi yang diselamatkan dari gangguan
role.en: The goddess saved from an advance

summary.id: Dalam Fasti Ovidius, Vesta (Hestia) tertidur saat pesta para dewa, dan Priapus mendekatinya. Keledai Silenus meringkik, sang dewi terbangun ketakutan, dan para hadirin berlari menolongnya sementara Priapus melarikan diri.
summary.en: In Ovid's Fasti, Vesta (Hestia) falls asleep during the gods' feast and Priapus approaches her. Silenus's donkey brays, the goddess wakes frightened, and the crowd rushes to her while Priapus flees.

description.id: Pusat simbolis kota tempat urusan pemerintahan setempat dijalankan; perapian umum di sana adalah tempat suci resmi Hestia.
description.en: The symbolic centre of a town where local government business was carried out; the public hearth there was Hestia's official sanctuary.

description.id: Kediaman para dewa, tempat Hestia dalam sebagian mitos melepaskan kedudukannya kepada Dionysos.
description.en: The home of the gods, where in some myths Hestia gives up her position to Dionysos.

description.id: Wilayah tempat pemujaan umum Hestia sangat marak, dengan kultus di Piraeus, Eleusis, Halimos, dan Krokonidai.
description.en: The region where public worship of Hestia was especially prevalent, with cults at Piraeus, Eleusis, Halimos, and Krokonidai.

description.id: Di kuil Delphi, Hestia dipuja bersama Apollo dan Poseidon, dan ia juga muncul pada friz Perbendaharaan Siphnos di sana.
description.en: At the temple of Delphi Hestia was worshipped together with Apollo and Poseidon, and she also appears on the Siphnian Treasury frieze there.

description.id: Tempat kuil Hestia tersendiri yang hanya berisi altar, tanpa arca.
description.en: Site of a separate temple of Hestia that contained only an altar and no image.

description.id: Kota tempat Hestia, yang kini dikenal sebagai Vesta, tetap dipuja pada masa Romawi dengan imam besar perempuan.
description.en: A city where Hestia, now known as Vesta, continued to be worshipped in the Roman period with a female high priest.

timeline.period: Greek epic C8th or C7th B.C.

description.id: Theogony menyebut Hestia, Demeter, dan Hera sebagai anak-anak Rhea dan Kronos.
description.en: The Theogony names Hestia, Demeter, and Hera as children of Rhea and Kronos.

description.id: Hestia muncul pada Vas Francois.
description.en: Hestia appears on the Francois Vase.

description.id: Hestia, kali ini dengan nama, tampak pada friz utara Perbendaharaan Siphnos di Delphi.
description.en: Hestia, this time named, appears on the north frieze of the Siphnian Treasury at Delphi.

description.id: Sebuah kylix figur merah menampilkan Hestia bersama Apollo dan Hermes yang menuntun Hercules ke Gunung Olimpus.
description.en: A red-figure kylix shows Hestia with Apollo and Hermes as they lead Hercules to Mount Olympus.

description.id: Imam dan imam perempuan yang khusus mengabdi kepada Hestia tampak sangat lazim sejak masa ini.
description.en: Priests and priestesses specifically dedicated to Hestia seem to have been particularly prevalent from this time.

description.id: Hestia, kini dikenal sebagai Vesta, terus dipuja, misalnya di Ephesus.
description.en: Hestia, now known as Vesta, continued to be worshipped, for example at Ephesus.

note.en: The fertility god who paid amorous attention to Hestia.

note.en: Often appears with Hestia as protector of the works of man.
