learning_questions.id: Mengapa perapian bisa menjadi simbol pusat rumah tangga sekaligus pusat kota bagi orang Yunani kuno?
learning_questions.en: Why could the hearth be a symbol of both the household's and the city's centre for the ancient Greeks?

learning_questions.id: Apa arti kehormatan menerima kurban pertama bagi kedudukan Hestia di antara para dewa?
learning_questions.en: What does the honour of the first sacrifice mean for Hestia's standing among the gods?

learning_questions.id: Mengapa dewi yang hampir tak punya mitos bisa begitu sering disebut dalam doa dan sumpah?
learning_questions.en: Why might a goddess with almost no myths be named so often in prayers and oaths?

sources.title: HESTIA - Greek Goddess of Hearth & Home

claims.quote: Hestia was the Greek virgin goddess of the hearth, home, and hospitality.

statement.id: Hestia adalah dewi perapian, rumah, dan keramahtamahan Yunani.
statement.en: Hestia is the Greek goddess of the hearth, home, and hospitality.

claims.quote: In Greek mythology, she is the eldest daughter of Cronus and Rhea.

statement.id: Hestia adalah putri sulung Cronus dan Rhea.
statement.en: Hestia is the eldest daughter of Cronus and Rhea.

claims.quote: To the Romans, the goddess was known as Vesta.

statement.id: Bangsa Romawi mengenalnya sebagai Vesta.
statement.en: The Romans knew her as Vesta.

claims.quote: Hestia never married and remained a virgin, despite the amorous attentions of Apollo, Poseidon, and Priapus, the fertility god.

statement.id: Hestia tetap perawan dan tidak menikah meskipun didekati Apollo, Poseidon, dan Priapus.
statement.en: Hestia remained unmarried despite the interest of Apollo, Poseidon, and Priapus.

claims.quote: The goddess was the personification of the hearth and so she received sacrifices in all the temples of the gods as each one had its own hearth.

statement.id: Hestia dipandang sebagai personifikasi perapian dan menerima persembahan di kuil para dewa.
statement.en: Hestia personified the hearth and received offerings in temples.

claims.quote: Hestia was also the goddess of the sacrificial flame and received a share of every sacrifice to the gods.

statement.id: Hestia terkait api kurban dan mendapat bagian dari setiap persembahan kepada para dewa.
statement.en: Hestia governed the sacrificial flame and received a share of each offering.

claims.quote: Hestia was depicted in Athenian vase painting as a modestly veiled woman sometimes holding a flowered branch (perhaps a chaste-tree).

statement.id: Lukisan vas Athena menggambarkan Hestia sebagai perempuan berkerudung, kadang memegang dahan berbunga.
statement.en: Athenian vase paintings show Hestia veiled and sometimes holding a flowering branch.

claims.quote: In her role as a protector of the family and political community, sacrifices and offerings were regularly made to Hestia at the hearth within each private home and at the town or city's public hearth.

statement.id: Sebagai pelindung keluarga dan komunitas politik, persembahan secara rutin dibuat bagi Hestia di perapian setiap rumah dan di perapian umum kota.
statement.en: As protector of the family and political community, offerings were regularly made to Hestia at the hearth in each private home and at the town or city's public hearth.

claims.quote: In the Greek myths, Hestia's parents were Cronus and Rhea and so her younger siblings were Zeus, Hera, Demeter, Poseidon, and Hades. Cronus, paranoid that one of his own children would overthrow his rule, swallowed them all.

statement.id: Orang tua Hestia adalah Cronus dan Rhea; adik-adiknya Zeus, Hera, Demeter, Poseidon, dan Hades. Cronus, yang takut ditumbangkan anaknya, menelan mereka semua.
statement.en: Hestia's parents were Cronus and Rhea; her younger siblings were Zeus, Hera, Demeter, Poseidon, and Hades. Cronus, fearing overthrow by his children, swallowed them all.

claims.quote: In some lists, Hestia is one of the 12 Olympian gods but more commonly her place is taken by Dionysos.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian daftar Hestia termasuk 12 dewa Olimpus, tetapi lebih umum tempatnya diisi Dionysos.
statement.en: In some lists Hestia is one of the 12 Olympian gods, but more commonly her place is taken by Dionysos.

claims.quote: In some myths the goddess voluntarily relinquishes her place amongst the gods on Mount Olympus, swapping with Dionysos because she prefers to withdraw from godly affairs and is sure of a fond welcome in any mortal city she chooses.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian mitos Hestia melepaskan tempatnya di Gunung Olimpus dan bertukar dengan Dionysos karena lebih suka menjauh dari urusan para dewa dan yakin disambut hangat di kota manusia mana pun.
statement.en: In some myths Hestia voluntarily gives up her place on Mount Olympus, swapping with Dionysos because she prefers to withdraw from godly affairs and is sure of a warm welcome in any mortal city.

claims.quote: By tradition, Hestia received any sacrifices before the other gods, even at such places as Olympia where Zeus was honoured. Hestia also received the first and last libations of wine offering at any feast and was usually mentioned first in any prayers and oaths.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi, Hestia menerima kurban lebih dulu daripada dewa lain, mendapat persembahan anggur pertama dan terakhir pada setiap pesta, dan biasanya disebut pertama dalam doa dan sumpah.
statement.en: By tradition Hestia received sacrifices before the other gods, received the first and last libations of wine at any feast, and was usually mentioned first in prayers and oaths.

claims.quote: In mythology, the honour of receiving the first sacrifice was given by Zeus when Hestia swore that she would always remain a virgin.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi, kehormatan menerima kurban pertama diberikan Zeus ketika Hestia bersumpah akan selalu perawan.
statement.en: In mythology Zeus gave Hestia the honour of the first sacrifice when she swore she would always remain a virgin.

claims.quote: Within a Greek house, the hearth was usually a portable brazier but it symbolised the heart and soul of the household and came to represent its centre.

statement.id: Di rumah Yunani, perapian biasanya berupa tungku portabel, tetapi melambangkan jantung dan jiwa rumah tangga dan menjadi pusatnya.
statement.en: In a Greek house the hearth was usually a portable brazier but symbolised the heart and soul of the household and came to represent its centre.

claims.quote: The goddesses personification as the hearth also linked her to ideas of hospitality, the protection of guests, and the inventor of good housebuilding.

statement.id: Personifikasi Hestia sebagai perapian juga mengaitkannya dengan keramahtamahan, perlindungan tamu, dan penemu pembangunan rumah yang baik.
statement.en: Hestia's personification as the hearth also linked her to hospitality, the protection of guests, and the inventor of good housebuilding.

claims.quote: Besides individual homes, Hestia was particularly associated with the prytaneion and bouleuterion, the symbolic centre of a town or city where civic functions were held and the business of local government was carried out.

statement.id: Selain rumah pribadi, Hestia terutama dikaitkan dengan prytaneion dan bouleuterion, pusat simbolis kota tempat urusan pemerintahan setempat dijalankan.
statement.en: Besides individual homes, Hestia was particularly associated with the prytaneion and bouleuterion, the symbolic centre of a town where local government business was carried out.

claims.quote: Public worship of Hestia was especially prevalent in Attica with notable cults at Piraeus, Eleusis, Halimos, and Krokonidai.

statement.id: Pemujaan umum Hestia terutama marak di Attica dengan kultus penting di Piraeus, Eleusis, Halimos, dan Krokonidai.
statement.en: Public worship of Hestia was especially prevalent in Attica, with notable cults at Piraeus, Eleusis, Halimos, and Krokonidai.

claims.quote: The Greek goddess was the only one to not join the Olympians in their failed attack on Zeus.

statement.id: Hestia adalah satu-satunya dewi yang tidak ikut para dewa Olimpus dalam serangan gagal mereka terhadap Zeus.
statement.en: Hestia was the only goddess who did not join the Olympians in their failed attack on Zeus.

claims.quote: Hestia is usually presented in Greek art as a young female wearing a head covering & modest clothing.

statement.id: Dalam seni Yunani, Hestia biasanya ditampilkan sebagai perempuan muda berpenutup kepala dan berpakaian sederhana.
statement.en: In Greek art Hestia is usually presented as a young woman wearing a head covering and modest clothing.

claims.quote: As Hestia has no particular mythology surrounding her, she does not appear very often in Greek art, and when she does, she can be difficult to distinguish from other goddesses

statement.id: Karena tidak punya mitologi khusus, Hestia jarang muncul dalam seni Yunani dan sulit dibedakan dari dewi lain.
statement.en: Because she has no particular mythology, Hestia appears rarely in Greek art and can be difficult to distinguish from other goddesses.

claims.quote: In the Roman period, Hestia, now known as Vesta, continued to be worshipped, for example at Ephesus where the high priest was a female.

statement.id: Pada masa Romawi, Hestia, yang kini dikenal sebagai Vesta, terus dipuja, misalnya di Ephesus tempat imam besarnya perempuan.
statement.en: In the Roman period Hestia, now known as Vesta, continued to be worshipped, for example at Ephesus where the high priest was a woman.

claims.quote: She appears on the celebrated Francois Vase (570-565 BCE) and, this time named, on the north frieze of the Siphinian Treasury at Delphi (c. 525 BCE) where she and an unidentified goddess face two giants in hoplite uniform.

statement.id: Hestia muncul pada Vas Francois (570-565 SM) dan, kali ini dengan nama, pada friz utara Perbendaharaan Siphnos di Delphi (sekitar 525 SM) menghadapi dua raksasa berbaju prajurit hoplit.
statement.en: Hestia appears on the Francois Vase (570-565 BCE) and, this time named, on the north frieze of the Siphnian Treasury at Delphi (c. 525 BCE), facing two giants in hoplite uniform with an unidentified goddess.

claims.quote: As the goddess of the family hearth she also presided over the cooking of bread and the preparation of the family meal.

statement.id: Sebagai dewi perapian keluarga, Hestia juga memimpin pembuatan roti dan penyiapan hidangan keluarga.
statement.en: As goddess of the family hearth, Hestia also presided over the baking of bread and the preparation of the family meal.

claims.quote: In myth Hestia was the first born child of Kronos (Cronus) and Rhea who was swallowed by her father at birth. Zeus later forced the old Titan to disgorge Hestia and her siblings.

statement.id: Dalam mitos Hestia adalah anak sulung Kronos dan Rhea yang ditelan ayahnya saat lahir; Zeus kemudian memaksa sang Titan memuntahkan Hestia dan saudara-saudaranya.
statement.en: In myth Hestia was the firstborn of Kronos and Rhea, swallowed by her father at birth; Zeus later forced the old Titan to disgorge Hestia and her siblings.

claims.quote: As the first to be swallowed she was also the last to be disgorged, and so was named as both the eldest and youngest of the six Kronides.

statement.id: Karena yang pertama ditelan sekaligus yang terakhir dimuntahkan, Hestia disebut sebagai yang tertua sekaligus termuda dari enam Kronid.
statement.en: Being the first swallowed and last disgorged, Hestia was named both the eldest and youngest of the six Kronides.

claims.quote: When the gods Apollon and Poseidon sought for her hand in marriage, Hestia refused and asked Zeus to let her remain an eternal virgin. He agreed and she took her place at his royal hearth.

statement.id: Ketika Apollon dan Poseidon melamarnya, Hestia menolak dan meminta Zeus membiarkannya tetap perawan; Zeus setuju dan ia mengambil tempat di perapian kerajaan Zeus.
statement.en: When Apollon and Poseidon sought her hand, Hestia refused and asked Zeus to let her remain an eternal virgin; he agreed and she took her place at his royal hearth.

claims.quote: So Zeus the Father gave her a high honour instead of marriage, and she has her place in the midst of the house and has the richest portion. In all the temples of the gods she has a share of honour, and among all mortal men she is chief of the goddesses.

statement.id: Menurut Himne Homerik untuk Aphrodite, Zeus memberinya kehormatan tinggi sebagai ganti pernikahan: tempat di tengah rumah, bagian terkaya, bagian kehormatan di semua kuil, dan kedudukan sebagai dewi utama di antara manusia.
statement.en: According to the Homeric Hymn to Aphrodite, Zeus gave her high honour instead of marriage: a place in the midst of the house, the richest portion, a share of honour in all temples, and the position of chief of the goddesses among mortals.

claims.quote: For without you mortals hold no banquet,--where one does not duly pour sweet wine in offering to Hestia both first and last.

statement.id: Menurut Himne Homerik untuk Hestia, manusia tidak mengadakan pesta tanpa Hestia, karena anggur manis dituangkan baginya lebih dulu dan terakhir.
statement.en: According to the Homeric Hymn to Hestia, mortals hold no banquet without her, since sweet wine is poured in offering to Hestia first and last.

claims.quote: Hestia was looked upon as presiding at all sacrifices, and, as the goddess of the sacred fire of the altar, she had a share in the sacrifices in all the temples of the gods.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Hestia dipandang memimpin semua kurban dan, sebagai dewi api suci altar, mendapat bagian dalam kurban di semua kuil para dewa.
statement.en: Hestia was regarded as presiding at all sacrifices and, as goddess of the sacred fire of the altar, had a share in the sacrifices in all the temples of the gods.

claims.quote: As the hearth was looked upon as the sacred centre of domestic life, so Hestia was the goddess of domestic life and the giver of all domestic happiness and blessings, and as such she was believed to dwell in the inner part of every house
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Karena perapian dipandang pusat suci kehidupan rumah tangga, Hestia dianggap dewi kehidupan rumah tangga dan pemberi segala kebahagiaan dan berkat rumah tangga, serta dipercaya berdiam di bagian dalam setiap rumah.
statement.en: As the hearth was seen as the sacred centre of domestic life, Hestia was the goddess of domestic life and giver of all domestic happiness and blessings, believed to dwell in the inner part of every house.

claims.quote: In classical sculpture she was also veiled, with a kettle as her attribute.

statement.id: Dalam patung klasik Hestia juga berkerudung, dengan ketel sebagai atributnya.
statement.en: In classical sculpture she was also veiled, with a kettle as her attribute.

claims.quote: Solemn oaths were sworn by the goddess of the hearth, and the hearth itself was the sacred asylum where suppliants implored the protection of the inhabitants of the house.

statement.id: Sumpah khidmat diucapkan demi dewi perapian, dan perapian sendiri adalah suaka suci tempat pemohon meminta perlindungan penghuni rumah.
statement.en: Solemn oaths were sworn by the goddess of the hearth, and the hearth itself was the sacred asylum where suppliants implored the protection of the household.

claims.quote: Her sacrifices consisted of the primitiae of fruit, water, oil, wine, and cows of one year old.

statement.id: Kurban bagi Hestia berupa buah sulung, air, minyak, anggur, dan sapi berumur satu tahun.
statement.en: Sacrifices to Hestia consisted of the first fruits, water, oil, wine, and cows one year old.

claims.quote: If ever the fire of her hearth became extinct, it was not allowed to be lighted again with ordinary fire, but either by fire produced by friction, or by burning glasses drawing fire from the sun.

statement.en: If the fire of her hearth went out, it could not be relit with ordinary fire but only by fire made by friction or by burning glasses drawing fire from the sun.

claims.quote: In this respect she appears often together with Hermes, who was likewise a deus penetralis, as protecting the works of man.

claims.quote: Vesta [Hestia] lies down and takes a quiet, carefree nap, just as she was, her head pillowed by turf. But the red saviour of gardens [Priapos] prowls for Nymphai and goddesses, and wanders back and forth. He spots Vesta.

claims.quote: the anonymous author of the hymn was trying to reconcile the two conflicting birth orders given by Hesiod and Homer; while in the Theogony the firstborn is Hestia, in the Iliad Hera states that she is the eldest child.

statement.en: Like Athena and Artemis, Hestia chose never to marry and remained an eternal virgin goddess, forever tending the hearth of Olympus.

statement.en: In Ancient Greek her name is written Ἑστία, literally 'hearth, fireplace, altar'.

claims.quote: Nor yet does the pure maiden Histia (Hestia) love Aphrodite's works.

statement.en: Because Hestia was named first, a saying developed: 'to begin from Hestia.'

short_description.id: Persephone, juga disebut Kore, adalah dewi Yunani pertanian dan tumbuhan, putri Demeter, yang menjadi ratu dunia bawah sebagai istri Hades dan kembali ke permukaan setiap tahun.
short_description.en: Persephone, also called Kore, is a Greek goddess of agriculture and vegetation, daughter of Demeter, who became queen of the underworld as Hades's wife and returns to the surface each year.

long_description.id: Persephone, atau Kore, adalah dewi Yunani yang terkait dengan pertanian, tumbuhan, dan khususnya biji-bijian. Ia putri Zeus dan Demeter, serta istri Hades, penguasa dunia bawah, sehingga ia dikenal sebagai ratu dunia bawah. Kore berarti "anak perempuan" sekaligus "gadis"; dalam bahasa Latin ia disebut Proserpina. Para sarjana menafsirkan mitosnya sebagai perwujudan musim semi dan tumbuhan, dan julukannya menunjukkan fungsi ganda sebagai dewi bawah tanah dan dewi tumbuhan.
long_description.en: Persephone, or Kore, is a Greek goddess associated with agriculture, vegetation and especially grain. She is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter and the wife of Hades, ruler of the underworld, so she is known as queen of the underworld. Kore means "daughter" and "maiden" at once; in Latin she is called Proserpina. Scholars interpret her myth as embodying spring and vegetation, and her epithets show a double function as chthonic and vegetation goddess.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah penculikannya, Persephone sedang memetik bunga di padang rumput bersama kawan-kawannya ketika Hades membawanya ke dunia bawah dengan kereta. Menurut Himne Homerik untuk Demeter, bumi menganga di dataran Nysa dan hanya Hecate dan Helios yang mendengar teriakannya. Demeter berkelana mencarinya hingga Eleusis; kesedihannya menyebabkan gagal panen dan kekeringan hingga Zeus memerintahkan Hades mengembalikannya.
long_description.en: In the story of her abduction, Persephone was picking flowers in a meadow with her companions when Hades carried her off to the underworld. According to the Homeric Hymn to Demeter, the earth yawned in the plain of Nysa and only Hecate and Helios heard her cry. Demeter wandered in search of her as far as Eleusis; her grief caused crops to fail and a drought until Zeus ordered Hades to return her.

long_description.id: Sebelum melepasnya, Hades memberi Persephone biji delima. Menurut Himne Homerik, Demeter menyatakan bahwa jika ia telah makan, ia harus tinggal di bawah bumi selama sepertiga tahun dan menyertai para dewa selama dua bagian lainnya; sumber lain menyebut sepertiga atau separuh tahun. Ia naik kembali ketika bumi mekar di musim semi, dan sejak itu Hecate menjadi pendampingnya. Kisah ini dapat melambangkan pergantian musim, meski ada tafsiran lain tentang penyimpanan gandum di bawah tanah.
long_description.en: Before releasing her, Hades gave Persephone pomegranate seed. According to the Homeric Hymn, Demeter declares that if she has eaten she must stay beneath the earth for a third of the year and be with the gods for the other two parts; another source says one-third or one-half of the year. She comes up again when the earth blooms in spring, and from then on Hecate is her companion. The story may symbolize the change of seasons, though another interpretation concerns the storage of grain underground.

long_description.id: Persephone adalah unsur penting dalam Misteri Eleusis, yang menjanjikan akhirat bahagia, dan dalam festival Thesmophoria; kultusnya kuat di Sisilia dan Italia selatan, dan di Locris ia dewi pernikahan dan kelahiran. Sebagai ratu dunia bawah ia sering dimohon dalam tablet kutukan. Dalam seni Yunani Klasik ia digambarkan berjubah, sering membawa seikat gandum, dan paling sering ditampilkan saat dibawa pergi Hades.
long_description.en: Persephone was an important element of the Eleusinian Mysteries, which promised a happy afterlife, and of the Thesmophoria festival; her cult was strong in Sicily and southern Italy, and at Locris she was a goddess of marriage and childbirth. As queen of the underworld she was often appealed to in curse tablets. In Classical Greek art she is shown robed, often carrying a sheaf of grain, and most often being carried off by Hades.

cultural_context.id: Persephone dan Demeter adalah tokoh sentral Misteri Eleusis, yang menjanjikan akhirat bahagia bagi yang diinisiasi, dan kisah mereka dibaca sebagai lambang pergantian musim serta daur hidup dan mati; ada pula tafsiran bahwa mitos itu merujuk pada penyimpanan gandum di bawah tanah. Mitos serupa tentang turun dan kembalinya juga muncul dalam kultus Attis, Adonis, dan Osiris.
cultural_context.en: Persephone and Demeter were central figures of the Eleusinian Mysteries, which promised initiates a happy afterlife, and their story is read as symbolizing the changing seasons and the cycle of life and death; another interpretation is that the myth refers to storing grain underground. Similar myths of descent and return also appear in the cults of Attis, Adonis and Osiris.

literal_meaning.id: Asal katanya tidak jelas; satu hipotesis memaknainya "ia yang memukul bulir gandum", etimologi rakyat memaknainya "membawa kematian".
literal_meaning.en: The etymology is obscure; one hypothesis reads it as "she who beats the ears of corn", a folk etymology as "to bring death".

who.id: Persephone adalah dewi Yunani pertanian dan tumbuhan sekaligus ratu dunia bawah.
who.en: Persephone is a Greek goddess of agriculture and vegetation and queen of the underworld.

origin.id: Ia putri Zeus dan Demeter dalam mitologi Yunani.
origin.en: She is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter in Greek mythology.

role.id: Ia istri Hades yang memerintah bersamanya di dunia bawah dan menjadi tokoh dalam Misteri Eleusis.
role.en: She is the wife of Hades who rules beside him in the underworld and a figure in the Eleusinian Mysteries.

famous_for.id: Ia paling dikenal karena diculik Hades dan kembali setiap tahun ke permukaan.
famous_for.en: She is best known for being abducted by Hades and returning to the surface each year.

did_you_know.id: Dalam seni, ia paling sering ditampilkan bukan sebagai ratu yang duduk di tahta, melainkan pada saat dibawa pergi oleh Hades.
did_you_know.en: In art she is most often shown not as an enthroned queen but in the moment of being carried off by Hades.

description.id: Dalam Himne Homerik, Hades menyatakan Persephone akan memerintah semua yang hidup dan bergerak dan memiliki hak terbesar di antara para dewa; mereka yang menipunya akan dihukum.
description.en: In the Homeric Hymn Hades declares Persephone shall rule all that lives and moves and have the greatest rights among the gods; those who defraud her shall be punished.

description.id: Sebagai ratu dunia bawah ia dipandang sebagai pelindung di alam baka, meski Hesiodos menyebutnya "menakutkan".
description.en: As queen of the underworld she was seen as a protectress in the after-life, though Hesiod calls her "dread".

description.id: Kisah penculikan dan kembalinya mewakili fungsinya sebagai perwujudan musim semi dan personifikasi tumbuhan, terutama biji-bijian.
description.en: The story of her abduction and return represents her functions as embodiment of spring and personification of vegetation, especially grain.

description.id: Dalam beberapa versi, Persephone bisa dibebaskan seandainya tidak makan apa pun di dunia bawah; biji delima yang diberikan Hades membuatnya harus kembali sebagian tahun.
description.en: In some versions Persephone could have been released had she eaten nothing in the underworld; the pomegranate seed Hades gave her obliges her to return for part of the year.

description.id: Nama Latin Persephone; orang Romawi juga mengidentifikasinya sebagai Libera, dewi Italik yang dipadukan dengan Proserpina.
description.en: The Latin name of Persephone; the Romans also identified her as Libera, an Italic goddess conflated with Proserpina.

description.id: Di wilayah itu ia dewi pernikahan dan kelahiran.
description.en: In this region she is a goddess of marriage and childbirth.

role.id: Gadis yang diculik Hades dan dibawa ke dunia bawah.
role.en: The maiden carried off by Hades to the underworld.

summary.id: Persephone memetik bunga di padang rumput ketika Hades membawanya dengan kereta ke dunia bawah. Dalam Himne Homerik, bunga narsis ditumbuhkan sebagai jerat baginya, bumi menganga di dataran Nysa, dan hanya Hecate dan Helios yang mendengar teriakannya.
summary.en: Persephone was picking flowers in a meadow when Hades carried her off in his chariot to the underworld. In the Homeric Hymn the narcissus was grown as a snare for her, the earth yawned in the plain of Nysa, and only Hecate and Helios heard her cry.

role.id: Putri yang kepergiannya memicu kekeringan.
role.en: The daughter whose loss triggers the drought.

summary.id: Demeter mencari putrinya hingga tiba di Eleusis, lalu menarik diri ke kuilnya dan menciptakan kekeringan besar agar para dewa melepaskan Persephone. Ketika korban bertambah, Zeus mengutus Hermes untuk membujuk Hades.
summary.en: Demeter searched for her daughter until she reached Eleusis, then withdrew into her temple and created a great drought so the gods would release Persephone. As the victims mounted, Zeus sent Hermes to persuade Hades.

role.id: Putri yang dilepas tetapi terikat pada dunia bawah oleh biji delima.
role.en: The daughter released but bound to the underworld by the pomegranate.

summary.id: Hades memberi Persephone biji delima sebelum melepasnya. Sebagai kompromi, ia harus kembali ke dunia bawah selama sepertiga tahun (atau separuh dalam versi lain) dan naik kembali ketika bumi mekar di musim semi.
summary.en: Hades gave Persephone a pomegranate seed before releasing her. As a compromise she must return to the underworld for a third of the year (or a half in other versions) and comes up again when the earth blooms in spring.

role.id: Pesaing Aphrodite dalam memperebutkan Adonis.
role.en: Aphrodite's rival for Adonis.

summary.en: In another myth Persephone squabbles with Aphrodite over Adonis until the two agree to share him in turns.

description.en: Where Demeter arrived in her search and the site of the Eleusinian Mysteries, in which Persephone was an important element.

description.en: In the Homeric Hymn, where the earth yawned and Hades sprang out to carry Persephone off.

claims.quote: Persephone (aka Kore) was the Greek goddess of agriculture and vegetation, especially grain, and the wife of Hades, the ruler of the Underworld.

statement.id: Persephone adalah dewi pertanian dan tumbuhan Yunani serta istri Hades.
statement.en: Persephone is a Greek goddess of agriculture and vegetation and wife of Hades.

claims.quote: In this guise she is most often referred to as Kore, signifying both 'daughter' and 'maiden'.
claims.locator: What are the Different Names of Persephone?

statement.id: Nama Kore berarti anak perempuan dan gadis.
statement.en: Kore means daughter and maiden.

claims.quote: In Greek mythology, the goddess, as wife of Hades, is the Queen of the Underworld and takes her other name, Persephone.
claims.locator: What are the Different Names of Persephone?

statement.id: Sebagai istri Hades, Persephone adalah ratu dunia bawah.
statement.en: As Hades's wife, Persephone is queen of the underworld.

claims.quote: Hades abducted Persephone while she was picking flowers with her companions in a meadow and carried her off to the Underworld

statement.id: Hades menculik Persephone saat ia memetik bunga dan membawanya ke dunia bawah.
statement.en: Hades abducted Persephone while she picked flowers and took her to the underworld.

claims.quote: There the wrath of the distressed mother caused a complete failure of the crops, prompting Zeus to order his brother Hades to return the girl.

statement.id: Kesedihan Demeter menyebabkan gagal panen sehingga Zeus meminta Hades mengembalikan Persephone.
statement.en: Demeter's grief caused crop failure, prompting Zeus to demand Persephone's return.

claims.quote: He cunningly tricked Persephone into eating some pomegranate seeds before leaving, thus condemning her to spend part of the year in the Underworld as his wife and the rest among the living with Demeter

statement.id: Karena biji delima, Persephone harus menghabiskan sebagian tahun di dunia bawah dan sisanya bersama Demeter.
statement.en: Pomegranate seeds obliged Persephone to spend part of the year below and the rest with Demeter.

claims.quote: The story of Demeter, Hades and Persephone was perhaps symbolic of the changing seasons and the perennial change from life to death, to life once more
claims.locator: What is the Significance of the Hades-Persephone Myth?

statement.id: Kisah ini dapat melambangkan pergantian musim dan daur kehidupan.
statement.en: The story may symbolize seasonal change and life's cycle.

claims.quote: Persephone was an important element of the Eleusinian Mysteries and the Thesmophoria festival and so the goddess was worshipped throughout the Greek world.

statement.id: Persephone terkait dengan Misteri Eleusis dan perayaan Thesmophoria.
statement.en: Persephone was linked to the Eleusinian Mysteries and Thesmophoria.

claims.quote: At the right is Persephone, her daughter and the wife of Hades, the god of the underworld.

statement.id: Relief Eleusis menggambarkan Persephone di sisi kanan sebagai putri Demeter.
statement.en: The Eleusinian relief depicts Persephone on the right as Demeter's daughter.

claims.quote: Hades, god of the Underworld, fell in love with beautiful Persephone when he saw her picking flowers one day in a meadow. The god then carried her off in his chariot to live with him in the dark Underworld.

statement.id: Hades, dewa dunia bawah, jatuh cinta pada Persephone yang cantik ketika melihatnya memetik bunga di padang rumput, lalu membawanya dengan kereta ke dunia bawah yang gelap.
statement.en: Hades, god of the Underworld, fell in love with the beautiful Persephone when he saw her picking flowers in a meadow, then carried her off in his chariot to the dark Underworld.

claims.quote: In some accounts, Zeus had given his consent to the abduction, the location of the crime being traditionally placed in either Sicily (famed for its fertility) or Asia.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian versi Zeus menyetujui penculikan itu, dan lokasinya secara tradisional ditempatkan di Sisilia (termasyhur kesuburannya) atau Asia.
statement.en: In some accounts Zeus had consented to the abduction, and the location is traditionally placed in either Sicily (famed for its fertility) or Asia.

claims.quote: Meanwhile, Demeter searched the earth for her lost divine daughter and though Helios (or Hermes) told her of her daughter's fate, she, nevertheless, continued her wanderings until she finally arrived at Eleusis.

statement.id: Demeter mencari putrinya ke seluruh bumi; meski Helios (atau Hermes) memberitahunya nasib putrinya, ia terus berkelana hingga tiba di Eleusis.
statement.en: Demeter searched the earth for her lost daughter; though Helios (or Hermes) told her her daughter's fate, she kept wandering until she arrived at Eleusis.

claims.quote: Once the temple was completed, Demeter withdrew from the world and lived inside it; at the same time, she created a great drought to convince the other gods to release Persephone from Hades. As the drought claimed ever more victims, Zeus finally sent Hermes to persuade Hades to release his ill-gotten bride.

statement.id: Setelah kuil selesai, Demeter menarik diri dan tinggal di dalamnya sambil menciptakan kekeringan besar agar dewa-dewa lain melepaskan Persephone; ketika korban kekeringan bertambah, Zeus mengutus Hermes membujuk Hades.
statement.en: Once the temple was finished, Demeter withdrew into it and created a great drought to convince the other gods to release Persephone; as the drought claimed more victims, Zeus sent Hermes to persuade Hades to release her.

claims.quote: Before giving her up though, the wily Hades put a pomegranate kernel in the girl's mouth, knowing its divine taste would compel her to return to him.

statement.id: Sebelum melepasnya, Hades yang licik menaruh sebutir biji delima di mulut Persephone karena tahu rasa ilahinya akan memaksanya kembali.
statement.en: Before giving her up, the wily Hades put a pomegranate kernel in her mouth, knowing its divine taste would compel her to return to him.

claims.quote: Finally, as a compromise, it was decided that Persephone would be released but that she would have to return to Hades for one-third of the year (or in other accounts one-half).

statement.id: Sebagai kompromi, diputuskan Persephone dilepas tetapi harus kembali kepada Hades selama sepertiga tahun (atau separuh tahun dalam versi lain).
statement.en: As a compromise, it was decided Persephone would be released but must return to Hades for one-third of the year (or one-half in other accounts).

claims.quote: Another interpretation of the Persephone myth may be that it represents when the Greeks stored their grain underground for part of the year in order to protect it from summer heat.
claims.locator: What is the Significance of the Hades-Persephone Myth?

statement.id: Tafsiran lain: mitos itu mungkin menggambarkan saat orang Yunani menyimpan gandum di bawah tanah selama sebagian tahun untuk melindunginya dari panas musim panas.
statement.en: Another interpretation is that the myth represents the Greeks storing their grain underground for part of the year to protect it from summer heat.

claims.quote: The cult of Persephone in the Greek religion was especially strong in Sicily and southern Italy, and besides the Eleusinian Mysteries at Eleusis there were sanctuaries to the goddess across the Greek world, most notably at Locri Epizephyrii, Mantinea, Megalopolis, and Sparta.

statement.id: Kultus Persephone dalam agama Yunani sangat kuat di Sisilia dan Italia selatan; selain Misteri Eleusis di Eleusis, ada tempat suci untuknya di seluruh dunia Yunani, terutama di Locri Epizephyrii, Mantinea, Megalopolis, dan Sparta.
statement.en: Persephone's cult was especially strong in Sicily and southern Italy; besides the Eleusinian Mysteries at Eleusis there were sanctuaries across the Greek world, notably at Locri Epizephyrii, Mantinea, Megalopolis and Sparta.

claims.quote: The Thesmophoria was a Greek-wide celebration of the goddess and her mother. Exclusive to women, it was held annually before the sowing period when sacrifices were made and putrefied pig's remains were mixed with the seeds.

statement.id: Thesmophoria adalah perayaan seluruh Yunani untuk sang dewi dan ibunya; khusus perempuan, diadakan tiap tahun sebelum masa menabur, dengan kurban dan sisa babi yang membusuk dicampur ke benih.
statement.en: The Thesmophoria was a Greek-wide celebration of the goddess and her mother, exclusive to women and held annually before sowing, when sacrifices were made and putrefied pig remains were mixed with the seeds.

claims.quote: Persephone, in her guise as Queen of the Underworld, was often appealed to in curse tablets and on the inscribed gold leaves buried with the dead followers of Orphism which gave instructions on how to conduct themselves in the after-life.

statement.id: Sebagai Ratu Dunia Bawah, Persephone sering dimohon dalam tablet kutukan dan pada lembaran emas bertulis yang dikubur bersama pengikut Orfisme yang meninggal.
statement.en: As Queen of the Underworld, Persephone was often appealed to in curse tablets and on inscribed gold leaves buried with dead followers of Orphism.

claims.quote: In this guise, she was seen as a protectress in the after-life, although Hesiod repeatedly describes her as 'dread Persephone' in his Theogony.
claims.locator: What are the Different Names of Persephone?

statement.id: Dalam peran itu ia dipandang sebagai pelindung di alam baka, meski Hesiodos berulang kali menyebutnya "Persephone yang menakutkan" dalam Theogony.
statement.en: In that guise she was seen as a protectress in the after-life, although Hesiod repeatedly calls her "dread Persephone" in his Theogony.

claims.quote: Persephone rarely appears in art before the 6th century BCE, and then she is usually shown with Demeter; often both wear crowns and hold a torch, sceptre, or stalks of grain.
claims.locator: How is Persephone Represented in Art?

statement.id: Persephone jarang muncul dalam seni sebelum abad ke-6 SM, dan kemudian biasanya ditampilkan bersama Demeter; keduanya sering bermahkota dan memegang obor, tongkat kerajaan, atau tangkai gandum.
statement.en: Persephone rarely appears in art before the 6th century BCE, then is usually shown with Demeter; both often wear crowns and hold a torch, sceptre or stalks of grain.

claims.quote: In various other myths, Persephone is the mother of Dionysos (with Zeus, who is also her father) - although Semele is the more usual candidate - and squabbles with Aphrodite for the attentions of devilishly handsome Adonis, the two settling to share the famous lover in split shifts.
claims.locator: What are the Different Names of Persephone?

statement.id: Dalam beberapa mitos lain Persephone ibu Dionysos (dengan Zeus, yang juga ayahnya), meski Semele kandidat yang lebih lazim, dan ia bersaing dengan Aphrodite memperebutkan Adonis hingga keduanya sepakat berbagi sang kekasih bergiliran.
statement.en: In various other myths Persephone is the mother of Dionysos (by Zeus, who is also her father), though Semele is the more usual candidate, and she squabbles with Aphrodite over Adonis, the two agreeing to share the lover in turns.

claims.quote: A famous relief slab from Eleusis depicts Demeter and Persephone (holding a torch) either side of Triptolemos; it dates to the 5th century BCE.
claims.locator: How is Persephone Represented in Art?

statement.id: Sebuah lempeng relief terkenal dari Eleusis menampilkan Demeter dan Persephone (memegang obor) di kedua sisi Triptolemos; berasal dari abad ke-5 SM.
statement.en: A famous relief slab from Eleusis shows Demeter and Persephone (holding a torch) on either side of Triptolemos; it dates to the 5th century BCE.

claims.quote: In other versions of the myth, Persephone could have been released if she had not eaten anything in the underworld during her captivity, but at the last moment, Hades gave her a pomegranate seed.

statement.id: Dalam versi lain Persephone bisa dibebaskan seandainya ia tidak makan apa pun di dunia bawah, tetapi pada detik terakhir Hades memberinya sebutir biji delima.
statement.en: In other versions Persephone could have been released had she eaten nothing in the underworld, but at the last moment Hades gave her a pomegranate seed.

claims.quote: and the girl was amazed and reached out with both hands to take the lovely toy; but the wide-pathed earth yawned there in the plain of Nysa, and the lord, Host of Many, with his immortal horses sprang out upon her

statement.id: Menurut Himne Homerik untuk Demeter, gadis itu takjub dan mengulurkan kedua tangan untuk mengambil bunga itu; lalu bumi menganga di dataran Nysa dan Sang Tuan Banyak Tamu melompat keluar dengan kuda-kuda abadinya.
statement.en: In the Homeric Hymn to Demeter the girl was amazed and reached out with both hands for the lovely flower; then the earth yawned in the plain of Nysa and the lord, Host of Many, sprang out with his immortal horses.

claims.quote: which Earth made to grow at the will of Zeus and to please the Host of Many, to be a snare for the bloom-like girl

statement.id: Bunga narsis itu ditumbuhkan Bumi atas kehendak Zeus dan untuk menyenangkan Sang Tuan Banyak Tamu, sebagai jerat bagi gadis yang segar bagai bunga.
statement.en: The narcissus was made to grow by Earth at the will of Zeus and to please the Host of Many, as a snare for the bloom-like girl.

claims.quote: only tender-hearted Hecate, bright-coiffed, the daughter of Persaeus, heard the girl from her cave, and the lord Helios, Hyperion's bright son

statement.id: Hanya Hecate yang berhati lembut, putri Persaeus, mendengar teriakan gadis itu dari guanya, begitu pula tuan Helios, putra Hyperion yang cemerlang.
statement.en: Only tender-hearted Hecate, daughter of Persaeus, heard the girl from her cave, and the lord Helios, Hyperion's bright son.

claims.quote: And while you are here, you shall rule all that lives and moves and shall have the greatest rights among the deathless gods: those who defraud you and do not appease your power with offerings, reverently performing rites and paying fit gifts, shall be punished for evermore.

statement.id: Dalam Himne Homerik, Hades berkata kepada Persephone bahwa selama di sana ia akan memerintah semua yang hidup dan bergerak dan memiliki hak terbesar di antara para dewa; mereka yang menipunya dan tidak menenangkan kuasanya dengan persembahan akan dihukum selamanya.
statement.en: In the Homeric Hymn Hades tells Persephone that while she is there she shall rule all that lives and moves and have the greatest rights among the gods; those who defraud her and do not appease her power with offerings shall be punished for evermore.

claims.quote: But he on his part secretly gave her sweet pomegranate seed to eat, taking care for himself that she might not remain continually with grave, dark-robed Demeter.

statement.id: Hades diam-diam memberinya biji delima manis untuk dimakan agar ia tidak terus-menerus tinggal bersama Demeter.
statement.en: Hades secretly gave her sweet pomegranate seed to eat, taking care that she might not remain continually with Demeter.

claims.quote: if you have tasted food, you must go back again beneath the secret places of the earth, there to dwell a third part of the seasons every year: yet for the two parts you shall be with me and the other deathless gods.

statement.id: Demeter berkata: jika Persephone telah mencicipi makanan, ia harus kembali ke bawah bumi dan tinggal di sana sepertiga musim setiap tahun, sedangkan dua bagian lainnya ia bersama Demeter dan para dewa.
statement.en: Demeter says that if Persephone has tasted food she must go back beneath the earth to dwell a third part of the seasons every year, and for the other two parts be with her and the other gods.

claims.quote: But when the earth shall bloom with the fragrant flowers of spring in every kind, then from the realm of darkness and gloom thou shalt come up once more to be a wonder for gods and mortal men.

statement.id: Ketika bumi mekar dengan bunga-bunga musim semi yang harum, Persephone akan naik lagi dari alam gelap menjadi keajaiban bagi dewa dan manusia.
statement.en: When the earth blooms with the fragrant flowers of spring, Persephone shall come up once more from the realm of darkness to be a wonder for gods and mortals.

claims.quote: from that time the lady Hecate was minister and companion to Persephone.

statement.id: Sejak saat itu Hecate menjadi pelayan dan pendamping Persephone.
statement.en: From that time Hecate was minister and companion to Persephone.

claims.quote: Ancient Greek: Περσεφόνη ) is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter. She became the queen of the underworld after her abduction by her uncle Hades, the king of the underworld, who later took her into marriage.

statement.id: Persephone (Περσεφόνη dalam bahasa Yunani Kuno) adalah putri Zeus dan Demeter; ia menjadi ratu dunia bawah setelah diculik pamannya, Hades, raja dunia bawah, yang kemudian menikahinya.
statement.en: Persephone (Περσεφόνη in Ancient Greek) is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter; she became queen of the underworld after her abduction by her uncle Hades, king of the underworld, who later took her into marriage.

claims.quote: The myth of her abduction, her sojourn in the underworld, and her cyclical return to the surface represents her functions as the embodiment of spring and the personification of vegetation, especially grain crops

statement.id: Mitos penculikan, masa tinggalnya di dunia bawah, dan kembalinya yang berulang ke permukaan mewakili fungsinya sebagai perwujudan musim semi dan personifikasi tumbuhan, terutama tanaman biji-bijian.
statement.en: The myth of her abduction, sojourn in the underworld and cyclical return to the surface represents her functions as embodiment of spring and personification of vegetation, especially grain crops.

claims.quote: In Classical Greek art, Persephone is invariably portrayed robed, often carrying a sheaf of grain. She may appear as a mystical divinity with a sceptre and a little box, but she was mostly represented in the process of being carried off by Hades.

statement.id: Dalam seni Yunani Klasik, Persephone selalu digambarkan berjubah, sering membawa seikat gandum; ia dapat tampil sebagai dewi mistik dengan tongkat dan kotak kecil, tetapi paling sering ditampilkan saat dibawa pergi Hades.
statement.en: In Classical Greek art Persephone is invariably robed, often carrying a sheaf of grain; she may appear as a mystical divinity with a sceptre and a little box, but was mostly shown being carried off by Hades.

claims.quote: Persephone, as a vegetation goddess, and her mother Demeter were the central figures of the Eleusinian Mysteries, which promised the initiated a happy afterlife.

statement.id: Persephone sebagai dewi tumbuhan dan ibunya, Demeter, adalah tokoh sentral Misteri Eleusis yang menjanjikan akhirat bahagia bagi para penganutnya.
statement.en: Persephone as a vegetation goddess and her mother Demeter were the central figures of the Eleusinian Mysteries, which promised initiates a happy afterlife.

claims.quote: She is a goddess of marriage and childbirth in the region of the city of Epizephyrian Locris, in modern Calabria (southern Italy).

statement.id: Di wilayah kota Locris Epizephyria, di Calabria modern (Italia selatan), ia adalah dewi pernikahan dan kelahiran.
statement.en: In the region of the city of Epizephyrian Locris, in modern Calabria (southern Italy), she is a goddess of marriage and childbirth.

claims.quote: In Latin, her name is rendered Proserpina. She was identified by the Romans as Libera, an Italic goddess who was conflated with Proserpina.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Latin namanya menjadi Proserpina; orang Romawi mengidentifikasinya sebagai Libera, dewi Italik yang dipadukan dengan Proserpina.
statement.en: In Latin her name is rendered Proserpina; the Romans identified her as Libera, an Italic goddess conflated with Proserpina.

claims.quote: The etymology of the word "Persephone" is obscure. ... pherein phonon, "to bring (or cause) death".

statement.id: Asal kata "Persephone" tidak jelas; etimologi rakyat yang populer mengaitkannya dengan pherein phonon, "membawa (atau menyebabkan) kematian".
statement.en: The etymology of "Persephone" is obscure; a popular folk etymology links it to pherein phonon, "to bring (or cause) death".

claims.quote: Günther Zuntz considers "Persephone" and "Kore" as distinct deities and writes that "no farmer prayed for corn to Persephone; no mourner thought of the dead as being with Kore." Ancient Greek writers were, however, not as consistent as Zuntz claims.

statement.id: Günther Zuntz menganggap "Persephone" dan "Kore" dewi yang berbeda ("tak ada petani memohon gandum kepada Persephone; tak ada orang berduka membayangkan yang mati bersama Kore"), tetapi para penulis Yunani kuno tidak sekonsisten klaimnya.
statement.en: Günther Zuntz considers "Persephone" and "Kore" distinct deities ("no farmer prayed for corn to Persephone; no mourner thought of the dead as being with Kore"), but ancient Greek writers were not as consistent as he claims.

claims.quote: Myths similar to Persephone's descent and return to earth also appear in the cults of male gods, including Attis, Adonis, and Osiris, and in Minoan Crete.

statement.id: Mitos serupa turunnya Persephone dan kembalinya ke bumi juga muncul dalam kultus dewa-dewa laki-laki, termasuk Attis, Adonis, dan Osiris, serta di Kreta Minoa.
statement.en: Myths similar to Persephone's descent and return also appear in the cults of male gods, including Attis, Adonis and Osiris, and in Minoan Crete.

claims.quote: The epithets of Persephone reveal her double function as chthonic and vegetation goddess.

statement.id: Julukan Persephone menunjukkan fungsi gandanya sebagai dewi kekuatan bawah tanah (khthonik) dan dewi tumbuhan.
statement.en: Persephone's epithets reveal her double function as chthonic and vegetation goddess.

claims.quote: According to a recent hypothesis advanced by Rudolf Wachter ... The combined sense would therefore be "she who beats the ears of corn", i.e., a "thresher of grain"

statement.id: Menurut hipotesis Rudolf Wachter, makna gabungan namanya adalah "ia yang memukul bulir gandum", yaitu "perontok gandum".
statement.en: According to a hypothesis by Rudolf Wachter, the combined sense of the name would be "she who beats the ears of corn", i.e. a "thresher of grain".

claims.quote: In cult, she was often referred to as Kore

statement.id: Dalam kultus ia sering disebut Kore.
statement.en: In cult she was often referred to as Kore.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
